Human.name: Human
Human.description: Humans are the most adaptable and ambitious people among the common races. Whatever drives them, humans are the innovators, the achievers, and the pioneers of the worlds.

Elf (High).name: Elf (High)
Elf (High).description: High elves have a keen mind and a mastery of at least the basics of magic. They are known for their grace and mastery of both sword and spell.

Elf (Wood).name: Elf (Wood)
Elf (Wood).description: Wood elves have keen senses and intuition, and their fleet feet carry them quickly and stealthily through their native forests.

Elf (Dark).name: Elf (Dark)
Elf (Dark).description: Dark elves, also known as drow, were banished from the surface world for following the goddess Lolth down the path of evil.

Dwarf (Hill).name: Dwarf (Hill)
Dwarf (Hill).description: Hill dwarves have keen senses, deep intuition, and remarkable resilience. They are found in many lands across the world.

Dwarf (Mountain).name: Dwarf (Mountain)
Dwarf (Mountain).description: Mountain dwarves are strong and hardy, accustomed to a difficult life in rugged terrain. They are taller than other dwarves.

Halfling (Lightfoot).name: Halfling (Lightfoot)
Halfling (Lightfoot).description: Lightfoot halflings are adept at blending in with the crowd. They are prone to wanderlust and make excellent companions.

Halfling (Stout).name: Halfling (Stout)
Halfling (Stout).description: Stout halflings are hardier than average and have some resistance to poison. Some say that stouts have dwarven blood.

Dragonborn.name: Dragonborn
Dragonborn.description: Born of dragons, dragonborn walk proudly through a world that greets them with fearful incomprehension. Shaped by draconic gods or the dragons themselves, dragonborn originally hatched from dragon eggs.

Gnome (Forest).name: Gnome (Forest)
Gnome (Forest).description: Forest gnomes have a knack for illusion and inherent quickness and stealth. They tend to be shy and reclusive.

Gnome (Rock).name: Gnome (Rock)
Gnome (Rock).description: Rock gnomes have a natural inventiveness and hardiness beyond that of other gnomes. They are well known for their tinkering.

Half-Elf.name: Half-Elf
Half-Elf.description: Half-elves combine what some say are the best qualities of their elf and human parents: human curiosity, inventiveness, and ambition tempered by the refined senses, love of nature, and artistic tastes of the elves.

Half-Orc.name: Half-Orc
Half-Orc.description: Half-orcs' grayish pigmentation, sloping foreheads, jutting jaws, prominent teeth, and towering builds make their orcish heritage plain for all to see. Half-orcs are not evil by nature, but evil does lurk within them.

Tiefling.name: Tiefling
Tiefling.description: Tieflings are derived from human bloodlines, and in the broadest possible sense, they still look human. However, their infernal heritage has left a clear imprint on their appearance.

Aasimar.name: Aasimar
Aasimar.description: Aasimar bear within their souls the light of the heavens. They are descended from humans with a touch of the power of Mount Celestia, the divine realm of many lawful good deities.

Genasi (Air).name: Genasi (Air)
Genasi (Air).description: Air genasi are descended from djinn and carry the power of elemental air. They are as free as the wind and share its temperamental nature.

Genasi (Earth).name: Genasi (Earth)
Genasi (Earth).description: Earth genasi are descended from dao and inherit the strength and solidity of stone. They are patient and deliberate.

Genasi (Fire).name: Genasi (Fire)
Genasi (Fire).description: Fire genasi are descended from efreet and carry the heat of the inner planes. They tend to be hot-tempered and quick to anger.

Genasi (Water).name: Genasi (Water)
Genasi (Water).description: Water genasi are descended from marids and carry the fluid grace of the elemental planes. They are independent and self-confident.

Goliath.name: Goliath
Goliath.description: At the highest mountain peaks dwell the reclusive goliaths. Few folk can claim to have seen a goliath, and fewer still can claim friendship with them. Goliaths wander a bleak realm of rock, wind, and cold.

Tabaxi.name: Tabaxi
Tabaxi.description: Hailing from a strange and distant land, wandering tabaxi are catlike humanoids driven by curiosity to collect interesting artifacts, gather tales and stories, and lay eyes on all the world's wonders.

Triton.name: Triton
Triton.description: Tritons guard the ocean depths, building small settlements beside deep trenches, portals to the elemental planes, and other dangerous spots far from the eyes of land-bound folk.

Yuan-ti Pureblood.name: Yuan-ti Pureblood
Yuan-ti Pureblood.description: Yuan-ti purebloods are the most human-seeming of all true yuan-ti. They are the product of breeding between human and yuan-ti, and are the most commonly encountered yuan-ti.

Aasimar (Protector).name: Aasimar (Protector)
Aasimar (Protector).description: Protector aasimar are charged by the powers of good to guard the weak and strike at evil. A protector aasimar receives advice from an angelic entity.

Aasimar (Scourge).name: Aasimar (Scourge)
Aasimar (Scourge).description: Scourge aasimar are imbued with a divine energy that blazes intensely within them. It feeds a powerful desire to destroy evil.

Aasimar (Fallen).name: Aasimar (Fallen)
Aasimar (Fallen).description: Fallen aasimar are touched by dark powers in their youth or have turned to evil. An inner shadow threatens to consume them.

Firbolg.name: Firbolg
Firbolg.description: Firbolg tribes cloister in remote forest strongholds, preferring to spend their days in quiet harmony with the woods. When provoked, firbolgs demonstrate formidable skills with weapons and druidic magic.

Kenku.name: Kenku
Kenku.description: Haunted by an ancient crime that robbed them of their wings, the kenku wander the world as vagabonds and burglars who live at the edge of human society.

Lizardfolk.name: Lizardfolk
Lizardfolk.description: Lizardfolk possess an alien and inscrutable mindset, their desires and thoughts driven by a different set of basic principles than those of warm-blooded creatures.

Dwarf.name: Dwarf
Dwarf.description: Bold and hardy, dwarves are known as skilled warriors, miners, and workers of stone and metal. Though they stand well under 5 feet tall, dwarves are so broad and compact that they can weigh as much as a human standing nearly two feet taller.

Elf.name: Elf
Elf.description: Elves are a magical people of otherworldly grace, living in the world but not entirely part of it. They live in places of ethereal beauty, in the midst of ancient forests or in silvery spires.

Gnome.name: Gnome
Gnome.description: A gnome's energy and enthusiasm for living shines through every inch of his or her tiny body. Gnomes are delighted by life, enjoying every moment of invention, exploration, investigation, creation, and play.

Halfling.name: Halfling
Halfling.description: The comforts of home are the goals of most halflings' lives: a place to settle in peace and quiet, far from marauding monsters and clashing armies. Others form nomadic bands that travel constantly.

Acolyte.name: Acolyte
Acolyte.feature_description: As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle.

personality_traits: I idolize a particular hero of my faith, and constantly refer to their deeds and example.
I can find common ground between the fiercest enemies, empathizing with them and always working toward peace.
I see omens in every event and action.
Nothing can shake my optimistic attitude.
I quote (or misquote) sacred texts and proverbs in almost every situation.
I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
I am tolerant (or intolerant) of other faiths and respect (or condemn) the worship of other gods.
I've enjoyed fine food, drink, and high society among my temple's elite. Rough living grates on me.
ideals: Change. We must help bring about the changes the gods are constantly working in the world. (Chaotic)
Tradition. The ancient ways of our faith must be preserved. (Lawful)
Charity. I always try to help those in need, no matter what the personal cost. (Good)
Power. I hope to one day rise to the top of my faith's religious hierarchy. (Lawful)
Faith. I trust that my deity will guide my actions. I have faith that if I work hard, things will go well. (Lawful)
Aspiration. I seek to prove myself worthy of my god's favor by matching my actions against his or her teachings. (Any)
bonds: I owe my life to the priest who took me in when my parents died.
Everything I do is for the common people.
I will someday get revenge on the corrupt temple hierarchy who branded me a heretic.
I owe a debt I can never repay to the people who helped me.
I pursue wealth to secure my family's future.
I'm convinced there's a powerful enemy after me, and their agents are everywhere I go.
flaws: I judge others harshly, and myself even more severely.
I put too much trust in those who wield power within my temple's hierarchy.
My piety sometimes leads me to blindly trust those that profess faith in my god.
I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
Once I pick a goal, I become obsessed with it to the detriment of everything else in my life.
I can't resist a pretty face.

Criminal.name: Criminal
Criminal.feature_description: You have a reliable and trustworthy contact who acts as your liaison to a network of criminals. You know how to get messages to and from your contact, even over great distances; specifically, you know the local messengers, corrupt caravan masters, and seedy sailors who can deliver messages for you.

Entertainer.name: Entertainer
Entertainer.feature_description: You can always find a place to perform, usually in an inn or tavern but possibly with a circus, at a theater, or even in a noble's court. At such a place, you receive free lodging and food of a modest or comfortable standard (depending on the quality of the establishment), as long as you perform each night. In addition, your performance makes you something of a local figure. When strangers recognize you in a town where you have performed, they typically take a liking to you.

Folk Hero.name: Folk Hero
Folk Hero.feature_description: Since you come from the ranks of the common folk, you fit in among them with ease. You can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among other commoners, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

Guild Artisan.name: Guild Artisan
Guild Artisan.feature_description: As an established and respected member of a guild, you can rely on certain benefits that membership provides. Your fellow guild members will provide you with lodging and food if necessary, and pay for your funeral if needed. In some cities and towns, a guildhall offers a central place to meet other members of your profession, which can be a good place to meet potential patrons, allies, or hirelings.

Hermit.name: Hermit
Hermit.feature_description: The quiet seclusion of your extended hermitage gave you access to a unique and powerful discovery. The exact nature of this revelation depends on the nature of your seclusion. It might be a great truth about the cosmos, the deities, the powerful beings of the outer planes, or the forces of nature. It could be a site that no one else has ever seen. You might have uncovered a fact that has long been forgotten, or unearthed some relic of the past that could rewrite history.

Noble.name: Noble
Noble.feature_description: Thanks to your noble birth, people are inclined to think the best of you. You are welcome in high society, and people assume you have the right to be wherever you are. The common folk make every effort to accommodate you and avoid your displeasure, and other people of high birth treat you as a member of the same social sphere. You can secure an audience with a local noble if you need to.

Outlander.name: Outlander
Outlander.feature_description: You have an excellent memory for maps and geography, and you can always recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other features around you. In addition, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day, provided that the land offers berries, small game, water, and so forth.

Sage.name: Sage
Sage.feature_description: When you attempt to learn or recall a piece of lore, if you do not know that information, you often know where and from whom you can obtain it. Usually, this information comes from a library, scriptorium, university, or a sage or other learned person or creature. Your DM might rule that the knowledge you seek is secreted away in an almost inaccessible place, or that it simply cannot be found. Unearthing the deepest secrets of the multiverse can require an adventure or even a whole campaign.

Sailor.name: Sailor
Sailor.feature_description: No matter where you go, people are afraid of you due to your reputation. When you are in a civilized settlement, you can get away with minor criminal offenses, such as refusing to pay for food at a tavern or breaking down doors at a local shop, since most people will not report your activity to the authorities.

Soldier.name: Soldier
Soldier.feature_description: You have a military rank from your career as a soldier. Soldiers loyal to your former military organization still recognize your authority and influence, and they defer to you if they are of a lower rank. You can invoke your rank to exert influence over other soldiers and requisition simple equipment or horses for temporary use. You can also usually gain access to friendly military encampments and fortresses where your rank is recognized.

Urchin.name: Urchin
Urchin.feature_description: You know the secret patterns and flow to cities and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you (and companions you lead) can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your speed would normally allow.

Shape Water.description: You choose an area of water that you can see within range and that fits within a 5-foot cube.

Shillelagh.description: The wood of a club or quarterstaff you are holding is imbued with nature's power.

Shocking Grasp.description: Lightning springs from your hand to deliver a shock to a creature you try to touch.

Spare the Dying.description: You touch a living creature that has 0 hit points.

Sword Burst.description: You create a momentary circle of spectral blades that sweep around you.

Thaumaturgy.description: You manifest a minor wonder, a sign of supernatural power, within range.

Thorn Whip.description: You create a long, vine-like whip covered in thorns that lashes out at your command toward a creature in range.

Thunderclap.description: You create a burst of thunderous sound that can be heard up to 100 feet away.

Toll the Dead.description: You point at one creature you can see within range, and the sound of a dolorous bell fills the air around it for a moment.

True Strike.description: You extend your hand and point a finger at a target in range.

Vicious Mockery.description: You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at a creature you can see within range.

Absorb Elements.description: The spell captures some of the incoming energy, lessening its effect on you and storing it for your next melee attack.

Alarm.description: You set an alarm against unwanted intrusion.

Animal Friendship.description: This spell lets you convince a beast that you mean it no harm.

Armor of Agathys.description: A protective magical force surrounds you, manifesting as a spectral frost that covers you and your gear.

Bane.description: Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must make Charisma saving throws.

Beast Bond.description: You establish a telepathic link with one beast you touch that is friendly to you or charmed by you.

Bless.description: You bless up to three creatures of your choice within range.

Burning Hands.description: As you hold your hands with thumbs touching and fingers spread, a thin sheet of flames shoots forth from your outstretched fingertips.

Charm Person.description: You attempt to charm a humanoid you can see within range.

Command.description: You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range.

Compelled Duel.description: You attempt to compel a creature into a duel.

Comprehend Languages.description: For the duration, you understand the literal meaning of any spoken language that you hear.

Create or Destroy Water.description: You either create or destroy water.

Cure Wounds.description: A creature you touch regains a number of hit points equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

Detect Evil and Good.description: For the duration, you know if there is an aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, or undead within 30 feet of you.

Detect Magic.description: For the duration, you sense the presence of magic within 30 feet of you.

Detect Poison and Disease.description: For the duration, you can sense the presence and location of poisons, poisonous creatures, and diseases within 30 feet of you.

Disguise Self.description: You make yourself—including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings on your person—appear different until the spell ends or until you use your action to dismiss it.

Divine Favor.description: Your prayer empowers you with divine radiance.

Ensnaring Strike.description: The next time you hit a creature with a weapon attack before this spell ends, a writhing mass of thorny vines appears at the point of impact.

Entangle.description: Grasping weeds and vines sprout from the ground in a 20-foot radius centered on a point within range.

Expeditious Retreat.description: This spell allows you to move at an incredible pace.

Faerie Fire.description: Each object in a 20-foot cube within range is outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice).

False Life.description: Bolstering yourself with a necromantic facsimile of life, you gain 1d4 + 4 temporary hit points for the duration.

Feather Fall.description: Choose up to five falling creatures within range.

Find Familiar.description: You gain the service of a familiar, a spirit that takes an animal form you choose.

Fog Cloud.description: You create a 20-foot-radius sphere of fog centered on a point within range.

Goodberry.description: Up to ten berries appear in your hand and are infused with magic for the duration.

Grease.description: Slick grease covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within range and turns it into difficult terrain for the duration.

Guiding Bolt.description: A flash of light streaks toward a creature of your choice within range.

Hail of Thorns.description: The next time you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack before the spell ends, this spell creates a rain of thorns that sprouts from your ranged weapon or ammunition.

Healing Word.description: A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains hit points equal to 1d4 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

Hellish Rebuke.description: You point your finger, and the creature that damaged you is momentarily surrounded by hellish flames.

Heroism.description: A willing creature you touch is imbued with bravery.

Hex.description: You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range.

Hunter's Mark.description: You choose a creature you can see within range and mystically mark it as your quarry.

Identify.description: You choose one object that you must touch throughout the casting of the spell.

Illusory Script.description: You write on parchment, paper, or some other suitable writing material and imbue it with a potent illusion that lasts for the duration.

Inflict Wounds.description: Make a melee spell attack against a creature you can reach.

Jump.description: You touch a creature. The creature's jump distance is tripled until the spell ends.

Longstrider.description: You touch a creature. The target's speed increases by 10 feet until the spell ends.

Magic Missile.description: You create three glowing darts of magical force.

Protection from Evil and Good.description: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch is protected against certain types of creatures.

Purify Food and Drink.description: All nonmagical food and drink within a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range is purified and rendered free of poison and disease.

Ray of Sickness.description: A ray of sickening greenish energy lashes out toward a creature within range.

Sanctuary.description: You ward a creature within range against attack.

Searing Smite.description: The next time you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack during this spell's duration, your weapon flares with white-hot intensity.

Shield.description: An invisible barrier of magical force appears and protects you.

Shield of Faith.description: A shimmering field appears and surrounds a creature of your choice within range, granting it a +2 bonus to AC for the duration.

Silent Image.description: You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot cube.

Sleep.description: This spell sends creatures into a magical slumber.

Snare.description: As you cast this spell, you use rope to create a circle with a 5-foot radius on the ground or the floor.

Speak with Animals.description: You gain the ability to comprehend and verbally communicate with beasts for the duration.

Tasha's Hideous Laughter.description: A creature of your choice that you can see within range perceives everything as hilariously funny and falls into fits of laughter if this spell affects it.

Tenser's Floating Disk.description: This spell creates a circular, horizontal plane of force, 3 feet in diameter and 1 inch thick, that floats 3 feet above the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within range.

Thunderous Smite.description: The first time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell's duration, your weapon rings with thunder that is audible within 300 feet of you.

Thunderwave.description: A wave of thunderous force sweeps out from you.

Unseen Servant.description: This spell creates an invisible, mindless, shapeless force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends.

Witch Bolt.description: A beam of crackling, blue energy lances out toward a creature within range.

Wrathful Smite.description: The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell's duration, your attack deals an extra 1d6 psychic damage.

Misty Step.description: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see.

Counterspell.description: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell.

Fireball.description: A bright streak flashes from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into an explosion of flame.

Lightning Bolt.description: A stroke of lightning forming a line 100 feet long and 5 feet wide blasts out from you in a direction you choose.

Haste.description: Choose a willing creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, the target's speed is doubled, it gains a +2 bonus to AC, it has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and it gains an additional action on each of its turns.

Slow.description: You alter time around up to six creatures of your choice in a 40-foot cube within range.

Fly.description: You touch a willing creature. The target gains a flying speed of 60 feet for the duration.

Invisibility.description: A creature you touch becomes invisible until the spell ends.

Polymorph.description: This spell transforms a creature that you can see within range into a new form.

Teleport.description: This spell instantly transports you and up to eight willing creatures of your choice that you can see within range, or a single object that you can see within range, to a destination you select.

Wish.description: Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal creature can cast. By simply speaking aloud, you can alter the very foundations of reality in accord with your desires.

Meteor Swarm.description: Blazing orbs of fire plummet to the ground at four different points you can see within range.

Power Word Kill.description: You utter a word of power that can compel one creature you can see within range to die instantly.

Time Stop.description: You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself.

Mass Heal.description: A flood of healing energy flows from you into injured creatures around you.

True Resurrection.description: You touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that didn't die of old age.

Gate.description: You conjure a portal linking an unoccupied space you can see within range to a precise location on a different plane of existence.

Astral Projection.description: You and up to eight willing creatures within range project your astral bodies into the Astral Plane.

Imprisonment.description: You create a magical restraint to hold a creature.

Weird.description: Drawing on the deepest fears of a group of creatures, you create illusory creatures in their minds, visible only to them.

Prismatic Wall.description: A shimmering, multicolored plane of light forms a vertical opaque wall—up to 90 feet long, 30 feet high, and 1 inch thick—centered on a point you can see within range.

Storm of Vengeance.description: A churning storm cloud forms, centered on a point you can see and spreading to a radius of 360 feet.

Foresight.description: You touch a willing creature and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future.

Invulnerability.description: You are immune to all damage until the spell ends.

Mass Polymorph.description: You transform up to ten creatures of your choice that you can see within range.

Power Word Heal.description: A wave of healing energy flows through you. Choose any number of creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide 700 hit points among them.

Psychic Scream.description: You unleash the power of your mind to blast the intellect of up to ten creatures of your choice that you can see within range.

Ravenous Void.description: A 20-foot-radius sphere of crushing force forms at a point you can see within range.

Shapechange.description: You assume the form of a different creature for the duration.

True Polymorph.description: Choose one creature or nonmagical object that you can see within range.

Mastiff.description: War dog, can be ridden by small creatures

Keelboat.description: River boat with sail and oars

Balloon.description: Hot air balloon for aerial travel

Dragon Turtle Ship.description: Ship built on dragon turtle shell

Phoenix Mount.description: Magical phoenix that can be ridden

Griffon.description: Flying mount with eagle head and lion body

Claws of Darkness.name: Claws of Darkness
Claws of Darkness.description:
You shape shadows into claws that grow from your fingers and drip inky blackness. The claws have a reach of 10 feet.

While the spell lasts, you can make a melee spellattackwith them that deals 1d10 cold damage.

Aspect of the Hope Devourer.name: Aspect of the Hope Devourer
Aspect of the Hope Devourer.description:
Your presence saps the hope and joy from your enemies. All enemies within 30 feet of you must succeed at aWisdomsaving throw or beparalyzedby the unbearable despair and hopelessness. Each round at the end of its turn, a creature affected by this spell may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect. On a successful save to break the ongoing effect, or if the 1 minute duration expires, the creature is no longerparalyzedbut has disadvantage onWisdomsaving throws for 24 hours and is Demoralized for 1d4 rounds. A creature that succeeds on the initial save is demoralized for 1d4 rounds. A creature immune to thefrightenedor Demoralized conditions is immune to theparalyzedcondition created by this spell, but a creature immune to theparalyzedcondition is not.

Doom of the Tentacle.name: Doom of the Tentacle
Doom of the Tentacle.description:
When you cast this spell, a creature of your choice within range must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw, or one of its arms turns into a tentacle. Any item the target was holding in the transformed arm is dropped at its feet. The tentacle randomly attacks one creature within 10 feet at the start of the target’s turn, which might be you or the target itself. The tentacle uses your spellattackbonus as itsattackbonus and deals damage equal to 1d8 + yourIntelligencemodifier. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The spell has no effect on a shapechanger or a creature with0 hit points.

Wastes of Chaos. © 2023 Open Design LLC; Authors: Richard Green, Tim Hitchcock, and Sarah Madsen.

Curse of Whispered Secrets.name: Curse of Whispered Secrets
Curse of Whispered Secrets.description:
Target: One creature within range

You curse a creature to unintentionally whisper secrets aloud. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed in this way, a creature occasionally utter secrets or sensitive information without realizing it.

A cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Spirit Guardians.name: Spirit Guardians
Spirit Guardians.description:
You call forth spirits to protect you. They flit around you to a distance of 15 feet for the duration. If you are good or neutral, their spectral form appears angelic or fey (your choice). If you are evil, they appear fiendish.

When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it. An affected creature’s speed is halved in the area, and when the creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d8 radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 necrotic damage (if you are evil). On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Cataclysm.name: Cataclysm
Cataclysm.components: V, S, M (fragment of a dying star, a primordial gem, and a tear from the weave of magic)
Cataclysm.description:
Classes: Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You summon the unrestrained forces of creation and destruction, bending the fabric of reality to your will. A cataclysmic explosion of energy erupts from you, engulfing everything within a 200-mile radius. Any creature within the area (including the caster) must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 40d12 force damage and 40d12 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the total damage taken. This reduction can’t be reverted by any means short of awishspell. Structures and objects in the area are disintegrated, leaving behind only fine dust. The ground is torn asunder, forming craters and chasms. The released magical energy turns the area affected by the spell into a barren landscape devoid of life. Additionally, the spell torn the weave of magic in the affected area: within this radius, spells can’t be cast, summoned creatures disappear, and magic items become mundane.

Fuel Charge.name: Fuel Charge
Fuel Charge.description:
You touch a magic item that requires charges and transfer some of your magical energy into the item. You expend your spell slots to power the item. For each level of spell slots you expend (beyond those used to cast this spell), the item gains one charge up to its maximum charges.

Rum Rations.name: Rum Rations
Rum Rations.description:
You conjure a small amount of rum to fill an empty bottle. A creature that drinks this rum gains a number oftemporary hit pointsequal to your spellcasting ability modifier for the next hour, but has disadvantage onDexterityability checks and saving throws for the duration.

Pirates and Plunder A Compendium For 5e © 2024 Published by Mythos Chronicles; Author Filippo Bardoscia

Shadow Tree.name: Shadow Tree
Shadow Tree.description:
This spell temporarily draws a willow tree from theShadowRealm to the location you designate within range. The tree is 5 feet in diameter and 20 feet tall. When you cast the spell, you can specify individuals who can interact with the tree. All other creatures see the tree as ashadowversion of itself and can’t grasp or climb it, passing through its shadowy substance.

A creature that can interact with the tree and that has Sunlight Sensitivity or Sunlight Hypersensitivity is protected from sunlight while within 20 feet of the tree. A creature that can interact with the tree can climb into its branches, giving the creature halfcover.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Solitary Fireball.name: Solitary Fireball
Solitary Fireball.components: V, S, M (candle and a pinch of sulfur)
Solitary Fireball.description:
A bright streak flashes from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range, where it blossoms with a low roar to engulf a single creature in searing flame. That creature takes 6d6 fire damage, or half damage with a successfulDexteritysaving throw. Solitaryfireballdoes not ignite other flammable objects.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

Corrosive Cloud.name: Corrosive Cloud
Corrosive Cloud.components: V, S, M (powdered iron worth 10 gp, which the spell consumes, and the antennae of
Corrosive Cloud.description:
A cloud of corrosive mist emanates in a 20-foot radius sphere centered on a point you can see within range. The cloud spreads around corners and through cracks, corroding nonmagical ferrous metals into rust. The cloud lasts for the duration of the spell or until a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles an hour) disperses it.

Any creature that starts its turn in the area may make aDexteritysaving throw to protect any objects they wear or carry from corroding. On a failed save, all nonmagical metal objects the creature carries are subject to the effects of the cloud. If an object is metal armor or a metalshieldbeing worn or carried, it receives a cumulative –1 penalty to AC. Armor reduced to an AC of 10 or ashieldthat drops to a +0 bonus is destroyed. If an object is a held metal weapon, it suffers a cumulative –1 penalty todamage rolls. If this penalty drops to –5, the weapon is destroyed. If a metal object in the area isn’t being worn or held, a one-foot cube of it is destroyed.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the radius of the cloud increases by 10 feet for each spell slot level above 4th.

Curse of the Sinking Stone.name: Curse of the Sinking Stone
Curse of the Sinking Stone.description:
Target: One creature or object you touch

Youtoucha creature and fill its mind with a feeling of being unnaturally heavy for a moment, causing it to forcefully sink or press down. The target must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be knockedprone.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Doom of Poor Fortune.name: Doom of Poor Fortune
Doom of Poor Fortune.description:
Components: V, S, M (a dead clover)

Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute

You turn luck against a creature of your choice within range. When the target makes an ability check, they must first make aCharismasaving throw or the check fails. This spell persists once cast, even if the target moves out of range. If cast with a higher-level slot, each subsequent effect is added to the effect noted above.

If the target ultimately succeeds on the check (or saving throw orattackat higher levels), then you take 1 psychic damage. If you ever lose concentration on the spell, you take 1d4 psychic damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd-level or higher, when the target is required to make a saving throw, it must make aCharismasaving throw in place of the required one, unless the required one is more difficult to make. When you cast this spell with a 4th-level slot, when the target makes anattackroll, it must make aCharismasaving throw prior to making theattack. On a failed save, theattackfails. If you cast this spell with an 8thlevel slot, this spell persists for the duration without requiring concentration.

Girallon Arms.name: Girallon Arms
Girallon Arms.description:
Components: V, S, M (a few strands of girallon hair)

You cause a willing creature’s torso and upper limbs to ripple and stretch, splitting into four long, muscular arms covered in shaggy white hair and tipped in clawed fingers. These arms do not increase the target’s reach, but they grant advantage onStrength(Athletics) checks made to climb or to grapple a creature. You can wield weapons or shields normally with the girallon arms, but the extra arms are not sufficiently dexterous to increase the number of weapons or shields you can wield. However, you can use all four claws as an action toattack(as the Multiattack ability), with each hit 11 dealing 1d4 slashing damage plus yourStrengthmodifier. If you hit a creature two or more times in the same round with these claws, as a bonus action you can rend and tear the target’s flesh, dealing an additional 2d4 slashing damage plus twice yourStrengthmodifier. You cannotattackwith other weapons and with your claws in the same round, but you could use a shield with one arm andattackwith up to three claws.

The Dragon’s Hoard #30© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, James-Levi Cooke.

Disheartening Darkness.name: Disheartening Darkness
Disheartening Darkness.description:
This spell operates as thedarknessspell except that any creature that enters or is within the radius ofdarknessmust succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or have disadvantage on saving throws against theFrightenedand Demoralized conditions while within the area ofdarkness. If an affected creature leaves the area ofdarknessthe disadvantage remains for 1d4 rounds but resumes anytime the creature enters thedarknessagain. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to the disadvantage effect for the duration of the spell.

GoodHope - Crushing Despair (5E), © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Prismatic Deluge.name: Prismatic Deluge
Prismatic Deluge.components: V, S, M (shard of glass forged by dragonfire)
Prismatic Deluge.description:
A cloud of multicolored light appears in a 10-foot-tall, 150-foot-radius cylinder centered on a point you can see 200 feet directly above you. The spell fails if you cannot see a point in the air where the cloud could appear. When you cast the spell and as an action on each of your turns until the spell ends, you may cause up to two different colored globes to rain down from the sky. Each globe strikes a separate 15-foot cube centered on a point within 300 ft.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell as a tier 3 Epic spell, you create three colored globes instead of two at the time of casting and each time you take an action to call down additional globes.

Summon Dragon Spirit.name: Summon Dragon Spirit
Summon Dragon Spirit.components: V, S, M (few scales from a serpent or lizard)
Summon Dragon Spirit.description:
You call forth a dragon spirit from the dragon lands. It manifests in an unoccupied space that you can see within range.

This corporeal form uses the Dragon Spirit stat block. When you cast the spell, choose an element (thunder, lightning, acid, cold, or fire). The creature resembles a dragon of that kind, which determines certain traits in its stat block. The creature disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The creature is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the creature shares yourinitiativecount, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any, it takes theDodgeaction and uses its move to avoid danger.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, use the higher level wherever the spell’s level appears on the stat block.

Armor Class11+ level of the spell (natural armor)Hit Points50 (6d8 + 12) +10 for each spell level above 4thSpeed30 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover)

SkillsDeception+2,Insight+4,Perception+2,Persuasion+5Sensesdarkvision60 ft., blindsense 10 ft., passivePerception12LanguagesDraconic, understands any

A giant, nigh translucent apparition in the form of a chromatic dragon.

Folklore tells the tales of dragon being bound to service by powerful wizards and mages. Whether through happenstance, forced binding, or other arcane means, some dragons may become so entwined with the souls of their masters that they become bound to spaces, to which their spirit remains long after death. These dragons remain with the souls yearning for connection whether through conversation or ethereal combat. It is said that powerful magics can catch the ear of one such dragon spirit willing to be unbound if not for the briefest of moments, aiding the call of those in need for a small chance at freedom.

Troubadours & Tenders of the Grove, Pugilists & Pact Makers A Scarred Lands Character Options Supplement By Vorpal Tales Authors: Patrick Warren, Shawn McNamara, Tyler Middleton, Zachery Naldrett

Wall of Fear.name: Wall of Fear
Wall of Fear.description:
Classes: bard, cleric, paladin, sorcerer, warlock, wizard

When you cast this spell, a thin black line appears along the ground starting at a point you can see within range.

You can make the line up to 30 feet long or create a circle up to 10 feet in diameter. The line is subtle, and spotting it requires a successfulWisdom(Perception) orIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC.

A creature that moves within 5 feet of the line for the first time on a turn or that starts its turn within 5 feet of the line must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the target isfrightenedby the line, even if it can’t perceive it, and it will not willingly cross the line while it remainsfrightened. If forced from one side of the line to the other, the target remainsfrightenedof the line and dares not cross from the other direction.

The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A target that successfully saves is immune to this casting of the spell.

Feast of Flesh.name: Feast of Flesh
Feast of Flesh.components: V, M (an animal tooth and a drop of your blood)
Feast of Flesh.description:
A creature of your choice within range is overcome with a need to consume the flesh of its own kind. The target must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, its teeth become needlelike, and it becomes able to pinpoint creatures of the same type as it within 150 feet by scent.

On its turn, the creature must move toward the nearest creature of its type by the fastest means possible. If it is within 5 feet of a creature of its type it must use its bonus action to make a biteattackagainst it. Your target has proficiency with its bite attack and deals damage equal to 1d6 + itsStrengthmodifier. If a creature of its type is not present within 150 feet of the target, it must attack the closest living creature to it.

At the end of each of its turns and each time it takes damage, the target can make a new saving throw. The target has advantage on its saving throw if it is triggered by damage. On a success, the spell ends, and the target ispoisonedfor 1 hour, unless it is a cannibal or comes from a cannibalistic culture.

Bond of Pain.name: Bond of Pain
Bond of Pain.description:
This spell creates a mystic connection between you and the target until the spell ends. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails, the target receives a –1 penalty to AC and saving throws, and it hasvulnerabilityto all damage types. Also, each time you take damage from any source, the target must immediately make aWisdomsaving throw. If they fail, they take the same amount of damage as you, ignoring all damage immunities or resistances. If the save is successful, the target takes half damage.

The spell ends if you drop to0 hit pointsor if you and the target become separated by more than 90 feet. It also ends if the spell is cast again on either of the connected creatures. You can also dismiss the spell as an action.

You create a mass of tiny, slimy toads in a 10-foot square on an area of ground you can see. This area is considereddifficult terrain. Old Growth Forest.name: Old Growth Forest
Old Growth Forest.description:
You weave ancient magic with vitality and potential for growth, causing a dense forest of fully-grown trees covered in iridescent runes to grow within a 1-mile radius of where you cast this spell. These trees grow densely as though a part of a forest that has not seen outside interference for centuries. They do not grow through or interfere with artificial structures, including roads made of stone or similarly resilient materials when the spell is complete.

All beasts within the forest are affected by this spell’s magic as well – each beast within the forest is considered to be under the effects of either anenlarge/reducespell (enlarging the creature) or anawakenspell(GM’s choice). If the beast spends 24 hours or more within the forest, this effect becomes permanent.

Otherwise, the effect ends when the beast leaves the forest.

While inside the forest, magical effects are bolstered.

Whenever a creature inside the forest casts a spell of 1st level or higher, they heal a number ofhit pointsequal to 5 x the level of the spell slot expended to cast the spell. Additionally, a creature capable of casting spells may expend a spell slot as an action toteleporta distance of up to 30 feet x the level of the spell slot expended.

Whenever a creature expends a hit die in the forest, they may choose to treat the hit die as having rolled its maximum result.

You may dismiss the spell by spending a minute in uninterrupted meditation, at which point the trees’ leaves fall and blow away on the wind and their trunks vanish in the flurry of leaves. If you do not dismiss the spell within 24 hours of casting it, the spell’s effects become permanent. The forest may continue to grow naturally over time if the surrounding land and climate are suitable, but only the initial area of effect has the magical effects described in this spell.

You may create only one Old Growth Forest at a time.

If you cast this spell again while another Old Growth Forest exists, the previous Old Growth Forest loses its magical effects, though its trees remain.

Capture Anima.name: Capture Anima
Capture Anima.description:
This necromantic ritual is one path used by wizards seeking lichdom. The spell is a modified version ofmagic jarand allows you to remove and store your anima — your soul — in a valuable container, protected from most harm (see below).

After casting capture anima, you must make two successful DC 18 saving throws:Constitution, to verify your soul survives the removal and replacement, andCharisma, to verify your personality remains intact. If theConstitutionsave fails, your soul is corrupted in transfer, and you become a soulless vessel that is permanentlyincapacitated, and you do not attempt theCharismasaving throw. You are unable to be raised or resurrected, although awishmay bring your soul back. If theCharismasave fails, your personality is destroyed, but you remain alive; however, you are permanentlystunned. If both saves are successful, your soul and personality are transferred into the specially prepared container (kept within reach for the casting of the spell). From there, you must possess a body within one hour or your soul dissipates to the outer realms.

You can attempt to possess any humanoid within 100 feet of you that you can see (creatures warded by aprotection from evil and goodor amagic circlespell can’t be possessed). The target must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failure, your soul moves into the target’s body, and the target’s soul is dispersed. On a success, the target resists your efforts to possess it, and you can’t attempt to possess it again for 24 hours.

Once you possess a creature’s body, you slowly, over the course of one hour, gain full control over it. Initially, your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the creature, though you retain your alignment and yourIntelligence,Wisdom, andCharismascores. You retain the benefit of your own class features. After the first hour, you complete the transmutation into your final form: that of a powerful undeadlich. The container or object used to complete the process becomes your phylactery!

The phylactery is magically strengthened by the process, as well as with pieces of your soul. The phylactery has AC 20, regardless of its material. It has 1d4hit pointsfor each of your caster levels and a damage threshold of 5. It is immune to necrotic, piercing, poison, and psychic damage; resistant to acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, and thunder damage, as well as bludgeoning and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks; and is vulnerable to radiant damage.

Sand and Stone.name: Sand and Stone
Sand and Stone.description:
You can transform up to ten 10-foot cubes of sand into a porous sandstone. Each cube must be adjacent to another one (including diagonally), but you can’t stack them vertically. A creature that is at least halfway buried in the sand must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or beRestrainedwhen the sand becomes stone. If they fail they save, they remainRestraineduntil they can break free. They can do this with aStrengthcheck with Disadvantage against your spell save DC. They (or allies) also can smash through the stone holding them; the stone has AC 15 and 60Hit Points. The stone has immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. When the stone is reduced to0 Hit Points, the impact of the shattering stone deals 3d6 Bludgeoning damage to the trapped creature as it crumbles.Stone Shape,Passwall, and similar magic also can free the trapped creature. If you maintain Concentration for 10 minutes; the transmutation becomes permanent and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the stone crumbles back into sand 1d4 rounds after you stop concentrating. You can instead cause natural, unworked stone to crumble into loose sand, but each cube you affect is only a 5-foot cube. You can’t affect unworked stone with a permanent structure built on top of it. This loose sand isDifficult Terrain, and creatures walking on it have Disadvantage onDexterity(Acrobatics) checks unless they are well adapted for walking on loose sand (GM’s discretion). You can target the ceiling of a cave or natural tunnel, causing a collapse that deals 4d6 Bludgeoning damage to creatures underneath it, or half as much with a successfulDexteritysaving throw. Stone turned to sand is permanently changed.

Wicked Burr.name: Wicked Burr
Wicked Burr.description:
Class(es):druid,ranger,sorcerer,wizard

You conjure a poisonous burr steeped in vexing magic and fling it at a target within range, making a ranged spellattack. On a hit, the target takes 1 piercing damage and 1d4 poison damage, and it has disadvantage onConstitutionsaving throws to maintain its concentration until the end of its next turn.

The spell creates and allows you to throw more than one burr when you reach higher levels: two burrs at 5th level, three burrs at 11th level, and four burrs at 17th level.

You can direct the burrs at the same target or at different ones. Make a separateattackroll for each burr.

Navigate.name: Navigate
Navigate.description:
You connect to the magnetic fields around you. You unerringly know your current heading and the direction of magnetic north. If you are in a location without a planet, “north” is the nearest star. In addition, for the duration of the spell, you always know the local time.

Fiery Body.name: Fiery Body
Fiery Body.description:
You transform your body into living flame. You and your equipment are immune to fire, and when you would normally take damage from fire you instead gain 1 temporary hit point for every 3 points of damage the fireattackwould normally have dealt (up to a maximum of 60temporary hit points). Your fiery body is immune to beingblinded,deafened,petrified,poisoned, orstunnedand you are immune to disease,exhaustion, and poison. You do not need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep. You gainresistanceto acid and lightning damage but gainvulnerabilityto cold damage.

Your fiery body sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius, and the glare is so bright that creatures within 10 feet of you take a -1 penalty on their attack rolls. Your fiery body allows you to fly with a speed of 40 feet, and you gain a melee weapon attack with your fiery fist that deals 3d6 fire damage. You are so nimble that you have advantage onDexteritychecks and saving throws and onmelee attackrolls you make with your flaming fist. This advantage does not apply when youattackcreatures made of water, metal, stone, earth, or other non-flammable substances.

You can handle physical objects, but flammable items like scrolls, cloth, and books take 3d6 fire damage from your touch, likely destroying them.

You can cast spells in this form, including spells that require material components, as long as you had them on your person (not in an extradimensional container) when you cast fiery body, and the save DC for fire spells you cast in this form is increased by 1.

You take 2d6 damage if you are immersed in water, taking this damage as soon as you enter the water and each round at the beginning ofyour turnthat you remain in water. However, while in the water you are surrounded by a 5-foot radius area of steam and bubbles that causes disadvantage onWisdom(Perception) checks and onattackrolls, both those that you make and that others make against you.

You can suppress your fiery body as an action without ending the spell; however, the spell’s duration continues to elapse while your fire is extinguished. You can switch back to your fiery body as an action.

You transform your mouth so that you gain glands that produce venom. Until the spell ends, you may make a biteattack; if you hit, you inflict an additional +2d6 poison damage. Alternately, you may lick up to your casting ability modifier in weapons to coat these weapons with venom. Envenomed weapons inflict an additional +1d6 poison damage on their next successfulattackroll. Using envenom to coat weapons ends the spell. Envenomed weapons remain potent for one minute, after which the venom becomes inert.

This allows you to monitor the status of every ally within your stronghold. You are aware of their general direction, if they are wounded, and any condition they suffer from. You create a wave of strange energy which transforms up to 5 creatures’ bones within range into a brittle crystal. Each target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. Advantage onStrengthandConstitutionability checks and saving throws.

You can launch the bullets at one target or several. Make a ranged spellattackfor each bullet. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 piercing damage. Instant Palisade.components: V, S, M (five pounds of tree seeds and a piece of amber worth 100 gp, all of which the spell consumes)
Instant Palisade.description:
Over the course of casting this spell, you plant tree seeds on the ground in a line up to a mile long. You can shape this line any way you want, including over hills and around obstacles like buildings, though for the spell to work the path must be contiguous and it must all be on natural soil.

As you complete this spell, a palisade emerges from the ground along the line you laid down. The palisade is 15 feet high. Each 10-foot section has AC 15, 75hit points, and a damage threshold of 15. It is immune to poison and psychic damage. Reducing a section to0 hit pointsdestroys it. Climbing the wall requires a successful DC 15Strength(Athletics) check.

At your option, you can choose to create a single gate in the palisade. The gate is 10 feet wide and has hinged double doors that can be barred from the inside. While closed, the gate has the same statistics as the wall.

Once the spell is complete, the palisade is a permanent, nonmagical structure and can’t be dispelled.

The touched target’s voice becomes magically enhanced. It becomes three times as loud as normal and they have Advantage onCharisma(Intimidation) checks.

Each creature in a 15-foot Cone makes aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 3d6 Thunder damage and having theStunnedcondition until the end of its next turn on a failed save, or half as much damage and no stun on a successful one. Hat Trick.name: Hat Trick
Hat Trick.description:
You touch a hat and create aninvisibleentrance within it that opens to an extradimensional space that lasts until the spell ends. The extradimensional space can be reached by reaching into the hat. The space can hold one Medium or smaller creature and its carried goods, or up to 100 pounds of unliving material. The hat always weighs about 1 pound, regardless of its contents.

The hat cannot be pulled into itself. Attacks and spells can’t cross through the entrance into or out of the extradimensional space, but a creature inside can see out of it through a small slit as wide as the hat. Anything inside the extradimensional space drops out when the spell ends or when the hat is destroyed.

Gnomish casters often crawl into their own hat to avoid detection or to be carried safely from town to town.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot greater than 1st, you extend the duration by 1 hour for each additional level, and the extradimensional space can hold one additional creature, or an additional 100 pounds.

You carry the blood of a saint within your veins, which harms your enemies when spilled. When a creature within 5 feet of you deals piercing or slashing damage to you, it must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 4d6 acid damage on a fail, or half as much on a successful one.

Named Bullet.components: V, S, M (an item taken fromcreature of the chosen type)
Named Bullet.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,ranger,warlock

You enchant a single piece of ammunition or thrown weapon with terrific potency against a selected creature type (such as fiends or aberrations). When used against a creature of that type, yourattackroll has advantage and you ignore any disadvantage on yourattackroll due tocoveror concealment. In addition, when the named bullet hits, it deals an additional 2d6 damage of the same type as the weapon normally deals (or 12 points on a critical hit). In addition, the target must attempt aWisdomsaving throw or befrightened1 round, with a new saving throw allowed each round at the end of its turn to end this condition.

Alternatively, you can focus the named bullet’s power against a single specific creature you know and can name.

Against that target, you ignore all forms of disadvantage on yourattackroll, and the named bullet deals an additional 4d6 damage of the same type as the weapon normally deals (or 24 points on a critical hit), and damage dealt by the named bullet is not reduced byresistance(though it cannot bypass immunity). A specifically named creature has disadvantage on its saving throw to avoid beingfrightenedby the named bullet.

Fiendish Servant.name: Fiendish Servant
Fiendish Servant.components: V, S, M(a pinch of sulfur and a drop of blood)
Fiendish Servant.description:
You summon forth a minor fiendish creature from the nether planes. This creature is under your command for the duration of the spell and will obey your commands, though it tends to obey the letter rather than the intent. The fiendish servant has AC 15, 15HP, aStrengthof 3, speed 30, and can’tattack. The fiendish servant can turninvisible, and has an effectiveArcana,History,Perception, andStealthbonuses of +6. If it is reduced to 0HPit disappears back to its home plane, ending the spell.

Once onyour turn, you may use a bonus action to direct the fiendish servant to perform a task. It can move any distance from you. It is capable of performing any task a creature can that does not involve an ability or skill check. It can fetch things, clean, mend, light a fire, or any other task ahumanservant could.

Additionally, you may command your fiendish servant to do one of the following:

Spy upon a single creature. The Fiendish servant will do its best to use its skills to locate and observe the target from a hidden vantage point. It will continue to watch the target until recalled, a specific amount of time has passed, or the duration of the spell ends.

Use its innate magic to cast one of the following spells, giving the information gleaned from the spell to you:comprehend languages,detect evil and good,detect poison and disease,detect magic, oridentify. If it uses its innate magic in your service the fiend returns to its home plane when the duration of the spell it cast or this spell ends, whichever is first.

Use its skills to your benefit, for example answering a question usingArcanaorHistory.

Annihilation.components: V, S, M (shard of void-touched obsidian)
Annihilation.description:
Target: One creature or object within range

You unleash a devastating wave of annihilating energy, attempting to erase a target from existence.

Choose a creature, object, or creation of magical force within range. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 16d10 force damage, ignoring damage resistances and treating immunities as resistances. If this damage reduces the target to0 hit points, the target is obliterated along with everything it is wearing and carrying, leaving no remains except for any magical items. A creature killed in this way cannot be resurrected by any means short of awishspell.

Possession.name: Possession
Possession.description:
This spell must be cast on a humanoid target who is either sleeping or otherwiseunconscious. When you cast this spell, your body goes completely limp as your consciousness enters the target’s mind. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw versus your spell save DC at disadvantage. If they fail, you suppress their consciousness for the duration and gain full control of their body. This does not give you access to spells or innate abilities the target knows unless they are involuntary and purely physical. The possession ends if the host body reaches0 hit pointsor if you end the spell. When the possession ends, the target may make aWisdomsaving throw versus your spell save DC to attempt to remember vague details about what happened while you were in control. When you cast this spell using a higher level spell slot, double the duration for every spell slot level above the original.

Instill Madness.name: Instill Madness
Instill Madness.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute One humanoid of
Instill Madness.description:
One humanoid of your choice that you can see within range must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or succumb to madness for the duration. While in the throes of madness, the target is no longer an ally, companion, or non-hostile creature toward any another creature for the purpose of determining whether ongoing or new spells and effects affect the target. While mad, the target cannot take bonusactionsorreactionsand can only move or take theAttackorDashactions. It cannot use or activate magic items, interact with objects it is not already holding, or use any class features unless those featuresaidits movement or attacks. The madness instantly breaks its concentration and causes the target to have disadvantage onCharisma,Intelligence, andWisdomchecks and saving throws, including those to end this spell.

The target is free to decide whether to move,Attack, orDash, but when it does so, it acts randomly. If the target moves or takes theDashaction, it uses all its movement to move in a random direction until it completes its movement or until another creature, obstacle, or obviously deadly hazard blocks its path. To determine the direction, roll a d8 and assign a direction to each die face. The target canattackonly with natural weapons or any weapon it held when it succumbed to its madness. If the target makes amelee attack, it attacks a random creature within its reach. If the target makes aranged attack, it targets a random creature it can see within range. The target continues toattackrandom creatures until another creature it can see hits it with anattack.

The target then attacks that creature until the spell ends. If more than one creature hits the target, the target randomly determines which creature it attacks.

At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make aWisdomsaving throw. If it succeeds, this effect ends for that target.

Incendiary Cloud.description:
A swirling cloud of smoke shot through with white-hot embers appears in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within range. The cloud spreads around corners and is heavilyobscured. It lasts for the duration or until a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.

When the cloud appears, each creature in it must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 10d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must also make this saving throw when it enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there.

The cloud moves 10 feet directly away from you in a direction that you choose at the start of each of your turns.

Baleful Blink.name: Baleful Blink
Baleful Blink.description:
Classes:bard,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You shunt the target erratically between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane if it fails aConstitutionsaving throw.

When the target attacks or casts a spell (or uses a similar magical ability, such as a breath weapon), roll a d20; on a roll of 11 or higher it shifts between planes just before the action occurs, wasting the action unless its target also exists on the Ethereal Plane. If the target makes multiple attacks or casts multiple spells in the same round, make this check prior to each one. The target can cast spells on itself without difficulty. Immediately after theattackor spellcasting (or both, if the spell requires anattackroll) is resolved, the target shifts back to the Material Plane. The target does not remain on the Ethereal Plane long enough to move. On its turn, if the target concentrates on trying to stabilize its planar movement 12 (precluding casting spells or performing otheractionsrequiring concentration), it can attempt a new saving throw at the end of that turn. On a success, the spell ends.

Wall of Mana.name: Wall of Mana
Wall of Mana.description:
Drawing on the defensive principles and properties of the Pool of Magic, you create a barrier of raw mystical energy. Aninvisiblewall of magical energy springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose, as a horizontal or vertical barrier or at an angle. It can be free-floating or resting on a solid surface. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a sphere with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1/4-inch thick. It lasts for the duration. If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (your choice which side).

Spells cast from the side of the wall where you stand pass through the wall normally. Spells of 4th level or lower cast in your direction from the side of the wall opposite you are stopped by the wall, their magical energy harmlessly impeded by the wall. The wall is immune to all damage and can’t be dispelled bydispel magic. Adisintegratespell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel through the wall.

At Higher Levels. When this spell is cast using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, it impedes spells of the level at which it is cast and lower from passing through the wall.

Returning Shield.components: V, S, M (an equipped shield you use for the attack)
Returning Shield.description:
You fling your equipped shield at a target within range.

Make a ranged spellattack. On a hit, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to 3d8 plus the AC bonus of the shield. At the end ofyour turn, the shield returns in a straight line to your location. Any creatures it passes through must make aDexteritysaving throw or take bludgeoning damage equal to 3d8 plus the AC bonus of the shield. If a solid object obstructs the path, such as a wall, the shield will stop and fall to the ground once it hits this obstruction.

Each creature in a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on each point you choose must make aDexteritysaving throw. The sphere spreads around corners. A creature takes 20d6 fire damage and 20d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature in the area of more than one fiery burst is affected only once.

The spell damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren’t being worn or carried.

You create a shadow tunnel between your location and one other creature you can see within range. You and that creature instantly swap positions. Earth Swim.description:
You and up to eight willing creatures can move through earth as easily as if it were water. Each of you can sink into an area of stone, soil, mud, clay, or other earth at least 5 feet wide, and move through the material without disturbing it. For this purpose, each affected creature has a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. You and your companions can breathe when submerged in the substance, and each of you also gains tremorsense out to a range of 60 feet while submerged. Any individuals who are submerged when the spell ends rise directly to the surface at a rate of 60 feet per round and appear in an unoccupied space nearest to where each one emerges.

Hypnotism.description:
DurationConcentration up to 1 minute

You perform gestures and make sounds or words that fascinate nearby creatures, causing them to stare blankly at you. On a failed save, the creature becomes charmed for the duration. While charmed by this spell, the creature is incapacitated and has a speed of 0.

The rapt attention also allows you to make plausible suggestions to the target. Roll 2d4 to see the total amount of levels worth of creatures you can affect. Creatures with lower levels are affected before those of higher levels. The creatures are not affected if their level exceeds your own.

If you attempt to use this spell in combat the creature gains advantage on their saving throw. If the spell is used on a single target not in combat the target takes disadvantage on the saving throw. A creature that fails their saving throw does not remember a spell was cast upon them. Their attitude is considered friendly in regards to the request you give them while under the hypnosis. The request must be reasonable and not be against the target’s alignment or safety.

When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it. An affected creature’s speed is halved in the area, and when the creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make aDexteritysaving throw. Surelife.name: Surelife
Surelife.description:
Classes: Cleric, Druid, Ranger, Warlock

You can guard your life absolutely against a natural, non-magical situation, environment, or condition. You describe the situation for your Surelife, and if that occurs you and your gear are unharmed and undamaged by it. This can include drowning, boiling in oil, drinking poison, falling into magma, being cast into the airless void of space, being lashed by hurricane winds, crushed by an avalanche, or virtually anything you can describe.

Surelife does not protect you from magical effects or the directactionsof creatures (such as being attacked with weapons), though it could protect you from dangerous situations that creatures place you in, such as being burned at the stake, thrown into the ocean, and so on. You can still be buried or otherwiserestrained, though you have Advantage onStrengthorDexterity-based D20 Tests or Saving Throws to escape from a situation covered by your Surelife.

This spell destroys one Tiny, nonmagical object you touch, such as a key, a dagger, or a tankard. The object must weigh less than 2 pounds and be no larger than 1 foot in any dimension. If the object you touch is a container, the contents within it spill out as the container dissolves. This spell has no effect on objects made at least partially of mithral or adamantine, and it has no effect on an object held, worn, or carried by another creature.

Divine light washes out from you and coalesces in a soft radiance in a 30-foot radius around you.

Creatures of your choice in that radius when you cast this spell shed dim light in a 5-foot radius and have advantage on all saving throws, and other creatures have disadvantage onattackrolls against them until the spell ends. In addition, when a celestial, fiend, or an undead hits an affected creature with a melee attack, the aura flashes with brilliant light. You whisper words of eldritch power, tormenting the mind of a creature within range. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or have disadvantage on all the saving throws it makes and take 1d6 psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the spell ends. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Burning Light.description:

You cause a light source you can see within range to intensify with searing brilliance. The light source casts bright light 15 feet in all directions, then casts its normal radius of bright and dim light beyond that. Oneiromancy.name: Oneiromancy

Oneiromancy.description:
Dreams can be gateways to understanding, and you can induce such prophetic and insightful dreams in yourself and others. You touch a willing creature of your choice.

The creature immediately falls into an enchanted dream state and remains that way for the full length of a normal long rest for that creature, unless awakened or if the target chooses to end the spell early.

During this long rest, the target experiences dreams and visions centering around one event or question of its choice, specified at the casting of the spell. The answer in the dreams may be literal, or it may be wrapped in symbolism, omens, and metaphor and left to the dreamer to interpret. This spell doesn’t disrupt the target’s long rest, and the target can still gain the benefits of a long rest if it finishes the long rest while affected by this spell.

If the target’s sleep is interrupted, this spell ends and must be cast again for the target to experience the dreams again.

Elves and other creatures with immunity to magicalsleepcan choose whether or not to be affected by this spell.

This spell has no effect on Constructs or Undead.

Ricochet.name: Ricochet
Ricochet.description:
You enchant up to ten arrows, bolts, darts, or sling stones with homing magic. If an enchanted projectile is used and hits its target, the enchantment on that projectile ends with no effect. If the projectile misses its target, the enchantment on it takes effect. The magic causes the projectile to bounce off nearby walls, trees, furniture, and creatures, until it strikes at the original target again. Make a spellattackroll to hit the target with the projectile. If you hit, add your spell casting ability modifier to the projectile’s damage. If thisattackroll misses, the enchantment on that projectile ends. If there are no surfaces at all for the weapon to ricochet off, the spell fails with no effect.

Hungering Shadows.description:
You open a gateway to the Plane of Shadows, a cold, colorless, and darkened distortion of your world. A 20-foot-radius sphere of hungering, writhing shadow appears, centered on a point within range and lasting for the duration of the spell. This void is filled with maddening whispers and cacophonous laughter that can be heard up to 30 feet away. No light, magical or otherwise, can illuminate the area, and creatures fully within the area areblinded.

The void creates a conduit between the planes, and the area isdifficult terrain. Any creature that starts its turn in the area takes 2d6 necrotic damage. Any creature that ends its turn in the area must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 2d6 cold damage as otherworldly shadows slowly drain its warmth.

Spirit Read.description:
Class(es):bard,cleric,sorcerer,wizard

Touching an object, you sense the link between an object and a spirit recently associated with it. For 1 minute, even after you stop touching the object, you can project one of the following illusory images in an empty space you can see within 10 feet of the object. You must choose which when you cast the spell.

The illusion looks real, but it is stationary and intangible. It includes no smell, taste, or sound. It can be identified as an illusion with a successfulIntelligence(Investigation) check with a DC equal to your spell save DC.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, its duration increases by 1 minute for each slot level above 3rd.

Faerie Fire.name: Faerie Fire
Faerie Fire.description:
Each object in a 20-foot cube within range is outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Any creature in the area when the spell is cast is also outlined in light if it fails aDexteritysaving throw.

For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed dim light in a 10-foot radius.

Any attack roll against an affected creature or object has advantage if the attacker can see it, and the affected creature or object can’t benefit from being invisible.

Avatar of the Apocalypse.name: Avatar of the Apocalypse
Avatar of the Apocalypse.description:
Class(es): druid, sorcerer, wizard

You transform into a formidable avatar of cataclysmic power. For the duration, your physical form is imbued with elemental fury, granting you the following benefits: You gainresistanceto bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

Your melee weapon attacks use your spellcasting ability modifier for theattackanddamage rolls, and they deal an additional 2d6 force damage.

You have advantage onStrengthandConstitutionsaving throws.
