Corrosive Solvent.name: Corrosive Solvent
Corrosive Solvent.description:
You conjure one square foot of strongly corrosive acid on an object or creature you can see within range. If the target is a creature or a worn or held object, the creature can make aDexteritysaving throw to avoid the solvent.

The solvent has the consistency of a slimy paste. If the target is an object, the acid eats through six inches of organic material, four inches of stone, or one inch of metal per round. It can be conjured on the ceiling, but if this is done, it eats through the ceiling at only half the rate as bits drip to the floor. If the target is a living creature, it takes 1d4 acid damage per round.

Drown.components: V, S, M (water from the lungs of
Drown.description:
Water swirls up in a sphere around a creature you can see within range, forcing itself into the creature’s mouth and nose. The creature must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, it is stunned until the start of its next turn by the water entering its lungs. On a successful save, the creature isn’t affected.

An affected creature can’t speak and begins to suffocate. As an action, the creature can try to cough the water out of its lungs by repeating the saving throw. On a success, the spell ends. A creature that can breathe water isn’t affected by this spell.

Shadow Army.description:
You create dozens of semi-real shadow-copies of yourself that appear in the spell area to fight your foes. The clones are exact copies of you, allowing you to useStealthtohideamong them and cause the targeting to randomly choose a target like the spellMirror Image.

An enemy that’s in the area when the spell is cast or ends their turn within the area are pummeled by the shadow copies taking 9d6 magical bludgeoning damage and suffer eitherpoisonedorrestrained, chosen when the spell is cast, until the beginning of their next turn.

Each round before taking damage, the enemy may make aWisdomsaving throw. On a success, they take half the damage and are not affected by the condition for the round. If the target rolls a natural 20 on their saving throw, they automatically succeed on their saving throws against this spell for 24 hours.

Greater Mount Mind.description:
You and your mount can predict each other’s movements and move in perfect synchronization. You and your mount gain the benefits of mount mind, and in addition as a bonus action you can direct your mount to make a singlemelee attackusing its hooves, bite, or other body part. This is in addition to any otheractionsyour mount takes on its turn. If you and your mountattackthe same creature during a round, you each gain a +1 bonus on yourattackanddamage rollsagainst it.

Sand Form.name: Sand Form
Sand Form.description:
Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard

You transform a willing creature you touch, along with everything it’s wearing and carrying, into a mobile pile of sand for the duration. The spell ends if the creature drops to0 hit points. An incorporeal creature isn’t affected. While in this form, the target’s only method of movement is a speed of 10 feet. The target can enter and occupy the space of another creature. The target hasresistanceto nonmagical damage, and it has advantage onStrength,Dexterity, andConstitutionsaving throws. The target can pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks, though it treats liquids as though they were solid surfaces. While in the form of sand, the target can’t talk or manipulate objects, and any objects it was carrying or holding can’t be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. The target can’tattackor cast spells.

Instant Karma.name: Instant Karma
Instant Karma.description:
Your magic punishes a creature for inflicting harm. Choose one creature that you can see within range. That creature must make aCharismasaving throw. On a success, the spell ends. On a failure, the creature suffers no ill effects until it makes an attack. Each time the target of this spell damages another creature with a melee, ranged, or spell attack, it takes 2d10 force damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 3rd.

Master’s Proficiency.name: Master’s Proficiency
Master’s Proficiency.description:
When you cast this spell you draw the focus with a flourish and gain proficiency with the specific item you are holding when casting the spell. If you are already proficient with the item you get a +1 bonus onattackrolls or skill checks with the item.

Breath of Life - The Scout (5e)© 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions; Authors: Norman Mitchell Jr. and Connor Bates

Orgiastic Rite.name: Orgiastic Rite
Orgiastic Rite.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a fertility idol)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

Classesbard,cleric,druid,warlock

You incite the passions, compelling the targets to engage in a frenzy of carnality. You target three creatures, no two of whom may be farther than 30 feet apart to be affected.

They must make aCharismasaving throw or be compelled to move towards the nearest creature that is also within the spell’s range and passionately kiss or caress that creature.

If there is no creature within 30 feet of a target that it could normally have lustful feelings towards, it gains advantage on its saving throw. If two or more creatures are equidistant, it chooses the target with the higherCharismascore. If the target of its affections is also affected by the spell, both creatures dropprone.

Affected creatures immediately drop any held objects, and if wearing any magical or mundane armor or clothing (including belts, vests, hats, and the like), they remove one random item per round and drop the item on the ground in their square. An affected creature wearing armor spends the first round of the spell’s effect removing portions of their armor before doffing any other worn items; thereafter, their armor’s AC bonus is reduced by half (rounding down) until they spend 1 minute putting their armor back together.

All targets of the spell must be of the same type, though they may have different subtypes. Each round after the first round of the spell’s effect, affected creatures can attempt a newWisdomsave to break free of the compulsion and end the effect. Once the spell ends, affected creatures must make aConstitutionsaving throw or gain 1 level ofexhaustion.

Conjure Devil.name: Conjure Devil
Conjure Devil.description:
You summon a fiend of lawful alignment with a challenge rating 4 or lower, which appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range.

The devil disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The devil is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Roll initiative for the devil, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you), as long as they don’t violate its alignment. If you don’t issue any commands to the devil, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions. The GM has the devil’s statistics.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th-level or higher, you summon one additional devil for each spell slot above 7th.

Summoning more than onedevilusing this spell turns it into a concentration spell.

Phantom Banisher.name: Phantom Banisher
Phantom Banisher.description:
This phantom from another dimension crawls into existence and attempts to drag someone back with them. When you cast this spell, select a creature within range as the target for the phantom. The phantom appears in a space adjacent to you and immediately rushes to its prey. The phantom is not a corporeal creature and has nohit pointsor AC. The phantom acts at the end ofyour turnand moves up to 40 feet toward the target. When it reaches the target, it attempts to grapple them, forcing anAthleticsorAcrobaticsskill check versus your spell save DC. If they fail, they aregrappledand the phantom begins to drag them back to their home dimension. This forces aCharismasaving throw versus your spell save DC. If they fail, they are immediately taken to whatever dimension the phantom came from and disappear from our reality. If they succeed, they may attempt to escape the grapple as an action. The phantom will continue to attempt to grapple and kidnap your target for the duration of the spell. If the duration ends and the phantom has not succeeded, it will simply vanish back to its realm. A creature taken to the phantom’s realm remains there even after the spell has ended and must find its own way home.

Warp Metal.description:
Class(es):cleric,paladin,sorcerer,wizard

You bend and warp up to 10 small metal objects within range, causing it to be deformed and weakened. Each item must be about thesizeof ashield, breastplate, chain shirt, or one-handed weapon. You can affect a single larger item, such as a two-handed weapon or full suit of armor, as if it were two small objects. You can affect an object up to a 10-foot cube as if it were five small objects, or a single object up to a 15-foot cube as if it were 10 objects.

A creature wearing or wielding an item you attempt to warp can attempt aConstitutionsaving throw to prevent the spell from affecting their items, with a separate save required for each item. The effects of being warped depend on the type of item:

Groom.description:
The touched creature is cleaned up as if they took a bath, cleaned with soap; their hair, both head and body, is trimmed or cleaned up to local fashion and their worn clothing is cleaned up and smoothed out. This does not repair any damage to weapons, armor, or clothing, but at least they’re cleaned and polished.

Animate Instrument.name: Animate Instrument
Animate Instrument.description:
ComponentsV S M (a musical instrument)

The touched instrument is able to keep up your tune, and is able to grant your bardic abilities without needing to hold or play the instrument.

You must still use your action to activate the abilities used.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

Fist of Iron.description:
You transform your naked hand into iron. Your unarmed attacks deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage and are considered magical.

Zobeck: Clockwork City © 2022 Open Design Llc; Author: Wolfgang Baur, Mike Franke, James J. Haeck, Ben Mcfarland, Richard Pett, Christina Stiles, Matthew Stinson.

Trick Shot.name: Trick Shot
Trick Shot.duration: Concentration, up to 30 seconds In an act of dramatic extravagance, fire
Trick Shot.description:
In an act of dramatic extravagance, fire a ranged weapon directly into the air with no particular target. The projectile soars up into the sky and out of sight. At any point during the duration of this spell, you may use yourreactionto call down the projectile and strike a target within range. Make a ranged weaponattackwith advantage against the target. Thisattackcritically hits on a roll of 18-20.

Conjure Flying Polyp.name: Conjure Flying Polyp
Conjure Flying Polyp.components: V, S, M (an Elder Sign with radius at least 10 feet)
Conjure Flying Polyp.description:
You summon a flying polyp with one body, which appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The polyp disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The polyp is friendly to you and your companions for the duration unless it succeeds on a Charisma saving throw, in which case it is hostile toward you and your companions.

Roll initiative for the polyp, which has its own turns. If you control it, it obeys any verbal or mental commands that you issue to it (no action required by you), as long as they don’t violate its interests. If you don’t issue any commands to it, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.

You can communicate telepathically with the polyp while it is within 100 feet and you maintain concentration, but the connection can also harm you. When the polyp is reduced to 0 hit points while you concentrate, any remaining damage is dealt to you. In addition, all psychic damage dealt to the polyp while you concentrate is also dealt to you; if the polyp takes psychic damage that would reduce its hit points below 0, that additional damage does not transfer to you.

If your concentration is broken, the polyp doesn’t disappear.

Instead, you lose control of the creature, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it might attack. An uncontrolled polyp can’t be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it.

Guards and Wards.components: V, S, M(burning incense, a small measure of brimstone and oil, a knotted string, a small amount of umber hulk blood, and a small silver rod worth at least 10 gp)
Guards and Wards.description:
You create a ward that protects up to 2,500 square feet of floor space (an area 50 feet square, or one hundred 5-foot squares or twenty-five 10-foot squares). The warded area can be up to 20 feet tall, and shaped as you desire. You can ward several stories of a stronghold by dividing the area among them, as long as you can walk into each contiguous area while you are casting the spell.

When you cast this spell, you can specify individuals that are unaffected by any or all of the effects that you choose. You can also specify a password that, when spoken aloud, makes the speaker immune to these effects.

Guards and wards creates the following effects within the warded area.

Corridors: Fog fills all the warded corridors, making them heavilyobscured. In addition, at each intersection or branching passage offering a choice of direction, there is a 50 percent chance that a creature other than you will believe it is going in the opposite direction from the one it chooses.

Doors: All doors in the warded area are magically locked, as if sealed by anarcane lockspell. In addition, you can cover up to ten doors with an illusion (equivalent to the illusory object function of theminor illusionspell) to make them appear as plain sections of wall.

Stairs: Webs fill all stairs in the warded area from top to bottom, as thewebspell. These strands regrow in 10 minutes if they are burned or torn away whileguards and wardslasts.

Other Spell Effect: You can place your choice of one of the following magical effects within the warded area of the stronghold.

The whole warded area radiates magic. Adispel magiccast on a specific effect, if successful, removes only that effect.

You can create a permanently guarded and warded structure by casting this spell there every day for one year.

Safeword Nikto.name: Safeword Nikto
Safeword Nikto.components: V, S, M (set of mundane gloves, which the spell consumes)
Safeword Nikto.description:
You touch a willing create, including yourself, and create a thin magical barrier around them. If they are wielding a cursed item, the effects of the curse are lifted for the duration of the spell. This does not break attunement to the item, it simply suppresses the curses effect on the spell target. If they touch a cursed item while the spell is active, there will be no adverse effects from the curse itself until the spell ends. This does not eliminate the other effects that moving a cursed item may cause, such as the curse effecting those around the target or traps being sprung.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration of the spell increases by 1 hour for every spell slot above 3rd.

Invested Protection.name: Invested Protection
Invested Protection.description:
You infuse a living creature with healing energies, restoring 1d6hit pointsimmediately. In addition, for 1 minute these energies surround the target and cause all attacks against them to take a -1 penalty ondamage rolls.

An undead creature striking the target in melee with a part of their body takes 1 radiant damage after each hit. Undead wielding a weapon do not take this damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you restore an additional 1d6hit pointsto the target and increase the penalty ondamage rollsagainst the target and radiant damage taken by undead striking the target in melee by 1.

Curse of the Shifting Sands.description:
Target: A 20-foot square within range

You cause the ground in the target area to become treacherous and constantly shifting, resembling the desert’s shifting sands. The area becomes difficult terrain for the duration. Additionally, each creature that start its turn in the area or enter it for the first time on a turn must make aStrengthsaving throw or have their speed reduced to 0 until the start of their next turn, as the sandsentangletheir feet.

Dark Lord’s Mantle.name: Dark Lord’s Mantle
Dark Lord’s Mantle.description:
You infuse yourself with fiendish power, which inspires your allies and intimidates your foes. While the spell lasts, you exude confidence. You gain advantage on saving throws against all enchantment spells and effects. In addition, each ally within 30 feet of you can roll a d4 once per round and add the result to anattackroll as a bonus action, or to a saving throw as areaction.

An enemy that starts its turn within 30 feet of you, or that moves within 30 feet of you on its turn, must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomefrightenedof you. Jazz Hands.name: Jazz Hands
Jazz Hands.description:
Choose a spell of 1st level or higher that you know. The next time you cast that spell, during the duration of this cantrip, you can cast it without the somatic components of the spell. You may only have one spell primed with this cantrip at a time.

Remortification.components: V, S, M (diamonds worth 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
Remortification.duration: ends or it is killed, even if it had been healed in the meantime. It has
Remortification.description:
You touch a corpse (not an undead creature) and return it briefly to life with a number of hit points equal to 4d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. It must have been dead for no longer than 8 hours when you cast the spell. It survives only until the spell’s duration ends or it is killed, even if it had been healed in the meantime. It has a -1 penalty on all attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks for the duration.

Conjure Fiends (Open Design).name: Conjure Fiends (Open Design)
Conjure Fiends (Open Design).description:
You summon fiends that appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within range. You choose one of the following options for what appears:

A fiend summoned by this spell disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The summoned creatures are friendly to you and your companions. Rollinitiativefor the summoned creatures as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures, but otherwise take noactions.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using certain higher-level spell slots, you choose one of the summoning options above, and more creatures appear: twice as many with a 6th-level spell slot and three times as many with an 8th-level spell slot.

Infernal Contract.components: V, S, M (vellum or parchment contract, a pen, and a drop of the targets blood)
Infernal Contract.description:
Classes:cleric,warlock(fiend patron only),wizard

A creature who signs this contract, whether willingly or through coercion or magical compulsion, is bound to obey the letter of the document. The first time the victim attempts to act in a manner counter to the contract they are violently ill and becomeincapacitatedfor 1 minute. The second time, they take 5d10 psychic damage and areincapacitatedfor 1 minute.

The third time their soul is ripped from their body and dragged to the lower planes.

Remove curse orgreater restorationcast with a 6th-level spell slot or higher, orwishcan break the contract anddispelthe effect. The signer’s death also ends the infernal contract, unless a clause within the contract specifically states otherwise.

Shining Beacon.name: Shining Beacon
Shining Beacon.description:
Area30 foot radius centered on you

Upon completing the spell, you are limned in a nimbus of light that shines like a torch. You gain advantage onCharismasaves and checks and are immune to thefrightenedand demoralized conditions. Additionally, you exude an aura that instills hope in your allies.

All allies within 30 feet gain advantage on saves against thefrightenedand demoralized conditions. Any ally that begins their turn in the aura may make an immediate save against afrightenedor demoralized condition affecting them. If they succeed it is treated as if they succeeded at their initial save.

Dissipation.name: Dissipation
Dissipation.description:
This spell uses teleportation magic to scatter some of the subjects’ flesh and tissue to random locations, leaving them with deep wounds. Choose up to six creatures you can see within range. Each creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw. A target takes 12d6 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spells and effects that prevent teleportation or dimensional travel also block all damage from this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Wind of The Outer Void.name: Wind of The Outer Void
Wind of The Outer Void.description:
You call forth a chilling presence from beyond the mortal world, forming it into a wall of frozen horror. You can make either a straight wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 10 feet wide or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick. The wall provides halfcoverto creatures behind it, and its space isdifficult terrain. When a creature enters the wall’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d10 cold damage and isfrightenedof you until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and is notfrightened.

Warlock Grimoire 4. ©2023 Open Design LLC. Authors: Lou Anders, Wolfgang Baur, HH Carlan, Robert Fairbanks, Basheer Ghouse, Richard Green, Tim Hitchcock, Jeremy Hochhalter, Victoria Jaczko, Rajan Khanna, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Jonathan Miley, Kelly Pawlik, Sebastian Rombach, Adam W. Dance of Ruin.name: Dance of Ruin
Dance of Ruin.components: V, S, M (demon’s feather or scale)
Dance of Ruin.description:
You dance with an ecstatic, obscene rhythm that invokes destruction. When you first cast this spell, and as a bonus action on each subsequent turn for its duration, you may release a bolt of ruinous energy, making a melee spellattackagainst a target within 5 feet of you or ranged spell attack against a target within 60 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes 3d4 acid damage and 3d4 lighting damage.

Immediately after you make the attack, you can also move up to 5 feet as long as your speed isn’t 0. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the acid and lightning damage each increase by 1d4 for each slot level above 4th.

Stone Call.name: Stone Call
Stone Call.description:
You cast the spell and a rain of dirt, gravel and stones comes down into a 40-foot radius dealing 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage to every creature in the area. The damage only occurs once.

For the remainder of the spell’s duration, the fallen dirt and stones create difficult terrain. At the end of the duration, the rocks and dirt disappear leaving no after-effects.

A successful Dexterity saving throw halves the damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, the bludgeoning damage caused by the stones increases by 1d6.

Read Magic: The Compilation, © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Swift Stars.name: Swift Stars
Swift Stars.description:
You create a series of large sparkling lights that rush towards your opponent and throughcover. Make a ranged spellattackagainst a target. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 slashing damage and 1d6 radiant damage. If you cannot see the target through thecover, thisattackis made at disadvantage. The star sparkles will travel through up to 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of steel, and no amount of solid lead. If a creature is wearing mundane armor of metal or leather, they gain no bonus to their AC from those items against this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the slashing damage increases by 1d6 and the radiant damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot used above 1st.

Bone Spurs.name: Bone Spurs
Bone Spurs.description:
Jagged spurs of bone erupt from the feet and ankles of a creature you can see that is in range. The creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature suffers 2d10 piercing damage. In addition, the creature’s speed is halved, and it suffers 1d8 piercing damage on each turn it moves more than 5 feet.

Detect Curse.name: Detect Curse
Detect Curse.duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes For the duration,
Detect Curse.description:
For the duration, you sense the presence and location of any cursed creatures, objects, or areas within 30 feet of you. If you detect a curse in this way, you can use your action to determine the nature and effect of that curse.

The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by one foot of stone, one inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or three feet of wood or dirt.

Mark Prey.name: Mark Prey
Mark Prey.description:
You choose a creature you can see within range as your prey. Until the spell ends, you have advantage onWisdom(Perception) andWisdom(Survival) checks to find or track your prey. In addition, the target is outlined in light that only you can see. Any attack roll you make against your prey has advantage if you can see it, and your prey can’t benefit from beinginvisibleagainst you. If the target drops to0 hit pointsbefore this spell ends, you can use a bonus action on a subsequent turn to mark a new target as your prey.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level, you can maintain your concentration on the spell for up to 8 hours. When you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can maintain your concentration on the spell for up to 24 hours.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Unnatural Causes.name: Unnatural Causes
Unnatural Causes.description:
You cause vengeful spirits of the wrongfully slain to manifest in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range. The sphere of spirits spreads around corners and lasts until the spell ends.

When a creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 cold and 3d6 necrotic damage and has disadvantage onattackrolls until the end of its next turn.

On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and doesn’t have disadvantage onattackrolls.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the cold damage or necrotic damage (your choice) increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 4th.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Temporal Disjunction.name: Temporal Disjunction
Temporal Disjunction.description:
Make a ranged spellattackagainst a creature within range.

On a hit, the target ispoisoned. Creatures immune to chronomancy are immune to this effect, but not creatures that are immune to poison. At the end of each of thepoisonedtarget’s turns, the target must make aCharismasaving throw. If the target succeeds on three of these saves, it is no longerpoisoned, and the spell ends. If the target fails three of these saves, the target is no longerpoisoned, but has disadvantage onDexteritychecks,Dexteritysaving throws, andattackrolls that useDexterity.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can increase the duration by 1 day for each slot level above 4th.

Slimeatize.name: Slimeatize
Slimeatize.description:
Touch a willing creature and loosen the bonds of their atoms, turning them into a viscous liquid. For the duration of the spell they become a conscious slimy substance. They have a climb speed equal to their movement speed, can stick to walls, can squeeze through cracks as small as 1 inch, take half damage from non-magical physical attacks, can see normally, and can regain a shape similar to their solid form. They cannotattack, cast spells, or speak while in this form. All saving throws are made normally and allStrengthandDexteritybased ability checks are made with disadvantage. When the spell ends, they return to their normal form if there is space to do so. If there is not space, they take 2d10 force damage at the start of each their turns until they move to adequate space or die, their liquid body simply ceasing movement where it is.

Unwilling creatures must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or be liquified. They can make an additional saving throw at the end of each of their turns, reverting to their normal form on a success.

Void Blessing.components: V, S, M (plate of satarre chitin)
Void Blessing.description:
This spell transforms a creature that you can see within range into a new form beloved of the Void. An unwilling creature must make aWisdomsaving throw to avoid the effect. A shapechanger automatically succeeds on this saving throw. The transformation lasts for

Death Spiral.name: Death Spiral
Death Spiral.components: V, S, M (coiled length of animal intestine)
Death Spiral.description:
Class(es):sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You unleash a coil of deadly energy that persists as long as it slays creatures. Choose a creature you can see within range. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw.

On a failure, it takes 5d12 necrotic damage, or half as much on a success. If the target is reduced to0 hit points, it dies, and you can choose a different creature within range of you. The new target must make aConstitutionsaving throw as above, taking damage which could allow you to choose another new target. The process continues until the spell fails to kill a creature or you choose not to select a new target.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d12 for each slot level above 5th.

Remove Curse.name: Remove Curse
Remove Curse.description:
At your touch, all curses affecting one creature or object end. If the object is a cursed magic item, its curse remains, but the spell breaks its owner’s attunement to the object so it can be removed or discarded.

3rd Party OptionsJust an FYI: You or your GM may want to considersome specific curses found here.

Rime.name: Rime
Rime.description:
You touch one nonmagical weapon and imbue it with frost. For the duration, the weapon and any ammunition it fires are coated in a thin, biting layer of ice, and any damage the weapon deals is cold damage instead of its normal damage type. If a hit with the weapon is a critical hit, the weapon deals an extra 1d4 cold damage, and the spell ends.

The cold damage from a critical hit increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

Whirlwind Smite.name: Whirlwind Smite
Whirlwind Smite.description:
Make a weaponmelee attackagainst each creature of your choice within range. The targets take an extra 1d8 Radiant damage from theattack. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or an Undead.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. If you cast this spell using a level 4 spell slot, the damage increases by 1d8.

Breath of Life: The Marshal (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Michael Messinger

Abominable Amorphous Amoeba.name: Abominable Amorphous Amoeba
Abominable Amorphous Amoeba.description:
You prepare a glass orb and fill it with an eldritch alchemical fluid. The crafting cost of the orb is 1,000 gp, and it takes 1d4 weeks to prepare. When you cast the spell, the liquid becomes a terrible, living, single-celled ooze. You can use an action to throw the orb against an opponent, at which point the sphere shatters and the uncontrolled creature is released. The ooze then begins to feed, fueling its awful growth. You are not in control of the creature.

The creature starts with 2d8hit pointsand fills one five-foot square. Any creature that starts its turn within five feet of the ooze or comes within that distance for the first time on its turn must make a DC 15Dexteritysaving throw. The creature takes 1d8 acid damage on a failure and half as much on a success. A creature brought to0 hit pointsby the beast is consumed and dead. A consumed creature cannot be brought back to life. The ooze gainshit pointsequal to the damage taken by its targets.

For every 30hit pointsthe creature has, it covers one additional five-foot square. The creature is an ooze and can share a square with another creature. A creature in the same square as the ooze has disadvantage on its saving throws against the ooze. The ooze has AC 15 and is immune to acid, bludgeoning, piercing, poison, and psychic damage. It is immune to thegrappledandproneconditions. It moves at 10 feet toward the closest living creature.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Déjà Vu.name: Déjà Vu
Déjà Vu.description:
This spell repeats any instantaneous evocation spell of 5th level or lower that takes effect within its area.

Upon completing this spell, you select a 40-foot cube within range to be charged with magic. The area remains charged until triggered or the duration expires.

The first instantaneous evocation spell of 5th level or lower that takes effect within the designated area triggers the déjà vu. Once triggered, the déjà vu repeats the triggering spell the following round onyour turn. Repeated spells are handled just as if the same caster had cast them again.

Earthen Prison.name: Earthen Prison
Earthen Prison.description:
You conjure a grasping vine from the earth that snatches your target and drags the creature beneath the earth. This vine makes a singlemelee attackagainst a target within range using your spell attack modifier. If this attack hits, the target is restrained and dragged beneath the earth. A targetrestrainedin this way cannot see above the earth, cannot speak, and cannot breathe.

A creaturerestrainedby the vine can use its action to make aStrength(Athletics) check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself and pops out of the earth.

Mass Cloud of Razors.components: V, S, M (1 small sewing needle)
Mass Cloud of Razors.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (1 small sewing needle)

Duration5 + spellcasting modifier rounds

NoteThis spell is a rework of the core spell of the same name.

You conjure a multitude of razors in a 30-foot-radius sphere that slice the flesh of the creatures within. If the targets fails aDexteritysaving throw, they are dealt 1 piercing damage at the beginning of each of their turns. This damage, while physical is considered to be from amagic weaponforresistancepurposes.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th or higher, the damage dealt each round increases to 2. The damage further increases to 3 if you instead use a 9thlevel spell slot.

Passing Glance.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 hour

When you cast this spell you seem hazy and nondescript to your enemies. Whenever a creature would target you with anattackor spell, they must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failure, they overlook you and must choose another target within range, including movement. If there is no other valid target in the attacker’s range, the spell has no effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature within 30 feet, beside yourself, for each slot level above 2nd.

Hopeless Shadow.name: Hopeless Shadow
Hopeless Shadow.description:
This spell operates as thedarknessspell except that any creature that enters or is within the radius ofdarknessmust succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be demoralized. If an affected creature leaves the area ofdarknessthe condition remains for 1d4 rounds but resumes anytime the creature enters thedarknessagain.

A creature that succeeds on the saving throw must make a saving throw each turn they are within the radius of thedarkness.

GoodHope - Crushing Despair (5E), © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Animated Object Swarm.name: Animated Object Swarm
Animated Object Swarm.description:
Myriad Tiny objects animate at your command, forming a swarm. The objects’ abilities conform to the rules stated in theanimate objectsspell, except that you animate only Tiny objects, which gather together into a Medium swarm.

The area of the swarm is considereddifficult terrain, and creatures in it are lightlyobscured. The swarm has the following statistics:

Armor Class18Hit Points20Strength4;Dexterity18Damage Resistancesbludgeoning, piercing, slashingCondition Immunitiescharmed,frightened,grappled,paralyzed,petrified,prone,restrained, stunned

Discern Curse.name: Discern Curse
Discern Curse.description:
You detect whether creatures, a location, or objects within 30 feet of you are cursed or carry a curse and can determine the nature of the curse with a successful DC 15Intelligence(Arcana) check. If attempting to examine a target or remove the curse risks affecting you with the curse as well, you gain advantage on your saving throw to resist being affected by it.

The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

Curse of Warts.name: Curse of Warts
Curse of Warts.description:
You curse a target with horrid warts that grow across their body. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw or suffer the curse. These warts are disfiguring, causing them to suffer disadvantage onCharismachecks until the spell ends. While they are affected by the warts, as a bonus action you may cause the warts to burst and inflict 2d8 necrotic damage on the target. This ends the spell.

Rage.name: Rage
Rage.description:
DurationConcentration up to 1 minute

You speak the words of the spell and the target is filled with an unbridled rage. The creature targeted must be willing to give into the anger of this spell. While raging, the target gains the following effects:

If the target has the rage class feature, they gain the benefits of their rage rather than the benefits listed above, including any effects provided by their subclass. The rage induced by this spell does not count against the uses of their rage per long rest.

At Higher Levels. When casting this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher, you can target one additional willing target for each spell slot level above 3rd.

Effortless Armor.name: Effortless Armor
Effortless Armor.description:
Classes: antipaladin,cleric,paladin,ranger

Armor that you wear no longer hampers your movement, regardless of yourStrengthscore, and you do not have disadvantage onStealthchecks due to wearing medium armor.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a 2nd-level slot, you can cast it on another creature with a range of touch. Alternatively, if you cast it on yourself the duration is increased to 1 hour and you no longer having disadvantage onDexterity(Stealth) checks when wearing heavy armor.

If you cast this spell using a 3rd-level slot, you can cast it with the above enhanced effects on an ally with a range of touch, or you can increase the duration to 8 hours if you cast it on yourself.

Shadow Trove.name: Shadow Trove
Shadow Trove.components: V, S, M(ink made from the blood of a raven)
Shadow Trove.description:
You paint a small door approximately 2 feet square on a hard surface to create a portal into the void of space. The portal “peels off” the surface you painted it on and follows you when you move, always floating in the air within 5 feet of you. An icy chill flows out from the portal. You can place up to 750 pounds of nonliving matter in the portal, where it stays suspended in the frigid void until you withdraw it. Items that are still inside the shadow trove when the duration ends spill out onto the ground. You can designate a number of creatures up to yourIntelligencemodifier who have access to the shadow trove; only you and those creatures can move objects into the portal.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration increases by 2 hours for each slot level above 3rd.

Crank Caller.description:
A shadowy illusion rushes the target creature from behind. The target must make anIntelligencesaving throw. On failure, the target turns swiftly around to defend themselves. Any creatures, within 5 feet who were already engaged with the target, then can make anattackof opportunity against the target. On success, the target is not fooled.

Enlarge Weapon.name: Enlarge Weapon
Enlarge Weapon.description:
You touch a nonmagical weapon and enlarge it so it is appropriate for creatures onesizelarger than it was. Typically, the weapon’s damage increases by one diesizewhen this occurs. For example, a longsword meant for a Medium creature can be made to work for a Large creature and would do 1d10 damage or 1d12 if used two-handed.

Each creature in a 30-foot cone must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 4d6 piercing damage and ispoisonedfor 1 minute on a failed save or half as much damage and is notpoisonedon a successful one.

When you cast this spell, you touch an object.

Event Horizon.name: Event Horizon
Event Horizon.components: V, S, M (shard of meteoric iron)
Event Horizon.description:
You form a mild gravity well around a creature. Choose a Large or smaller creature you can see within range. All creatures of your choice within 15 feet of the target must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or berestrained. Arestrainedcreature that starts its turn within 15 feet of the target can use its action on its turn to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC to stop beingrestrainedand move away from the target. If the target moves, allrestrainedcreatures within 15 feet of it move as well, maintaining the same distance and position from the target if possible. If an object or creature already occupies that space, the creature moves to the nearest empty space to it.Restrainedcreatures that move as a result of the target’s movement are considered to use their own movement and draw opportunity attacks as normal.

A creature that isrestrainedby the target at the end of its turn ages 1 year. The target ages 1 year per creaturerestrainedby it at the time the spell ends.

Out of Sight.name: Out of Sight

Out of Sight.description:
The spell inhibits the memories of creatures that perceive you. While creatures can perceive you normally, when a creature stops observing you, it must attempt aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails, it loses all memory of its awareness of you and youractionswhile you were under the effects of this spell. The spell’s duration measures how long the out of sight effect lasts on you, but the memory alteration is instantaneous and can be reversed only by magic such asmodify memory.

The creature is still aware of any other changes to itself or its environment. For instance, a guard will remember running, and may notice a newly unlocked door, but will not remember that he was chasing after you. Creatures that cannot becharmedare immune to this spell.

Barnacle.name: Barnacle
Barnacle.description:
You cause painful barnacles to grow on a single target within 60 feet. These parasites at first appear as small buds on the skin of the target but quickly expand to about six inches wide each. As they grow, their mass increases, with their combined weight slowing the target.

An affected target’s speed is halved, and it gains a –2 penalty toDexteritysaving throws. However, the hardened barnacles grant it a +2 bonus to AC. The barnacles can be scraped off by a creature using an action to do so, but this inflicts 1d4 slashing damage to the affected creature.

You create two colossal rocks and smash a target between them. You make a ranged spellattack. The target takes 20d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit and the target needs to make aDexteritysaving throw.

On a failure, the target is knockedproneand crushed under a pile of stone like a cave-in.

On a miss, the target still takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage.

A vertical column of divine fire roars down from the heavens in a location you specify. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point within range must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 4d6 fire damage and 4d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the fire damage or the radiant damage (your choice) increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 5th.

Electrical Charge.components: V, S, M (1 piece of copper)
Electrical Charge.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (1 piece of copper)

Duration5 + spellcasting modifier rounds

You charge the target’s body with electricity.

If the target fails aConstitutionsaving throw, they are dealt 1 lightning damage at the beginning of each of their turns. If this spell is cast upon a creature affected by a vitriol spell of equal level, both spells end. If the vitriol spell is of higher level, this spell fails, if this spell is higher level, the vitriol spell ends.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, the damage each round increases to 2. The damage further increases to 3 if you instead use a spell slot of 5th or higher.

The weapon you are wielding gathers great magical power which is to be released as you strike. The next time you hit a creature with a weaponattackbefore this spell ends, the target and other creatures in a 30-foot-long and 5-foot-wide line behind the target take 2d6 force damage. The creatures except the target can make aDexteritysaving throw to negate the effect.

Insight of Good Fortune.components: V, S, M (golden die worth at least 20 gp)
Insight of Good Fortune.description:

You a golden die toward a creature within range, which then whirls around them flashing with golden light each time the target needs to roll a d20. At any point during the spell when the target rolls a d20, they can tap into the power of the golden die, granting them Advantage on that roll and causing the golden die to disappear. By wrapping your hand around a small eyelike object, you becomeinvisibleuntil the spell ends. Anything you are wearing or carrying isinvisibleas long as it is on your person. The spell ends if youattackor cast another spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 1st level or higher, you can extend the duration by 1 round for each slot level (2 rounds at 1st and 3 rounds at 2nd).

Planar Trace.name: Planar Trace
Planar Trace.description:
Classes: Cleric, Sorcerer, Summoner, Wizard

For the duration, you sense the presence of summoned creatures, portals, and planar rifts within range. The spell reveals:

The spell can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

Forced Mercy.name: Forced Mercy
Forced Mercy.description:
You compel a living creature to soften its blows, avoiding vital areas and causing little lasting harm. The target takes a -1 penalty on attack rolls against living foes for 1 round and must attempt aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails the save, the penalty continues as long as the spell lasts, and all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage the target deals to living creatures is temporary, lasting only until the target completes a Short or Long Rest. A creature reduced to0 hit pointsby this temporary damage is immediatelyUnconsciousbut Stable and need not make Death Saving Throws. A willing creature can intentionally accept the spell’s effects for 1 minute, even if you do not concentrate.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Your range is increased by 30 feet and you can affect 2 additional creatures for each spell slot level above 1.

Rupture.name: Rupture
Rupture.description:
Selecting a creature within range that you can see, you utter the word “Suffer!” while crushing a small skull. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failure, its skull fractures, causing 5d6 slashing damage. If this damage is enough to reduce the target to0 hit points, the creature isunconsciousand stable.

The victim of a fractured skull isstunnedand may make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns to end thestunnedcondition. A fractured skull causes the target to makeattackrolls, saving throws, and skill checks at disadvantage until healed, as per fracture.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 5th.

Frostlands of Fenrilik © 2020 Travis Legge

Steelskin.name: Steelskin
Steelskin.components: V, S, M (scrap of plate armor)
Steelskin.description:
Classes:cleric,paladin,sorcerer,wizard

You touch a willing creature. Until the spell ends, the target’s skin has a smooth, steel-like appearance, and the target’s AC can’t be less than 19, regardless of what kind of armor it is wearing.

Legendary Classes: Templars & Tyrants© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Clinton J. Boomer, Amber Scott

Disruptive Mote.name: Disruptive Mote
Disruptive Mote.description:
Class(es):bard,cleric,paladin,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You conjure a mote of pseudo-sentient chaos, anchoring it to orbit protectively around you. For the duration, when a creature within 5 feet of you attacks you, the mote lashes out with discordant energy.

Roll 1d6 (before theattackroll is made) to determine the effect.

2 The attacker makes aDexteritysaving throw.

On a failure, it takes 3d12 force damage, or half as much on a success.

The attacker makes anIntelligencesaving throw. On a failure, it fallsprone, and its speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.

Before the spell ends, you can use yourreactionwhen you are hit by an attack to gainresistanceto the attack’s damage. If you do so, the spell ends immediately.

Unnerving Gaze.name: Unnerving Gaze
Unnerving Gaze.description:
You complete the spell, and your face shifts into the form of the target’s bitter enemy or departed loved ones. While they can see you, the target has disadvantage on saving throws against thefrightenedcondition andattackrolls by the target against you take a -1d4 penalty.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

Sunbeam.name: Sunbeam
Sunbeam.description:
A beam of brilliant light flashes out from your hand in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long line. Each creature in the line must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 radiant damage and isblindeduntil your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’tblindedby this spell. Undead and oozes have disadvantage on this saving throw.

You can create a new line of radiance as your action on any turn until the spell ends.

For the duration, a mote of brilliant radiance shines in your hand. It sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. This light is sunlight.

Manufacture.name: Manufacture
Manufacture.components: V, S, M(an amount of raw materials, see below)
Manufacture.description:
You turn an amount of raw materials into finished goods. You must have an amount of raw materials need to make an item, iron and wood for spear, leather and cloth for clothing, or gold and brass for a clock. This amount of raw materials is consumed during the casting of the spell. The raw material need not be processed but must be inert and not coming directly from a living creature; you can make a variety of wooden objects out of a fallen tree, but the spell fails if the only source of raw material is from a living creature. At the end of the spell the finished good is complete and whole, just as if it came out of a master craftsman’s shop.

You can only use this spell to create an object weighing less than 500 lbs whose total dimensions would fit in a 10-foot cube. Only mundane items can be created, you cannot use this to create magical items. You must know what the item you are creating is, but do not know how to make it yourself. The item can be as simple as a spear or as complex as a clock.

At higher levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the weight of the object you can create increase by a factor of ten, and thesizeof the cube it must fit in to increases by 10 feet.

The Lost Lands World Setting: 5th Edition Rules Addendum, © 2020, Frog God Games; Author Kenneth Spencer

Divine Absolution.name: Divine Absolution
Divine Absolution.description:
You touch one willing creature and declare them forgiven of all sins and wrongdoing against your deity. This surrounds them in a brief but powerful sacred aura that grants them immunity tofear, charm, and possession until the spell ends.

The Dragon’s Hoard #45© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darren Drader, Robert J. Grady, Nicholas Hite, Matt Kimmel

Monsoon.name: Monsoon
Monsoon.description:
You create a dark rain cloud in the shape of a cylinder that is 10 feet tall with a 40-foot radius, centered on the point you can see 100 feet in the sky directly above you. The spell fails if you can’t see a point in the air where the rain cloud could appear (for example, if you are in a room that can’t accommodate the cloud). The cloud remains centered on you in the sky above you, and moving to a place where you don’t have a clear path to the sky ends the spell early.

Until the spell ends, heavy rain and hailstones fall in the area within 40 feet of you, pummeling creatures and objects and loosening the ground. Nonmagical fires in the area are extinguished, the area is lightly obscured, and the ground in the area isdifficult terrain. Any creature other than you that starts its turn in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 2d10 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 6th.

Never Surrender.name: Never Surrender
Never Surrender.description:
When the target is reduced to0 hit points, it can fight looming death to stay in the fight. The target doesn’t fallunconsciousbut must still make death saving throws, as normal. The target doesn’t need to make a death saving throw until the end of its next turn, but it has disadvantage on that first death saving throw. In addition, massive damage required to kill the target outright must equal or exceed twice the target’s hit point maximum instead. If the target regains 1 or morehit points, this spell ends.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the target doesn’t have disadvantage on its first death saving throw.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Phase Weapon.name: Phase Weapon
Phase Weapon.description:
You shift a single weapon within range subtly out of phase with inanimate objects, allowing it to pass through them without impediment and without harm.Attackrolls made with a phase weapon ignore any AC provided by armor or shields and are instead resolved against what the target’s AC would be without them, typically 10 + the target’sDexteritymodifier (including any limits on itsDexteritymodifier imposed by the armor it is wearing). For targets where it is unclear what portion of their AC is granted by armor or a shield, the GM may instead simply grant advantage on attack rolls rather than resetting the target’s AC without its armor.

A phase weapon provides no benefit against creatures whose AC is granted by natural armor. A phase weapon cannot harm non-living creatures like constructs or undead, passing through them without affecting them. It can affect living creatures with bodies made of stone or similar material, like earth elementals.

The Dragon’s Hoard #33© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Scott D. Young, Matt Kimmel, Jeff Lee, James Abendroth.

Mystic Aegis.name: Mystic Aegis
Mystic Aegis.description:
You interfere with the power of a spell as it targets you, granting you advantage on your saving throw against the spell. If you already have advantage on that saving throw before casting the mystic aegis and you succeed on your saving throw, you are instead totally unharmed by the spell.

This applies only to effects of the spell that directly affect you; effects on the environment, like obscuring vision or destroying nearby objects or structures, still affect you normally.

The Dragon’s Hoard #50© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Robert J. Grady, Rich Howard, and Michael Mifsud

Arrow of Vengeance.name: Arrow of Vengeance
Arrow of Vengeance.description:
ComponentsS, M (a ranged weapon)

Witnessing an ally in need, you make a sign in the air marking an oath of vengeance and loose a deadlyattack. When an ally within the normal range of a ranged weapon you are currently wielding is attacked, you may cast this spell. Make a single attack with Advantage using your ranged weapon against the enemy who attacked your ally.

If the attack hits, it deals additional damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 2d6 of the same type for each spell slot level above 2.

Bloodbath.name: Bloodbath
Bloodbath.description:
Classes:cleric,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You select up to two living creature while cutting yourself with the ceremonial dagger, dealing yourself 1d6 necrotic damage which repeats at the start ofyour turnso long as you continue to concentrate on this spell (the damage from this spell does not force aConstitutionsaving throw to maintain concentration). So long as you keep taking this necrotic damage, any targets that have failed aConstitutionsaving throw also take the same amount of damage. The necrotic damage on any target ends if that target receives magicalhealing, or if your necrotic damage ends for any reason.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you may add an additional target for each slot level above 2nd. Secondary targets must be within 30 feet of each other.

Ultimate Treasury (5E)© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors: Jason Nelson, Loren Sieg, Pedro Coelho, Matt Goodall, Linda Zayas-Palmer, Thurston Hillman, Jeff Ibach, and Alex Augunas

Terrify.name: Terrify
Terrify.description:
Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You fill a creature’s mind with feelings of paranoia. A construct or an undead is immune to this effect. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomefrightenedof you until the spell ends. A creaturefrightenedin this way has its speed halved. Thefrightenedtarget can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Time Tracker.name: Time Tracker
Time Tracker.components: S, M (focus worth at least 1,000 gp, such as a crystal ball or a silver mirror)
Time Tracker.description:
You can view a creature up to 10 years into the past or into the future. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw, which is modified by how well you know the target and the sort of physical connection you have to it. If a target knows you’re casting this spell, it can fail the saving throw voluntarily if it wants to be observed.

On a successful save, the target isn’t affected, and you can’t use this spell against it again for 24 hours. On a failed save, the spell creates aninvisiblesensor within 10 feet of the target. You can see and hear through the sensor as if you were there. The sensor moves with the target, remaining within 10 feet of it for the duration. A creature that can seeinvisibleobjects sees the sensor as a luminous orb about the size of your fist. Instead of targeting a creature, you can choose a location you have seen in the past as the target of this spell. When you do, the sensor appears at that location and doesn’t move.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level, you can extend your tracking up to 100 years in the past or future; at 8th level, 1,000 years in the past or future, and at 9th level you can detect the target at any point in time.

Zephyr Shredder.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You unleash a barrage of razor-sharp blades made of compressed air toward targets within range. You can target up to six creatures. Make a ranged spellattackfor each blade. On a hit, a target takes 2d6 slashing damage. You can onlyattackeach creature with two blades per spell cast.

Hold Plant.name: Hold Plant
Hold Plant.description:
Choose a plant that you can see within range. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or beparalyzedfor the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional plant for each slot level above 3rd. The plants must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Radiant Blast.name: Radiant Blast
Radiant Blast.description:
You call down an explosion of radiant fire from the heavens on a point you can see in range. Each creature in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 radiant damage and is marked with holy radiance until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t marked.

The nextattackroll against a marked creature before the end of your next turn has advantage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Grim Harvest.name: Grim Harvest
Grim Harvest.components: V, S, M (pinch of gray sand and a bone chip)
Grim Harvest.description:
You reap the life force of a dying creature and use it to empower the next spell you cast. Your target must be at0 hit pointsand dying or must have died within the last round. If the target is dying, it must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or die. The next time youcast a spell, you gain 1d10 + your spellcasting ability modifier intemporary hit pointsand can choose one of the following effects to inflict on the spell’s target in addition to the usual effects of the spell you are casting. If the spell has more than one target, pick only one target to suffer the effect. If you don’t cast another spell within 1 minute of casting this one, the effect is lost.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Breath of Life.name: Breath of Life
Breath of Life.description:
One creature you touch has its airways immediately cleared. If the creature is choking or suffocating, the effect ends. If the effect is caused by a creature, the creature must make aStrengthsaving throw or release the target. If the conditions to choke the target are still in effect on the creature’s next turn (underwater, something wrapped around its throat, etc.), it starts choking again as if it had taken a deep breath first, resetting the number of minutes it can hold its breath.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Assuage Hunger and Thirst.name: Assuage Hunger and Thirst
Assuage Hunger and Thirst.description:
Classes: Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Wizard

The creature touched can go without food or drink for a number of days equal to 7 + itsConstitutionmodifier (minimum 1).

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Unseen Custodian.name: Unseen Custodian
Unseen Custodian.description:
This spell creates aninvisiblecleaning force. The custodian springs into existence in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and aStrengthof 2, and it can’tattack. If it drops to0 hit points, the spell ends. Once on each of your turns you can use a bonus action tocommandit to clean in a radius around you, polishing,mending, and folding everything in its path.

It can expand its circle inward or outward at your command, from a 5-foot radius to a 10-foot radius and so on until it reaches a maximum of 60 feet. Upon hitting a wall or obstacle, it makes a right turn and continues until it can move no further. It continues in this fashion until it has cleaned everything in the room or the duration ends.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Zone of Truth.name: Zone of Truth
Zone of Truth.description:
You create a magical zone that guards against deception in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range. Until the spell ends, a creature that enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, a creature can’t speak a deliberate lie while in the radius. You know whether each creature succeeds or fails on its saving throw.

An affected creature is aware of the spell and can thus avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive in its answers as long as it remains within the boundaries of the truth.

Ironhide.name: Ironhide
Ironhide.description:
Wolves have a tradition for having hides immune to sling stones and arrows. This spell bestows thatresistanceto ranged weapons.

Until the spell ends, you haveresistanceto nonmagical piercing damage.

NoteThe material component for this spell includes a wolf’s pelt. The wolf’s pelt can be actually worn by the caster, but it must be taken from a canine (defined above) equal in Hit Dice to the caster’s level. Being a lycan in lupocephalus form also counts as “wearing” a wolf’s pelt.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Tornado.name: Tornado
Tornado.description:
Class(es): Druid, Wizard, Sorcerer

You summon a massive tornado that tears through the landscape, following a path you direct. The tornado has a 50-foot-radius and moves 60 feet in a direction of your choosing as soon as it is cast.

Each creature in its path must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d6 bludgeoning damage and 5d6 slashing damage, is lifted by 50 feet into the tornado, and is thrown up to 100 feet in a random direction, landingprone.

On a success, a creature takes half damage and is not thrown. The tornado can uproot trees, buildings, and other large structures, causing additional destruction as determined by the GM. While concentrating on this spell, you can use your action each round to direct the movement of the tornado up to 60 feet in any direction. When you move the tornado, creatures within its path must make aStrengthsaving throw, suffering damage and potential effects as described above.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Fearful Rapture.name: Fearful Rapture
Fearful Rapture.description:
Classes: antipaladin,bard,cleric

You unleash a surge of emotion in a 30-foot cone that cows your enemies and simultaneously inspires your allies with your awesome power. Living enemies within the area are affected asfearon a failedWisdomsaving throw. Living allies gain a +1d4 bonus toattackrolls and saving throws against beingfrightened. In addition, any ally currentlyfrightenedgains a new saving throw to break the effect. This has no effect if the original effect did not allow a saving throw.

Clerics & Cultists© 2021, Legendary Games; Author Darrin Drader, Nicholas Hite, Sean K Reynolds, Jason Nelson, Jenny Jarzabski, Miguel Colon, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Daley, Nathan Reinecke.

Mass Vitality.name: Mass Vitality
Mass Vitality.description:
Your heart and blood burn as you extend your own guarded essence to your allies. Choose up to six creatures within range. For the duration of this spell, they cannot have their maxhit pointsreduced, cannot gainexhaustion, and are immune to the following conditions;paralyzed,poisoned, andstunned.

Blood Toll. You may choose to sacrifice a number ofhit pointsequal to 8d8. If you do, increase the duration of this spell to 1 hour.

Oversized Paws.description:
Until this spell ends, the hands and feet of one willing creature you choose within range become oversized and more powerful. For the duration, the creature adds 1d4 to damage it deals with its unarmed strike.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each spell slot above 2nd.

Let Me In!.name: Let Me In!
Let Me In!.description:
This spell forces open doors with the incantation, “little pig, little pig, let me in!”

Choose a door that you can see within range. A door that is held shut by a mundane lock or that is stuck or barred becomes unlocked, unstuck, or unbarred. If the door has multiple locks, only one of them is unlocked. If you choose a door that is held shut witharcane lock, that spell is suppressed for 1 minutes during which time the door can be opened and shut normally.

NoteThe material component for this spell includes a wolf’s pelt. The wolf’s pelt can be actually worn by the caster, but it must be taken from a canine (defined above) equal in Hit Dice to the caster’s level. Being a lycan in lupocephalus form also counts as “wearing” a wolf’s pelt.

Shared Pain.name: Shared Pain
Shared Pain.description:
You make a small cut on your body and a larger wound appears on the target. You take 1 point of damage and the target takes 1d8 necrotic damage. The target must then make a Constitution saving throw or be overwhelmed with the pain. On a failed saving throw, the subject is poisoned due to the pain until the end of your next turn.

At Higher Levels. This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

Labyrinth Mastery.name: Labyrinth Mastery
Labyrinth Mastery.components: V, S, M (piece of blank parchment)
Labyrinth Mastery.description:
Upon casting this spell, you immediately gain a sense of your surroundings. If you are in a physical maze or any similar structure with multiple paths and dead ends, this spell guides you to the nearest exit, although not necessarily along the fastest or shortest route. In addition, while the spell is guiding you out of such a structure, you have advantage on ability checks to avoid being surprised and oninitiativerolls.

You gain a perfect memory of all portions of the structure you move through during the spell’s duration.

If you revisit such a portion, you recognize that you’ve been there before and automatically notice any changes to the environment.

Also, while under the effect of this spell, you can exit anymaze spell(and its lesser and greater varieties) as an action without needing to make anIntelligencecheck.

You summon a concentrated burst of natural energy at a point within range. Each creature in a 20-foot radius Sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 3d8 damage on a failed save, or half on a success. You choose one of the following effects when casting:

Conjure Celestial.name: Conjure Celestial
Conjure Celestial.description:
You summon acelestialof challenge rating 4 or lower, which appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The celestial disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The celestial is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Rollinitiativefor the celestial, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you), as long as they don’t violate its alignment. If you don’t issue any commands to the celestial, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.

The GM has the celestial’s statistics.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, you summon a celestial of challenge rating 5 or lower.

Mass Healing Word.name: Mass Healing Word
Mass Healing Word.description:
As you call out words of restoration, up to six creatures of your choice that you can see within range regain hit points equal to 1d4 + your spellcasting ability modifier. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the healing increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 3rd.

Orb of Shadow.name: Orb of Shadow
Orb of Shadow.description:
An inky black orb of shadow launches from your hand toward your target. You must succeed on a spellattackwith the orb to deal damage to the target. On a hit, the orb deals 3d8 necrotic damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd or higher, you deal an additional 1d8 necrotic damage for each slot level above 1st.

Spellcrash.name: Spellcrash
Spellcrash.description:
Your touch causes a creature to form a jagged vicious scar over a wound they have taken. The process is painful, but heals 2d6 damage and imposes disadvantage on attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws. The disadvantage caused by the pain lasts for 1 minute per 5 hit points healed. If the creature is immune to pain, they are not healed.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd or higher, the healing provided is increased by 2d6 per spell level over 1st. The pain duration is increased for the amount healed.

Read Magic: 1st Path Magic 5E, © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Catastrophe.name: Catastrophe
Catastrophe.components: V, S, M (handful of earth taken from a dead world)
Catastrophe.description:
Your touch infects a creature with a dangerous infusion of the essence of death. Make a single melee spellattackagainst a creature within range. On a successful hit, the target becomes wreathed in negative energy for 1 minute. When a target so wreathed would regainhit points, the negative energy prevents the creature from regaining thosehit points, and it instead loses that manyhit points. Once the spell prevents a target from regaining 200hit pointsin this manner, the effect ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell as a tier 2 Epic spell or higher, the number ofhit pointsthe spell can prevent the target from regaining increases by 100 per tier above tier 1.

Doom of Blue Crystal.name: Doom of Blue Crystal
Doom of Blue Crystal.description:
You are surrounded by a field of glowing, blue energy lasting 3 rounds. Creatures within 5 feet of you, including yourself, must make aConstitutionsaving throw when the spell is cast and again at the start of each of your turns while the spell is in effect. A creature whose saving throw fails isrestrained; arestrainedcreature whose saving throw fails isparalyzed; and aparalyzedcreature whose saving throw fails ispetrifiedand transforms into a statue of blue crystal. As with all concentration spells, you can end the field at any time (no action required). If you are turned to crystal, the spell ends after all affected creatures make their saving throws.Restrainedandparalyzedcreatures recover immediately when the spell ends, but petrification is permanent.

Creatures turned to crystal can see, hear, and smell normally, but they don’t need to eat or breathe. Ifshatteris cast on a crystal creature, it must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw against the caster’s spell save DC or be killed.

Creatures transformed into blue crystal can be restored withdispel magic,greater restoration, or comparable magic.

Drive-Thru.name: Drive-Thru
Drive-Thru.components: V, S, M (food receipt from Revval’s Cantina)
Drive-Thru.description:
You create a small window a multidimensional cantina. For the duration, you can order food, drink, and non-magical equipment (such as armor, tools, or weapons) from the window for five times the normal cost. The cantina has access to both basic foods and lavish meals, but outlandish requests may result in the portal being closed prematurely from inside. Creatures cannot force their way into the portal, taking 1d10 force damage and being banned from ordering again if they attempt to do so. Any leftovers, containers, utensils, and dishes turn to ash 1 hour after the spell ends.

Undo Paradox.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can automatically end the effects of a spell on the target if the spell’s level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you used. Alternately, you can target one additional creature or object for each slot level above 4th.

Circle of Sounds.name: Circle of Sounds
Circle of Sounds.description:
The druids and rangers of Azoth learned to cloak the sounds of their communication among the chirps and whistles of the forest. This spell is in high demand among scouting parties and small traveling groups seeking to pass through natural areas undetected. Choose a number of creatures to whom you have line of effect within 30 feet of you who share a language with you. For the duration, you and each creature you choose can communicate verbally in your shared language, but to anyone not included in the spell your words sound like the normal, natural sounds of the local fauna. Any creature affected by this spell may choose to speak normally or speak under thecoverof the circle of sounds.

Deadpan.duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour This magic dulls the senses and allows
Deadpan.description:
This magic dulls the senses and allows you to express information in a pure and unbiased form. While under the influence of this spell, you gain advantage on all skill checks to lie or deceive others. Magical means of determining the truth have no effect on you.

Rally Point.components: V, S, M (holy symbol orfragment of a banner or flag)
Rally Point.description:
You infuse a 5-foot square you occupy or that is adjacent to you with symbols of courage and faithfulness. Any ally entering that square while the spell is active gains 5temporary hit points, and on their nextattackroll or saving throw they make before the end of their next turn they can roll a d4 and add the result to theirattackroll or saving throw. Your ally loses these benefits at the end of their next turn (after the turn in which they move through the rally point). Each ally cannot benefit from this spell more than once from the same casting of the spell.
