Mass Suggestion.name: Mass Suggestion
Mass Suggestion.components: V, M(a snake’s tongue and either a bit of honeycomb or a drop of sweet oil)
Mass Suggestion.description:
You suggest a course of activity (limited to a sentence or two) and magically influence up to twelve creatures of your choice that you can see within range and that can hear and understand you. Creatures that can’t becharmedare immune to this effect. The suggestion must be worded in such a manner as to make the course of action sound reasonable. Asking the creature to stab itself, throw itself onto a spear, immolate itself, or do some other obviously harmful act automatically negates the effect of the spell.

Each target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, it pursues the course of action you described to the best of its ability. The suggested course of action can continue for the entire duration. If the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the spell ends when the subject finishes what it was asked to do.

You can also specify conditions that will trigger a special activity during the duration. For example, you might suggest that a group of soldiers give all their money to the first beggar they meet. If the condition isn’t met before the spell ends, the activity isn’t performed.

If you or any of your companions damage a creature affected by this spell, the spell ends for that creature.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 7th-level spell slot, the duration is 10 days. When you use an 8th-level spell slot, the duration is 30 days. When you use a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is a year and a day.
Mass Suggestion.material_component: a snake’s tongue and either a bit of honeycomb or a drop of sweet oil

Necrosis.name: Necrosis
Necrosis.description:
Duration5 + spellcasting modifier rounds

NoteThis spell is a rework of the core spell of the same name.

You instill the target with a mote of necrotic energy. For an undead creature this causes them to heal 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns.

If the target is living, they instead take one necrotic damage per round at the beginning of their turn.

This spell has no effect on constructs.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, the damage healed or dealt each round increases to 2. The damage and healing further increases to 3 if you instead use a spell slot of 5th or higher.

Read Magic: Vigor (5E) © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions; Authors: Connor Bates

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Fast Cast.name: Fast Cast
Fast Cast.description:
When you cast this spell, you can cast spells that have a casting time of areactiontwice, effectively giving you two reactions that can only be used to cast spells. You can cast this reaction spell once on every creature’s turn, except your own turn. You can’t use this reaction on the same turn that you take a normal reaction.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bashing Blade.name: Bashing Blade
Bashing Blade.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,paladin,ranger

You surround the target weapon with a flickering blue halo of energy that sheds bright light within 20 feet. Regardless of which type of damage your weapon usually deals, it now deals bludgeoning damage instead. In addition, the force halo of your bashing blade adds 1d6 force damage to its normal damage. On a critical hit, it flares with a bright blue light and deals an extra 3d6 force damage instead of 1d6.

The Dragon’s Hoard #33© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Scott D. Young, Matt Kimmel, Jeff Lee, James Abendroth.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Entropic Strike.name: Entropic Strike
Entropic Strike.components: S, M (melee weapon smeared with dust or ash)
Entropic Strike.description:
Class(es):paladin,ranger,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

Wielding the weapon you used to cast this spell, make a melee weaponattackwith it against a creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the target suffers the normal effects of the attack, and it must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failure, the target suffers 1d10 force damage, and its hit point maximum is reduced by the same amount until it finishes a long rest.

At Higher Levels. This spell’s damage increases by 1d10 when you reach 5th level (2d10), 11th level (3d10), and 17th level (4d10).

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Entropic Strike.material_component: melee weapon smeared with dust or ash

Impossible Labyrinth.name: Impossible Labyrinth
Impossible Labyrinth.components: V, S, M (glove from a goblin king)
Impossible Labyrinth.description:
You generate a selective illusion of an impossibly complex labyrinth in a 120-foot cube centered on you. When you do so, you may choose any number of creatures of your choice to be immune to the effects of the spell for its duration. All other creatures in the affected area when you cast the spell must succeed on anIntelligencesaving throw or become trapped in the labyrinth, hopelessly lost, wandering its impossible corridors in a subversion of physics. While lost in this manner, a creature cannot leave its current space (even by magical means), and other creatures in the labyrinth are hidden from it (detect DC equal to your spell save DC). At the end of each of its turns, an affected creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the illusion for itself on a success. A creature with truesight has Epic advantage on saving throws against this spell.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Reign In Hell.name: Reign In Hell
Reign In Hell.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a crown worth at least 1,000 gp)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 hour

You don the crown and it begins to glow with a hellishlight. For the duration you have advantage on saving throws against fiends and their attacks have disadvantage against you. A successfulCharismasaving throw by the fiend allows them to negate this effect for 1 round.

While under the effects of this spell you are immune to thecharmedcondition imposed by fiends. Any such effects that are active on you prior to the casting of this spell are suppressed while this spell is active.

Finally, while the spell is active, all fiends start with a disposition of indifferent toward you and you gain advantage onCharisma-based skills and ability checks against them.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Merciful Gesture.name: Merciful Gesture
Merciful Gesture.description:
You make a gesture, pointing at a creature within range.

The creature is bombarded by the magical energies of unmaking and it must make oneStrength, oneDexterity, oneConstitution, oneIntelligence, oneWisdom, and oneCharismasaving throw in a row. For each failed save, the creature takes 8d10 force damage. If the creature is slain by this spell, it feels no pain in its final moments and it can’t be brought back by any means, except by the direct intervention of a deity.

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Comprehend Languages.name: Comprehend Languages
Comprehend Languages.components: V, S, M(a pinch of soot and salt)
Comprehend Languages.description:
For the duration, you understand the literal meaning of any spoken language that you hear. You also understand any written language that you see, but you must be touching the surface on which the words are written. It takes about 1 minute to read one page of text.

This spell doesn’t decode secret messages in a text or a glyph, such as an arcane sigil, that isn’t part of a written language.
Comprehend Languages.material_component: a pinch of soot and salt

Shipshape.name: Shipshape
Shipshape.description:
Classes: Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard

You touch a damaged ship or boat, magically repairing it. The vessel regains 40hit points. This spell can repair broken masts, torn sails, and breaches in the hull. The spell cannot restore a ship that has been completely destroyed or sunken.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the vessel regains an extra 10hit pointsfor each slot level above 4th.

Pirates and Plunder A Compendium For 5e © 2024 Published by Mythos Chronicles; Author Filippo Bardoscia

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Well of Frozen Missiles.name: Well of Frozen Missiles
Well of Frozen Missiles.components: V, S, M (piece of quartz carved into a snowflake)
Well of Frozen Missiles.description:
A Small, swirling cloud of ice and snow appears and hovers in an unoccupied space you can see within range.

The cloud occupies that space and emits a mild chill in the air around it, but it is otherwise indistinct except for a small flurry of snow.

When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be capable of interacting with the cloud. While within 5 feet of the cloud, a designated creature can use a bonus action to reach into the cloud, pull out a javelin of magical ice, and throw it at a target within 60 feet. The creature throwing the javelin is proficient with the javelin and makes anattackroll using itsStrengthorDexteritymodifier (the creature’s choice).

On a hit, the javelin deals 2d6 cold damage, and the target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

The cloud lasts for the duration or until six icy javelins have been pulled from it.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage dealt by the javelin on a hit increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Well of Frozen Missiles.material_component: piece of quartz carved into a snowflake

Awakened from Death.name: Awakened from Death
Awakened from Death.components: V, S, M (white shawl or prayer cloth and incense)
Awakened from Death.description:
This spell functions likeRaise Dead, but while its body is restored the target is not fully brought back to life. Its body ceases to decay, asGentle Repose, and like that spell, time spent Awakened from Death does not count against the time limit on bringing a creature back from the dead. While reanimated by this spell, the target hovers on death’s door, able to take only a singleDashaction each round and unable toattack, cast spells, or activate magic items. It can be wounded and healed, but its maximumhit pointscan never exceed 1 hit point per Hit Die it possesses. Increases to itsConstitutionscore cannot increase itshit points, though the target can benefit from effects that grant temporaryHit Points.

The target’s mind is clouded while Awakened from Death, as if feebleminded, as per the spellFeeblemind. While the target can speak, its memory is confused and disjointed, with great difficulty remembering even basic details of its past life. AHeal,Wish, orGreater Restorationspell can restore the target’s memories and intellect, but its physical state can be restored only by returning it fully to life withRaise Deador a similar effect.

The Dragon’s Hoard #55© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Tom Knauss, Darrin Drader.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Awakened from Death.material_component: white shawl or prayer cloth and incense

Sightburst.name: Sightburst
Sightburst.description:
A wave of echoing sound emanates from you. Until the start of your next turn, you have blindsight out to a range of 100 feet, and you know the location of any natural hazards within that area. You have advantage on saving throws made against hazards detected with this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 1 minute. When you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 1 hour.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Brilliant Harrier.name: Brilliant Harrier
Brilliant Harrier.description:
You create a glowing bird of flame on a point you can see within range.

The harrier bird hovers in place, shedding bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet, and it lasts for the duration or until you cast this spell again. Until this spell ends, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of the harrier makes anattackroll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use yourreactionto give that target disadvantage on that roll, as the glowing harrier swoops down to distract the target. If the roll fails, the target takes 1d4 fire damage.

The harrier has an AC equal to your spell save DC. Each time it is hit, roll a d20. On a result of 9 or less, it vanishes.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Antipathy/Sympathy.name: Antipathy/Sympathy
Antipathy/Sympathy.components: V, S, M(either a lump of alum soaked in vinegar for theantipathyeffect or a drop of honey for thesympathyeffect)
Antipathy/Sympathy.description:
This spell attracts or repels creatures of your choice. You target something within range, either a Huge or smaller object or creature or an area that is no larger than a 200-foot cube. Then specify a kind of intelligent creature, such as red dragons, goblins, or vampires. You invest the target with an aura that either attracts or repels the specified creatures for the duration. Choose antipathy or sympathy as the aura’s effect.

Antipathy: The enchantment causes creatures of the kind you designated to feel an intense urge to leave the area and avoid the target. When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomefrightened. The creature remainsfrightenedwhile it can see the target or is within 60 feet of it. Whilefrightenedby the target, the creature must use its movement to move to the nearest safe spot from which it can’t see the target. If the creature moves more than 60 feet from the target and can’t see it, the creature is no longerfrightened, but the creature becomesfrightenedagain if it regains sight of the target or moves within 60 feet of it.

Sympathy: The enchantment causes the specified creatures to feel an intense urge to approach the target while within 60 feet of it or able to see it. When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or use its movement on each of its turns to enter the area or move within reach of the target. When the creature has done so, it can’t willingly move away from the target.

If the target damages or otherwise harms an affected creature, the affected creature can make aWisdomsaving throw to end the effect, as described below.

Ending the Effect: If an affected creature ends its turn while not within 60 feet of the target or able to see it, the creature makes aWisdomsaving throw. On a successful save, the creature is no longer affected by the target and recognizes the feeling of repugnance or attraction as magical. In addition, a creature affected by the spell is allowed anotherWisdomsaving throw every 24 hours while the spell persists.

A creature that successfully saves against this effect is immune to it for 1 minute, after which time it can be affected again.
Antipathy/Sympathy.material_component: either a lump of alum soaked in vinegar for theantipathyeffect or a drop of honey for thesympathyeffect

Viridian Mark.name: Viridian Mark
Viridian Mark.components: V, S, M (handful of rotten scales)
Viridian Mark.description:
Classes: antipaladin,cleric,druid,warlock,wizard

You curse a creature within range with a flesh-witheringblightdealing 1d6 necrotic damage and 1d6 acid damage. In addition, if the target fails aConstitutionsaving throw, the area of damaged flesh becomes scaly, rough, and disfigured to a sickly green, glowing as bright as a torch of emerald flames when the creature is within 60 feet of you. A creature blighted with a viridian mark takes a -1 penalty to its AC and any saving throws against your attacks and spells.

Each day a creature remains cursed, they take damage again as above and must make aConstitutionsaving throw or have theirCharismascore permanently reduced by 1d4 due to the rotting disfigurement sapping their body, mind, and soul. If a creature’sCharismascore is reduced to 0, their flesh sloughs away entirely into corruption, leaving a harmless Tiny lizard or similar creature behind (treat as if transformed by a permanentpolymorphspell); this creature is always bright green in color.

A viridian mark cannot be dispelled butremove curseends the spell. If the creature has had theirCharismascore reduced, this returns at a rate of 2 points after each completed long rest, or immediately withgreater restoration.

You conjure a shapeless,invisibleforce that hovers around you, taking ammunition from your quiver and shooting your bow, crossbow, or sling for you. Each round you concentrate on the spell, as a bonus action you can take an extra ranged weaponattack. Thisattackuses your normalattackanddamage rolls, including bonuses for spells affecting you and your combat style. There must be ammunition for the bow spirit to use, and it expends ammunition normally. It can use magical arrows or other special ammunition if you command it to do so.

The bow spirit occupies your space and moves with you, but it can’t be harmed by attacks. It can be dispelled, and if your concentration is broken the spell ends.

Bottomless Pit.duration: of the spell, the creatures in the pit are shunted back out of the extradimensional are
Bottomless Pit.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a miniature shovel costing 10 gp)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

This spell creates a 10-ft.-by-10-ft. bottomless pit so the creatures that fall into the pit, fall until the end of the duration or they find some other means of stopping a fall. A creature in the area or adjacent to the pit must make aDexteritysaving throw or fall in. A creature that subsequently moves up to or into the pit must also make the saving throw.

If the creature canfly, they are immune to this spell’s effects as long as they make aDexteritysaving throw.

Each round such a flying creature can reattempt theDexteritysaving throw to catch themselves. On their turn, a falling creature can attempt tocast a spellif they have the ability, however, the creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw of DC 10 or half of 6d6, whichever is higher. The walls of the pit are difficult to get a hold of and falling creatures must make a DC 22Athleticscheck to stop their fall, and the sameAthleticsDC to climb up its sides.

Each full round spent falling in the extradimensional pit counts as 60 feet. If the creature is able toflyorlevitate, they must move the total distance they fell before they can leave the pit. If a creature moves up to the Bottomless Pit and fails aDexteritysaving throw, they deduct their previous movement from the 60 feet maximum fall during the turn, to a minimum of 10 feet.

Retrieving and using items is very difficult while falling in the pit. Any creature attempting to retrieve and use an item, like a potion or a scroll, must make aDexteritysaving throw or drop the item. They can attempt the sameDexteritysaving throw each round on their turn to grab the item out of the air next to them. At the end of the spell’s duration, falling items do not take damage.

At the end of the duration of the spell, the creatures in the pit are shunted back out of the extradimensional area taking 1d6 damage per 10 feet from the top of the pit, to a maximum of 10d6. Effects like amonk’sslowfall orFeather Falldo not negate this damage but such creatures only fall 30 feet per full round and have advantage on their saving throws while within the pit.

Mark of Implacable Hunting.name: Mark of Implacable Hunting
Mark of Implacable Hunting.description:
You mark a target as your quarry. As long as the target is on the same plane, you know the distance and direction the creature is in relation to you. You also know if it is moving and if so, in what direction. You gain advantage toPerceptionchecks to notice the target if it is usingStealthor recognize it if it is disguised. If the target succeeds on their saving throw, this spell instead acts as the spell tracking mark except its duration is 1 hour per level.

If you have cast this spell on a target within the last 24 hours, you can cast it on the same target, regardless of range, so long as they are still on the same plane.

Plague Walk.name: Plague Walk
Plague Walk.description:
You conjure a trail of sickly, yellowish-green miasma that follows in your footsteps and lingers on your trail. This miasma is visible as a mist hovering in each space you leave. The mist remains in each of those spaces, forming a trail behind you, for 10 minutes before fading. The mist forms only along the ground and doesn’t form in spaces you left by flying, swimming, or similarly not in contact with the ground.

A creature that enters the miasma for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed aConstitutionsaving throw or take 2d8 poison damage and bepoisonedfor 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, apoisonedcreature can make anotherConstitutionsaving throw, ending thepoisonedcondition on itself on a success.

Nonmagical plants that aren’t creatures, such as trees and shrubs, wither and die in the miasma in your wake.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the miasma lasts for an additional 10 minutes for each slot level above 3rd.

Water Breathing.description: This spell grants up to ten willing creatures you can see within range the ability to breathe underwater until the spell ends. Affected creatures also retain their normal mode of respiration.
Water Breathing.material_component: a short reed or piece of straw

Blistering Radiance.name: Blistering Radiance
Blistering Radiance.description:
You hurl a coruscating ball of light to any point within range, where it erupts into a 50-foot-radius sphere of intense light and heat. Each round at the beginning of their turn (or upon entering the area of blistering radiance, if they enter the area during their turn) all creatures within the area take 1d6 fire damage and 1d6 radiance damage and must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failure, they take a -1 penalty onattackrolls and have disadvantage onWisdom(Perception) checks based on vision due to the intense glare. Undead,fungi, oozes, and creatures that have light sensitivity take double damage from this spell and have disadvantage on their saving throw.

If there is a magicaldarknessspell in the area of blistering radiance, it is immediately dispelled if that spell is 3rd level or lower. Such spells are negated without effect if cast into the area of blistering radiance. If higher level darkness spells are present, as a bonus action you can make an ability check using your spellcasting ability modifier with a DC of 10 plus the level of the spell. If you succeed on the check, that darkness spell ends as if you had castdispel magic. If the check fails, you can make additional checks in future rounds to continue trying todispelthe darkness. As long as such magicaldarknesspersists, creatures within it are unaffected by the blistering radiance.

Ley Chain.name: Ley Chain
Ley Chain.description:
You create tendrils of ley energy that burst from the ground and wrap around a Large or smaller creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or berestrainedby the ley energy.

At the end of each of its turns, the target can make aStrengthsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

Exorcise.name: Exorcise
Exorcise.description:
By casting this spell, you can negate possession of a creature or object by any force, whether creature (aghost, for example) or magic (a spellcaster usingmagic jaror a spirit trapped using the binding spell, for example). When you cast this spell, the creature inhabiting the object or body must succeed at aWisdomsaving throw or be forcibly ejected from the host. An ejected creature isstunneduntil the end of its next turn. This spell can be cast on alich’s phylactery or the soul object of an ancient vampire. If the creature currently inhabits its phylactery or soul object, it is immediately ejected and possesses the closest material body (which could very well be yours). A creature so inhabited (possessed) is affected as if bymagic jar. If holy water is sprinkled on the object or creature during the casting of this spell, the save DC is increased by +2.

Call of the Ancients.name: Call of the Ancients
Call of the Ancients.description:
Classes: Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You call forth a being of immense power from across the planes, compelling it to serve you.

Choose a specific creature with a Challenge Rating of 30 or lower whose true name you know. This creature must be a unique, named entity, such as an ancient dragon, archfiend, or celestial, which appears in an unoccupied space you can see.

Upon its arrival, the target is bound to your will for the duration of the spell, compelled to follow your commands. The creature acts on yourinitiativeorder, obeying any command you issue to it (no action required by you).

The summoned creature retains its intelligence, personality, and alignment. If commanded to act against its deeply held beliefs or to face certain destruction, the creature can make aCharismasaving throw. On a successful save, the creature breaks free from your control, becoming hostile towards you and your allies.

Summoning a being of such immense power is not an act that goes unnoticed in the multiverse. The arrival of a powerful entity can send ripples across the planes, drawing the attention of other beings of similar or even greater strength. Allies of the summoned creature, whether they be other powerful entities, ancient beings, or entire factions aligned with its goals, may view this act as a provocation or an opportunity to intervene. They might attempt to free the summoned being, rallying forces to launch a rescue mission or enact retribution against the summoner.

When the spell ends, the creature itself is likely to seek vengeance for the binding. The memory of being summoned and forced to act against its will does not fade easily. Freed from the magical compulsion, the creature might harbor a deep resentment and anger towards the summoner. This enmity could lead the creature to use its vast powers to track them down, exacting retribution that could range from subtle and insidious sabotage to outright destruction.

In some cases, the summoning of such a powerful being might even draw the attention of deities, who may see the summoner as a threat to the cosmic balance or as a tool to be manipulated for their own ends. Divine retribution, celestial negotiations, or infernal bargains could all result from this single act of summoning, as the forces unleashed by the caster may spiral beyond their control.

You create a globe of vile cold that explodes in the area dealing 6d8 cold damage and 6d4 necrotic damage. A successfulDexteritysave halves this damage.

Additionally, the burst of darkness snuffs out any non-magical light sources (exceptdaylight) and dispels any magicallightwith a spell level of 5th level or lower.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the base damage increases by 1d8 cold and 1d4 necrotic for each slot level above 7th.

Compassionate Ally.name: Compassionate Ally
Compassionate Ally.description:
The target is filled with pity and the urge tohelpwhen they see an ally in distress. If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw and there is an injured ally visible, it immediately disengages from its current course of action (potentially provoking opportunity attacks if enemies are nearby) to provideaidto that ally, or the nearest ally if several are nearby.

It can use curative spells or magic items toaidthat ally; if they do not possess such magic, they attempt aWisdom(Medicine) check against the save DC of the spell. The target has disadvantage on this check if the ally it is helping is currently in combat. The target remains adjacent to their injured ally to assure their safety and continue treating their wounds, attempting to assist them each round until the spell ends or until the ally’s damage is completely removed. If the target is attacked while following this compulsion, they can defend themselves normally andattackback against any creature that has attacked them.

Devouring Darkness.name: Devouring Darkness
Devouring Darkness.description:
Terrifying and nightmarish monsters exist within the unknown void of the in-between. Choose up to six points you can see within range. Voidlike, magicaldarknessspreads from each point to fill a 10-footradius sphere for the duration. The darkness spreads around corners. A creature withdarkvisioncan’t see through this darkness, and no light, magical or nonmagical, can illuminate it.

Each creature inside a sphere when this spell is cast must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 6d10 piercing damage and 5d6 psychic damage and isrestraineduntil it breaks free as unseen entities bite and tear at it from the Void.

Once a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’trestrained. Arestrainedcreature can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longerrestrained. When a creature enters a sphere for the first time on a turn or starts its turn in a sphere, that creature must make anIntelligencesaving throw. The creature takes 5d6 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Once created, the spheres can’t be moved. A creature in overlapping spheres doesn’t suffer additional effects for being in more than one sphere at a time.

You touch a living creature and send a jolt of psychic information flooding into their mind. You must succeed at a melee spellattackto affect the target. The target takes 10d8 mental damage on a failedWisdomsaving throw and half as much on a successful one. On a failed save, the target gains two levels ofexhaustion, to a maximum of 2.

You grant machinelike stamina to a creature you touch.

For the duration of the spell, the target requires no food or drink or rest. It can move at three times its normal speed overland and perform three times the usual amount of labor. The target is not protected from fatigue orexhaustioncaused by a magical effect.

Eyebite.name: Eyebite
Eyebite.description:
For the spell’s duration, your eyes become an inky void imbued with dread power. One creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that you can see must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be affected by one of the following effects of your choice for the duration. On each of your turns until the spell ends, you can use your action to target another creature but can’t target a creature again if it has succeeded on a saving throw against this casting ofeyebite.

Asleep: The target falls unconscious. It wakes up if it takes any damage or if another creature uses its action to shake the sleeper awake.

Panicked: The target isfrightenedof you. On each of its turns, thefrightenedcreature must take the Dash action and move away from you by the safest and shortest available route, unless there is nowhere to move. If the target moves to a place at least 60 feet away from you where it can no longer see you, this effect ends.

Sickened: The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. At the end of each of its turns, it can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. If it succeeds, the effect ends.

Paralyzing Strike.name: Paralyzing Strike
Paralyzing Strike.description:
Choose a creature that you successfully damaged with a sneak attack this round. That target must make aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails the saving throw, the target isparalyzedfor the duration. This spell has no effect on undead. At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends for that target.

You can shift and alter existing darkness and shadow, whether natural or magical. You can cause one of the following effects:

You can only have one effect operating at a time but you can switch between them as a free action once per round. The chosen effect covers the entire affected area. When the spell expires all shadows and darkness reverts to their original light levels and locations.

Dream Preparation.name: Dream Preparation
Dream Preparation.duration: 1 day or until expended Dreaming Descriptor Spells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest.
Dream Preparation.description:
Dreaming DescriptorSpells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest. You must have the spell slots needed to do so when you go to sleep, but the same slots are also expended when you wake—you cannot regain them for use the next day. You cannot cast more than 8 spell-levels worth of dreaming spells in a single night. These spells generally have casting times of hours, but those are hours during which you are asleep. Regardless of how long you sleep, you cannot cast more than 8 hours worth of dreaming spells in one 24-hour period. Dreaming spells with a duration of “1 day or until expended” also end if you sleep for 1 hour or more before they are expended.

You dream of a magic academy, where you are taught tocast a spellyou normally cannot. You select one spell you are aware of to prepare in your dream. If the spell is one available to your class, it must be at least 1 spell level lower than the spell slot you use for dream preparation. If it is from a different class, it must be at least 3 spell levels lower than the spell slot you use for dream preparation. You can cast the selected spell once over the next 24 hours without expending an additional spell slot. You must meet any other requirements to cast the spell (such as casting time, any expensive material required, and so on). While the spell acts normally for those that believe in it, it is only quasireal. Any target of the spell is allowed aWisdomsaving throw in addition to any other saving throws the spell allows. On a successful save, the target completely ignores the spell (even if the spell has effects that do not normally allow saves – if you created a physical object with the spell and a target made the initialWisdomsave, that object does not exist for them). If the spell itself allows a save (even anotherWisdomsave), any target is allowed to make that as well.

A spell with a duration of instantaneous or permanent has any ongoing effects end when you nextsleepfor 1 or more hours, or 24 hours later, whichever comes first.

At Higher Levels: You can cast this spell using a higher-level spell slot in order to prepare more powerfuldreamspells.

A green ray of light springs from the caster’s hand toward a creature within range. The target must make a Reflex Saving Throw. On failure, the target is subject to redirection any time they attempt toteleportor use any form of extradimensional movement. Instead of their destination, they appear in a random desert or wasteland, far from civilization, and subject to extreme heat conditions. This could be somewhere hundreds of miles away, on the same continent, or if a suitable location is not closer, somewhere in the same plane of existence. The target may make aWisdomsaving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell for that creature on a Success.

You curse the target with a thirst no drink can quench. If the target fails aConstitutionsaving throw, it immediately gains one level ofexhaustion, as though it had spent an entire day without water. Each day thereafter, the target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or gain another level ofexhaustionfrom their parching thirst.

If you hit, the target takes 8d6 fire damage, or half as much on a successfulDexteritysaving throw. You sense the presence of water within range whenever you concentrate. If you remain still until your next turn, as anActionyou and focus the spell to determine the number of water sources within range and the approximatesizeof the largest: Tiny (pool up to 4 feet wide, stream up to 1 foot across), Small (20-foot pool or 5-foot stream), Medium (200-foot pond or 20-foot stream), Large (lake more than square mile or river less than a mile wide), Huge (lake more than 100 square miles or river over a mile wide), or Vast (ocean or inland sea).

You target a weapon on the target creature that is currently sheathed, slung, or otherwise stowed and not being wielded.

If the target fails aStrengthsaving throw, that weapon is locked in place and cannot be drawn, readied, or wielded unless the target creature takes an action to make aStrengthcheck against the spell’s save DC. For the duration, as a bonus action orreaction, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature within reach. Spear of Yggdrasil.description:

On a failed save, the target takes 4d6 piercing damage and isrestrainedby being impaled on the root. A successful save deals half the damage and the target is notrestrained.

Unluck On That.name: Unluck On That
Unluck On That.description:
By uttering a swift curse (“Unluck on that!”), you bring misfortune to the target’s attempt; the affected creature has disadvantage on the roll.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the range of the spell increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 1st.

Deep Magic for 5th Edition(c) 2020 Open Design LLC; Authors: Dan Dillon, Chris Harris, and Jeff Lee.

Wind Compass.name: Wind Compass
Wind Compass.description:
You create a tiny moaning wind that is tied to a specific compass direction. As long as you continue moving in that direction, the wind compass sighs contentedly in your ear to tell you so. If you diverge from that direction, the wind compass begins to moan with rising and falling pitch in proportion to how far you have veered from your intended course. As long as it persists, you can maintain an accurate heading. A wind compass does not necessarily help you find a specific destination, but it does grant you advantage onWisdom(Survival) checks to avoid getting lost along the way. This spell does not function underwater or in areas that otherwise lack air, and you cannot benefit from it if you aredeafened.

Solar Flare.name: Solar Flare
Solar Flare.description:
With a snap of your fingers, a miniature sunburst erupts at a point you can see within range. Each creature within a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 4d6 radiant damage and 4d6 fire damage, and isblindeduntil the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half damage and is notblinded.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the radius of the sphere created by this spell increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 4th.

Warped Weapons.name: Warped Weapons
Warped Weapons.components: V, S, M (bit of the item you wish to mimic)
Warped Weapons.description:
You target a non-magical weapon that a creature wields, creating the illusion that the weapon is made of snakes, bugs, or some other unsettling creation. The creature possessing the weapon must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or rid themselves of the weapon for the duration of the spell. This spell cannot be used to target natural weapons, such as fangs or claws.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one magical weapon or three non-magical weapons.

Cloud of Hept-na.name: Cloud of Hept-na
Cloud of Hept-na.description:
You create a 20-foot-radius sphere of sooty fog centered on a point you choose within range. The fog spreads around corners, and its area is heavily obscured. The fog lingers in the air for the duration.

If a creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw, losing 1d3 points ofWisdomon a failed save. Creatures are affected even if they hold their breath or don’t need to breathe. LostWisdomis regained at a rate of 1 point per hour after the creature leaves the area of effect.

The fog moves 10 feet away from you at the start of each of your turns, rolling along the surface of the ground. The vapors, being heavier than air, sink to the lowest level of the land, even pouring down openings. It cannot penetrate liquids and cannot be cast underwater.

A moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses the fog after four rounds. A strong wind (at least 20 miles per hour) disperses it after one round.

Daybreak Arrow.name: Daybreak Arrow
Daybreak Arrow.description:
You touch up to 20 pieces of ammunition, causing them to erupt in a blaze of light when they strike. Each arrow, bolt, sling bullet, or other piece of ammunition deals 1d6 radiant damage on a hit, in addition to any other damage. In addition, each daybreak arrow creates an area ofdaylight(as the spell) that lasts for 1 round when it hits, centered on the target struck. You can target an object if you just wish to create light in an area. Each piece of ammunition can be used only once.

The Dragon’s Hoard #22© 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Eyes of the Void.name: Eyes of the Void
Eyes of the Void.components: V, S, M (pinch of dried carrot or an agate)
Eyes of the Void.description:
For the duration, you can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

Lands of Theia - 5th Edition© 2024, Samurai Sheepdog; Authors: Steven Rasheed James, Kevin Glusing

Halo of Spines.name: Halo of Spines
Halo of Spines.components: V, M (crown of spines worth at least 25 gp)
Halo of Spines.duration: of the spell, the crown turns into an intangible halo that floats above the
Halo of Spines.description:
You place the crown upon the head of a willing creature. For the duration of the spell, the crown turns into an intangible halo that floats above the target’s head. The halo sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius. Whenever the target is dealt damage by another creature it can see, the target can use itsreactionto inflict 1d4 piercing damage on the creature that dealt the damage. You can end the spell by using your action to dismiss it while you can see the target. The target can also end the spell by using its action to grab the halo from above its head.

If you harvest a ring of spikes from a cacodaemon (worth 250 gp; harvest DC 10 for 1, 15 for 2, 20 for 3), use it as the spell’s material component, and allow the spell to consume it, you can choose cold, fire, or lightning when you cast the spell. The spell deals damage of that type instead of piercing.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d4 for every slot level above 1st.

Summoner’s Call.name: Summoner’s Call
Summoner’s Call.description:
Youteleportyour Summon to an unoccupied space you can see within range. Your Summon must be within range both before and after theteleport.

Combust The Dead.name: Combust The Dead
Combust The Dead.description:
You fill the body of one Medium or smaller dead creature you can see within range with fiery magic, causing it to explode in a burst of flame and bony shrapnel. Each creature within 10 feet of the body must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 1d8 fire damage and 2d8 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

A body can be targeted by this spell only once. If the target body was dead for more than one week, the body is completely destroyed, and the creature can be restored to life only by means of atrue resurrectionor awishspell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the fire damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

Inflict Pain.name: Inflict Pain
Inflict Pain.description:
You overload the target’s mind with pain, causing it to believe they are in immense bodily and mental pain and stress.

The target takes disadvantage on attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, the target is unable to perform any action other than move for the duration due to the pain.

Read Magic: 1st Path Magic 5E, © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Vital Contract.name: Vital Contract
Vital Contract.description:
This spell creates a binding agreement between two individuals with dire consequences if broken.

To prepare for casting this spell, you must first produce a written contract on any surface in a language both parties can understand. For the spell to take effect, both parties must read and fully understand the contents and intent of the contract. Any wordplay or miscommunication, intentional or not, will result in spell failure.

Once the contract is understood, the parties must then sign the document with either their name or mark. They cannot be forced or coerced into signing. Once this is complete, the spell is cast and the magic takes effect. If either party breaks the terms of the contract, the offending individual must make a DC 30Charismasaving throw. On a failure, they immediately die and their soul is transported to a realm of tortured liars. They may only be revived by the spellstrue resurrectionorwish. On a success, their body begins to wither away and they gain 1 level ofexhaustionevery 8 hours. The only way to stop receiving levels ofexhaustionare the spellsGreater RestorationorWish.

5E: Age of Antiquity Adventure and Intrigue in the Ancient World © 2019 Aruzian Publishing, Stephen Delucchi, Marcus Lundin

Faithful Hound.name: Faithful Hound
Faithful Hound.components: V, S, M(a tiny silver whistle, a piece of bone, and a thread)
Faithful Hound.description:
You conjure a phantom watchdog in an unoccupied space that you can see within range, where it remains for the duration, until you dismiss it as an action, or until you move more than 100 feet away from it.

The hound is invisible to all creatures except you and can’t be harmed. When a Small or larger creature comes within 30 feet of it without first speaking the password that you specify when you cast this spell, the hound starts barking loudly. The hound sees invisible creatures and can see into the Ethereal Plane. It ignores illusions.

At the start of each of your turns, the hound attempts to bite one creature within 5 feet of it that is hostile to you. The hound’s attack bonus is equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a hit, it deals 4d8 piercing damage.
Faithful Hound.material_component: a tiny silver whistle, a piece of bone, and a thread

Toll the Dead.name: Toll the Dead
Toll the Dead.description:
You point at a creature you choose and a tolling bell sounds in the distance. The target takes 1d8 necrotic damage (1d12 if it is missing any of itshit points) unless it succeeds on aWisdomsaving throw. The spell’s damage increases by one die when you reach 5th level (2d8/2d12), 11th level (3d8/3d12), and 17th level (4d8/4d12).

Latin American Monsters (5E)© 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Miguel Colon, Ismael Alvarez, Robert J. Grady, Jason Nelson.

Triplicate.name: Triplicate
Triplicate.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself, which you can use as the origin point for your spells, appear at unoccupied points you can see within range. Neither you nor the duplicate can occupy the same space. The duplicates last for the duration or until you cast this spell again, cast another spell that creates duplicates of yourself (such asmirror image), or use an action to dismiss the illusory duplicates. The duplicates imitate youractionsbut remain stationary. As a bonus action onyour turn, you can move one of your duplicates up to 20 feet. A duplicate more than 60 feet away from you is immediately destroyed. Creatures who see you when you cast this spell can track your position unless you conceal your exact location afterward. Otherwise, a creature who examines a duplicate can determine it is a duplicate with a successfulIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC. A duplicate’s AC equals 10 + yourDexteritymodifier. If an attack hits a duplicate, the duplicate is destroyed. A duplicate can be destroyed only by an attack that hits it. It ignores all other damage and effects. The spell ends when all three duplicates are destroyed. When youcast a spell, you can designate one of your duplicates as another spell’s point of origin, treating it as if it were yourself when determining range, available targets, and its spellattackroll. Weaponattackrolls made by a duplicate automatically miss. You must be able to see the duplicate as well as any targets and areas the other spell affects. If you cannot do so, the other spell fails and is lost.

Adventures in Tehuatl, © 2020, Frog God Games; Authors Tom Knauss, Tim Hitchcock, and Rob Manning

Reloading Hands.name: Reloading Hands
Reloading Hands.description:
You create a pair of phantom hands that help reload the touched ranged weapon with conjured phantom ammunition. Because the reloading hands do the work of reloading the weapon, you are not limited to a singleattackeach round when using a ranged weapon with the loading property, such as a crossbow or firearm; you can make as many attacks as you could normally make.

This ammunition created by this spell counts as magical for the purpose of the target’s resistances but otherwise is normal ammunition of its type. The conjured ammunition disappears 1 round after it is removed from the weapon or when the reloading hands expire, whichever comes first.

The Dragon’s Hoard #22© 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Wall of Portals.name: Wall of Portals
Wall of Portals.description:
Classes: bard, sorcerer, warlock, wizard

You conjure a wall made from dozens of doors, windows, and similar openings all fused together. The wall is 6 inches thick and is composed of up to twenty 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with at least one other panel, but you can otherwise choose the shape. The wall need not be supported by a solid surface and can even hang magically in midair. If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (your choice).

You and up to six creatures you designate when you cast the spell can open a door and step through it, emerging from any other door on either side of the wall. A creature other than one you designate can attempt to do the same, though they must make anIntelligencesaving throw as they pass through the door. On a successful save, it travels to the door of its choice. On a failure, it travels to a door of your choice on either side of the wall. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is instead transported to a random plane of existence.

Each panel of the wall has AC 13 and 90hit points, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage. Reducing a panel to0 hit pointsdestroys it.

A creature that damages the wall or attempts to climb it must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failure, the creature is teleported 1d20 × 10 feet in a random direction (arriving in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied).

Frailform.name: Frailform
Frailform.components: V, S, M (mummified heart encased in amber, worth at least 1,500 gp)
Frailform.description:
You blast a creature within range with a beam of pure, entropic energy that ages it rapidly. The target takes 4d6 necrotic damage and must make a successfulConstitutionsaving throw; on a failure, itsStrengthandDexterityare both reduced to 1. While itsStrengthandDexterityare reduced in this way, the creature can’t hold weapons weighing more than 3 pounds, its speed is halved, and it can’t takereactions. The creature’s Armor Class andattackrolls are modified to account for its reduced attributes.

The creature can cast spells normally.

An affected creature can repeat the saving throw after it finishes a long rest, ending the effect on a success. The effect can also be ended bygreater restoration,wish, or comparable magic.

Animate Blades.name: Animate Blades
Animate Blades.description:
You animate a number of unattended objects, causing them tolevitatein the air and strike at targets you designate of their own accord. Each object must weigh 10 pounds or less, and you can animate a number of objects equal to 2 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

When you cast the spell you can move each controlled object up to 50 feet and make one attack with it. You can concentrate multiple objects on one target or divide the objects among multiple targets.

Weapons you control strike with an attack bonus equal to your spellcasting ability plus your level bonus, and deal normal damage (for example, a dagger strikes for 1d4 piercing damage). Improvised weapons such as fist-sized stones, heavy branches, or even sturdy bottles deal 1d4 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage as appropriate. If you roll a natural 1 when attacking with a weapon or object in this manner, that object is “dropped” and you can no longer control it with this spell.

As a bonus action in subsequent turns, you can cause the animated objects to move and attack again.

The most common use of animate blade is to animate the daggers and swords of fallen warriors found on a battlefield or in a crypt; hence the name. However, the magic of the spell does not discriminate between blades, cudgels, rocks, or other potential weapons of the right size.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, increase the number of objects you animate by 2 for each slot level above 3rd.

Angry Mob.name: Angry Mob
Angry Mob.components: V, S, M (bit of fleece and shoe leather)
Angry Mob.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a bit of fleece and shoe leather)

DurationConcentration, up to 10 minutes

Classesbard,cleric,warlock,wizard

You create a stationary crowd of illusory commoners of any humanoid race desired, similar in most respects tomajor image. You can generally shape their nondescript appearance, but they cannot be made to resemble any specific individual(s). The angry mob threatens and menaces creatures within, shouting and muttering unintelligibly while brandishing fists and cudgels. Unlike amajor image, however, the angry mob has limited substance and impedes vision and movement like an actual crowd. The area it fills is lightly obscured, and any creature within the angry mob that has not disbelieved the illusion treats the area asdifficult terrainand has disadvantage onDexterity(Acrobatics) checks.

Creatures that have not disbelieved the illusion that are within the angry mob take a -1 penalty to AC due to being jostled about by shadowy forces. In addition, you can use your bonus action to Shove a creature that has not disbelieved and is within or adjacent to the angry mob. You must make anIntelligence(Arcana) check with disadvantage, and the target can make aStrength(Athletics) orDexterity(Acrobatics) check to resist being shoved. As long as you are within or adjacent to the angry mob, you have advantage onCharisma(Intimidation) checks against any creature that has not disbelieved the illusion.

The Dragon’s Hoard #31© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, James-Levi Cooke.

Rage Against Death.name: Rage Against Death
Rage Against Death.components: V, S, M (drop of your blood)
Rage Against Death.description:
When an ally within range that you can see drops to0 hit points, as areactionyou can spend 1 point of ki to cast this spell. You can cast this spell on yourself if you are about to drop to0 hit points. The target instead drops to 1 hit point and any ongoing damage ends. In addition, the target gains a +1 bonus toattackanddamage rolls, but takes a -2 penalty to AC. In addition, every time the target hits with amelee attackit gains 1 temporary hit point.

The Dragon’s Hoard #27 © 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

Earthen Trap.name: Earthen Trap
Earthen Trap.components: V, S, M (piece of a stalactite)
Earthen Trap.description:
A mass of sharp rocks erupts from the ground in a 20-foot radius centered on a point you choose within range. The jagged rocks close on each other like the jaws of a giantbeartrap. Each creature in that area must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 2d10 piercing damage and 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Creatures that failed the save are also partially buried in the earth and arerestrained. They can free themselves with aStrengthsaving throw made against your spell DC. Additionally, the ground in the area becomesdifficult terrainuntil cleared. Each 5-foot square section of the area requires at least 1 minute to clear by hand.

Flicker.name: Flicker
Flicker.description:
You interrupt electrical currents and signals in a 30-footsphere. Electronic machines are turned off and equipment dependent on electricity to operate lose power, regardless of whether that power comes from an outside source or an internal battery, power cell, or similar power supply. Magic items that deal lightning damage or create any other kind of electricity effect cease functioning and any spell that uses lightning or electricity descriptor is suppressed (see below). Sentient creatures and objects can attempt to reactivate themselves, an object they are wearing or wielding, or a device they are operating once per round by attempting aConstitutionsaving throw; however, even if successful a new save is required every round thereafter to keep the object or ability functioning. During any round in which the save is failed, the object or ability once again cease functioning.

Creating a lightning effect within the flicker is difficult. Such effects are suppressed within the area unless the caster succeeds on a saving throw using their casting ability score. If the effect affects an area or multiple targets, some of whom are inside and some outside the flicker, those outside its area are affected normally.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, increase the radius of effect by 10 feet per spell slot used above 4th.

Legendary Planet Adventure Path (5E)© 2020, Legendary Games; Authors: Authors: Matt Goodall, Jim Groves, Steven T. Helt, Tim Hitchcock, Jason Nelson, Richard Pett, Tom Phillips, Mike Shel, Neil Spicer, Mike D. Welham.

Sewer Swarm.name: Sewer Swarm
Sewer Swarm.components: V, S, M (sewer, cesspool, midden pit, or area containing at least a ton of filth)
Sewer Swarm.description:
You awaken the spark of life within a pile of putrescent refuse, creating a trio ofotyughsto serve your will. These otyughs are friendly to you and your companions for up to 1 hour. In combat, rollinitiativefor theotyughs, which act together on one turn (separately fromyour turn). They communicate with you telepathically, and if you are not fluent in their language can still be given basic commands by visualizing where you want them to go or creatures you want them toattack.

If you can speak Otyugh, you can bargain with them to perform a service that is simple enough for them to understand. If the service is simply to guard a location, they will serve you in this way for up to 1 month. Other tasks they will perform for up to 24 hours. Once the duration of the spell expires, or when they are reduced to0 hit points, theseotyughscollapse back into the offal and refuse from which they were formed. If you cast this spell while you already have an active sewer swarm, the oldotyughsimmediately perish when the new ones are created.

The Dragon’s Hoard #34© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Ismael Alvarez, Miguel Colon, Jeff Lee, Michael Mifsud.

Ice Shards.name: Ice Shards
Ice Shards.components: V, S, M (waterskin’s worth of water)
Ice Shards.description:
An ice shard appears and dances around you, granting you a +1 bonus to your AC. You may launch the ice shard as a ranged spellattackat a target you can see within 30 feet, dealing 1d6 cold damage on a successful hit.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you create an extra ice shard for each slot level above 2nd. Your AC increases by +1 for each shard you have active and you may make ranged spell attacks with any or all of the shards at the same time.

Frostlands of Fenrilik © 2020 Travis Legge

Doom of Laughter.name: Doom of Laughter
Doom of Laughter.description:
All creatures within range (including you) perceive everything as hilariously funny and fall into fits of laughter if this spell affects them. The targets must make aWisdomsaving throw.

You must also make this save. On a failed save, targets fallprone, becomingincapacitatedand unable to stand up for the duration. Creatures with anIntelligencescore of 4 or less are not affected. At the end of each of its turns, and each time it takes damage, a target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. The target has advantage on the saving throw if it’s triggered by damage. On a success, the spell’s effect ends.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Divine Interdiction.name: Divine Interdiction
Divine Interdiction.description:
You create a void of divine power in a 10-foot sphere centered on a point you designate. Any creature within the area that attempts to use Channel Divinity or cast a Cleric or Paladin spell must make aCharismasaving throw or the attempt fails but the use or spell slot is expended.

At Higher Levels. Using a 3rd-level slot or higher, the radius of the sphere increases by 5 feet for each spell slot level used above 2nd.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Ambush.name: Ambush
Ambush.components: S, M(a raven’s feather or a bit of panther fur)
Ambush.description:
The forest floor swirls and shifts around you to welcome you into its embrace. While in a forest, you have advantage onDexterity(Stealth) checks toHide.

While hidden in a forest, you have advantage on your nextInitiativecheck. The spell ends if youattackorcast a spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can affect one additional creature for each slot level above 1st. The spell ends if you or any target of this spell attacks or casts a spell.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Guilty Feet.name: Guilty Feet
Guilty Feet.description:
You target a creature and disrupt their natural movement rhythm. The target must succeed on aWisdomthrow or be affected by this spell for the duration. On a failure, their movement speed is halved, they lose any bonuses to their AC or attacks fromDexterity, they have disadvantage on anyDexteritychecks or saving throws, and anyPerformancechecks are made with disadvantage. If they are ondifficult terrain, their movement speed is reduced to 0. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the spell on a success.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Acid Storm.name: Acid Storm
Acid Storm.description:
You create a storm of gelatinous acid rain that covers a 10-foot-radius circle centered on a point within range. All creatures within the area are coated in corrosive acid. The acid can be neutralized by vinegar, wine, or a successfuldispel magic.

The acid storm becomes more damaging as time goes on. A creature that starts its turn within the area or enters the area for the first time on its turn must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On the first round, a creature that fails takes 1d4 acid damage, 1d6 acid damage on the second round, and 2d8 acid damage on the third and subsequent rounds. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw takes half this damage. If the target uses an action to cleanse itself of the acid, the progression begins again.

Tome of Alchemy, © 2020, Necromancer Games; Author Courtney Campbell, Matt Finch

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Oathbound Implement.name: Oathbound Implement
Oathbound Implement.description:
You place a magical oath upon a creature you can see within range, compelling it to complete a specific task or service that involves using a weapon as you decide.

If the creature can understand you, it must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or become bound by the task. When acting to complete the directed task, the target has advantage on the firstattackroll it makes on each of its turns using a weapon. If the target attempts to use a weapon for a purpose other than completing the specific task or service, it has disadvantage onattackrolls with a weapon and must roll the weapon’s damage dice twice, using the lower total.

Completing the task ends the spell early. Should you issue a suicidal task, the spell ends. You can end the spell early by using an action to dismiss it. Aremove curse,greater restoration, orwishspell also ends it.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Festering Fever.name: Festering Fever
Festering Fever.components: V, S, M (stone soaked in vinegar)
Festering Fever.description:
You infect a creature you can see within range with a magical, transmissible disease. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 4d8 necrotic damage and be infected with the disease. At the start of the target’s next turn, the disease ends on the target and moves to a creature hostile to you within 10 feet of the target. The new target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 3d8 necrotic damage and be infected with the disease. The disease continues moving from target to target in this way, reducing the amount of necrotic damage by 1d8 each time the disease moves to a new target. On a failed save, the final target takes 1d8 necrotic damage and this spell ends. If a target succeeds on aConstitutionsaving throw, it takes half the damage, and the disease doesn’t jump to a new target, ending the spell. A creature can take damage from this spell only once per casting of this spell.

You fire a beam of necrotic energy into a target causing their internal organs to burst one at a time. Then, at the beginning of each of your turns the creature takes and additional 3d6 necrotic damage and becomes poisoned for one round. Holy energy radiates from you as your speak your sacred oaths. The threads of Vaya become distorted within a 30-foot radius centered on you. The sphere moves with you. Stepping Stones.description:
When crossing a body of water, you make stepping stones rise up out of the water, as long as there is the space to do it. Each stone is wide enough and strong enough for a Mediumsizecreature to stand on it.

Ancestral Perversion.duration: of the spell. After failing its saving throw, at the end of each of its turns the creature makes
Ancestral Perversion.description:
Reaching back through time, you choose a creature you can see within range and call up from the ground ghastly visions of their loved ones. These wailing, malice-filled spirits are visible to all creatures. The target and all creatures within 30 feet of it must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save the target is swarmed by the twisted forms of those they hold dear, taking 3d10 necrotic damage and 3d10 psychic damage. All other affected creatures take half of this damage (no saving throw). The exact form this spell takes varies greatly depending on the target, though disappointed ancestors, deceased family members, and hollow-eyed children are common. They are always accompanied by the cold and stench of the grave, and often by trademark perfumes or scents. The loved ones of the target do not need to be dead to manifest, though they will appear so. Creatures with anIntelligenceof 5 or lower are unaffected by this spell. You can also choose to spend 1 vilis point to inflict thestunnedcondition on the target creature for the duration of the spell. After failing its saving throw, at the end of each of its turns the creature makes a new saving throw to end thestunnedcondition.

Insomnia.description:
You call forth the wrath of your deity to affect one target creature’s mind. The creature must attempt aConstitutionsaving throw. If successful, this spell has no effect. If the target fails, it cannot take a long or short rest for the duration of the spell. This results in the creature failing to receive the healing benefits of rest, they do not regain lost Hit Dice, and spellcasting creatures do not regain spell slots. Additionally, the creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each day without sleep, starting at DC 10 and increasing by 5 for every additional 24 hours without sleep. If the creature fails the save, they gain a level ofexhaustion.

At Higher Levels. When cast above 4th level, this spell can target one additional creature per spell level and the duration lasts for one additional day.

Hidden Hand.name: Hidden Hand
Hidden Hand.description:
You create a Small hand of magical force, which isinvisibleto everyone except you or those able to seeinvisiblecreatures and objects. While you must create it in an unoccupied space you can see, it does not fill its own space. It has AC 16 and hit points equal to half your hit point maximum, disappearing if reduced to0 hit points. It uses your saving throws. It is immune to psychic or poison damage but takes damage from all other effects normally.

Creatures unable to seeinvisiblethings have disadvantage on their attack rolls against the hidden hand.

When created, you can direct to act as a guardian or toattack. It continues following either command as long as you concentrate or until you use a bonus action to switch commands. If you cease concentrating on the spell while it is in its unseen guardian mode, the spell does not immediately end but the hidden hand loses 2d6 hit points each round at the end of your turn until it reaches 0 and disappears. You cannot resume concentration, move it, or switch it back to attack mode.

Cursed Lullaby.description:
Target: One creature within range

You sing a haunting lullaby that clouds the mind of a creature. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or take 1d4 psychic damage and be unable to takereactionsuntil the start of your next turn. Fire Dance.components: S, M (burning mass of rags, a pair of torches, or similar fire in both hands)
Fire Dance.description:
You dance and twirl two sources of fire in a rapid pattern that leaves glowing trails.

Creatures of your choice in the area that see your fire dance must make aWisdomsaving throw. Any creature that can’t becharmedsucceeds on this saving throw automatically, and if you or your companions are fighting a creature, it has advantage on the save. On a failed save, a target becomescharmedfor the duration.

Whilecharmedby this spell, the creature isincapacitatedand has a speed of 0.

When a creature you can see is about to make amelee attackagainst a creature other than you, you can force it to waver and hesitate rather than striking. If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw, it cannot follow through on itsattack(or any attacks that would be made as part of the same action, such as by a creature with Multiattack), wasting that action entirely. Boots on the Ground.name: Boots on the Ground
Boots on the Ground.description:
You create the illusion of a large army encamped, which takes the form of three 20-foot-square bodies of troops. You can give these illusory soldiers basic tasks to perform, such as standing or marching in formation, performing guard-like movements, or loading or unloading illusory boxes and barrels. The troops can’t perform any actual tasks, and while the illusion includes appropriate sounds for their “actions,” it can’t create clear speech or music.

The illusory troops can be attacked, with an AC equal to your spell save DC and with saving throw modifiers equal to your spell save DC minus 10. If one of the troops is hit by anattackor fails its saving throw, you must make a DC 15Constitutionsaving throw. If you succeed, that illusory troop vanishes but the others remain. If you fail the save, all troops from your spell disappear. Any troop that is more than 500 feet from you disappears.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can create one additional illusory troop, and theConstitutionsave DC to avoid your troops disappearing is reduced by 1, for each spell slot level above 5.

Cloudkill.name: Cloudkill
Cloudkill.description:
You create a 20-foot-radius sphere of poisonous, yellow-green fog centered on a point you choose within range. The fog spreads around corners. It lasts for the duration or until strong wind disperses the fog, ending the spell. Its area is heavilyobscured.

When a creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw. The creature takes 5d8 poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Creatures are affected even if they hold their breath or don’t need to breathe.

The fog moves 10 feet away from you at the start of each of your turns, rolling along the surface of the ground. The vapors, being heavier than air, sink to the lowest level of the land, even pouring down openings.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 5th.

Greater Invisibility.name: Greater Invisibility
Greater Invisibility.description: You or a creature you touch becomes invisible until the spell ends. Anything the target is wearing or carrying is invisible as long as it is on the target’s person.

Mind Twist.name: Mind Twist
Mind Twist.description:
Target: A creature within range

You assault and twist the mind of a creature, spawning delusions and provoking uncontrolledactions. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be affected by the spell for the duration. An affected target can’t takereactionsand must roll a d10 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior for that turn. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Bright Sparks.name: Bright Sparks
Bright Sparks.description:
Sparks fly from your fingers for a moment, generating bright blue light. This illuminates the region around you to a distance of 60 feet until the start of your next turn.Wisdom(Perception) checks have advantage to spot creatures hidden in shadows.

Rat Plague.description:
Your touch inflicts disease. Make a melee spellattackagainst a creature within reach. On a hit, you afflict the creature with one of two possible rat plagues, described below. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it must make aConstitutionsaving throw. After failing three of these saving throws, the disease’s effects last for the duration, and the creature stops making these saves.

After succeeding on three of these saving throws, the creature recovers from the disease, and the spell ends.

Since this spell induces a natural disease in its target, any effect that removes a disease or otherwise ameliorates a disease’s effects apply to it.

Zobeck: Clockwork City © 2022 Open Design Llc; Author: Wolfgang Baur, Mike Franke, James J. Haeck, Ben Mcfarland, Richard Pett, Christina Stiles, Matthew Stinson.

Healing Lore.name: Healing Lore
Healing Lore.description:
Classes:cleric,druid,paladin,ranger

You tap into your medical knowledge and combine it with the power of your magical healing to provide a salubrious synergy that enhances both. If you are proficient inWisdom(Medicine) andcast a spellthat cures at least 10 hit points to the target, you can also remove one level ofexhaustionfrom the target, or if the target is currentlypoisonedit can attempt an immediate saving throw (no action required) to end thepoisonedcondition. In addition, you can attempt aWisdom(Medicine) check whenever you cast a spell that restores hit points with a DC of 10 plus the spell’s level. If the check succeeds, you can add the spell’s level to the number of hit points restored.
