Lunar Transfer.name: Lunar Transfer
Lunar Transfer.components: V, S, M (an opal worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
Lunar Transfer.description:
This spell instantly summons a glittering moonbeam that transports one sleeping creature or object of your choice that you can see within range to a destination you select.

If you target an unwilling creature, it can make aWisdomsaving throw. On a successful save, the spell fails, and you appear in the target location instead. A transferred creature wakes up as soon as it arrives at its destination. If you target an object, it must be able to fit entirely inside a 10-foot cube, and it can’t be held or carried by an unwilling creature. The destination you choose must be known to you, and it must be on the same plane of existence as you.

Your familiarity with the destination determines whether the creature or object arrives there successfully.

The GM rolls a d20 and consults the Lunar Transfer table below.

Perhaps you tried to scry an enemy’s sanctum but instead viewed an illusion, or perhaps you are attempting toteleportto a familiar location that no longer exists.

On Target. The target creature or object appears where you want it to.

Off Target. The target creature or object appears a random distance away from the destination in a random direction. Distance off target is 5 miles times a d20 roll, though never more than half the distance traveled. For example, if you sent someone 250 miles and they landed off target, and you rolled an 8 on the d20, then they would arrive off target by 40 miles. If you had sent them only 20 miles, they could not be more than 10 miles off target.

The GM determines the direction off target randomly by rolling a d8 and designating 1 as north, 2 as northeast, 3 as east, and so on around the points of the compass. If you were teleporting someone to a coastal city and they wound up 20 miles out at sea, they could be in trouble.

Similar. Your target creature or object winds up in a different area that’s visually or thematically similar to the target area. If you are sending someone to your home laboratory, for example, they might wind up in anotherwizard’slaboratory or in an alchemical supply shop that has many of the same tools and implements as your laboratory. Generally, the creature or object appears in the closest similar place, but since the spell has no range limit, they could conceivably wind up anywhere on the plane.

Mishap. The spell’s unpredictable magic results in a difficult journey. The teleporting creature or object takes 2d12 force damage, and the GM rerolls on the table to see where you (instead of the target) wind up. (Multiple mishaps can occur, dealing damage each time.)

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Violent Obsession.components: V, S, M (twisted silk ribbon worth at least 1 gp)
Violent Obsession.description:
You twist the mind of a creature you can see within range, causing it to fixate dangerously on another creature. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or become violently obsessed with another creature of your choice that you can see within range. When the target can see the object of its obsession at the end of the target’s turn, it takes 2d8 psychic damage, or 1d8 more (3d8 total) if the target is also more than 5 feet from the object of its obsession. After taking this damage, the target can make a newWisdomsaving throw against the spell, ending it if successful.

You stir your allies to fight with renewed aggression using words magically crafted to dishearten your foes.

Until the end of your next turn, when you or a creature friendly to you within 30 feet of you misses with a melee weaponattack, you deal 1d6 psychic damage to the target. A creature can only deal this damage once per turn.

While you are concentrating on this spell, you may use your bonus action to extend its duration by 1 round.

Compelling Question.name: Compelling Question
Compelling Question.description:
You ask a creature one question. The creature must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, the creature answers truthfully. You know whether the creature succeeds or fails on its saving throw. Elemental Ward.name: Elemental Ward
Elemental Ward.description:
Class(es): Bard, Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

Upon casting, this spell weaves a protective barrier around you, diminishing the impact of elemental forces. You gainresistanceto the triggering damage type until the start of your next turn. Additionally, for the duration, any time you take damage from amelee attack, the attacker takes damage of the triggering type equal to half your spellcasting ability modifier (rounded up)

Fist of the End Times.name: Fist of the End Times
Fist of the End Times.description:
Class(es): cleric, druid, paladin, sorcerer, wizard

You imbue your fists with the power of apocalyptic forces. For the duration, your unarmed strikes deal 3d10 force damage, and each hit creates a shockwave that deals 1d6 force damage to all other creatures within 5 feet of the target. Additionally, your strikes can break nonmagical barriers, such as walls or doors, dealing double damage to such objects.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage of your unarmed strikes increases by 1d10 and the damage of your shockwaves increases by 1d6 for each two slot levels above 5th.

Conjure Vermin.name: Conjure Vermin
Conjure Vermin.description:
You summon fiendish spirits that take the form of sickly swarms of crows, maggots, or rats in unoccupied spaces you can see within range. Choose one of the following options for what appears:

Each swarm is also considered a Fiend, and it disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The summoned swarms are friendly to you and your companions. Rollinitiativefor the swarms as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures but otherwise take noactions.

Until this spell ends, you can use an action to force one of the swarms you control to cause one of the following effects, based on the type of swarm. Once you use this action, that swarm disappears.

The GM has the creatures’ statistics.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using higher-level spell slots, you choose one of the summoning options above, and more creatures appear: twice as many with a 4th-level slot, three times as many with a 6th-level slot, and four times as many with an 8th-level slot.

Crowd Pleaser.name: Crowd Pleaser
Crowd Pleaser.description:
You begin performing a raucous crowd-pleasing jig. You cannot cast another spell through your spellcasting focus while concentrating on this spell.

Whenever a creature other than you enters the spell’s area for the first time on its turn or starts its turn there, it must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save creatures becomecharmedby you and begin partying. While maintaining concentration on this spell, you can use your bonus action to order all creatures currentlycharmedby you to act in one of the following ways.Charmedcreatures continue carrying out these orders until you issue another order or they are no longercharmed.

A creaturecharmedin this way hinders anyone who opposes you, although it avoids violence unless it was already inclined to fight on your behalf. When acharmedcreature takes damage, witnesses you attacking or damaging its allies, or when another creature takes an action to try and shake it awake, it makes anotherCharismasaving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once a creature successfully resists this spell, it is immune to crowd pleaser for the next 24 hours. The radius of this spell increases by 5 feet for each creature currentlycharmedby it, up to a maximum of a 60-foot radius.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the spell’s initial radius increases by an additional 10 feet for each slot level above 4th.

Angelic Executioner.name: Angelic Executioner
Angelic Executioner.components: V, S, M (piece of coal, which is consumed by the spell)
Angelic Executioner.description:
Choose a target that can see or hear you within range. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or believe that the coal burns with a holy fire, which it sees take the shape of a Large, halberd-wielding angel. This angelic figure, the angelic executioner, starts chasing the target, dealing 1d6 psychic damage at the start of each of the target’s turns. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Remove Insulation.name: Remove Insulation
Remove Insulation.description:
You target a creature within range, and that creature must succeed on a Fortitude saving throw or become less resistant to lightning damage. A creature with immunity to lightning damage has advantage on this saving throw. On a failure, a creature with immunity to lightning damage instead hasresistanceto lightning damage for the spell’s duration, and a creature withresistanceto lightning damage loses itsresistancefor the duration. A creature withoutresistanceto lightning damage that fails its saving throw takes double damage from lightning for the spell’s duration.

Remove curse or similar magic ends this spell.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the duration is 24 hours. If you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, a creature with immunity to lightning damage no longer has advantage on its saving throw. If you use a spell slot of 9th level or higher, the spell lasts until it is dispelled.

Authors: Wolfgang Baur, Celeste Conowitch, David “Zeb” Cook, Dan Dillon, Robert Fairbanks, Scott Gable, Richard Green, Victoria Jaczko, TK Johnson, Christopher Lockey, Sarah Madsen, Greg Marks, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Lysa Penrose, Richard Pett, Marc Radle, Hannah Rose, Jon Sawatsky, Robert Schwalb, Brian Suskind, Ashley Warren, Mike Welham. © 2020 Open Design LLC.

When you are exposed to any inhaled poison or disease, including pheromones or scent-based attacks, you suck in a rough breath that filters out those toxins, giving you Advantage on your saving throw andResistanceto Poison damage against such effects.

Chorus of Thunder.name: Chorus of Thunder
Chorus of Thunder.description:
You utter, shout, or sing a short verse to damage and deafen your enemies. A cacophonous clap of thunder slams out from you in a 30-foot cone that is audible out to 300 feet. Each creature in the cone must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 thunder damage and isdeafeneduntil the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’tdeafened.

When you cast this spell, up to four friendly creatures within 30 feet of you that can see you can each use areactionto join the chorus with a clash of weapon against shield, a ringing shout, or other loud noise. For each creature that joins the chorus, the spell’s damage increases by 1d6, and the cone’ssizeincreases by 5 feet.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the primary damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Dismantle.name: Dismantle
Dismantle.description:
You target one nonmagical trap you can see within range and harmlessly disassemble it into its component parts, which hover in the air briefly before arranging themselves neatly on the ground in front of you. This disarms the trap without triggering it, though it does not allow elements of the trap to pass through solid barriers. For example, if a portion of the trap is hidden behind a stone wall, that portion remains in place or falls harmlessly to the ground, but it would not pass through the wall to get to you.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can dismantle one additional trap for every two slot levels above 3rd (so two traps at 5th, three at 7th, and four at 9th).

Roy, Paul Scofield, Amber Stewart, Brian Suskind, Mike Welham.

True Telekinesis.name: True Telekinesis
True Telekinesis.description:
Your mind overflows with telekinetic power, allowing you to manipulate creatures and objects by thought alone. When you use your action to cast this spell and do so each round for the duration, you can telekinetically manipulate any number of creatures or objects within range, causing one of the following effects to each of them. An unwilling target can attempt aStrengthsaving throw to prevent the effect. The maximum weight of a single target you manipulate is 50,000 pounds.

Total Party Kill Bestiary - Volume 2 2020 © 2CGaming, LLC. Author Ryan Servis

Demand Offering.name: Demand Offering
Demand Offering.components: V, S, M (pinch of gold dust)
Demand Offering.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a pinch of gold dust)

You manifest an impulse of greed so overpowering that the target is compelled to offer up whatever it has in its hands to attempt to satisfy you on a failedWisdomsaving throw. The creature moves toward you at its best speed, moving to avoid obvious dangers en route to you. Once within reach, the target gives you whatever it holds in its hands (or wears on its hands or wrists) owns, and as an action, bonus action, orreactionyou can take possession of the item as long as you have a free hand. If your hands are full, you can instead demand that the target drop the item at your feet as a bonus action orreactionif they are adjacent to you. If you do not take the item or demand the target drop it at your feet by the end of your next turn, the compulsion ends. The target is not prevented from defending itself if attacked.

The spell has no effect if the target has no means of moving toward you to deliver its gift, including if it isrestrainedfrom moving or faced with an impassable or obviously dangerous barrier, such as awall of fire.

Animal Friendship.name: Animal Friendship
Animal Friendship.components: V, S, M(a morsel of food)
Animal Friendship.description:
This spell lets you convince a beast that you mean it no harm. Choose a beast that you can see within range. It must see and hear you. If the beast’sIntelligenceis 4 or higher, the spell fails. Otherwise, the beast must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becharmedby you for the spell’s duration. If you or one of your companions harms the target, the spells ends.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can affect one additional beast for each slot level above 1st.

Animate Dead (revised).name: Animate Dead (revised)
Animate Dead (revised).description:
This spell creates an undead servant. Choose a pile of bones or a corpse of a creature within range. Your spell imbues the target with a foul mimicry of life, raising up to 1/4 CR of undead creatures (CR 0 counts as CR 1/8 for this purpose). The bones or corpse must be appropriate to the undead created, such as agnoll’scorpse for agnollwitherling or any humanoid’s corpse for azombie.

As a free action, you can mentally command any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

The creature is under your control for 24 hours, after which it stops obeying any command you’ve given it. To maintain control of the creature for another 24 hours, you must cast this spell on the creature again before the current 24-hour period ends. This use of the spell reasserts your control over up to 1 challenge rating worth of creatures you have animated with this spell, rather than animating a new one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you animate or reassert control over 1/2 CR worth of additional undead creatures for each spell slot level above 3rd. Each of the creatures must come from a different corpse or pile of bones.

Power Word Fling.name: Power Word Fling
Power Word Fling.description:
You mutter a word of power that causes a creature you can see within range to be flung vertically or horizontally. The creature must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be thrown up to 15 feet vertically or horizontally. If the target impacts a surface, such as a ceiling or wall, it stops moving and takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target was thrown vertically, it plummets to the ground, taking falling damage as normal, unless it has a flying speed or other method of preventing a fall. If the target impacts a creature, the target stops moving and takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage, and the creature the target hits must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be forcedprone. After the target is thrown horizontally or it falls from being thrown vertically, regardless of whether it impacted a surface, it is forcedprone.

As a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns, you can attempt to fling the same creature again. The target must succeed on anotherStrengthsaving throw or be thrown.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the distance you can fling the target increases by 5 feet, and the damage from impacting a surface or creature increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Grant Undeath.name: Grant Undeath
Grant Undeath.description:
You imbue with unlife the body of one dead creature within range. It reanimates, its type becomes undead, it gainsdarkvisionof 60 feet if it did not already have it, immunity to poison damage,exhaustion, and thepoisonedcondition, and it no longer requires air, food, or sleep, and loses any legendaryactionsor class features.

The creature can complete a long rest by spending eight hours doing onlylightactivity such as keeping watch. You choose whether the body becomes askeletonor azombie. If you create askeleton, the creature’sDexterityscore increases by 2, itsIntelligenceandCharismascores decrease by 4, and it gainsvulnerabilityto bludgeoning damage. If you create azombie, the creature’sConstitutionscore increases by 2, and itsStrengthscore increases by 1. ItsWisdomandCharismascores decrease by 4, and itsIntelligencedecreases by 6. Its walking speed decreases by 10 feet to a minimum of five feet, and it gains the following trait:

You can issue a command to one or more creatures you created with this spell as a bonus action. A creature remains under your control for 24 hours, after which it stops following any order you gave it, unless you cast this spell on it again, which causes it to remain under your control for another day. One year after this spell is cast, the creature dies unless you cast this spell on it again before then. Reasserting control over a creature does not consume the material component but increasing the time it remains animate does.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Conjure Acorns.name: Conjure Acorns
Conjure Acorns.description:
You create 1 pound of acorns on the ground or in a container within range. The acorns spoil if uneaten after 24 hours.

Ratatosk ©2022 Open Design LLC; Author: Brian Suskind.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Plunderer’s Greed.name: Plunderer’s Greed
Plunderer’s Greed.description:
Classes: Bard, Cleric, Paladin, Sorcerer

You incite a creature within range into a state of greedy fervor. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature is compelled to seek out and hoard any valuables it can find, disregarding all otheractions. An affected creature must use its movement and action each turn to move toward and collect any visible valuables within its reach. If no valuables are in sight, the creature still tries tosearchfor them. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Pirates and Plunder A Compendium For 5e © 2024 Published by Mythos Chronicles; Author Filippo Bardoscia

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Artesian Spring.name: Artesian Spring
Artesian Spring.description:
You create a spring of pure, fresh water bubbling forth from an area of natural rock or earth you strike with the focus item, producing a flow of 1d6 gallons of cool potable water each hour. You cannot create an artesian spring in a building or an area of worked stone, nor can you create an artesian spring within 1 mile of an existing artesian spring.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 3rd-level spell slot the artesian spring’s duration increases to 1 week. When you cast this spell using a 4th-level spell slot the artesian spring’s duration increases to 1 month. When you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot or higher the artesian spring’s duration increases to 1 year. When you cast this spell using a 6th-level spell slot the artesian spring’s duration increases to permanent.

Latin American Monsters (5E)© 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Miguel Colon, Ismael Alvarez, Robert J. Grady, Jason Nelson.

Time Stop.name: Time Stop
Time Stop.description:
You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. No time passes for other creatures, while you take 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, during which you can use actions and move as normal.

This spell ends if one of the actions you use during this period, or any effects that you create during this period, affects a creature other than you or an object being worn or carried by someone other than you. In addition, the spell ends if you move to a place more than 1,000 feet from the location where you cast it.

Water Serpents.name: Water Serpents
Water Serpents.components: V, S, M (scale from a fish)
Water Serpents.description:
Class(es): Druid, Sorcerer, Synthetist

You conjure two large serpents made of water in spaces you can see within range. The serpents are under your control and canattackyour enemies.

Use the statistics for a giant constrictor snake. The serpents are also resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing non magical damage and can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. The serpents act on their owninitiativeand follow your commands to the best of their ability, vanishing when they reach0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Wrath of The Sun.name: Wrath of The Sun
Wrath of The Sun.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 minute

You fill the area with the sun’s burning light.

Illumination conditions are increased by two steps (to a maximum of bright light), and all creatures in the area take 5d6 points of fire damage and 1 level ofexhaustionper round. Theexhaustioncannot be raised above level 2. A successfulConstitutionsave each round negates theexhaustionbut not the fire damage. Any creature that fails theirConstitutionsaving throw two consecutive times catches fire, taking an additional 1d6 fire damage each round until the creature uses an action to put the fire out, however, the fire cannot be extinguished while within the radius of the spell.

Subsequent failures increase the fire damage by being on fine by 1d6 each round. Corpses in the area for longer than 1 round are burnt to ash; reviving the incinerated corpse requirestrue resurrectionorwish. As a bonus action, you may move the area of effect up to 10 feet in any direction.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Sapphire Helm.name: Sapphire Helm
Sapphire Helm.description:
You create a mask of sapphire around your face which magnifies your vision immensely. For the duration of the spell, when youcast a spellthat has a range of 5 feet or greater, the range of that spell increases by 10 feet times your spellcasting modifier (minimum 10 feet). Additionally, you have advantage on anyWisdom(Perception) checks which rely on sight.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Toadstool Ring.name: Toadstool Ring
Toadstool Ring.components: V, S, M(a bit of dried mushroom)
Toadstool Ring.description:
You coax a toadstool ring to sprout from the ground.

A creature of your choice can sit in the center of the ring and meditate for the duration, catching glimpses of the past, present, and future. The creature can ask up to three questions: one about the past, one about the present, and one about the future. The GM offers truthful answers in the form of dreamlike visions that may be subject to interpretation. When the spell ends, the toadstools turn black and dissolve back into the earth.

If you cast the spell two or more times before finishing your next long rest, there is a cumulative 25 percent chance for each casting after the first that the meditating creature gets a random vision unrelated to the question. The GM makes this roll in secret.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Craft Wonder.name: Craft Wonder
Craft Wonder.duration: instantaneous Through the weaving of magic, and the combination of rare and wonderful materials,
Craft Wonder.description:
Through the weaving of magic, and the combination of rare and wonderful materials, you can create a common magical item, and instantly attune it to one creature that can use that item as long as that creature was present for the entire casting of the spell. If that creature ever becomes unattuned to the item, the item crumbles to dust. The material component for this spell depends on the rarity of the wonder. You must expend 100 gp for a common or 500 gp for an uncommon item.

If an item is uncommon, the GM can determine that an additional rare material component is necessary, such as arocfeather or the dragon’s dewclaw. At the DM’s discretion, specific magic items may not be available to create with this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, you can create an uncommon item without requiring a curse, or a rare item that is subject to a minor curse. To create a rare item, the casting requires material components costing up to 5000 gp, as well as one or more rare ingredients.

Simple Settings: Fairy Tales. 2020, Fat Goblin Games; Author: Rick Hershey, Ismael Alvarez, Jason Owen Black

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Oil Slick.name: Oil Slick
Oil Slick.components: V, S, M (bit of grease, oil, or butter)
Oil Slick.description:
You cover the ground in your space with slippery oil, and when you move you leave a trail of this slickness behind you, filling every square you pass through until you have filled up to 20 squares. If you move farther than that, the oil slick stops expanding but the remaining oil persists as long as the spell lasts. If you climb while using this spell, the oil slick covers the surface on which you are climbing. As a bonus action, you can choose to not leave an oil slick behind you as you move onyour turn, but resume leaving the oil slick on your next turn.

Any creature other than you treats the oil slick asdifficult terrainand has disadvantage onDexterity(Acrobatics) andStrength(Athletics) checks within it. In addition, a creature entering the area (including moving into your space) or ending its turn there must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fallprone(or fall, if climbing).

An oil slick has no effect if you are flying, and flying creatures are not affected by it. If you are swimming, an oil slick instead leaves each square you pass through lightly obscured for the duration of the spell rather than its usual effects.

Your movement is never affected by your own oil slick.

The oil slick is not flammable.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the oil slick can fill an additional 10 squares for each slot level above 2nd.

The Dragon’s Hoard #41 © 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke

Oil Slick.material_component: bit of grease, oil, or butter

Choking Sands.name: Choking Sands
Choking Sands.description:
You fill the lungs (or gills, for a water-breathing creature) of a living creature with choking sand. If it fails aConstitutionsave, it starts suffocating and can’t speak. It can cough out the sand as anActionwith a successfulConstitutionsave. If it doesn’t succeed on this save within a number of rounds equal to itsConstitutionmodifier (minimum 1 round), it drops to0 Hit Pointsand begins dying and can’t be stabilized or regainHit Pointsuntil it can breathe again.

A dying creature can attempt aConstitutionsave on each of its turns.

The Dragon’s Hoard #56© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, Jeff Ibach, Mike D. Welham, Alex Riggs, Scott Young, James-Levi Cooke.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Earworm.name: Earworm
Earworm.description:
You begin performing an infuriatingly catchy tune that makes it increasingly hard to concentrate on anything else. You cannot cast another spell through your spellcasting focus while concentrating on this spell.

A creature that is concentrating on a spell that starts its turn within the area or enters the area for the first time on its turn must make a concentration check with a DC equal to 10 + the number of rounds you’ve maintained concentration on this spell (including the turn you cast it). On a failure, it loses concentration on the spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, add +2 to the DC of concentration checks inflicted by this spell for each slot level above 2nd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Eyeburst.name: Eyeburst
Eyeburst.description:
Choose a creature to whom you have line of effect within 30 feet. A spark of blinding light leaps from your hand and explodes in the target’s face, searing its visage and causing the fluid in its eyes to boil and possibly rupture. The victim of eyeburst must make aConstitutionsaving throw or suffer 10d10 points of radiant damage and be permanentlyblinded. A successful save halves this damage and avoids the blindness effect.

Eyes destroyed by this spell can only be restored by aregenerateorwishspell, or another spell or effect that permits the regrowth of missing body parts.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Staggering Blows.name: Staggering Blows
Staggering Blows.description:
You touch a nonmagical bludgeoning weapon. Until the spell ends, the weapon inflicts an additional 1d6 thunder damage. Any creature ofsizeLarge or smaller that is struck with that weapon must also make aDexteritysaving throw or be knockedprone.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Caustic Blood.name: Caustic Blood
Caustic Blood.description:
Your blood becomes caustic when exposed to the air. When you take damage, you can use yourreactionto select up to three targets within 30 feet of you. Each target takes 1d10 acid damage unless it makes a successfulDexteritysaving throw.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the number of targets increases by one for each slot level above 2nd.

The Scarlet Citadel. © 2021 Open Design LLC. Authors: Steve Winter, Wolfgang Baur, Scott Gable, and Victoria Jaczo.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bombardment.name: Bombardment
Bombardment.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a piece of quartz)

You cause a rain of rocks to crash down in a 15-foot-radius, 30-foot-high Cylinder and cover creatures in the area. Each creature in the Cylinder makes aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 12d6 Bludgeoning damage and isproneandRestrainedon a failed save, or half as much damage and is not prone and Restrained on a successful one. A creature Restrained by this spell cannot breath.

A creatureRestrainedby the rocks, or an adjacent creature, can take an action to make aStrength(Athletics) check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained.

Rocks turn ground in the Cylinder intoDifficult Terrainfor 10 minutes.

Breath of Life: The Marshal (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Michael Messinger

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Curse.name: Curse
Curse.description:
You place a curse on a creature you can see, within range. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell has no effect.

Choose one effect. The effect lasts until you use an Action to end the curse or until the creature is affected byremove curse. Curses do not stack and a creature can only have a number of curse effects from one source affecting them at a time, depending on your level; one from 1st level, two from 5th level, three from 11th level, and four from 17th level.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Curse of Binding Shadows.name: Curse of Binding Shadows
Curse of Binding Shadows.description:
Target: One creature within range

Shadows lash out at a creature within range, attempting to bind it in place. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target’s speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn, as shadowy tendrils wrap around its legs.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Wall of Stars.name: Wall of Stars
Wall of Stars.components: V, S, M (Powdered glass suspended in
Wall of Stars.description:
You create a translucent wall of blackness dotted with starlight at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose: horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. It can be free floating, or it can rest on a solid surface. The wall can be up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall does not block line of sight, but everything seen through the wall is lightly obscured and has halfcover. If a creature passes through the wall, their movement immediately ends and their speed becomes 0 until the end of their next turn.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the length of the wall you create increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 5th.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Borrowed Beauty.name: Borrowed Beauty
Borrowed Beauty.description:
You target a humanoid creature within range and siphon its lifeforce into you. The target must make aCharismasaving throw. If the target fails the saving throw, itsCharismadecreases by 1d4 + your spellcasting attribute modifier for the spell’s duration, and the target’s appearance changes so that it appears older and less attractive by that creature’s standard of beauty. In turn, yourCharismaincreases by the same amount, and your appearance changes so that you appear younger and more attractive by your standard of beauty. The spell’s target may make a newCharismasaving throw at the end of each of its turns (using its newCharismascore), ending the effect on a successful save. The target’sCharismacannot be reduced to lower than 1 by means of this spell.

Contract Spell: If cast as a contract spell, the duration is permanent until the contract ends.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Nexus.name: Nexus
Nexus.components: V, S, M (platinum thread and needle worth at least 700 gp, which the spell consumes)
Nexus.description:
You conjure up to four magical doorways in a surface you touch. The surface must be large enough to accommodate the doors, which are large enough for a Large or smaller creature to pass through. When you cast this spell, choose a nonmagical archway, doorway, or other threshold you have moved through at least once within 100 miles of you for each magical doorway you create. Each magical doorway opens onto the location of its associated nonmagical threshold for the duration. The spell ends early if the surface on which the magical doorways appear is destroyed.

When you cast this spell, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

You and the chosen creatures are the only creatures able to use the magical doorways. The magical doorways are two-way for such creatures, allowing the creatures to pass between the two locations by moving through the doorways, opening the destination doors if necessary.

All other creatures see the magical doorways as door-like outlines or silhouettes in a style of your choice on the surface you touched, and they see and can interact with the nonmagical thresholds at the destinations as if the locations weren’t tied to magical doorways.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Nexus.material_component: platinum thread and needle worth at least 700 gp, which the spell consumes

Call Companion.name: Call Companion
Call Companion.description:
You summon a spirit that assumes the form of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal companion, creating a long-lasting bond with it. Appearing in an unoccupied space within range, the creature takes on a form that you choose of a beast with a CR of ¼ (the creature summoned is subject to the GM’s approval). The creature has the statistics of the chosen form, though it is celestial, fey or fiend (your choice) instead of its normal type. Additionally, if the creature has an intelligence of 5 or less, itsIntelligencebecomes 6, and it gains the ability to understand one language of your choice that you speak. Your companion may serve you as a mount if it is large enough, both in combat and out, and you have an instinctive bond with it that allows you to fight as a seamless unit (no animal handling check required, but a persuasion may be). While mounted on or touching your companion, you can make any spell you cast that targets only you also target your companion.

When the companion drops to0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. You can also dismiss your companion at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same spirit which can take a different form if you choose. All equipment stored or worn by the creature when it disappears falls to the ground. While your companion is within 1 mile of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. You can’t have more than one companion bonded by this spell at a time; in addition, if the companion is not destroyed or dismissed by dawn of the next day, the spell slot used to summon it is consumed again. If the spell slot is not available, then the companion disappears.

At Higher Levels. You may spend higher level spell slots to choose a more powerful companion.

2nd level: You may choose a beast with a CR of ½ or lower. If the creature has a fly speed, it must be small or smaller insize.

3rd level: You may choose a beast with a CR of 1 or lower.

4th level: You may choose a beast with a CR of 2 or lower.

5th level: You may choose a beast with a CR of 4 or lower.

Special:Nightmare(minimum 15th level), Hellhound,Manticore(minimum 15th level),Unicorn(Minimum 17th level).

6th level and above: You may not upgrade this spell beyond 5th level.

Stone Mother’s Assault - © 2020, Adrian Arduini; Author: Adrian Arduini

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bloodlust Contamination.name: Bloodlust Contamination
Bloodlust Contamination.description:
You cast the spell on a single targetsendingthem into a blinding rage. If the target fails aWisdomsaving, they are sent into a rage as a 1st-levelbarbarian, or of theirbarbarianlevel if applicable. The rage lasts for 1 minute. Even if the initial target succeeds on theirWisdomsaving throw, they can still cause adjacent creatures toflyinto a rage for 1 minute, see below.

For the 1 minute of the effect, anytime the original target or a creature subject to the rage effect of this spell is adjacent to a creature who is not currently raging, that adjacent creature must make aWisdomsaving throw or be subject to the rage effect for 1 minute. The original target of the spell or a creature that has been subject to aWisdomsaving throw by this effect cannot be affected again by this casting of the spell. They still transmit the rage for 1 minute after the initialWisdomsaving throw.

The rage can be triggered on a creature that isfatigued, unlikebarbarianrage and anyfrightenedeffect is suppressed while the creature is subject to the rage effect.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Barrier Sight.name: Barrier Sight
Barrier Sight.description:
You can see through objects, structures, and creatures within range. To you, solid objects within that radius appear transparent and don’t prevent light from passing through them.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Necrotic Explosion.name: Necrotic Explosion
Necrotic Explosion.description:
Target: Each creature in a 20-foot radius

You release a burst of necrotic energy, devastating nearby foes. Each other creature within 20 feet of you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 necrotic damage and is knockedproneby the pain. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t knockedprone. If a target is cursed and fails on the saving throw, it also has its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn as necrotic tendrils cling to it.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Demiplane.name: Demiplane
Demiplane.description:
You create a shadowy door on a flat solid surface that you can see within range. The door is large enough to allow Medium creatures to pass through unhindered. When opened, the door leads to a demiplane that appears to be an empty room 30 feet in each dimension, made of wood or stone. When the spell ends, the door disappears, and any creatures or objects inside the demiplane remain trapped there, as the door also disappears from the other side.

Each time you cast this spell, you can create a new demiplane, or have the shadowy door connect to a demiplane you created with a previous casting of this spell. Additionally, if you know the nature and contents of a demiplane created by a casting of this spell by another creature, you can have the shadowy door connect to its demiplane instead.

Soul Smite.name: Soul Smite
Soul Smite.description:
This spell fills you with necromantic energy that is released when you strike an opponent with amelee attack. The spell ends whether you hit the target or not. If you hit the target, your weapon strikes both body and soul, dealing an extra 4d6 necrotic damage to the target. The target must also make aConstitutionsaving throw or have disadvantage on allattackrolls and ability checks, and be unable to takereactions, until the end of its next turn.

Constructs are immune to this spell and undead are bolstered by it, gaining 4d6temporary hit pointsinstead.

Impaling Glory.name: Impaling Glory
Impaling Glory.description:
You call down glowing spears to skewer and pin your enemies. The golden spears fall on up to three creatures on the ground you can see within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst each target. On a hit, a creature takes 1d8 piercing damage and 1d8 radiant damage and isrestrainedas the glowing spear pierces it and pins it to the ground. A creaturerestrainedby a spear can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. On a success, it is no longerrestrained.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the piercing damage or radiant damage (your choice) increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Epoch’s Collapse.name: Epoch’s Collapse
Epoch’s Collapse.description:
You unleash a potent force that causes a localized collapse of time and space. Choose a point on the ground within range. A 100-foot radius sphere centered on that point implodes, creating a powerful gravity well.

Each creature in the sphere must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 20d10 force damage and is pulled to the center, with those closer to the center reaching it first and occupying the nearest available position to the center. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and is not pulled to the center.

For the next minute, the area becomes a gravity well.

Movement towards the center of the sphere requires half the usual amount of movement (double movement speed towards the center). Conversely, any movement away from the center requires double the usual amount of movement (movement speed halved when moving away from the center).

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Speak with Objects.name: Speak with Objects
Speak with Objects.description:
You attune your senses to communicate with pseudo?sentient spirits within or attached to inanimate objects for the duration. While touching an object, you can telepathically communicate with it as though you share a common language. Objects aren’t intelligent, and their senses are different than those of most humanoids, so they are limited to conveying simple ideas and may not understand complex questions or statements. For example, a chair is unlikely to know if it was a phantavir,human, ordwarfthat sat on it earlier that day, nor would it know if the creature’s state of mind, but it could know a Medium humanoid that was very heavy and covered in hard metal sat in it for a long time earlier that day. Likewise, the chair won’t understand if you ask it where the person came from or went, but it might note that the person ate or drank something while sitting by the window. It might even suggest that the nearby table might have more specific information about that.

You can also touch a construct and communicate with it as if you shared a common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Singularity.name: Singularity
Singularity.description:
You create an intense gravity well centered at a point you can see within range. For the duration of the spell, a creature starting its turn within a 90 foot radius of the center of the gravity well must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be pulled 30 feet towards the center, or half as much on a successful one. If the creature is pulled within 30 feet of the gravity well’s center, it takes 9d12 bludgeoning damage and fallsprone.

If a creature makes aranged attackwhose line of sight passes through the gravity well, it is made at disadvantage.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bullying Brogue.name: Bullying Brogue
Bullying Brogue.description:
You toss a nonmagical shoe toward a creature you can see within range. The shoe grows to tremendoussizebefore falling onto the target. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 5d10 bludgeoning damage and is knockedproneandrestrained.

On a successful save, the target takes half the damage and isn’t knockedproneorrestrained, and the spell ends.

Until the spell ends, you can use a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns to deal 2d10 bludgeoning damage to the target as the shoe grinds the target into the ground.

At the end of each of its turns, the target can make aStrengthsaving throw, breaking free on a success. When the target breaks free or when the spell ends, the shoe shrinks to its normalsize, becoming a nonmagical shoe once again.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Winter’s Breath.name: Winter’s Breath
Winter’s Breath.description:
You breathe out a freezing blast of cold air. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make aConstitutionsaving throw. A creature takes 8d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Additionally, on a saving throw failed by 5 or more, the target isstunnedfor 1 round.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Prayer - Gods of Winter and Hunting (5E), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Ember Flick.name: Ember Flick
Ember Flick.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You flick your wrist, sending a small ember to a point you choose within range. Any creature in a 5-foot radius of a point within range must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 1d6 fire damage.

At Higher Levels. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Tomb of Sand.description:

Feather Step.name: Feather Step
Feather Step.description:
You make the target’s steps light and easy in spite of obstructions. For the duration of the spell, the target ignores the adverse movement effects ofdifficult terrainand can move at their normal speed.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can affect 2 additional creatures for each slot level above 1st.

Glamor.name: Glamor
Glamor.description:
You attempt to endear yourself to people you interact with, on a subconscious level. Choose up to three people within 30 feet of you. Each creature must make aWisdomsaving throw. A creature that fails views your appearance and voice as having qualities they consider idyllic or terrifying (your choice). Make all yourCharismachecks with them at advantage for the duration of the spell.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Party Ball.name: Party Ball
Party Ball.components: V, S, M (handful of colorful marbles)
Party Ball.description:
You choose a point that you can see within range. A tiny sized, bright shining ball appears in that space. It illuminates a space of 30 feet with bright light and flashes multicolored rays all around. Any creatures, that can see the ball and are within 10 feet of it upon creation, must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On failure, they areblindeduntil the start of their next turn.

When the ball is destroyed, either by ending the spell or by taking damage (AC 12), it explodes in a hail of shrapnel. Any creatures within 10 feet of the ball when it explodes must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 3d6 slashing damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When the spell is cast with a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the range on the illumination, blinding effect, and explosion all increase by 5 feet for every spell slot used above 2nd. If casting this spell with a 6th level spells slot or higher, allinvisiblecreatures within the illuminated area are visible.

Dampening Field.name: Dampening Field
Dampening Field.description:
A 30-foot radius sphere around you seems to become more drab in color, and magical energy loses its potency in this area. A creature can’t cast a cantrip within this area. When a creature casts a spell in this area, they must expend a spell slot 1 level higher than normal.

For example, afireballcast at 3rd level by a creature in this area must be cast using a spell slot of 4th level.

Thisfireballwould still be considered to be cast at 3rd level, meaning that it would not benefit from the additional damage from casting the spell at higher levels, unless the caster used a spell slot of a greater level than 4th.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the spell slot expended must be at least 2 levels higher than normal.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Animate Necrosis.name: Animate Necrosis
Animate Necrosis.components: V, S, M (bit of string coated in animal fat)
Animate Necrosis.description:
You animate the dead tissue in one wound of a living creature (the creature must currently be below its maximum number ofhit pointsdue to an injury), causing bits of animated flesh to form a sickly tendril that reaches up and out of one of the creature’s wounds.

The tendril attempts to attack the living portion of the creature, choking and strangling it. The tendril’sattackbonus is equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a hit, it deals 3d8 bludgeoning damage and the target is grappled. Until this grapple ends, the target can’t breathe, and the tendril has advantage on attack rolls against the creature. The tendril attacks again at the start of your next three turns.

The tendril has AC 15 and 2 hit points per Hit Die of the target. It automatically fails all saving throws.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 3d8 for each slot level above 5th.

Animate Necrosis.material_component: bit of string coated in animal fat

Life Blast.name: Life Blast
Life Blast.description:
You draw the life force from the surrounding land and hurl it at your enemies in a line 100 feet long and 5 feet wide in a direction you choose. Creatures in this line take 8d6 radiant damage, or half as much on a successfulWisdomsaving throw. However, leaching the life energy from the land causes all ordinary vegetation within 20 feet of you to wither and die. Plant creatures within this area take 2d6 necrotic damage, or half as much with a successfulWisdomsaving throw. A plant creature within 20 feet that is in the path of the life blast makes only one saving throw, taking half damage from both effects on a success.

Trees greater than 1 foot thick are not destroyed by a life blast. This spell cannot be cast if there is not at least 100 square feet of vegetation within 20 feet of you.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you increase the length of the line by 10 feet and the radius of the plant-withering effect by 5 feet for each level above 3rd.

The Dragon’s Hoard #24 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Gusting Palm.name: Gusting Palm
Gusting Palm.description:
Class(es): Druid, Sorcerer, Synthetist

You release a short blast of wind from your palm.

Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature is pushed 5 feet away from you and takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage.

At Higher Levels. The spell’s damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Rising Sun.name: Rising Sun
Rising Sun.description:
You shed the dazzling radiance of the sun in a 10-foot-radius burst, blinding all creatures entering or beginning their turn within this area. Your allies are immune to the blinding effect, but undead and fiends have disadvantage on their saving throw. Undead take 10d6 radiant damage every time they enter or start their turn in this area. A successful saving throw negates theblindedcondition and halves the damage.

The Dragon’s Hoard #9 © 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach

Mumchance.name: Mumchance
Mumchance.description:
For the duration, creatures in a 20-foot square within range cannot understand each other or creatures outside the area, and creatures outside the area cannot understand creatures in the area. A creature can make a DC 15Wisdom(Perception) check as an action to decipher up to 5 words.

Attempts to cast spells that include a verbal component require a DC 10Constitutionsaving throw to maintain concentration while in the area.

Creatures casting or affected bycomprehend languages, or similar magic, have advantage on theirWisdomchecks andConstitutionsaving throws against mumchance.Tonguesends the effects of mumchance on a creature immediately.

Lands of Theia - 5th Edition© 2024, Samurai Sheepdog; Authors: Steven Rasheed James, Kevin Glusing

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Commune With The City.name: Commune With The City
Commune With The City.components: V, S, M (map of the settlement you are in)
Commune With The City.description:
You draw upon the gestalt knowledge of all the residents of the settlement and ask up to three yes-or-no questions pertaining to the community in some way. You must ask your questions before the spell ends. If someone in the settlement knows the correct answer, you receive a correct answer for the question; otherwise you receive no answer at all. So if you cast the spell and ask, “Is the box of shadows within the Tower of (insert name)?” you will get an answer only if someone in the local community knows the answer. The local people whose knowledge provides these answers are unaware that the magic is using their knowledge, even if only one person knows the answer. You can cast this spell only within a settlement that is home to at least one hundred people.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Commune With The City.material_component: map of the settlement you are in

Open Mind.name: Open Mind
Open Mind.description:
You crush the mental defenses of the target, causing it to have disadvantage onWisdomandIntelligencesaving throws on a failed saving throw for as long as you concentrate on the spell and for 1 round after you stop concentrating on it. A successfulWisdomsaving throw negates this effect. If the target is currently using a spell or spell-like ability that grants it protection or immunity againstdivinationor enchant spells, you can attempt anIntelligence(Arcana) ability check to identify that spell as a free action when you touch the target. If you identify such an effect, you can forgo the normal effect of open mind and instead attempt todispelthat effect, as if you had castdispel magicin a 2nd level spell slot.

The Dragon’s Hoard #14 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

Mummification.name: Mummification
Mummification.description:
A living creature you see within range makes aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 8d8 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. In addition, a humanoid or other suitable creature reduced to0 Hit Pointsby this spell must make aWisdomsaving throw.

On a Failure, they rise 1d4 rounds later as amummy. A successful Remove Curse prevents this transformation.

Themummyhas no memory of its past life and follows the caster’s commands for 1 round/level, after which it becomes a free-willed undead creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 2d8 for each spell slot above 7.

Ancient Tombs (5E) © 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Alex Riggs, Anthony Adam, Jason Nelson, Loren Sieg, and Robert J. Grady

Buoyancy.name: Buoyancy
Buoyancy.components: V, S, M(a small cork and a pinch of bromine salt)
Buoyancy.description:
Select a number of objects within range that weigh less than 100 pounds total and do not normally float. You cause them to float upon a small layer of bubbles. This allows heavy objects such as gold, lead, stone, or even living creatures to float in water. It can also be used to raise up objects that have sunk.

At higher levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot higher than first, you increase the total weight of objects you can float by 100 pounds for each level above first.

Tome of Alchemy, © 2020, Necromancer Games; Author Courtney Campbell, Matt Finch

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Buoyancy.material_component: a small cork and a pinch of bromine salt

Crystal Casket.name: Crystal Casket
Crystal Casket.description:
You encase the target in a crystalline structure that is 10 inches thick. If the target fails aDexteritysaving throw, it is helpless, but held in stasis and will not age, need to eat, or breathe. A creature that succeeds on their saving throw isrestrainedbut not held in stasis for the duration or until the crystal is broken. The crystal blocks line of effect, but not line of sight, though the creature cannot be affected by any mental effects while in the crystal. The crystal has a damage threshold of 2 and 40hit points. If the crystal is broken, the creature is freed. A creature can break the crystal by using an action to make aStrengthcheck against the DC of the spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can target an additional creature for each slot level above 5th. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bumble.name: Bumble
Bumble.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or its initial attempt to interact with an object fails, as if the attempt never happened. If the target used an action to interact with the object, the action is lost. The target cannot attempt to interact with the same object again until the end of your next turn. This spell affects only a creature’s first attempt to interact with an object rather than ending an existing interaction. For instance, the spell can prevent the target from drawing a weapon from its sheath or picking a weapon up from the ground, but it cannot cause the target to drop a weapon it is already holding in its hand.

At Higher Levels. The spell prevents the target from interacting with the same object for a longer period at higher levels: 2 rounds at 5th level, 3 rounds at 11th level, and 4 rounds at 17th level.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Healing Tide.name: Healing Tide
Healing Tide.description:
Target: A creature you can see within range

You call forth thehealingpower of the sea, washing over a primary target within range and then leaping to additional targets. The primary target regainshit pointsequal to 5d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. Thehealingenergy then leaps to a second creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of the first target, causing it to regainhit pointsequal to 4d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

Thehealingenergy continues to leap to new targets within 30 feet of the last, with each successive target regaining 1d8 fewerhit pointsthan the previous one. The chain continues to leap until it either has no more valid targets within range, or until thehealingwould be less than 1d8. The spell can’t target the same creature more than once and has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the initialhealingincreases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Telepathic Bond.name: Telepathic Bond
Telepathic Bond.components: V, S, M(pieces of eggshell from two different kinds of creatures)
Telepathic Bond.description:
You forge a telepathic link among up to eight willing creatures of your choice within range, psychically linking each creature to all the others for the duration. Creatures withIntelligencescores of 2 or less aren’t affected by this spell.

Until the spell ends, the targets can communicate telepathically through the bond whether or not they have a common language. The communication is possible over any distance, though it can’t extend to other planes of existence.
Telepathic Bond.material_component: pieces of eggshell from two different kinds of creatures

Dust Cloud.name: Dust Cloud
Dust Cloud.description:
You create a 20-foot-radius sphere of billowing, swirling dust centered on a point within range. The sphere spreads around corners, and its area is heavily obscured. It lasts for the duration or until a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the radius of the cloud increases by 20 feet for each slot level above 1st.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Mind Thrust.name: Mind Thrust
Mind Thrust.description:
You divine the most vulnerable portions of the target’s mind and overload them with psychic information. The target takes 2d6 psychic damage, or half as much damage on a successful save. A creature failing its save cannot take bonusactionsfor 1 round.

Mind thrust does not affect creatures withIntelligence1 or creatures immune to thecharmedcondition.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 1st.

The Dragon’s Hoard #49© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Nick Hite, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Dan Dillon, Matt Kimmel, David N. Ross

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Fury Blossom.name: Fury Blossom
Fury Blossom.description:
You produce a bouquet of up to ten bunches of fiery red yarrow. A creature can eat the leaves of a bunch as an action to induce a warrior’s fugue. For the next minute, that creature cannot cast spells. Itsmelee attacksare made at advantage, and if they hit, they deal additional damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. If that creature would be reduced to0 hit pointsby anattack, they can instead choose to take a level ofexhaustionto remain at 1 hit point.

The yarrow loses its potency if it has not been consumed within 1 hour of casting this spell.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Smug Narcissism.name: Smug Narcissism
Smug Narcissism.components: V, S, M (shard of a broken mirror)
Smug Narcissism.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,warlock,wizard

You fill your target with overweening pride and vainglorious self-obsession about its own importance, talents, and attractiveness if it fails aCharismasaving throw. The target cannothelpcommenting on their own beauty and comparing it to the ugliness of others and is compelled to gaze on its own reflection whenever possible. The target’s vanity causes it to have disadvantage on allCharismachecks.

In combat situations, the target must attempt aWisdomsaving throw or spend its bonus action looking for some kind of reflecting surface and gazing at its own reflection.

In addition, if it fails this saving throw it becomes incredibly worried about enemies damaging its appearance and focuses on defense (such as casting a defensive spell likeshieldor using theDodgeaction) or retreat in combat during that round rather than risking its pretty face being marred.

The Dragon’s Hoard #21 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Bombard.name: Bombard
Bombard.components: V, S, M (shard of cooled magma)
Bombard.description:
A barrage of fiery projectiles begins falling in the shape of a cylinder that is 30 feet tall with a 15-foot-radius centered on a point within range. A creature that starts its turn there must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 fire damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knockedprone.

As a bonus action onyour turn, you can move the sphere up to 20 feet.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 6th.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Discord.name: Discord
Discord.description:
You disrupt the harmony between up to three creatures you can see within range. Each target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or become hostile to each other target until the start of your next turn. Until the spell ends, targets that failed the saving throw can’t help each other, target each other with beneficial spells or effects, or similarly work together on their turns. At the GM’s discretion, the creatures mightattackeach other, might compete for the tastiest among you and your friends, or similarly act against each other.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Just Reversal.name: Just Reversal
Just Reversal.description:
You protect yourself against mind-controlling spells (such ascharm personandsuggestion) of 3rd level or lower. If you make your saving throw against such a spell, the spell has no effect on you and instead targets the caster, using the slot level, spell save DC,attackbonus, and spellcasting ability of the caster. If the caster fails their save, the spell takes effect on them as if you had cast it upon them.

This spell only affects spells that target only you, not area of effect spells.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the level of mind-controlling spells it can turn upon their source increases by 1 for each slot level above 5th. Thus, using a 4th-level spell slot protects against mind-controlling spells up to 4th level, a 5th-level spell slot protects against ones up to 5th level, and so on.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Heartfire.name: Heartfire
Heartfire.description:
You ignite the inner fire within you and your companions, stoking it into a magical flame against your enemies. A gout of fire emerges from your chest and streaks toward one creature you can see within range. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

When you cast this spell, up to three friendly creatures within 30 feet of you that can see you can each use areactionto lend its heartfire to yours. For each creature that joins its heartfire with yours, the spell’s damage increases by 1d6.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the primary damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Obscryation.name: Obscryation
Obscryation.description:
A creature you touch appears normal unless magic is used to view it remotely (likearcane eye,clairvoyanceorscrying). To the caster of the remote sensor, the creature’s face and voice are obscured such that they cannot be identified: faces appear as blurred smears with no recognizable features and voices are muted. A viewer can make aWisdom(Insight) check at disadvantage to get a general sense of what the target is doing (for example, what it’s looking at by the direction its facing, its emotional state from how it gestures, etc. ), but not detailed information. The spell does not conceal the rest of the target, and distinctive dress or other features are readily identifiable.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Dishearten.name: Dishearten
Dishearten.duration: and attempt to convince their allies that fighting
Dishearten.description:
You choose a target within range and force them to live out dozens of ways you could kill them and those present that they fear to lose. They must make anIntelligencesaving throw. On a success, they understand that the visions were illusions; on a failure, they arefrightenedfor the duration and attempt to convince their allies that fighting you is hopeless and that they should flee.

Devouring worms: The worms crawl in, the worms crawl out … the worms crawl all over you.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Body Blaze.name: Body Blaze
Body Blaze.description:
You shroud your body with flames and leave a trail of fire behind you when you move that forms a 20-foot-high wall of opaque flames just a few inches thick. The wall occupies each square of ground you pass through and lasts until the spell ends. It does not form if you Climb, Fly, or Swim but resumes when you reach a horizontal surface again.

Creatures or small, loose objects (such as arrows) entering the wall or ending their turn in it take 4d6 Fire damage, even if they pass through more than one square of the fiery wall. If you knock a creaturePronewhile surrounded by the Body Blaze, you can move through their space, forming the fiery curtain there. The flames created by your Body Blaze do not harm you but do block your vision.

Any part of the blazing wall that takes 20 Cold damage in 1 round is extinguished; this does not affect any other part of the wall.

Static Field.name: Static Field
Static Field.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You create a field of crackling static energy in a 50-foot-radius sphere at a point you choose within range. The area isdifficult terrainfor creatures other than you. Each creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 4d8 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to move the static field up to 10 feet in any direction.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 lightning damage for each slot level above 5th.

True Alchemy.name: True Alchemy
True Alchemy.components: V, S, M (primordial matter from before time worth 100,000 gp)
True Alchemy.description:
You touch an object or structure no bigger than a 50-foot cube and disrupt its form with magic, permanently transmuting it into a form of your choice. When you affect an object in this manner, you choose what properties it loses or gains (such ashit points, AC, or other properties). However, the object cannot be transformed into something worth more 100,000 gp in raw materials, nor can its dimensions be increased beyond that of a 50-foot cube. If the object you touched is a magical item, you can instead transform it into another item of the same rarity. To affect an artifact in this manner, you must first succeed on a DC 40 saving throw of a type equal to your spellcasting ability. On a failure, you take arcane damage1equal to your hit point maximum.

Anything you transform the target into in this manner must be something that exists or has existed in your universe.

If you attempt to transmute a target into something that has never existed in your universe, the spell fails.

1Arcane damage is an Epic damage type.

Last Light.description:
You summon the last burst of light from a celestial body, casting a radiant explosion at a point you choose. Each creature within a 30-foot radius of that point is engulfed in the celestial radiance, taking 12d10 radiant damage and becomingblindedif they fail on aConstitutionsaving throw. Creaturesblindedby this spell make anotherConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on themselves on a success.

Head of The Medusa.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (amedusamask worth at least 1,000 gp)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You complete the spell and don themedusa-head mask.

The eyes in themedusa’s mask glow and its mouth opens in a violent snarl. Any enemy that meets your gaze, must make aConstitutionsaving throw or bepetrified. A creature can avert their eyes but you can focus your gaze on a target as a action to force a saving throw on them though they get advantage on the saving throw.

Dream Banquet.name: Dream Banquet
Dream Banquet.duration: 1 day/level Dreaming Descriptor Spells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest.
Dream Banquet.description:
Dreaming DescriptorSpells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest. You must have the spell slots needed to do so when you go to sleep, but the same slots are also expended when you wake—you cannot regain them for use the next day. You cannot cast more than 8 spell-levels worth of dreaming spells in a single night. These spells generally have casting times of hours, but those are hours during which you are asleep. Regardless of how long you sleep, you cannot cast more than 8 hours worth of dreaming spells in one 24-hour period. Dreaming spells with a duration of “1 day or until expended” also end if you sleep for 1 hour or more before they are expended.

You cause up to sleeping creatures within range to dream of a sumptuous spread of their favorite food and drink anytime they sleep during the spell’s duration, from which they can eat and drink to their content. This allows each creature to avoid gaining any penalties for lack of food and water for 1 day after each time it sleeps, though penalties already suffered for lack of nutrition are not removed through access to this dream food. Each creature also gains advantage on saves against ingested poisons.
