World Wave.name: World Wave
World Wave.description:
You cause natural terrain (including water, forest, desert, tundra, and so on) to surge beneath you and propel you with devastating force over great distances. The world wave travels in a direction you choose at the time of casting and cannot be redirected afterwards. It rises in a 30-foot-high surge resembling a tidal wave, extending 10 feet in front of you and behind you and 100 feet to the right and left of you in a straight line, surging forward at a speed of 200 feet per round. You can stand or sit on the crest of the world wave and treat it as stable ground and can grant up to 20 additional creatures the ability to travel along with you atop the wave’s crest.

Objects, creatures, or phenomena connected to the natural world, including animals, plants, elementals, and fey, simply rise up and down with the wave as it passes without being harmed as the wave passes by.

As above, you may choose to allow them to stay atop the world wave and move along with it; if you do not, they simply slide down its trailing edge and are left behind. Other creatures, objects, or structures in the world wave’s path take 6d6 bludgeoning damage, or 12d6 for aberrations and undead, and must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be forcedproneand pushed 20 feet in the direction the world wave is moving. Humanoids with at least 1 level in therangerordruidclass are considered part of the natural world. If cast on another plane, creatures native to that plane are treated as part of the natural world and are unharmed by the world wave.

The world wave can travel up or down slopes up to 45 degrees. If it encounters a surface it cannot traverse, such as barriers made primarily of fire or molten rock, open air (including canyons or cliffs), or man-made barriers, such as cities and castles. It flows over or around obstacles less than 30 feet high or 100 feet wide, with creatures riding on it harmlessly displaced to the side to avoid the obstacle. If the obstacle is higher and wider than this, the world wave stops moving and collapses 1 round later. A world wave cannot be cast underground unless in a very large cavern or underground lake large enough for its entire area to fit.

Special: You can create a smaller world wave as a gentle swell only 5 feet high, which deals only 1d6 damage to unnatural creatures (as described above), or 2d6 damage to aberrations or undead. This swell moves at 100 feet per round and continues moving for up to 16 hours or until you command it to stop without requiring concentration.

You and any other passengers can lie down and sleep atop this version of the world wave.

The Dragon’s Hoard #25 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

Soul Siblings.duration: is increased to 1 hour. It increases to 8 hours with
Soul Siblings.description:
You bind luck and fate between two willing creatures. When those creatures are adjacent, each of them gains a +1 bonus on all saving throws. In addition, when either character must make a saving throw, both creatures can roll the save (including any modifiers that affect them) and both creatures can take the better result. If either save succeeds, both creatures succeed on the save. If both creatures fail the save, both are affected by the failed save even if whatever prompted the saving throw would normally only affect one of them. After triggering this effect, or if either creature moves more than 100 feet away from the other, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level, the duration is increased to 1 hour. It increases to 8 hours with a 4th-level slot and to 24 hours with a 5th-level slot.

Stormshot.name: Stormshot
Stormshot.description:
You channel the primal energy of storms into your free hand or spellcasting focus before releasing an instantaneous blast of lightning at a creature you can see within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 lightning damage. If the target is wearing armor or carrying a weapon made of metal, it instead takes 1d10 lightning damage.

This spell’s damage increases by one die when you reach 5th level (2d8 or 2d10), 11th level (3d8 or 3d10), and 17th level (4d8 and 4d10).

Master of Swift Strikes.name: Master of Swift Strikes
Master of Swift Strikes.components: V, S, M (single hair from a young rabbit)
Master of Swift Strikes.description:
You move and fight with exceptional speed and agility. You gain the ability to make one additional weaponattackper round. If you do not make anattackonyour turn, your walking speed is doubled. This increase applies to all movement types you have, such as climbing or swimming, and your jump distance is increased accordingly. Additionally, during any turn in which you do not all of your attacks, you gain Advantage on attack rolls,Dexteritysaving throws, and a +2 bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn. This spell does not stack with similar effects, such ashaste.

The Dragon’s Hoard #58© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, James-Levi Cooke.

Holy Verdict: Redemption.name: Holy Verdict: Redemption
Holy Verdict: Redemption.description:
You become an emissary ofangelsand the spirits of redemption to reach those who seek forgiveness. You and the target sit up to 10 feet away from each other, and you speak with the target about its past sins and the reasons for theirsearchfor redemption, embellishing the dialogue with the magical words of the divine. You speak for the casting time and the conversation acts as the material component of the spell. At the end of it, if the divine find the target’s intentions to be righteous, they present the target with a quest that must be completed within the next 77 days. If the target succeeds in their quest, it is redeemed of all sins.

For these 77 days, the target has advantage on all saving throws unless it deviates from the path of redemption.

Solid Note.name: Solid Note
Solid Note.description:
You give physical form to a single musical note that floats suspended anywhere within range. This music note can be spiked or smooth, simple or convoluted, and any color you wish, and you may cause it to shed light as a candle.

The solid note is the size of your hand. The solid note is stationary, and any creature trying to move through the space it occupies must either squeeze around it (if there is enough room to allow squeezing) or must push past it with a successfulStrengthcheck (DC 10 + your proficiency modifier). You also can hang objects from the solid note, as it can support up to 500 pounds. If you overload the solid note or a creature succeeds on theirStrengthcheck against it, it disappears. The solid note also can be attacked; it is AC 10 and has 1 hit point.

The Dragon’s Hoard #18 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Cowardice.name: Cowardice
Cowardice.description:
A creature you touch is filled with dread and a craven need to save themselves. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or have disadvantage on saving throws against thefrightenedand demoralized conditions for the duration of the spell. If the target is normally immune to such effects, they are no longer immune for the duration but they gain advantage on saving throws against such effects.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

GoodHope - Crushing Despair (5E), © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Shifting Sand.name: Shifting Sand
Shifting Sand.description:
You cause a 20-foot-radius circle of earthen or sandy ground to shift and churn. The area is treated asdifficult terrainand all tracks through the area are wiped away. Creatures within the area have disadvantage onDexteritychecks, and a creature entering the shifting sand or beginning its turn in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw or become mired in the clinging sand, taking a -2 penalty onattackrolls and AC and having their speed halved for as long as they remain in the shifting sand. A creature attempting to move while mired must make a secondDexteritysaving throw or fallprone.

As a bonus action, you can move the shifting sand 10 feet.

Large or smaller creatures mired orpronein the shifting sand move along with it, as do objects that are not fixed in place. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. The shifting sand itself can move around fixed obstacles like statues and pillars and under doorways and through similar small gaps but creatures or objects moving with it do not.

Shifting sand has no effect on floors of stone, wood, metal, or other non-earthen surfaces.

The Dragon’s Hoard #49© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Nick Hite, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Dan Dillon, Matt Kimmel, David N. Ross

Wracking Sobs.name: Wracking Sobs
Wracking Sobs.description:
ComponentsV S M (a vial of tears)

You cause the target to be wracked with debilitating sobs and torrents of tears. For the duration of the spell, the target ispoisonedandblinded. A successfulWisdomsaving throw negates the effect entirely.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

Hide From Enemies.name: Hide From Enemies
Hide From Enemies.description:
You touch up to six creatures to be warded. Creatures that are hostile to warded creatures cannot see, hear, or smell creatures warded by this spell unless they succeed aWisdomsaving throw. Even extraordinary or supernatural sensory capabilities such as blindsight or tremorsense cannot detect or locate warded creatures. Creatures withIntelligenceof 2 or less can perceive the target normally, as their motivations are based on instinct and survival rather than actual hostility.

Ruin’s Embrace.name: Ruin’s Embrace
Ruin’s Embrace.description:
You touch a living creature and infuse it with necrotic energy. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, it takes 4d10 necrotic damage, or half as much damage on a successful save. If this damage reduces the target to0 hit points, you regainhit pointsequal to half the damage dealt.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 2nd.

Rune of Supreme Enhancement.name: Rune of Supreme Enhancement
Rune of Supreme Enhancement.components: V, S, M (gems and diamonds worth up to 500,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
Rune of Supreme Enhancement.description:
You inscribe a supreme rune onto a non-magical item, granting it the effects of a rune or magic item of Legendary rarity.

At the Gamemaster’s discretion, the Rune of Supreme Enhancement spell can be also used for crafting Artifacts, the most legendary and unique items ever existed. The creation of an artifact should be an extraordinary event in a campaign, typically involving a quest of epic proportions. Such quests might include seeking out ancient and forgotten lore about runecarving, undertaking a perilous journey to find a legendary material required for the rune, or even fulfilling a prophecy or a task set by a deity or ancient being. In any case, crafting such a powerful item should be a memorable part of the campaign, with implications for the story and the characters involved.

Battlecry.name: Battlecry
Battlecry.description:
By infusing a fervent shout with mystical energy from the Source, you can overwhelm your enemies. Confronted with your mystical might, lesser foes find themselvesstunned. You let out a thunderous cry that strikes fear into the heart of your enemies. Each creature in a 15-foot cube originating from you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature isstunneduntil the end of their next turn.

Focused Scrutiny.name: Focused Scrutiny
Focused Scrutiny.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,paladin,ranger,wizard

You focus your senses on a single creature you can perceive, making you highly sensitive to its mannerisms,reactions, and body language and allowing you to easily sense its state of mind and helping you influence it. You gain advantage onWisdom(Insight),Wisdom(Perception),Charisma(Intimidation), andCharisma(Persuasion) checks against it, as well asWisdom(Survival) checks made to track the target creature. If the creature attacks you, it takes a -1 penalty on itsattackrolls as you are able to anticipate its movements.

You cannot have focused scrutiny on more than one creature at a time. If you cast the spell again on a different creature, any previous focused scrutiny spell ends.

The Dragon’s Hoard #41 © 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke

Enchanted Bloom.name: Enchanted Bloom
Enchanted Bloom.components: V, S, M(a rose cut within the past 24 hours and ritual oils worth 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
Enchanted Bloom.description:
You spend an hour anointing a rose with scented oils and imbuing it with fey magic. The first creature other than you that touches the rose before the spell ends pricks itself on the thorns and must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, the creature falls into a deep slumber for 24 hours, and it can be awoken only by thegreater restorationspell or similar magic or if you choose to end the spell as an action. While slumbering, the creature doesn’t need to eat or drink, and it doesn’t age.

Each time the creature takes damage, it makes a newCharismasaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the creature.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of a higher level, the duration of the slumber increases to 7 days with a 6th-level slot, to 30 days with a 7th-level slot, to 180 days with an 8th-level slot, and to a year with a 9th-level spell slot.

Flame’s Kiss.name: Flame’s Kiss
Flame’s Kiss.description:
Flames erupt from your hand, burning a creature you try to touch and making it susceptible to further burns.

Make a melee spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 fire damage, and the next time it takes fire damage before the start of your next turn, the target takes an additional 1d4 fire damage.

The spell’s damage (both initial and later) increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4) and 17th level (4d4).

Power Word: Sicken.name: Power Word: Sicken
Power Word: Sicken.description:
You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving them feeling sickened. If the target has less than 50hit pointsor fewer, it becomespoisoned.

Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

Thepoisonedtarget must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this poisoned effect ends.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

Daylight.name: Daylight
Daylight.description:
A 60-foot-radius sphere of light spreads out from a point you choose within range. The sphere is bright light and sheds dim light for an additional 60 feet.

If you chose a point on an object you are holding or one that isn’t being worn or carried, the light shines from the object and moves with it. Completely covering the affected object with an opaque object, such as a bowl or a helm, blocks the light.

If any of this spell’s area overlaps with an area of darkness created by aspellof 3rd level or lower, the spell that created the darkness is dispelled.

Circle Regeneration.name: Circle Regeneration
Circle Regeneration.description:
You gain power from a myconid circle.

You regain fourhit pointsper round. If you take acid or fire damage, this trait doesn’t function at the start of your next turn.

You die only if you startyour turnwith0 hit pointsand don’tregenerate.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Call Shadow Mastiff.name: Call Shadow Mastiff
Call Shadow Mastiff.description:
You tap into the power of the Plane of Shadow and conjure a large dog made of pure shadow in an unoccupied space you can see within range.

The shadow mastiff disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. The mastiff is friendly to you and your companions. Rollinitiativefor the mastiff, which has its own turns. It obeys verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to it, the mastiff defends itself from hostile creatures, but otherwise takes noactions. The GM has the shadow mastiff ’s statistics, using a dire wolf, except it is a monstrosity, it doubles its proficiency bonus when makingDexterity(Stealth) checks, and it has the Bay action and theShadow Stealthbonus action, both of which are described below:

Mass Necrotic Word.name: Mass Necrotic Word
Mass Necrotic Word.description:
Duration2 + 1/2 spellcasting modifier rounds

NoteThis spell is a rework of the core spell of the same name.

You speak a word of power filling creatures in a 30-foot-radius sphere with a minor amount of negative energy. For an undead creature this causes them to heal 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns.

If the creature is living, they instead take one necrotic damage per round at the beginning of their turn.

This spell has no effect on constructs.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th or higher, the damage healed or dealt each round increases to 2. The damage and healing further increases to 3 if you instead use a 9th-level spell slot.

Read Magic: Vigor (5E) © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions; Authors: Connor Bates

Conceal.name: Conceal
Conceal.description:
You conceal an object no larger than 1 cubic foot on your person. Skill checks to find the object on your person have disadvantage for the duration.

Unwelcome Halo.name: Unwelcome Halo
Unwelcome Halo.description:
This spell causes one creature you can see to glow as if surrounded by a halo of light. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed saving throw, the halo sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius from the creature, and dim light for additional 20 feet. This light effectively gives away the creature’s location, and imposes disadvantage onDexterity(Stealth) checks when the creature is able to hide at all. At the end of each of the creature’s turn, it may make a new saving throw; on a success, the spell ends.

Forest Kingdom Campaign Compendium 5e© 2017, Legendary Games; Lead Designer Jason Nelson. Authors: Clinton J. Boomer, Benjamin Bruck, Matt Goodall, Tim Hitchcock, N. Flame Wave.name: Flame Wave
Flame Wave.description:
A rushing burst of fire rips out from you in a rolling wave, filling a 40-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 fire damage and is pushed 20 feet away from you, or takes half as much damage and isn’t pushed on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

Deep Magic: Elemental Magic © 2017 Open Design; Author: Dan Dillon.

Heightened Reflexes.name: Heightened Reflexes
Heightened Reflexes.description:
You enhance the reflexes of every ally within range. At any point within the spell’s duration that an affected ally must make aDexteritycheck orDexteritysaving throw, they can choose to gain advantage on that roll. Alternatively, if they have disadvantage on aDexteritycheck orDexteritysaving throw, they can choose to negate that disadvantage. This does not require an action and has no effect if you already have advantage on the roll. After using either effect, the spell ends for that individual. A creature cannot have more than one heightened reflexes spell in effect at a time.

The Dragon’s Hoard #41 © 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke

Flamewalk Portal.name: Flamewalk Portal
Flamewalk Portal.description:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a small rune next to a source of fire. The source can be a fireplace, campfire, signal beacon, or other source of fire that is large enough for a Medium creature to stand in the fire. This rune lasts for 30 days, and it remains even if the fire is extinguished.

For the duration, when you cast this spell again, you can link any two runes together to form a gateway between the two locations. The two runes linked in this way must be on the same plane of existence, and each rune must have an active fire source within 5 feet of it. While casting this spell, you know if a rune you inscribed has an active fire source within 5 feet of it. For 1 minute or until you end the effect as a bonus action, any creature within 5 feet of one of the fire sources can use 5 feet of its movement to step into that fire source and exit from the other fire source, appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the destination fire source. A creature doesn’t take fire damage from stepping into the fire. When this effect ends, the runes disappear from both locations, ending the spell if those were the only two runes inscribed with this spell.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Phantom Army.name: Phantom Army
Phantom Army.description:
Classes: Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You summon phantom soldiers to fill a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range. When the army appears, each creature in the sphere must make aWisdomsaving throw. A creature takes 4d10 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must also make this saving throw when it enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 5th.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Unadulterated Loathing.name: Unadulterated Loathing
Unadulterated Loathing.description:
You fill the target with a terrible loathing aimed at a specific creature. At the time of the casting, you designate a single creature as the object of the target’s revulsion. Thereafter, the target does all it can to remain at least 60 feet away from the object of its loathing. As soon as the target moves within this range, the target suffers disadvantage on ability checks andattackrolls until it can again get away from the object of its revulsion. If traveling beyond 60 feet of the object of its loathing would place the target in obvious physical danger, the target can attempt a second saving throw to break the spell’s effect.

Legendary Villains: Dark Druids (5E)© 2017, Legendary Games; Authors Clinton J. Boomer, Jason Nelson, and RJ Grady.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Illusory Script.name: Illusory Script
Illusory Script.components: S, M(a lead-based ink worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes)
Illusory Script.description:
You write on parchment, paper, or some other suitable writing material and imbue it with a potent illusion that lasts for the duration.

To you and any creatures you designate when you cast the spell, the writing appears normal, written in your hand, and conveys whatever meaning you intended when you wrote the text. To all others, the writing appears as if it were written in an unknown or magical script that is unintelligible. Alternatively, you can cause the writing to appear to be an entirely different message, written in a different hand and language, though the language must be one you know.

Should the spell be dispelled, the original script and the illusion both disappear.

A creature withtruesightcan read the hidden message.
Illusory Script.material_component: a lead-based ink worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes

Toast The Goddess.name: Toast The Goddess
Toast The Goddess.description:
When you cast this spell, you create six full tankards of beer or ale that resemble the tankard and beverage used in the casting.

Creatures that consume one of the tankards within the next hour gaintemporary hit pointsequal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Violent Fortification.name: Violent Fortification
Violent Fortification.duration: Concentration, up to 6 seconds. The savage nature of combat influences the invisible energies of an area. By briefly tapping into this energy,
Violent Fortification.description:
The savage nature of combat influences theinvisibleenergies of an area. By briefly tapping into this energy, you can convert it into its opposite. When you cast this spell, you must concentrate on it until the beginning of your next turn. Once you begin concentrating on this spell, you cannot take any bonusactions,reactions, or move. If you are interrupted and your concentration is broken, the spell fails. At the beginning of your next turn, all damage allied creatures within range have dealt during your concentration is converted totemporary hit pointsand distributed evenly among all allied creatures within range up to a maximum of 15 per creature.

5E: Age of Antiquity Adventure and Intrigue in the Ancient World © 2019 Aruzian Publishing, Stephen Delucchi, Marcus Lundin

Protective Lullaby.name: Protective Lullaby
Protective Lullaby.description:
You ward the target’s minds and souls using a traditional lullaby to protect them in their sleep. While sleeping, the targets gain advantage to wisdom saving throws and against effects that specifically target sleeping orunconsciouscreatures.

Targets sleeping with an attuned somnifer are also immune to effects that call for a wisdom saving throw. If a target with an attuned somnifer loses their somnifer before the next time they go tosleep, the benefits of protective lullaby are suppressed and the target has misfortune on wisdom saving throws. This penalty lasts until the target is reunited with their somnifer, or the duration of protective lullaby would expire.

Now I Lay Me Down To Sleep, 5e © 2020, Owen K.C. Stephens; Author: Dustin Knight. Project manager and Planning: Lj Stephens. Bon Vivant: Stan!

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Dream Spores.name: Dream Spores
Dream Spores.description:
You release hallucinogenic spores in a 10-foot-radius sphere.

Those within the area must succeed at aConstitutionsaving throw or be captivated by the hallucinations they experience. While captivated, they arestunned. A captivated creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a successful save.

The spores do not follow you if they move, and they dissipate after the spell duration ends.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Life Robber.name: Life Robber
Life Robber.description:
You imbue a projectile or piece of ammunition with necromantic energy, linking its strike to your health.

When you hit a creature with the enchanted ammunition, you heal a number of hp equal to half the damage taken by the target. If thishealingbrings you above your maximum hp, the excess is gained as temporary hp that last for 1 hour. You cannot gain more temporary hp than one-half your normal Hit Point maximum.

The projectile loses its potency if not used within 1 round.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you heal hp equal to the damage dealt.

On a failed save, it takes 7d10 psychic damage and becomes mentally disrupted for the duration. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and does not suffer the mental disruption.

While under the effects of this spell, the creature’s skin, eyes, hair, and features take on a gleaming, metallic appearance, and the target gains a +2 bonus toCharisma, and +1 bonus to its Armor Class and saving throws against attacks or effects by evil creatures. When you cast this spell, choose up to three creatures within range that can see the apparition. Each target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becharmedby the apparition until this spell ends. Pillar of Thousand Blessings.description:
You conjure a 10-foot tall cylindrical marble pillar of a 5-foot radius within range that has decorative carvings, small water fountains, ornamental plants, oil lamps, and celestial writings on it. The pillar remains for the spell’s duration and then turns to dust, leaving no traces of its existence behind.

The pillar offers special benefits to creatures who use their action to offer a copper coin worth at least 1 copper piece.

Once a copper piece has been offered to the pillar in this way, it cannot be retrieved by any means. Each creature that donated at least 1 copper piece must choose up to six benefits from the following list with which they are affected for 1 hour.

A creature cannot choose the same benefit twice.

When standing on a riverbank or on the shore of some other body of water, you summon a ferry spirit and its boat, which appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The spirit disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. The spirit is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Rollinitiativefor the creature, which has its own turns. It takes you and up to 1 companion per your level across the river or body of water (no action required by you) or to other locations along the same water. If you don’t issue any such commands, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes noactions.

If your concentration is broken, the ferry and its guide don’t disappear. Instead, you lose control of the conjured spirit, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it mightattack. An uncontrolled ferryman can’t be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it.

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the boat can take you and your companions across a planar boundary into the Ethereal Plane and then exit on another body of water. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, it can traverse the River Styx between planes, taking you and your companions to distant parts of the multiverse.

You place a magical command on up to six creatures that you can see within range, forcing them to carry out some service or refrain from some action or course of activity as you decide. Each creature that can understand you must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomecharmedby you for the duration. While a creature ischarmedby you, it pursues the suggested course of action to the best of its ability. A creature that can’t understand you is unaffected by the spell.

You can issue any command you choose, short of an activity that would result in certain death. Should you issue a suicidal command, the spell ends. A creature that completes the assigned task is under no further compulsion from the spell.

You can end the spell early by using an action to dismiss it. Aremove curse,greater restoration, orwishspell also ends it, although a creature subject to greatergeaswill not willingly allow itself to be released.

The target takes an extra 2d6 necrotic damage and becomes visible if it’sinvisible, being limned with eerie radiance that sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius, and it can’t becomeinvisibleuntil the spell ends.

Draconic Reservoir.description:
For the duration, you haveresistanceagainst one type of damage, which must match the damage dealt by the dragon scale used as the component of the spell. Whenever you take damage of that type, your draconic reservoir stores 1 point of energy for each hit point of damage you ignore because of yourresistance. Your draconic reservoir can store a maximum of 60hit points, and once you reach this limit you lose yourresistanceto that damage type.

When you hit with a melee or ranged weapon attack, as a bonus action you can discharge some of your stored energy, adding 1d10 damage of the type you have stored to the damage otherwise dealt by the attack. If the attack is a critical hit, you can instead add 10 damage of that type.

If you cast a spell that deals the same type of damage, as a bonus action you can discharge stored energy in the same way, adding 1d10 damage to the damage normally dealt by the spell.

Damage dealt by using your draconic reservoir cannot exceed the points remaining in your draconic reservoir. Your draconic reservoir cannot be refilled; expending points from it does not allow you to then absorb further damage. Once all energy is released, the spell ends.

If the caramel isn’t anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the conjured caramel collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Caramel layered over a flat surface has a depth of 5 feet. Each creature that starts its turn in the caramel or that enters it during its turn must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature isrestrainedas long as it remains in the caramel or until it breaks free. A creaturerestrainedby the caramel can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longerrestrained. The caramel is flammable. Any 5-foot cube of caramel exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire. The resulting ice is also treated asdifficult terrainfor any creature moving across it. In temperatures above freezing, the ice remains for 1 hour for each cubic foot of volume before melting away.

Unless removed, the target takes 1d8 piercing damage at the end of each of its next two turns.

The creature remains fully aware of its surroundings and can engage in light activity, such as standing guard, reading, or conversing, without any interruption to the rest provided by the spell. Anything that causes more intense activity, such as combat or sustained travel cancels the spell.

Arduous Shuffle.description:
All creatures in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you that have fewerhit pointsthan you when you cast the spell are compelled to dance a swaying, side-to-side shuffle-step. Any creature that can’t becharmedis immune to the effects of this spell. An affected creature has its movement halved, cannot usereactions, and can make only one weapon or spellattackon its turn. At the beginning of its turn, a creature in the area can choose to take 1d4 levels ofexhaustionto end the effect of this spell on itself.

You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a sphere with a radius of up 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made of 10 by 10 foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. The wall is six inches thick and lasts for the duration of the spell, dissipating as a strong breeze when the duration ends.

If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it is formed, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall and must succeed at aDexteritysave or suffer 5d6 slashing damage, half damage with a successful save. The wall is clear, but blocks effects and attacks that attempt to pass through it, as well as creatures.

Until this spell ends, the target has disadvantage on ability checks. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends. After failing three of these saving throws, the spell’s effects last for the duration.

Related to linnorms according to some scholars, or to sea serpents according to others, the tarantasio haunts peaceful lakes in the woods. People deem it responsible for persistent fog banks, epidemics, and rotting plants in the whole region around its den. They spend most of their time underwater, but when prey approaches their huge, horned head emerges from the lake’s troubled waters on top of a long, snakelike body, with flames and noxious fumes erupting from its mouth and flared nostrils.

Thunderwave.description:
A wave of thunderous force sweeps out from you. Each creature in a 15-foot cube originating from you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t pushed.

In addition, unsecured objects that are completely within the area of effect are automatically pushed 10 feet away from you by the spell’s effect, and the spell emits a thunderous boom audible out to 300 feet.

You must walk a path of at least one mile while casting this spell, taking winding and erratic paths and marking runes ofconfusionand misdirection into the earth as you go. You then designate up to 10 1-mile squares, each of which must be adjacent to at least one other square, creating a subtle but powerful illusion that leads creatures astray when trying to move through the area. A creature trying to reach a destination within the labyrinthine wilds must succeed on anIntelligencesaving throw to successfully navigate the illusion, or else they wander aimlessly for 2d4 hours before arriving back at the place where they entered the area with no memory of their wanderings but having gained 1 level ofexhaustionfrom the journey.

If multiple creatures are traveling together through the labyrinthine wilds, whichever creature is leading the way, guiding the others, or at the front of their group makes the saving throw. A creature proficient inSurvivalgains a +2 bonus on their saving throw against labyrinthine wilds.

If there are other creatures in the group proficient inSurvival, each of them adds an additional +1 to the leader’s saving throw, to a maximum of +3.

Creatures in the labyrinthine wilds are not confused,charmed, or otherwise impaired, and combat within the area proceeds normally. This spell has no effect within a city, village, or town, but roads, maps, signposts, landmarks, and other guidings do not help navigate the area.

You fill a target creature with dread, fearful that death is around every corner, haunted by the image of menacing spectral raven. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw or else they become haunted by the vision of a large shadowy raven, gripping them with fear during their waking hours and denying them restful sleep. If they succeed at this initial Wisdom saving throw they are frightened for 1 minute.

They can circumvent the raven by walking around it in a wide arc, but they can get no closer than the distance at which it first appeared. Success means they are still frightened but may approach. However, if they end their turn adjacent to the ravenwight they take 3d6 necrotic damage as their life force is disrupted. The creature must also make a Wisdom saving throw when it completes a long rest, failure means it has 1 level of exhaustion and does not gain the benefits of the long rest. The exhaustion does not stack, but is replaced each time the target takes a long rest. You may use an action to cause the ravenwight to appear in a square of your choice within 30 ft of the target.

If a creature you designate within range fails aCharismasaving throw, you cause the target’s shadow to come to life and reveal one of the creature’s most scandalous secrets: some fact that the target would not want widely known (GM’s choice). When casting the spell, you choose whether everyone present will hear the secret, in which case the shadow speaks loudly in a twisted version of the target’s voice, or if the secret is whispered only to you. The shadow speaks in the target’s native language.

If the target does not have a scandalous secret or does not have a spoken language, the spell fails as if the creature’s saving throw had succeeded.

If the secret was spoken aloud, the target takes a –2 penalty toCharismachecks involving anyone who was present when it was revealed. This penalty lasts until the target finishes a long rest.

Glyph of Summoning.description:
Target: A surface or object within range

Classes: Bard, Cleric, Summoner, Wizard

When you cast this spell, you inscribe a magical glyph on a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, scroll, or chest) to conceal the glyph. If you choose a surface, the glyph cancoveran area of up to 10 feet in diameter. If you choose an object, it must remain in its place; if the object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearlyinvisibleand requires anIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be found.

You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. The trigger must be a circumstance that occurs within 30 feet of the glyph, and it can be as general or as detailed as you like (for example, summoning a creature when a door is opened or when a specific creature enters the area). Once triggered, the glyph glows briefly, then disappears, summoning a creature and ending the spell.

You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind, or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don’t trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password or act in a specific way.

When the glyph is triggered, a creature of Challenge Rating 3 or lower appears in the nearest unoccupied space within 10 feet of the glyph’s surface. You choose the creature’s form at the time of casting, and it can be of any creature type other than humanoid. When casting the spell, you designate how the summoned creature will act upon appearing, such as defending an area, attacking intruders, or following a specific individual. The creature follows these instructions to the best of its ability. If no action is specified, it defends itself but takes no otheractions. The summoned creature remains for 1 hour or until it drops to0 hit points.

If the glyph is dispelled before being triggered, the stored summoning magic is lost.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the maximum Challenge Rating of the summoned creature increases by 1 per slot level above 3rd.

Food harvested regrows within a week. After one year, the land slowly reverts to its normal fertility, unable to stave off the march of nature.

Living creatures that take a short rest within the area of a bloom spell receive the maximumhit pointsfor Hit Dice expended. Bloom counters the effects of a desolation spell.

For the duration, the weapon gains that damage type in addition to its normal damage type. The weapon also becomes magical, if it isn’t already. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the space you just left must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from your original space. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed.

If a pushed creature strikes a solid surface, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was pushed. If a pushed creature is pushed into another creature, that creature must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or take the same damage and be knockedprone.

Candle.description:
This spell allows the caster to enchant a candle with any abjuration,divination, enchantment, or illusion spell they know, infusing the candle with the spell.

Choose a spell that you are able to cast from one of those schools of magic. The chosen spell must have a duration of at least 1 minute and have a spell level no greater than 5th. When you cast this spell you also cast the chosen spell, expending spell slots and material components for both. When you do so the candle used as the material component for the casting is filled with the magic of the chosen spell. Whoever lights the candle can then cast the stored spell, and as long as the candle is burning the chosen spell’s effect is manifested. The spell’s range and any possible targets are limited to a radius of 10 feet from the candle. If the spell requires the caster to use a spellcasting ability or spell save DC, it uses yours.

The candle can burn for an amount of time equal to the chosen spell’s duration before it burns out. For example, a candle infused withcharm personwill burn for up to 1 hour, while adetect magiccandle would burn for up to 10 minutes. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts while the candle is burning.

The user can extinguish the candle at will, or it can be put out by a magically created wind such as from thegust of windspell. It cannot be extinguished by non-magical means, and it will even burn under water.

If the candle is extinguished before it is completely burnt out, you can relight the candle as an action, at which point the chosen spell’s effect begins again.

You can only enchant one candle at a time. If you cast this spell again before the first candle has completely burned out, it melts into a heap of worthless wax.

A feather made of water appears in your hand in frozen form and deals cold damage instead of piercing damage. Target: One creature within range

Classes: Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock

You curse a creature with a malevolent, blood-draining hex. The target takes 4d6 necrotic damage and must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed in this way, a creature takes an additional 1d6 necrotic damage each time it takes damage from any source. You see with your normal visual senses, and in addition you can clearly see creatures and objects that are lightly obscured by foliage and treat heavily obscured creatures and objects as if they were lightly obscured instead.

Alternatively, you can shape the wall into a hemisphere up to 30 feet in diameter centered on a point you choose within range. The wall remains in place for the duration.

You attempt to charm ahumanoidyou can see within range. It must make aWisdomsaving throw, and does so withadvantageif you or your companions are fighting it. Charm personis the classic enchantment, dating to the origins of the game in 1974. Its appeal is obvious: an enemy grants a bit of friendly head start to retreating foes, a recalcitrant informant suddenly becomes talkative, or a town guard agrees to ignore a crime because that’s what friends do for each other. The five variant spells presented here all work on this theme but with differing levels of power and specificity.

You attempt to charm a humanoid you can see within range. The targeted creature makes aWisdomsaving throw, with advantage if you or your companions are fighting it or threatening it. If the saving throw fails, the humanoid ischarmedby you until the spell’s duration expires, until you or any of your companions do anything harmful to it, or until it performs a minor favor for you. Thecharmedcreature regards you as a friendly acquaintance or distant kin. It is willing to reveal a secret, open a door, lift an object, share food or water, or perform another favor on a similar level. It won’t fight on your behalf, defend you in combat, put its life or property at risk, or threaten or harm someone else it considers a friend. When the spell ends, the creature knows it wascharmedby you.

Ascharm personbut with a longer duration. The target of the spell remainscharmedfor one day per level you’ve attained in your spellcasting class. You attempt to charm a humanoid you can see within range. It makes aWisdomsaving throw, with advantage if you or your companions are fighting it or threatening it. If the saving throw fails, the humanoid ischarmedby a third humanoid you designate that both of you can see.

Divine Usurpation.name: Divine Usurpation
Divine Usurpation.components: V, S, M (stone-filled gizzard of a gold great wyrm, tarrasque blood, and 12-headed hydra bile)
Divine Usurpation.description:
You steal the power of a chosen deity, stripping them of their divine essence. The targeted deity loses all of its divine powers and abilities, becoming a mortal and retaining only their non-divine powers.

As you absorb the divine essence, your physical form is transformed, taking on a godly visage that reflects the nature of the deity whose power you have stolen. You gain the following benefits:

Yoursizegrows by up to two categories (e.g. from Medium to Huge).

Three of your ability scores (your choice betweenStrength,Dexterity,Constitution,Intelligence,Wisdom, andCharisma) increase to 30, reflecting your newfound divine power.

The remaining three ability scores each increase to 24.

You gainresistanceto all damage types.

When youcast a spellof 1st level or higher, you may choose to cast it as if you were using a 9th-level slot.

You gain advantage on all saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

As an action duringyour turn, you can cast thedispel magicspell without expending a spell slot.

When you hit a creature with a melee weaponattack, you can choose to deal an extra 2d10 force damage to the target.

You can’t age or be aged magically, and your form can’t be altered against your will.

At the GM’s discretion, you may also gain additional benefits based on the domains or aspects of the deity you have usurped. For example, taking the power of a god of war might grant you unparalleled combat prowess, while usurping a god of knowledge could give you infinite wisdom and insight into all things.

Divine Usurpation is a spell that no deity would likely ever allow to be cast. The very idea of a mortal stealing the power of a god is an affront to the natural order of the cosmos. The extended casting time of 24 hours provides ample opportunity for deities to sense the disturbance in the weave of magic and intervene. In many settings, where deities are seen as omniscient and omnipotent beings, they could easily detect the ritual and retaliate long before its completion. The mere preparation for this spell could send ripples across the planes, alerting powerful beings and possibly triggering divine omens, especially since the components required for this spell are incredibly rare and may not even exist in the caster’s world. Greatwyrms, tarrasques, and 12-headed hydras are beings of legend, and obtaining their essences would require quests of epic proportions. The pursuit of these components alone could attract the attention of powerful entities, both allies and enemies of the gods, as well as creatures guarding these rare resources.

The knowledge of Divine Usurpation itself is almost impossible to obtain, as it would likely be scattered among the far reaches of the cosmos, hidden away in forgotten planes guarded by entities that have no intention of allowing such a spell to be used.

Ancient prophecies might foretell the coming of those who dare to wield such power, marking the caster as a target for those who wish to prevent a disruption in the balance of the divine order.

Even if a caster were to somehow gather the components and knowledge necessary, the act of casting this spell is a perilous gamble. The gods themselves may take offense at such audacity, viewing it as a direct challenge to their authority.

This could result in unforeseen consequences or divine intervention, with other deities or cosmic forces rallying against the caster. The act of attempting to steal divine power is the embodiment of hubris and ambition, and it is likely to provoke a response that could be catastrophic not only for the caster but for the world surrounding them.

Corrupt the Weak.description:
You manipulate the will of the weak-minded to suit you. Over the casting time, you repeat a task as if it were a mantra and the target, which must have an intelligence of 5 or less, assumes that task to be a goal they came up with and follows it to the best of their ability.

The task must be simple, such as to guard a cave from all creatures. It may also include other elements such as allowing the caster and creatures with them to pass through. The GM may find some tasks unreasonable and not allow them.

Disintegration Wave.description:
Target: Each creature in a 30-foot cone

A green wave of energy sweeps from your hands in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 10d6 + 40 force damage. If this damage reduces a target to0 hit points, it is disintegrated. A disintegrated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A disintegrated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. The creature can be restored to life only by means of atrue resurrectionor awishspell. Dominate Person.name: Dominate Person
Dominate Person.description:
You attempt to beguile ahumanoidthat you can see within range. It must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becharmedby you for the duration. If you or creatures that are friendly to you are fighting it, it has advantage on the saving throw.

While the target ischarmed, you have a telepathic link with it as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence. You can use this telepathic link to issue commands to the creature while you are conscious (no action required), which it does its best to obey. You can specify a simple and general course of action, such as “Attack that creature,” “Run over there,” or “Fetch that object.” If the creature completes the order and doesn’t receive further direction from you, it defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability.

You can use your action to take total and precise control of the target. Until the end of your next turn, the creature takes only the actions you choose, and doesn’t do anything that you don’t allow it to do.

During this time you can also cause the creature to use a reaction, but this requires you to use your own reaction as well.

Each time the target takes damage, it makes a newWisdomsaving throw against the spell. If the saving throw succeeds, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 6th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. When you use a 7th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 1 hour. When you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours.

Tranquil thoughts.name: Tranquil thoughts
Tranquil thoughts.description:
You pronounce a blessing of overwhelming peace and tranquility over a 60-foot radius around you, affecting all creatures a Wisdom saving throw as calm emotions. Even creatures succeeding on their saving throws are quelled in their ability to commit violence, needing to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw whenever they take an offensive action to avoid being affected as a slow spell until the end of their next turn. If an affected creature is attacked by an unaffected creature or a creature that has succeeded on its saving throw, the calming effect of the tranquil thoughts is broken only for that creature. If you take an offensive action, the tranquil thoughts ends for all creatures.

The effects of tranquil thoughts persist whenever affected creatures are within 60 feet of you. If they leave that radius, the effects of tranquil thoughts subside, but they return if the creature comes within 60 feet of you again prior to the expiration of the spell.

The Dragon’s Hoard #11 © 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Thurston Hillman.

A thin green ray springs from your pointing finger to a target that you can see within range. The target can be a creature, an object, or a creation of magical force, such as the wall created bywall of force.

A creature targeted by this spell must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 10d6 + 40 force damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, it is disintegrated.

A 20-foot-radius sphere of whirling air springs into existence centered on a point you choose within range.

The sphere remains for the spell’s duration. Each creature in the sphere when it appears or that ends its turn there must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 7 (2d6) cold damage. The sphere’s space isdifficult terrain.

Until the spell ends, you can use a bonus action on each of your turns to cause a creature in the sphere to berestrained. It must make aConstitutionsaving throw. If it fails the saving throw, it isrestraineduntil the spell ends. A creature can also repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. Lesser Inscribe Vilespeech.name: Lesser Inscribe Vilespeech
Lesser Inscribe Vilespeech.components: V, S, M (piece of humanoid-skin vellum)
Lesser Inscribe Vilespeech.description:
Forming the odious sigils in your mind, you cause letters of Vilespeech to appear on the vellum, maddening the souls of those that see it. After casting this spell, any creature that opens the vellum triggers the following effects. You can refine the trigger so the spell is activated only under certain circumstances or according to a creature’s physical characteristics (such as height or weight), or type of creature (for example, the Vilespeech could be set to affect humans or shapechangers). You can also specify creatures that don’t trigger the Vilespeech, such as those who say a certain password. Once triggered, every creature within a 15-foot cone must make aWisdomsaving throw or find its gaze drifting to the Vilespeech. Creatures takes 2d6 psychic damage on a failed save and gain a short-term madness. This madness lasts for 1d10 minutes, though the Vilespeech only retain their ability to affect new targets for 1 minute after being triggered. Alesser restorationspell cast on the creature removes this madness. On a successful save a creature takes half damage but is otherwise unaffected. You must know Vilespeech in order to cast this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd-level or higher, the psychic damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot above 1st.

Vile spells are cruel and exploitative, bent to inflict unnatural pain or gain power from the suffering of victims.

They manipulate blood, blaspheme existence, pervert the physical form, conjure evil entities, or worse. Classes able to cast spells add all vile spells to their class spell list, but only creatures with a Sin ability score or evil alignment are able to cast spells from this school of magic without using a scroll or other magic item.

Vile spells leave an evil aura behind them, detectable withdetect evil and good. If the caster has no Sin ability score, use double the spell level to determine the strength of the aura left behind. Evil auras dissipate 10 minutes for every spell level + a number of minutes equal to double the caster’s Sin score. For example, a vile spell of 3rd-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 15 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour; a 3rd-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 30 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 15 doubled. A vile spell of 5th-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 20 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour and 30 minutes; a 5th-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 50 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 20 doubled.

As part of the casting of this cantrip, you inflict 2 points of damage to yourself. The blood from your self-inflicted injury forms into a sharpened spear of crimson that rapidly soars toward a creature within range, drying as it flies through the air. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d12 piercing damage. The spell creates more than one blood spear when you reach higher levels (you take 2 additional points of damage for every extra spear formed): two spears at 5th level, three spears at 11th level, and four spears at 17th level. You can direct the spears at the same target or at different ones. Make a separateattackroll for each spear.

Undo Action.name: Undo Action
Undo Action.description:
You undo one action,reaction, or bonus action one round in the past. If this causes a paradox (for example, you undo movement and should not be in the place you currently are) you take 3d10 force damage and the spell has no effect.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you increase the amount of past rounds you can travel to undo one action, up to a maximum of 9 rounds at ninth level.

Pincer.name: Pincer
Pincer.description:
You force your enemies into a tight spot. Choose two points you can see within range. The points must be at least 30 feet apart from each other. Each point then emits a thunderous boom in a 30-foot cone in the direction of the other point. The boom is audible out to 300 feet.

Each creature within a cone must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 thunder damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from the point that emitted the cone.

On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t pushed. Objects that aren’t being worn or carried within each cone are automatically pushed.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 6th.

Icy Simulacrum.name: Icy Simulacrum
Icy Simulacrum.description:
You create a powerful freezing rain on the target that deals 4d6 cold damage, or half as much on a successfulDexteritysaving throw.On a failure, the target is frozen in place, covered with a thick sheet of ice for 1 round.

The target isparalyzedand may only take mentalactionsbut may make a DC 18Strengthcheck to free themselves as an action. Allies may also attempt to break the target free by making theStrengthcheck themselves or attempting to break the ice which is treated as having 30hpand DT of 5.

If the target remains frozen for 1 round, the target is freed but the ice turns into a moving copy of the target under your control. The simulacrum lasts for 1 minute.

The copy has none of the spellcasting, innate spellcasting, or special attacks of the target, though it has the same melee or ranged weapon attacks. The simulacrum uses your spellattackmodifier for their attacks. Giving direction to the simulacrum is a bonus action that may be performed mentally. If given no orders, the simulacrum continues with its previous orders or attacks the original target of the spell.

The simulacrum deals damage and attacks using a copy of the weapon used by the target except it has none of the magical properties of the weapon, if applicable.

However, the weapon deals half of the normal physical damage and half cold damage, is considered magical forresistanceand immunity purposes and adds your spellcasting modifier to damage instead ofStrengthorDexterity. If the simulacrum has no weapon, is disarmed, or is ordered to drop its copy weapon, it has a Slamattackthat deals 1d6 damage, half of which is bludgeoning, half is cold damage.

The simulacrum has 30 hit point, AC equal to 10 + your spellcasting modifier and DT of 5. If the simulacrum is destroyed, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the simulacrum gains 10 extrahit pointsfor each spell slot above 4th.

Chains of the Inquisitor.name: Chains of the Inquisitor
Chains of the Inquisitor.description:
You summon chains from the positiveelementalplane and they fly out from you to bind one creature. If the creature succeeds on aConstitutionsave, it shrugs off the chains and the spell has no further effect. If it fails the save, it is bound by the chains in its current square and cannotplane shift, as though it is under the effect ofplanar binding. A chained creature takes 5d8 points of bludgeoning damage, isrestrainedandincapacitated, and it is coerced to answer questions truthfully.

If the target creature does not wish to answer a question you ask truthfully, it must make a successfulWisdomsave. If it fails, it must answer the question truthfully to the best of its knowledge. If the saving throw is successful, it may choose not to answer the question, and if it is asked the same question again, it has advantage on its saving throw.

You create a temporary portal to the Elemental Plane of Fire in front of you and draw power from it. A barrage of giant arrows of pure fire project from the portal in a line that is 20 feet wide and 120 feet long in the direction of your choosing. Each creature in the area of effect must make aDexteritysaving throw.

On a failed save, the creature takes 12d6 fire damage and is knockedproneandrestrainedas the arrows pin it down. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and is not knocked prone or restrained. A creature restrained in this way can make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC at the end of their turn, ending the effect on itself on a success. Any creature ofsizeHuge or larger has advantage on theStrengthsaving throw to end beingrestrained.

A Large quasi-real, horselike creature appears on the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. You decide the creature’s appearance, but it is equipped with a saddle, bit, and bridle. Any of the equipment created by the spell vanishes in a puff of smoke if it is carried more than 10 feet away from the steed.

For the duration, you or a creature you choose can ride the steed. The creature uses the statistics for a riding horse, except it has a speed of 100 feet and can travel 10 miles in an hour, or 13 miles at a fast pace. When the spell ends, the steed gradually fades, giving the rider 1 minute to dismount. The spell ends if you use an action to dismiss it or if the steed takes any damage.

Crying out a single stirring word grants your ally sudden strength and resilience. The target may add yourCharismamodifier to the result of their saving throw.

Hide In One’s Shadow.name: Hide In One’s Shadow
Hide In One’s Shadow.description:
When you touch a willing creature with a piece of charcoal while casting this spell, the target and everything it carries blends into and becomes part of the target’sshadow, which remains discernible, although its body seems to disappear. Theshadowis incorporeal, has no weight, and is immune to all but psychic and radiant damage. The target remains aware of its surroundings and can move, but only as a shadow could move—flowing along surfaces as if the creature were moving normally. The creature can step out of the shadow at will, resuming its physical shape in theshadow’sspace and ending the spell.

This spell cannot be cast in an area devoid of light, where a shadow would not normally appear. Even a faint light source, such as moonlight or starlight, is sufficient. If that light source is removed, or if theshadowis flooded with light in such a way that the physical creature wouldn’t cast a shadow, the spell ends, and the creature reappears in theshadow’sspace.

First, the target must make aConstitutionsaving throw or take 12d6 cold damage. A successful saving throw halves this damage.

Second, the target must make aDexteritysaving throw or be thrown 1d4 x 10 feet in a random direction, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet traveled and knockedprone. Whenever a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with amelee attack, the shield drains life from them. The attacker takes 2d8 necrotic damage and you gaintemporary hit pointsequal to half of the damage taken, round down.

Wall of Bees.name: Wall of Bees
Wall of Bees.description:
Despite its name, the wall created by this spell is not composed entirely of bees. Instead, it is made of wax honeycombs that are crawling with bees. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick or create a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick.

A creature that climbs or attacks the wall can attempt aWisdom(Animal Handling) check against a DC equal to your spell save DC. If you are proficient inAnimal Handling, you automatically succeed on this check. A creature that climbs or attacks the wall with amelee attackwithout first succeeding on this check angers the bees, as does a creature that would be pushed into the wall’s space. A swarm of insects with a fly speed of 30 feet attacks the creature, ignoring all other creatures. A maximum of six swarms can be active at any given time, and no more than one swarm canattackthe same creature. The swarms disappear when reduced to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The wall can be destroyed one section at a time. Each 10-foot section has AC 11 and 20hit points. It is immune to poison and psychic damage but vulnerable to fire damage. Reducing a section to0 hit pointsdestroys it.

Lock and Load.name: Lock and Load
Lock and Load.description:
You touch a firearm, enchanting it so that it automatically loads the powder and ammunition after being fired. This temporarily negates the loading property of the firearm; the wielder doesn’t have to use an action or bonus action to reload it, and if they can make multiple attacks per round, they can use the firearm for any or all of them. The powder and ammunition are drawn from the wielder’s equipment (if the wielder is out of either, the spell cannot reload the weapon).

This spell is especially useful when cast on a cannon.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can affect one additional weapon for each spell slot above 2nd.

Mask of Shadows.name: Mask of Shadows
Mask of Shadows.description:
You shroud your face in a mask of darkness that completely hides your facial features. The mask of shadows does not impede your vision, but it does protect you from visual effects. You lose anylightblindness,lightsensitivity, or similar weakness while the mask of shadows lasts. In addition, you gain advantage on saving throws against gaze attacks, beingblindedby bright light, visual effects likehypnotic pattern, or special creature abilities that depend on seeing a creature (like a nymph’s blinding beauty).

Whine.name: Whine
Whine.description:
Edward was unsure why they were being framed, but thebardcertainly didn’t accidentallylightanyone on fire, at least not in this town. He thought the charges their accuser was listing were a wee bit wanky, ranging from consuming threecourse meals to violating the town’s lute guild rights. Then, out of nowhere, the accuser’s voice became a grating, nasal whine as he described how the party was clearly an omen of doom upon them all.

Alter Instrument.name: Alter Instrument
Alter Instrument.description:
You alter a musical instrument so it sounds like a different kind of instrument you are familiar with. The change can be minor (such as making a lute sound like a guitar) or major (making a keyboard sound like drums). All other aspects of the instrument-such as volume, pitch, and how it is played-are unchanged. For example, a piccolo made to sound like an organ is no louder than a normal piccolo, can produce only high notes in the piccolo range, and is a wind instrument.

The effect ends on a creature if it takes damage, or if a creature uses their action to shake them.

You touch a nonmagical javelin, spear, or pike.

The target weapon drips blood but also sheds the blood of your enemies. If you hit a creature with the bloodspear, you deal an additional 1d8 necrotic damage and recover half as manyhit pointsas the additional damage. Constructs and undead are unaffected. Breeze Walker.description:
Choosing a direction, you summon a strong, steady breeze to swirl beneath your feet and propel you. Youlevitateto a sustained height of 3 feet for the duration, and travel in the chosen direction at 150% of your movement.

Travel in any other direction is at 50% of your movement.

Burst Bonds.name: Burst Bonds
Burst Bonds.description:

You create an area inaccessible to anyone but you and your compatriots at the heart of a wilderness. A druidhome is equally a place and a representation of the druid’s spirit. Good-aligned druids’ groves are bright, with lush grass, immortal trees, and populated with good fey and creatures appropriate to the climate and terrain. Evil-aligned druids create groves thick with dangerous thorns, dying trees, and dangerous fey creatures. Once cast, this spell creates a hidden grove with a radius of 60 feet. The entrance is usually a tight tangle of vines or thorns or a dense copse of trees. The druidhome is only accessible by the druid who created it or those the druid names or invites into the druidhome.

Anyone attempting to enter a druidhome without permission becomes lost and eventually make their way back to where they started after 1d4 hours of wandering. At the center of the grove is an enormous central tree that produces fruit year round. The fruit is edible, and is identical to a goodberry. This tree may always be the destination of atree stridespell you cast regardless of the type of tree you enter or the distance involved. A spring bubbles and feeds a small pond of drinkable water. The grove attracts a number of like-minded fey and other creatures, such as nymphs, dryads, satyrs, and blink dogs. Evil druids may find that their druidhome attracts hags and other evil creatures. These creatures are not under the druid’s control, but they recognize the druid’s ownership of their abode and protects the druidhome from invaders. The druid may choose to expel any creature as an action, requiring the creature to make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, the creature is expelled from the druidhome and cannot re-enter for 1 month. Each subsequent casting may enlarge the druidhome by an additional 20 feet. Although a druidhome may be anysize, it functions as an extradimensional space and takes up no space on the Material Plane.

Two or more druids may work together, casting the spell to create a larger and more substantial druidhome. For each druid involved in the creation of a druidhome another central tree grows, and eachdruidshares an equal claim to the druidhome as a whole. When the ownership of a druidhome comes into dispute, druids war against each other and the survivors gain control of the entire region.

Identify Device.name: Identify Device
Identify Device.description:
You choose one mechanical or chaositech device that you touch throughout the casting of the spell. You learn its basic properties and how to use them, whether it requires attunement to use, and how many charges it has. For example, casting this on ademongun would tell you that it is a “weapon,” while casting it on a spyglass would tell you that it is a “device for seeing faraway things.”

If a device has different functions that are equally basic, the spell determines the weakest or simplest function. If these functions are also of equal level or power, the GM decides randomly which is identified.

If you instead touch a creature throughout the casting, you learn what devices, if any, are attached to it.

Frost Tomb.name: Frost Tomb
Frost Tomb.description:
You encase a creature you can see within range in a chilling tomb of frost. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or be cursed andrestrainedfor the duration as ice forms around it. Whilerestrainedin this way, a creature takes 2d6 cold damage at the start of each turn. A creaturerestrainedby the ice can use its action to make aStrengthcheck, shattering the tomb on a success.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Mount Mind.name: Mount Mind
Mount Mind.description:
Classes:antipaladin,paladin,ranger

You form a strong mental bond with your mount as long as you remain within 10 feet of it. You and your mount’s passivePerceptionincreases by 2. Your mount gains a +1 bonus to its AC, and if the mount’s movement provokes an opportunityattack, you (rather than the attacker) can choose whether theattacktargets you or the mount.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a 2nd-level slot, you increase the duration to 8 hours.

Savage Strike.name: Savage Strike
Savage Strike.description:
Your melee weapon glows with primal energy. For the duration, attacks with the weapon you choose deals an extra 1d6 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Radiant damage. Additionally, you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

The Dragon’s Hoard #58© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, James-Levi Cooke.

Crush.name: Crush
Crush.description:
You squeeze your fingers together and peer at a target you can see between the gap. The target must make aStrengthsaving throw, taking 3d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half this damage with a success.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you inflict an additional 1d10 bludgeoning damage per spell slot level above 2nd.

Curse of Shifting Shadows.name: Curse of Shifting Shadows
Curse of Shifting Shadows.description:
Target: One creature within range

You curse a creature within range to see shifting shadows that obscure its vision. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed until the end of its next turn. While cursed in this way, a creature is unable to see further than 30 feet away, no matter its normal vision range.

Awaken Heresy.name: Awaken Heresy
Awaken Heresy.components: V, S, M (pus from an infected wound)
Awaken Heresy.description:
The blasphemy you speak reaches out and brands the soul of a creature you can see within range. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save the target gains an inherent heresy. When casting this spell you can choose whether the creature gains an inherent heresy that you have or to roll to choose randomly.

At the end of the duration, the creature must make an additionalWisdomsaving throw or the inherent heresy becomes permanent. You can end the spell early by using an action to dismiss it. Aremove curse,greater restoration, orwishspell also ends it At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th-level the duration is 1 year. When using a spell slot of 8th-level the creature makes its secondWisdomsaving throw with disadvantage. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th-level, the spell’s duration lasts until it is ended by one of the spells mentioned above.
