You target one living creature within range and it gains 1 level ofexhaustionon a failedConstitutionsaving throw each round as its skin loosens and splits. Once it has taken 5 levels ofexhaustionin this way, its skin falls off to reveal its musculature.

The creature ceases takingexhaustionlevels but has disadvantage on physical based saving throws (Str, Con, Dex), pain effects (GM’s discretion), or poison damage. The target automatically fails anyCharismabased checks with the exception of Intimidate. You conjure a surging wave of water that lashes out from your hand to strike one creature or 5-foot square. Normal fires on a creature or object or that fill the target square are extinguished but magical fires are unaffected. You also can make a melee spellattackagainst a creature within range. If theattackhits, the creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage and if the creature is Large or smaller, treat the result of yourattackroll as if it were aStrength(Athletics) check made to Shove the target away from you. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th (2d6), 11th (3d6), and 17th level (4d6). You can choose to strike a creature, object, or square with the hydraulic lash without dealing damage.

The creature must make aCharismasaving throw. It takes the same amount (up to 20 damage in total) and type of damage you inflicted with the triggeringattackon a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the damage exceeds

You assault the ears of nearby creatures with a powerful shout. Each creature in a 30-foot cone originating from you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. A target takes 4d10 thunder damage and isdeafenedfor the duration on a failed save, or half as much damage and isdeafeneduntil the end of its next turn on a successful one. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends.

Camouflage.description:
You touch a creature which gains the ability to alter its coloration to match its background, including changing and shifting to match that background when it is moving less than 20 feet per round, granting the creature advantage onDexterity(Stealth) ability checks and enabling it to makeStealthchecks even when it does not havecoveror concealment. If the creature moves more than 20 feet per round or attacks, or if it moves between two areas with radically different backgrounds (such as moving from a gray stone wall into a forest or open field), the effects of the spell are suppressed until the beginning of the creature’s next turn.

Sky’s Vengeance.name: Sky’s Vengeance
Sky’s Vengeance.description:
You call forth the sky’s fury, targeting a creature you can see under the open sky. A colossal bolt of lightning descends from the heavens to strike. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 13d6 lightning damage, or half as much on a successful one. If the target is a creature wearing metal armor or a metal object, they make this saving throw with disadvantage. The strike ignites flammable objects within a 10-foot radius of the impact.

Sorrowful Grove.components: V, S, M (twig from the Woe Wood)
Sorrowful Grove.duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Classes: Cleric, Druid, Warlock
Sorrowful Grove.description:
Classes: Cleric, Druid, Warlock

You transform up to ten creatures of your choice that you can see within range. If the target’s body is made of flesh, the creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, it isrestrainedas its flesh begins to harden. On a successful save, the creature isn’t affected. A creaturerestrainedby this spell must make anotherConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. If it successfully saves against this spell three times, the spell ends. If it fails its saves three times, it is turned to wood and subjected to thepetrifiedcondition for the duration.

The successes and failures don’t need to be consecutive; keep track of both until the target collects three of a kind.

If the creature is physically broken whilepetrified, it suffers from similar deformities if it reverts to its original state.

The closest inspection cannot reveal that the tree in question is actually a magically concealed creature. To all normal tests the creature is, in fact, a tree, although adetect magicspell reveals a faint transmutation on the tree. While in tree form, the creature can observe all that transpires around it just as if it were in its normal form. Its armor class is 15. All clothing and gear carried or worn changes with it. If you maintain your concentration on this spell for the entire possible duration, the creatures are turned to wood until the effect is removed. Any creatures that come within 60 feet of the Sorrowful Grove must make aCharismasaving throw or be overwhelmed with despair for 1 minute, during which time it can’tattackor target any creatures with harmful abilities, spells, or other magical effects.

Phase Runner.name: Phase Runner
Phase Runner.components: V, S, M (drop of phase spider blood)
Phase Runner.description:
Your body oscillates rapidly between the Material Plane and Ethereal Plane for the duration. When you take theDashaction, you can move through other creatures and objects as if they weredifficult terrain. If you endyour turnin an occupied space, you are moved into the nearest unoccupied space (chosen at random if more than one space is equally near) and take 1d6 force damage for every 5 feet you are moved. After you take theDashaction, until the start of your next turn, attacks against you are made with disadvantage as your body continues to phase between the two planes.

For the duration, you can be seen and affected by creatures on the Ethereal Plane. When the spell ends, you are on the Material Plane. This spell fails and the casting is wasted if you attempt to cast it while on a plane other than the Material Plane.

Sublime Detachment.name: Sublime Detachment
Sublime Detachment.description:
You erasefear, suffering, want, and pain in the minds of the one creature, washing away their sorrows and replacing them with a pleasurable contentment and calming fugue.

Any pain effects affecting the targets are immediately ended, as thecharmedandfrightenedconditions and the targets gain immunity to such conditions for the duration of the spell. In addition, any effects that deal hit point damage deal only half damage to the targets of your sublime detachment.

Magic Circle against Shapechangers.components: S, M (50 gp powdered silver, which the spell consumes)
Magic Circle against Shapechangers.description:
Classes: Cleric, Paladin, Sorcerer, Wizard

You create a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-tall cylinder of magical energy centered on a point on the ground that you can see within range. Glowing runes appear wherever the cylinder intersects with the floor or other surface. Any creature with the shapechanger subtype can’t willingly enter the cylinder by nonmagical means. If the shapechanger tries to use teleportation or interplanar travel to do so, it must first succeed on aCharismasaving throw. The shapechanger has disadvantage onattackrolls against targets within the cylinder. Targets within the cylinder can’t becharmed,frightened, or possessed by the shapechanger. When you cast this spell, you can elect to cause its magic to operate in the reverse direction, preventing shapechanger from leaving the cylinder and protecting targets outside it.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level or higher, the duration is until dispelled.

Passwall.name: Passwall
Passwall.components: V, S, M(a pinch of sesame seeds)
Passwall.description:
A passage appears at a point of your choice that you can see on a wooden, plaster, or stone surface (such as a wall, a ceiling, or a floor) within range, and lasts for the duration. You choose the opening’s dimensions: up to 5 feet wide, 8 feet tall, and 20 feet deep. The passage creates no instability in a structure surrounding it.

When the opening disappears, any creatures or objects still in the passage created by the spell are safely ejected to an unoccupied space nearest to the surface on which you cast the spell.

Resonating Solo.name: Resonating Solo
Resonating Solo.description:
You begin performing an emotionally powerful song through your spellcasting focus that slowly increases in intensity. You cannot cast another spell through your spellcasting focus while concentrating on this spell.

Until the spell ends, you can use an action to make a ranged spellattackand strike a chord to send powerful sound waves at a target within range. On a hit, a target takes a number of d8 in thunder damage equal to the number of rounds you have maintained concentration on this spell (including the turn you cast it).

You don’t need advantage on theattackroll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and you don’t have disadvantage on theattackroll.

At 11th and 17th level you gain an additional d6 of Sneak Attack damage.

At 11th level, the Stone Crow can spend 2 ki points and choose one type of creature. For the next minute, the Stone Crow increases their threat range by +1 against all creatures of that type.

At 17th level, the Stone Crow can spend 2 points of ki and call upon their ancestors for protection. For the next minute, they gainresistanceto all nonmagical piercing, slashing, and bludgeoning damage.

Eldritch Cataclysm.components: V, S, M (dark crystal carved with forbidden symbols)
Eldritch Cataclysm.description:
Target: 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within range

Classes: Warlock, Sorcerer, Wizard

You unleash a surge of eldritch energy, tearing open the veil of reality and flooding the minds of creatures within a 30-foot radius with incomprehensible horrors. Each creature in the area must make anIntelligencesaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 12d6 psychic damage and is overwhelmed with visions for the duration.

On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects.

While affected, a creature isblindedanddeafened, hearing only the chaotic whispers from beyond reality. An affected creature must also make aWisdomsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d6 psychic damage. On a successful one, the effect ends on the target.

Illuminate Spoor.description:
You touch a set of tracks created by a single creature.

That set of tracks and all other tracks made by the same creature give off a faint glow. You and up to three creatures you designate when you cast this spell can see the glow. A creature that can see the glow automatically succeeds onWisdom(Survival) checks to track that creature. If the tracks are covered by obscuring objects such as leaves or mud, you and the creatures you designate have advantage onWisdom(Survival) checks to follow the tracks.

If the creature leaving the tracks changes its tracks, such as by adding or removing footwear, the glow stops where the tracks change. Until the spell ends, you can use an action to touch and illuminate a new set of tracks.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours. When you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 24 hours.

You become one with the living storm, a creature of wind and lightning. You can fly with a speed of 40 feet and you have immunity to damage from ranged weapon attacks. You haveresistanceto lightning and thunder damage. Natural and magical winds do not affect you unless you wish it.

Once per round as a bonus action, you can discharge a thunderbolt from your eyes or hands as a ranged spellattack. You have advantage on your attack roll if the target is wearing metal armor or is made of metal. On a hit, the target takes 4d6 lightning damage and 4d6 thunder damage.

You surround the target with a glowing green aura of ill-fated prophecy that fills its mind with tangled visions of possible futures, causing it to commit missteps and errors even as it tries to avoid those misfortunes. Each time the target attempts toattackorcast a spell, it must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, it has disadvantage onattackrolls made as part of thatattackor spell and targets have advantage on their saving throws. In addition, the spell orattackdeals only half normal damage.

You point at a Medium-sized or smaller creature you can see with your wand. If it fails aConstitutionsaving throw, it begins to inflate like a balloon. It increases by onesize, loses all forms of movement, his disadvantage onDexterity-based checks, and gainsvulnerabilityto piercing damage. On each of the creature’s turns it floats upwards at a speed of 20 feet. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target. If some solid object (such as a ceiling) is encountered, it remains there, oscillating slightly, for the duration. The target can move only by pushing or pulling against a fixed object or surface within reach (such as a wall or a ceiling), which allows it to move as if it were climbing. You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the heart of one creature you can see within range, leaving it near death. You send a single living creature into a magical slumber. If the target has fewer than 50hit points, it fallsunconsciousuntil the spell ends, it takes damage, or someone uses an action to shake or slap the sleeper awake. If the target has more than 50hit points, it can attempt aWisdomsaving throw to avoid falling asleep. Undead, creatures with more than 100hit points, and creatures immune to beingcharmedaren’t affected by this spell.

When the spell ends, the sleeper has no memory of the spell being cast or any events for 5 minutes prior to the spell being cast. These lost memories can be restored byremove curse.

Saint Dawkins’ Safe Passage.description:
When you cast this spell, you remove the protection from a 2,500-foot square space (an area 50 feet square, or one hundred 5-foot squares or 25 10-foot squares). Identify.description:

If it is a magic item or some other magic-imbued object, you learn its properties and how to use them, whether it requires attunement to use, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any spells are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a spell, you learn which spell created it.

Towering Presence.description:
You adjust your posture and seem to suddenly overshadow all others around you. When you take the Influence action to Intimidate one creature, that creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or gain theFrightenedcondition for the duration. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can attempt to Intimidate one additional creature at a time for each spell slot level above 1.

Seeping Death.description:
Your touch inflicts a virulent, flesh-eating disease. Make a melee spellattackagainst a creature within your reach. On a hit, the creature’sDexterityscore is reduced by 1d4, and it is afflicted with the seeping death disease for the duration.

Since this spell induces a natural disease in its target, any effect that removes a disease or otherwise ameliorates a disease’s effects applies to it and can end the spell early.

Seeping Death. The creature’s flesh is slowly liquefied by a lingering necrotic pestilence. At the end of each long rest, the diseased creature must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or itsDexterityscore is reduced by 1d4. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. If the disease reduces the creature’sDexterityto 0, the creature dies.

You surround yourself with a glowing aura that sheds bright light within 30 feet and dim light for an additional 30 feet beyond that. At any time, as a bonus action you can gather the nimbus of light into a glowing ball surrounding one hand and hurl it at a target within 30 feet as a ranged spellattack, dealing 2d6 radiant damage on a hit. This ends the spell.

Great Wall.name: Great Wall
Great Wall.description:
As you finish casting this spell, a massive stone wall erupts from the earth. This wall can stretch up to ten miles long.

You can shape the wall to curve and bend as you choose, though it must be contiguous and remain structurally sound. It can’t pass through existing structures.

The wall stands 30 feet high and is 20 feet thick at the base and 15 feet thick at the top. You can choose to include a walkway along the top of the wall. Each 10-foot-square section of wall has AC 17, 5,000hit points, and a damage threshold of 30. It is immune to poison and psychic damage. Reducing a section to0 hit pointsdestroys it. Climbing the wall requires a successful DC 15Strength(Athletics) check.

You can create up to ten watchtowers along the length of the wall. These watchtowers stand 60 feet high and 50 feet wide. They have quarters to house up to 50 troops each. You can choose to include a gate in any of these towers. The gates are up to 15 feet high and wide and include both inner and outer portcullises. Each portcullis has AC 19, 100hit points, and a damage threshold of 20.

The gates are immune to poison and psychic damage. Once you finish casting the spell, the wall and any towers you create become permanent, nonmagical structures and can’t be dispelled.

Fleet Feet.name: Fleet Feet
Fleet Feet.description:
Classes: Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard

You imbue up to six creatures you can see within range with incredible speed. For the duration, each target’s walking speed is doubled, and they gain the ability todashas a bonus action. Additionally, they have advantage onDexterityability checks and saving throws while the spell lasts.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can target two additional creatures for each slot level above 6th.

Blood-Soaked Armament.name: Blood-Soaked Armament
Blood-Soaked Armament.duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Hemorrhage Trait
Blood-Soaked Armament.description:
Hemorrhage TraitA spell with the hemorrhage trait have an effect below the expectations of the spell’s level, but this effect increases if the caster is bleeding when the spell is cast. You are bleeding if you aren’t at a fullhit pointsand you’ve taken piercing or slashing damage in the past hour. The spell description designates these effects with “If you are bleeding…” before presenting the additional effects. To gain greater control of their bleeding, casters who dabble in blood magic often learn the bit of blood cantrip and use it to ensure the steady stream of blood necessary to empower their spells. That such spellcasters would so carelessly spill their own blood for more powerful magic makes them seem reckless in many people’s eyes.

You touch a nonmagical melee weapon. The weapon becomes magically sheathed in a slick film of blood and flicks droplets of blood when swung. The weapon gains an additional effect whenever a creature critically hits with it, based on the type of damage it deals.

Weaponized Loss.name: Weaponized Loss
Weaponized Loss.description:
You instill the target creature with an underlying dread that is enhanced when their allies fall around them.

The target takes disadvantage on saving throws against thefrightenedcondition. If an ally is reduced to0 hit pointsor killed within 60 feet of the target, they must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, they have disadvantage onIntelligence,Wisdom, andCharismasaving throws for the remainder of the spell’s duration.

If the target witnesses an illusion of a triggering event, they still must make a saving throw against this spell.

If a target creature already failed their saving throw on this spell and witnesses a triggering effect, they arefrightenedinstead.

Awaken Location.duration: Permanent There are places in the world that have
Awaken Location.description:
There are places in the world that have a life of their own and can be powerful conduits for certain energies. When you cast this spell, you cause the area within range to gain a subtle sentience. This intelligence does not manifest in a normally recognizable way and cannot be directly communicated with. It does, however, take on a will of its own and is influenced by the events that occur at that location.

Meld Into Ice.name: Meld Into Ice
Meld Into Ice.description:
You step into a piece of ice large enough to contain your body, melding yourself and any equipment you carry with the ice for the duration. Using your movement, you step into the ice. Nothing of your presences remains to non-magical detection.

While merged with the ice you can see your surroundings as only a hazy and indistinct image. AllWisdom(Perception) checks to see your surroundings or to hear nearby sounds are made with disadvantage. You are aware of the passage of time and can cast spells on yourself while in the ice. You can use your movement to leave the ice were you entered, which ends the spell. You cannot otherwise move.

Minor psychical damage to the ice, such as chipping or melting, has no effect on you. A partial destruction of the ice, anything that reduces the volume to less than you can fit in to, ends the spell and you are expelled from the ice suffering 6d6 bludgeoning damage. The ice’s complete destruction inflicts 50 bludgeoning damage and expels you. If you are expelled form the ice you landproneadjacent to the point where you entered the ice, or the closest unoccupied space

Reset.name: Reset
Reset.description:
Choose up to four creatures within range. If a target is your ally, it can rerollinitiative, keeping whichever of the two results it prefers. If a target is your enemy, it must make a successfulWisdomsaving throw or reroll initiative, keeping whichever of the two results you prefer. Changes to the initiative order go into effect at the start of the next round.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can affect one additional creature for each slot level above 4th.

Void Strike.description:
With a short phrase of void speech, you gather writhing darkness around your hand. When you cast the spell, and as an action on subsequent turns, you can unleash a bolt of darkness at a target within range. Make a ranged spellattack. If your target is in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on the roll. On a hit, the target takes 5d8 necrotic damage and isfrightenedof you until the start of your next turn.

Bedtime Guardian.name: Bedtime Guardian
Bedtime Guardian.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 hour

You channel the psychic imbuement of an attuned somnifer, summoning its essence from the owner’s dreamscape to manifest as a creature.

Choose one of the following forms most appropriate for the somnifer, and the same somnifer will always manifest as the same creature regardless of form.

All summoned creatures are also considered fey, and returns to its original form when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. If the summon is reduced to 0HPor less, the somnifer returns broken and must be repaired before it can provide benefits as a somnifer (including use as a focus in manifest somnifer).

Rollinitiativefor the summoned creatures as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands the creature attuned to the somnifore issues to them. If they are not given any commands, they defend the attuned creature, but otherwise take noactions.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using certain higher-level spell slots, the somnifer can take a more powerful form, choosing a creature with a challenge rating equal to the level of the spell-slot used to cast the spell.

Blessing of Courage and Life.description:
You grant an ally long-lasting succor to a creature that wards it from danger and dread. The target has advantage on saving throws against becomingfrightenedor any effect that deals necrotic damage. In addition, at any time the target can choose to end the spell as a bonus action or as areaction. The target’s hit point maximum and currenthit pointsincrease by 10 for the remainder of the spell’s duration but the spell’s other benefits end.

Chariot.name: Chariot
Chariot.description:
You create a 5-foot-radius, 30-foot-tall cylinder of swirling air on a point you can see within range. Each Huge or smaller creature in the cylinder when it appears or that ends its turn within 5 feet of the cylinder must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or berestrainedby it. A creaturerestrainedby the whirlwind can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. On a success, it is no longerrestrainedand is safely ejected into an unoccupied space of its choice within 5 feet of the whirlwind.

As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can move the whirlwind up to 30 feet. If you move the whirlwind, creaturesrestrainedby the whirlwind are moved with it when it moves. If you move the whirlwind into a creature, that creature must make the saving throw against being restrained by the cylinder, and the whirlwind stops moving this turn. If you are within 5 feet of the whirlwind when it moves, you can choose to be carried along with it and safely deposited in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of its destination. You can’t be restrained by the whirlwind.

Alternatively, as a bonus action on each of your turns, you can choose to violently eject a creature restrained by the whirlwind instead of moving the whirlwind.

The creature is thrown up to 40 feet in a random direction and knockedprone. If a thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw against your spell save DC or take the same damage and be knockedprone.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the whirlwind’s radius increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 4th.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Curse Object.name: Curse Object
Curse Object.description:
You craft a curse and attach it to an object.

That object can be up to large size, such as a spinning wheel, or tiny, such as an apple. You dictate the interaction with the object and the name of a target that will interact with it. If the target is within 30 feet of the object, they must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, the target ischarmed, and compelled to interact with the object in the prescribed way. A named target that interacts with the object is subject to a curse and receives no saving throw. The effects of the curse must otherwise conform to all the effects ofbestow curse, with an indefinite duration. Such curses are ended with spells and effects such asgreater restorationorremove cursethat specifically end curses.

A suspicious character can investigate the item, either making anIntelligence(Arcana),Intelligence(Investigation),Wisdom(Insight), orWisdom(Perception) check to determine that the object is dangerous. The DC is equal to your spell save DC. Effects such asdetect magicshow the object as having an aura of necromancy, and creatures with truesight can instantly recognize the object to be cursed. At the DM’s option, a character with a passive score in any of those skills equal to the DC is automatically alerted to the object’s cursed status.

Simple Settings: Fairy Tales. 2020, Fat Goblin Games; Author: Rick Hershey, Ismael Alvarez, Jason Owen Black

Misdirection.name: Misdirection
Misdirection.description:
You create a brief flash of light, loud sound, or other distraction that interrupts a creature’s attack. When a creature you can see within range makes anattack, you can impose disadvantage on itsattackroll.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Time Tunnel.name: Time Tunnel
Time Tunnel.components: S, M (diamond worth at least 5,000 gp)
Time Tunnel.description:
You create a wormhole to the Temporal Plane, allowing you and your companions to travel beyond the limitations of time and space.

You conjure a portal linking an unoccupied space you can see within range to the Temporal Plane. The portal is a circular opening, which you can make 5 to 20 feet in diameter. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose. The portal lasts for the duration. The portal has a front and a back on both the Prime and Temporal Planes.

Travel through the portal is possible only by moving through its front. Anything that does so is instantly transported to the other plane, appearing in the unoccupied space nearest to the portal. Upon arriving at the Temporal Plane, your body resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics and possessions. The principal difference is the addition of a silvery cord that extends from between your shoulder blades and trails behind you, fading toinvisibilityafter 1 foot. This cord is your timeline to your primary timestream.

As long as the timeline remains intact, you can find your way home. If the timeline is cut—something that can happen only when an effect specifically states that it does—your soul and body are separated, killing you instantly. Your temporal form can freely travel through the Temporal Plane. While on the Temporal Plane, you can move in any direction. If you move up or down, every foot of movement costs an extra foot. You can see and hear the plane you originated from, but everything there looks gray, and you can’t see anything more than 60 feet away. While on the Temporal Plane, you can only affect and be affected by other creatures on that plane. Creatures that aren’t on the Temporal Plane can’t perceive you and can’t interact with you, unless a special ability or magic has given them the ability to do so. You ignore all objects and effects that aren’t on the Temporal Plane, allowing you to move through objects you perceive on the plane you originated from. The Temporal Plane allows travel to the far reaches of time, including the Beginning and End, and billions of years in the past or future.

Charge of Glory.description:

Premature Celebration.description:
Classes: Arcane Trickster, Bard, Wizard

Choose a creature within range that you can see. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure it sees the next attack it makes as wildly successful with the victim exploding into sparkling particles, whether it hits or misses. If the target has a feature that allows it to attack more than once, it does not use any remaining attacks that turn.

At the start of its next turn, the target can make the saving throw again. If it fails, it remains under the illusion. If it can see its original victim, it believes it is a new opponent and may attack it again, or a different target, with the same result.

Contagious Healing.name: Contagious Healing
Contagious Healing.description:
Your touch infects a friendly creature with a magical disease. The target regains a number ofhit pointsequal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. The next time the target takes damage, the disease ends on the target and infects a new friendly creature within 10 feet of the first. The new target regainshit pointsequal to 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier. The next time the new target takes damage, the disease ends on it and moves to another friendly creature within 10 feet of it, continuing in this manner until no valid targets are in range or the spell ends. A creature can be healed by your contagioushealingonly once per casting of this spell. This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, thehealingincreases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

Druidcraft.name: Druidcraft
Druidcraft.description: Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range:

Purify Food and Drink.name: Purify Food and Drink
Purify Food and Drink.description: All nonmagical food and drink within a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range is purified and rendered free of poison and disease.

Summon Clockwork Warriors.name: Summon Clockwork Warriors
Summon Clockwork Warriors.description:
ComponentsV, M (a gear and a spring)

DurationConcentration, up to 10 minutes

You summon sevenClockworkSoldiers within range thatattackyour foes. The creatures are allies to you and your allies. In combat, the creatures share yourInitiativecount, but they take their turns immediately after yours. They obey your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any, they take theDodgeaction and use their movement to avoid danger.

Dimensional Shift.name: Dimensional Shift
Dimensional Shift.description:
Classes:sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You cause a creature to be instantly teleported up to 10 feet away, reappearing in an unoccupied space that you can see that can support it. If the creature is unwilling, it can make aWisdomsaving throw to resist being teleported.

If you attempt toteleportagrappledcreature, the creature grappling it can attempt aWisdomsaving throw with disadvantage. If it succeeds, it can choose to prevent thegrappledcreature from teleporting or toteleportalong with the target.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can increase the spell’s range by 20 feet for each slot level above 2nd.

Xarche.name: Xarche
Xarche.description:
If the target is native to a different plane of existence than the one you’re on, the target is banished with a faint popping noise, returning to its home plane. If the spell ends before 1 minute has passed, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. Otherwise, the target doesn’t return.

Challenge Evil.name: Challenge Evil
Challenge Evil.description:
You challenge an evil creature to focus its wrath upon you or suffer the consequences. You can make a melee spellattack, or you can cast this spell as a bonus action immediately after striking the target with a melee weaponattack. If the target fails aCharismasaving throw, you are linked in fury.

You gain a +1 bonus onattackanddamage rollsagainst the target. In addition, if at the end of any of the target’s turns it has not attacked you during its turn, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. The spell ends immediately if you voluntarily move away from the target or if you attack a different creature.

The Dragon’s Hoard #19© 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Wraith Walk.name: Wraith Walk
Wraith Walk.description:
You step into the boundary between the physical world and the shadow realm, becoming ethereal like awraith. For the duration, you gainresistanceto all damage except radiant and psychic, and you can move through other creatures and objects as if they weredifficult terrain. If you endyour turninside an object, you take 1d10 force damage.

Sense Spell.name: Sense Spell
Sense Spell.description:
You specify one spell at the time of casting; it must not have a duration of “instantaneous.”

The spell must be on your spell list, and you must be of a high-enough level to cast it. If the specified spell is in effect within the area, you become aware of it. You gain no other information-you don’t know the caster, caster level, remaining duration, or even the number of such spells in the area.

Spells whose effects confuse or block divinations (such asnondetection) automatically foil this cantrip, and therefore cannot be detected with it. If a creature has a spell on it that changes or conceals its appearance (such asdisguise self) and that spell is the one you specified, the creature can make aWisdomsaving throw against your spell save DC to prevent the cantrip from detecting their spell.

Recall Health.name: Recall Health
Recall Health.description:
A creature you touch regains a number ofhit pointsequal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

Night Shift.name: Night Shift
Night Shift.components: V, S, M (diamond dust worth 10 gp, which the spell consumes, and an hourglass worth 50 gp) Range Touch
Night Shift.duration: 8 hours The caster pours diamond dust into
Night Shift.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (diamond dust worth 10 gp, which the spell consumes, and an hourglass worth 50 gp)

The caster pours diamond dust into a large hourglass, which slowly turns to sand as the lucid dreamer is cast into an ever-evolving dreamscape. The target experiences up to one day per caster level during which time it can perform any appropriate downtime activity that does not require the presence of other beings or tools it cannot access within the dream. Any interruption during the rest (such as being awoken) ends the effect of the spell on the awakened target.

Targets sleeping with an attuned somnifer can manifest one or more physical representations of their somnifer as a placeholder for a required instructor or contact, preparing for the activity in the real world and reducing the time this activity would take outside of a dream by up to 25%.

If a target with an attuned somnifer loses their somnifer before they awaken, they do not benefit from night shift and suffer two levels ofexhaustionwhen they wake up. The subject may recover from thisexhaustionby taking a short rest with their recovered somnifer.

Greater Overcharge.name: Greater Overcharge
Greater Overcharge.description:
You touch a rare or very rare magic item that has charges and isn’t cursed. This funnels loose magical energy into it beyond its normal capacity, causing it to thrum and vibrate with barely contained arcane power. It is clear there is something wrong with the magic item. When the spell ends, the magic item detonates with a blast of deadly arcane energy. All creatures within 30 feet of the magic item must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 8d12 force damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects.

Warlock Grimoire 4. ©2023 Open Design LLC. Authors: Lou Anders, Wolfgang Baur, HH Carlan, Robert Fairbanks, Basheer Ghouse, Richard Green, Tim Hitchcock, Jeremy Hochhalter, Victoria Jaczko, Rajan Khanna, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Jonathan Miley, Kelly Pawlik, Sebastian Rombach, Adam W. Parching Touch.name: Parching Touch
Parching Touch.description:
You can leach moisture from a living target as a melee spellattack, and you can make an additional suchattackeach round onyour turnas anAction. The target takes 1d6 Necrotic damage (2d6 if the target is an aquatic creature or a creature made of liquid, including most Oozes) and must make aConstitutionsaving throw or gain 1 level ofExhaustionand have its MaximumHit Pointsreduced by the amount of damage taken. TheseHit Pointscannot be regained until theExhaustionis removed. A creature cannot gain more than 1 level ofExhaustionfrom Parching Touch.

Power Word: Distract.name: Power Word: Distract
Power Word: Distract.description:
You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving them distracted. If the target has less than 150hit pointsor fewer, all attacks against it has advantage and it cannot usereactionsfor 1 round.

Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

1st-levelenchantment(bard,sorcerer,warlock,wizard)

You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving themfatigued. If the target has less than 100hit pointsor fewer, it gains 1 levelexhaustion. Otherwise, the spell has no effect. Thisexhaustioncannot raise the target’sexhaustionlevel above 1.

The exhausted target must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, thisexhaustioneffect ends.

Falling Logs.name: Falling Logs
Falling Logs.description:
Three vertical, 10-foot long, five-foot-diameter logs appear in individual spaces of your choosing in the air within a 40-foot radius, centered on a point you can see that is 50 feet above the ground. The spell fails if you cannot see a point in the air where the logs could appear (for example, if you are in a room with a low ceiling). The logs must be at least 10 feet from one another. The logs simultaneously fall 50 feet to the ground in a straight, vertical line. A creature directly beneath a log must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 8d6 bludgeoning damage, fall to the groundprone, and bestunned. On a successful saving throw, the creature takes half as much damage, remains standing, and is notstunned.

Each creature within five feet of the point where the log fell, except the creature struck, must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or be knockedprone. The point where the log fell and a random space within five feet of that point then becomedifficult terrain. At the end of each of its turns, astunnedcreature can make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the creature is no longerstunned.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Templar’s Bellow.name: Templar’s Bellow
Templar’s Bellow.description:
Your faith is focused into a short utterance or warcry, which extends out from you in a 15-foot radius and causes one of the following effects of your choice:

Rise. Each friendly creature within range that can hear you is magically set upright if it isproneand has advantage on the firstattackroll it makes before the start of your next turn.

Ruin. Each hostile creature within range that can hear you must make aWisdomsaving throw, taking 2d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage dealt by the Ruin aspect increases by 1d6 each slot level above 2nd. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the range increases by 5 feet for every two slot levels above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Shape of the Wind.name: Shape of the Wind
Shape of the Wind.description:
You choose a point within range and a warm wind blows within a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on it. Wind, in the shape of Tiny animals (of your choice), runs freely within the area. You create one of the following magical effects within range:

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

Halucinatory Maze.name: Halucinatory Maze
Halucinatory Maze.description:
Your illusion creates multiple paths that branch in all directions, confusing all within a 150-foot cube. Each creature within the cube must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw when you cast this spell or be affected by it.

An affected target can’t takereactionsand uses all its movement to move in a random direction. A creature that moves out of the cube is no longer affected.

This spell turns handkerchiefs into fully furnished tents.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Unearthly Chorus.name: Unearthly Chorus
Unearthly Chorus.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,warlock(fiend patron only)

You channel the cacophony of the lower planes through your voice. Creatures within the area of the spell must make aWisdomsave and aCharismasave. Creatures that fail theWisdomsave fallunconsciousfor the duration of the spell.

Creatures who fail theCharismasave arestunnedfor 1 round.

Fiends and creatures that cannot hear you are immune to this spell.

Anunconsciouscreature can make a newWisdomsaving throw at the end of their turn. On a successful save, the spell ends for that creature.

Clerics & Cultists© 2021, Legendary Games; Author Darrin Drader, Nicholas Hite, Sean K Reynolds, Jason Nelson, Jenny Jarzabski, Miguel Colon, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Daley, Nathan Reinecke.

Essence Pulse.name: Essence Pulse
Essence Pulse.description:
You release a pulse of energy that emanates from your Summon. Each creature within 10 feet of your Summon (other than your Summon) must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or take 1d6 force damage and be knocked up to 5 feet away from your Summon. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Dispel Evil and Good.name: Dispel Evil and Good
Dispel Evil and Good.components: V, S, M(holy water or powdered silver and iron)
Dispel Evil and Good.description:
Shimmering energy surrounds and protects you from fey, undead, and creatures originating from beyond the Material Plane. For the duration, celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

You can end the spell early by using either of the following special functions.

Break Enchantment: As your action, you touch a creature you can reach that ischarmed,frightened, or possessed by a celestial, an elemental, a fey, a fiend, or an undead. The creature you touch is no longercharmed,frightened, or possessed by such creatures.

Dismissal: As your action, make a melee spell attack against a celestial, an elemental, a fey, a fiend, or an undead you can reach. On a hit, you attempt to drive the creature back to its home plane. The creature must succeed on aCharismasaving throw or be sent back to its home plane (if it isn’t there already). If they aren’t on their home plane, undead are sent to the Plane of Shadow, and fey are sent to the Plane of Faerie.
Dispel Evil and Good.material_component: holy water or powdered silver and iron

Deprive Nutrition.name: Deprive Nutrition
Deprive Nutrition.description:
A creature you touch must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or suddenly starve. A starving creature suffers one level ofexhaustion. If it eats one pound of food, the spell andexhaustioneffects end. The starvation andexhaustioneffects go away when the spell ends.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Cremation.name: Cremation
Cremation.description:
You touch a corpse or other remains. The target is instantly reduced to a pile of fine, gray dust that cannot be turned into an undead. The creature can be restored to life only by means of atrue resurrectionor awishspell. If it is restored to life, the creature can later be turned into an undead.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Gelatinous Wall.name: Gelatinous Wall
Gelatinous Wall.description:
You create a transparent, stationary wall of gelatinous slime.

The wall appears within range on a solid surface and lasts for the duration. You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and five feet thick or in a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and five feet thick.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature can choose to be pushed five feet back or to the side of the wall. A creature that chooses not to be pushed suffers the consequences of a failed saving throw. On a failed save, the wall engulfs the creature, and the creature takes 3d6 acid damage. The engulfed creature can’t breathe, isrestrained, and takes 6d6 acid damage at the start of each of your turns. An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within five feet of the wall.

A creature can attempt to move through the wall but suffers the same effect as a failed save mentioned above.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 6th.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Gas Mask.name: Gas Mask
Gas Mask.description:
You touch a living creature. A translucent, spectral mask covers the nose and mouth of the target. While this spell is in effect, the creature is immune topoisonedorexhaustioneffects from impaired breathing, such as poisonous gas (likestinking cloud) and stenches (like a troglodyte’s or ghast’s stench), but not effects that would stop breath (like being underwater or completely buried).

For effects that inflict damage as a result of a gas, likecloudkillor a green dragon’s breath, the spell grants advantage on a saving throw against the effect. When used in this way, the spell ends.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Intercessory Martyr.name: Intercessory Martyr
Intercessory Martyr.description:
When an ally within range would take damage, you can use yourreactionto cast this spell and provide your ally with 2d8temporary hit pointsplus 1 additional temporary for every level ofpaladinyou possess. Thesetemporary hit pointslast for 1 minute or until they are used up, and any damage taken by the target is deducted from thesetemporary hit pointsfirst.

Immediately after casting the spell, you take damage equal to half the number oftemporary hit points(rounded up) that you granted to your ally.

Legendary Classes: Templars & Tyrants© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Clinton J. Boomer, Amber Scott

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Seize the Heart.name: Seize the Heart
Seize the Heart.description:
You reach out with grasping tendrils of necrotic energy that plunge into the chest of living creatures you designate and having them crawl into the hearts of creatures in a 20-foot cube. All creatures must succeed aConstitutionsaving throw or take 8d6 necrotic damage. Living creatures that do not have hearts, such as elementals, oozes, plants, and many types of aberrations, are unaffected by this spell. A creature that fails its saving throw gains 1 level ofexhaustion. A creature cannot surpass 2 levels of exhaustion because of this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 5th level spell slot or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 4th.

Legendary Shamans (5E) © 2021, Legendary Games; Author Miguel Colon.

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
Three illusory duplicates of yourself appear in your space. Until the spell ends, the duplicates move with you and mimic your actions, shifting position so it’s impossible to track which image is real. You can use your action to dismiss the illusory duplicates.

Each time a creature targets you with an attack during the spell’s duration, roll a d20 to determine whether the attack instead targets one of your duplicates.

If you have three duplicates, you must roll a 6 or higher to change the attack’s target to a duplicate. With two duplicates, you must roll an 8 or higher. With one duplicate, you must roll an 11 or higher.

A duplicate’s AC equals 10 + yourDexteritymodifier. If an attack hits a duplicate, the duplicate is destroyed. A duplicate can be destroyed only by an attack that hits it. It ignores all other damage and effects. The spell ends when all three duplicates are destroyed.

A creature is unaffected by this spell if it can’t see, if it relies on senses other than sight, such asblindsight, or if it can perceive illusions as false, as withtruesight.

Burning Grasp.name: Burning Grasp
Burning Grasp.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You reach out and touch a creature, engulfing it in flames. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d10 fire damage, or half as much damage on a successful save.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 1st.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Tooth Grinder.name: Tooth Grinder
Tooth Grinder.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a cracked tooth)

You cause immense pain in a target and cause their teeth to turn to dust. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failure, the target takes 3d6 damage and is unable to use any attacks using their mouth or mouths. If the target succeeds on their saving throw, they take half damage and do not lose their mouth-based attacks. If the target has no teeth, they are immune to this spell. At the end of the duration the target’s teeth return to normal.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target an additional creature as a target or increase the damage by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Fire Lance.name: Fire Lance
Fire Lance.description:
Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You create a lance of fire and hurl it at a target within range. Make a ranged spellattack. On a hit, the target takes 28 (8d6) fire damage.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you create one additional lance for each slot level above 4th. You can hurl these additional lances at one target or several.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Riptide.name: Riptide
Riptide.description:
With a sweeping gesture, you cause a great swell of water to rise up in a 20-foot tall, 20-foot radius cylinder centered on a point on the ground that you can see. Each creature in the area must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature isrestrainedand suspended in the cylinder or moves to the nearest edge of cylinder on a successful one.

At the start of your next turn, you can direct the current of the swell as it dissipates. Choose one of the following options:

Deep Magic: Elemental Magic © 2017 Open Design; Author: Dan Dillon.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Detect Thoughts.name: Detect Thoughts
Detect Thoughts.description:
For the duration, you can read the thoughts of certain creatures. When you cast the spell and as your action on each turn until the spell ends, you can focus your mind on any one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature you choose has anIntelligenceof 3 or lower or doesn’t speak any language, the creature is unaffected.

You initially learn the surface thoughts of the creature-what is most on its mind in that moment. As an action, you can either shift your attention to another creature’s thoughts or attempt to probe deeper into the same creature’s mind. If you probe deeper, the target must make aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails, you gain insight into its reasoning (if any), its emotional state, and something that looms large in its mind (such as something it worries over, loves, or hates). If it succeeds, the spell ends. Either way, the target knows that you are probing into its mind, and unless you shift your attention to another creature’s thoughts, the creature can use its action on its turn to make anIntelligencecheck contested by yourIntelligencecheck; if it succeeds, the spell ends.

Questions verbally directed at the target creature naturally shape the course of its thoughts, so this spell is particularly effective as part of an interrogation.

You can also use this spell to detect the presence of thinking creatures you can’t see. When you cast the spell or as your action during the duration, you can search for thoughts within 30 feet of you. The spell can penetrate barriers, but 2 feet of rock, 2 inches of any metal other than lead, or a thin sheet of lead blocks you. You can’t detect a creature with anIntelligenceof 3 or lower or one that doesn’t speak any language.

Once you detect the presence of a creature in this way, you can read its thoughts for the rest of the duration as described above, even if you can’t see it, but it must still be within range.

The following is content created by a publisher other than Wizards of the Coast.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can scan the thoughts of all creatures within range and locate one creature currently thinking about a single subject you choose when you cast the spell. You can read its thoughts as described in the spell’s description. This spell does not reveal which creature has these thoughts, and until you do you cannot speak to it in order to shape the course of its thoughts, and thus the information you receive may be limited.

When you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot, increase the spell’s range to 1 mile. Using a 7thlevel slot, increase the range to 10 miles. Increase the range to 1,000 miles if you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot.

Dimension Door.name: Dimension Door
Dimension Door.description:
You teleport yourself from your current location to any other spot within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction, such as “200 feet straight downward” or “upward to the northwest at a 45-degree angle, 300 feet.”

You can bring along objects as long as their weight doesn’t exceed what you can carry. You can also bring one willing creature of your size or smaller who is carrying gear up to its carrying capacity. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you cast this spell.

If you would arrive in a place already occupied by an object or a creature, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 force damage, and the spell fails to teleport you.

Faerie Fire, Mass.name: Faerie Fire, Mass
Faerie Fire, Mass.description:
You can place up to three 20-foot cubes each centered on a point you can see within range. Each object in a cube is outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Any creature in a cube when the spell is cast is also outlined in light if it fails aDexteritysaving throw. A creature in the area of more than one cube is affected only once. Each affected object and creature sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius for the duration.

Anyattackroll against an affected object or creature has advantage if the attacker can see it, and the affected creature or object can’t benefit from beinginvisible.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Raise Blind.name: Raise Blind
Raise Blind.components: V, S, M (handful of vines or twigs)
Raise Blind.description:
You cause vines and branches to sprout from the earth, forming a 30-foot-long wall that occupies a 5-foot-wide area. The wall is fragile, having an Armor Class of 10 and 5Hit Pointsper 5-foot section. The wall provides totalcoverto creatures on opposite sides, but creatures adjacent to it can see through small gaps. As a bonus action, you can slide the blade back into your body to conceal it. When the duration ends, the incision in your body disappears, your hit point maximum is restored, and the material component reappears.

You create a tangle of wickedly sharp briars that lash out to scathe a creature within range. Make a melee spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 piercing damage and becomes tangled in briars until the start of your next turn. While tangled with briars, a creature takes 1 piercing damage each time it willingly moves 5 feet. For example, a tangled creature that moves 20 feet would suffer 1 piercing damage four separate times: once after each 5-foot space it moves.

The pattern clearly outlines the target asfaerie fire, and in addition a living target isincapacitateduntil the end of its next turn if fails aWisdomsaving throw. At the end of its turn, the target makes anotherWisdomsaving throw.

By closing one eye, you reduce the light radius to 20 feet and dim light to an additional 20 feet. If you close both eyes, the light stops until you open one or both eyes again. You can see normally when your eyes are open. You can change the light level as a bonus action.

You touch a willing creature. Until the spell ends, the target’s body turns to sand. If the creature accepts your geas, it must complete the task within 30 days. If it accepts but fails to meet the conditions of the geas, it dies on the dawn of the 31st day and its spirit again departs the mortal world. You shape milky moonlight into a rail-less ribbon of translucent white force that resembles smooth glass. Your moonbridge can be up to 150 feet long and can be from 5 to 20 feet wide, as you choose; you can vary its width if you wish. You can form the moonbridge as a flat bridge, inclined ramp, or stair up to 45 degrees. It must be straight, continuous, and unbroken; if its surface would be interrupted by any creature or object, the ritual fails and the moonbridge does not form. When you touch a living target, it takes 8d8 necrotic damage on a failedConstitutionsaving throw, or half as much on a successful save. If reduced to0 hit points, it dies immediately and cannot attempt death saving throws. In death, its body putrefies and rots, and if any living creatures touches the body within 10 minutes after death the bloatbomb explodes in a 10-foot radius, causing all creatures in this area to take 2d4 acid damage and 2d4 poison damage, or half as much on a successfulDexteritysaving throw.

You bring down a curse upon a creature of your choice within range, intending to hasten the creature toward its death. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the nextattackthat hits the target before the end of the round deals an extra 1 damage. The firstattackthat hits the target during each subsequent round deals an extra 1 damage for each round that has preceded it: a total of an extra 2 damage at the end of the second round, and so forth, up to an extra 5 damage at the end of the fifth round, at which point the effect ends. Raise Nemesis.name: Raise Nemesis
Raise Nemesis.components: V, S, M (diamond worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
Raise Nemesis.description:
This spell is identical toraise dead, except it simultaneously raises two creatures with opposite alignments. For example, if you raise a Lawful Goodpaladin, then somewhere nearby, a Chaotic Evil warrior of similar power also returns to life. The second corpse must be within 100 miles. The two raised creatures have a vague sense of the direction and distance to their nemesis.

They aren’t compelled to battle one another or even to seek each other out. Their lives are, however, inextricably bound together in such a way that if either of them dies, the other also drops dead instantly.

Evil Npcs brought back with raise nemesis typically see it as an opportunity to create every sort of trouble imaginable.

If the spell is cast on a creature of true Neutral alignment, only that creature is restored to life.

You surround yourself with a protective aura of spectral energy. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and all saving throws.

You create a spectral, magic two-handed great hammer into the hands of the caster. Only the caster may use the weapon, and the spell ends if the hammer is dropped. The caster strikes with the sacred hammer, making a melee spellattackagainst a creature On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to 2d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. Revenge’s Eye.name: Revenge’s Eye
Revenge’s Eye.description:
You touch a creature’s visual organs and grant them the ability to see the trail left by creatures damaged by a weapon you cast order of revenge upon.

The targeted creature can distinguish between multiple affected creatures without effort. If you lose a trail due to a creature’s sudden shift in location, like jumping or teleporting, you may concentrate as a move action, which does not provoke opportunity attacks.

This reveals the direction and distance to where the trail resumes, so long as it is on the same plane. The trail remains visible if a creature flies or swims. It only stops if the creature dies, becomes the target ofdispel magic, leaves the plane of existence, or the duration ends.

This spell does not help the target discern illusions and does not identify magically altered, concealed creatures, orinvisiblecreatures. It only reveals trails left by those affected by order of revenge also cast by the spellcaster.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target +1 creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Call Lightning.name: Call Lightning
Call Lightning.description:
A storm cloud appears in the shape of a cylinder that is 10 feet tall with a 60-foot radius, centered on a point you can see 100 feet directly above you. The spell fails if you can’t see a point in the air where the storm cloud could appear (for example, if you are in a room that can’t accommodate the cloud).

When you cast the spell, choose a point you can see within range. A bolt of lightning flashes down from the cloud to that point. Each creature within 5 feet of that point must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 3d10 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On each of your turns until the spell ends, you can use your action to call down lightning in this way again, targeting the same point or a different one.

If you are outdoors in stormy conditions when you cast this spell, the spell gives you control over the existing storm instead of creating a new one. Under such conditions, the spell’s damage increases by 1d10.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher level, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 3rd.

Fragmentation Shot.name: Fragmentation Shot
Fragmentation Shot.description:
Class(es): eldritch knight,ranger

You imbue a piece of ammunition or a thrown weapon with explosive energy. If the projectile hits a creature or object before the spell ends, it detonates in a fiery explosion. The target of theattacktakes an additional 1d6 fire damage, and all creatures within a 5-foot radius of the target must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d6 fire damage, or no damage on a successful save.

The projectile or weapon reverts to normal if not used before the spell ends. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Spectral Knife.description:
Target: One creature within range

Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You conjure a ghostly, spectral knife and hurl it toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 necrotic damage. Hit or miss, the knife then explodes in a burst of psychic energy. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 2d6 psychic damage. This damage is increased to 3d6 for each creature that is below half itshit pointsmaximum.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the psychic damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Detect Shapechanger.name: Detect Shapechanger
Detect Shapechanger.description:
You can sense when a creature is marked by a supernatural force.

You have the ability to see shapechangers for what they are.

You can see the true form of creatures within 60 feet. Each round, you can examine one creature you can see to determine whether it is polymorphed, disguised, or transmuted, and what its true form is. If you look at a shapechanger in its true form, you immediately sense its shapechanging ability, but you can’t determine what other forms it might be capable of assuming.

Entranced By Calamity.name: Entranced By Calamity
Entranced By Calamity.description:
You cast the spell and implant into the target a fascination with violence and calamity. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, anytime the target sees or senses damage being dealt to a creature or object that deals more than 10hpof damage within 30 feet, they are unable to move or act while they witness the violence until the end of their next, or current if they dealt the damage, turn. At the end of their turn they are allowed aWisdomsaving throw to end the effect early. On a successful saving throw, either at the outset of the spell, or made during the normal duration, the next time the creature sees a qualifying violent event, it has disadvantage onattackrolls, ability checks, and skill checks until the end of its next turn and the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target an additional creature for each slot level above 2nd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Radiant Beacon.name: Radiant Beacon
Radiant Beacon.description:
A pillar of light falls from the air, filling the square you are in and the area within 5 feet of you. Each other creature in the area must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d8 radiant damage and isblindeduntil the start of your next turn.

On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’tblindedby this spell. Undead and oozes have disadvantage on this saving throw.

For the duration, a pillar of brilliant radiance shines around you and moves with you. It sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light is sunlight.

This spell’s light can be seen from a distance of up to 10 miles outdoors at night or 5 miles during twilight.

Chamber of Restoring Amber.name: Chamber of Restoring Amber
Chamber of Restoring Amber.components: V, S, M (piece of amber worth at least 50 gp)
Chamber of Restoring Amber.description:
A 15-foot-radius immobile dome of amber springs into existence around and above you and remains stationary for the duration. The spell ends if you leave the area.

The amber can fit up to twelve Medium or smaller creatures inside of it. The spell fails if its area includes a larger creature or more than twelve creatures. Only creatures you designate can enter the dome through an entrance in one of the dome’s walls. All other creatures are barred from entering the amber dome. Spells and other magical effects can’t extend through the amber or be cast through it. The atmosphere inside the amber is comfortable and dry, regardless of the weather outside. The interior is dimly lit in a soft, amber glow. The amber is opaque from the outside, but it is transparent from the inside.

A creature that remains in the amber for its full duration gains the benefits of a short rest, and it can’t be affected by this spell again until it finishes a long rest.

At Higher Levels. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Inconvenient Gathering.name: Inconvenient Gathering
Inconvenient Gathering.description:
One creature you can see within range becomes magically charged. Make a ranged spellattack. On a hit, the target magically attracts loose objects, such as rocks, mugs, grass, or papers. At the start of each of its turns, small, nonmagical objects that aren’t being worn or carried within 10 feet of the target roll, float, or otherwise move up to 10 feet and magically cling to the target. Each object must weigh no more than 10 pounds. The target, or a creature within reach of the target, can use an action to remove the objects from the target until the start of the target’s next turn. While objects are stuck to it, the target’s speed is halved, and it has disadvantage on weaponattackrolls that useDexterity.

At the end of each of its turns, the target can make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends.

Spite.name: Spite
Spite.description:
You prick your finger and anoint your forehead with your own blood, taking 1 piercing damage and warding yourself against hostile attacks. The first time a creature hits you with anattackduring this spell’s duration, it takes 3d6 psychic damage. Then the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

Mire Deep.name: Mire Deep
Mire Deep.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You create a 20-foot-by-20-foot, 20-foot deep patch of deep quicksand. Creatures in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failure the target falls into the quicksand right where they are and must immediately make anAthleticscheck to keep from going under the surface. On a successful saving throw, the target moves 5 feet closer to the edge, or if they are already at the edge of the area, they get to move to just outside the area assuming it is safe to do so.

Creatures must make anAthleticscheck against the spell’s save DC to move 5 feet in any direction, or make the same check with advantage to remain in the same spot. If a creature fails by the check 5 or more, they sink down 5 feet and must begin holding their breath or drown. Such creatures can attempt to swim back to the surface with anAthleticscheck, though if they spend 2 rounds consecutively under the surface, they have disadvantage on the check. In all cases theAthleticschecks use all of the target’s movement, but any creature under the surface must make a Concentration check to cast spells to the viscousNatureof the quicksand and retrieving or stowing items requires aStrengthcheck against the spell save DC.

A creature may attempt to save a creature stuck in the magical quicksand with a long branch or other long item. The rescuer must make aStrengthcheck against the spell save DC as an action to pull and the rescuee must also make aStrengthcheck against the same DC but with advantage to hold onto the item. If both checks succeed, the trapped creature is pulled 5 feet closer to safety. If the trapped creature fails to hold on they must make anAthleticscheck against the spell save DC or go under by 5 feet. The action to save the stuck creature does not include retrieving an item with which to save them.

Creatures that are large, with the exception of swarms, require more turns than smaller creatures to be affected.

Huge creatures treat the area asdifficult terrainon their first turn, then on subsequent failures, they are stuck.

Creatures larger than huge treat the area asdifficult terrainonly and do not need to make a saving throw.

The suction and viscous nature of the quicksand prevents flight or levitation from helping a stuck creature from escaping, but such creatures that are flying or levitating do not initially get affected by the spell.Control Watercan be used to grant creatures in the affected area to gain a +5 bonus on theirAthleticschecks. Transmute Rock turns the affected area to its original state, trapping creatures within, per that spell.

Other spells and their interaction with the quicksand are at the discretion of the GM.

Otherwise this quicksand operates as normal and when the spell ends, any trapped creatures are left on the ground where the quicksand was.

Glimpse The End.name: Glimpse The End
Glimpse The End.components: V, M (pinch of grave dust or a piece from a tombstone)
Glimpse The End.description:
You examine the life force in a creature you touch and sense when it will expire. You and the creature share a vision of the most likely way in which the creature will die. You both sense approximately how far into the future the event occurs. The vision is not a prophecy or a definite fate; life can take unexpected twists and turns. It is, however, the most likely outcome at the current time unless the creature alters the course of its life. The vision can seem to last as little as a few moments or as long as 30 minutes to you and the spell’s target, but in the objective world, the knowledge is received instantaneously.

Viper’s Essence.description:
You infuse your arrows with the venomous essence of the viper. The next time you hit with a ranged weaponattack, the target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, the target takes an additional 5d8 poison damage and ispoisoneduntil the spell ends. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and is notpoisoned.

Shadow Armor.name: Shadow Armor
Shadow Armor.description:
You weave together moving strands of shadow to create a barrier around you until the spell ends. This barrier provides a protective force, and your AC can’t be less than 13 for the duration. In addition, the strands of shadow make you harder to target by sight. For the duration,ranged attackrolls and ranged spellattackrolls are made with disadvantage against you. An attacker is immune to this effect if it doesn’t rely on sight or can see through illusions.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration is 1 hour. If you use a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is 8 hours.

Funereal Hallucinations.name: Funereal Hallucinations
Funereal Hallucinations.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 minute

You complete the spell and fill the targets mind with the illusion that they have died and are on the path to their afterlife. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, they stand and march in place, taking no other action, including purely mentalactions. The target is effectively helpless and takes no measures to defend itself.

However, if the target takes any damage, is subject to a spell that imposes a detrimental condition or effect, or they reach the end of their turn, they get another saving throw to end the spell early.

Seal.name: Seal
Seal.components: V, S, M (an ounce of wax with flakes of gold worth at least 50 gp)
Seal.description:
You magically seal the cracks, crevices, gaps, and breaches of a room or vehicle, protecting those inside it. You must be in a room, structure, vehicle, or chamber with a ceiling, walls, and windows, doors, portcullises, or other ways of physically closing off ingress and egress, or the spell fails.

When you cast this spell, you touch the floor of a chamber that is up to fifty 5-foot squares and up to 10 feet tall, shaped as you desire. You can ward a long hallway, a square bedchamber, the lowest deck of a ship, the interior of a siege engine, or a similar chamber.

Until the spell ends, the chamber is protected in the following ways.
