Protection from Serpents.name: Protection from Serpents
Protection from Serpents.description:
Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch is protected against serpents that are aberrations, beasts, monstrosities, and humanoids (but not dragons, fey, or fiends).

The protection grants several benefits. An affected creature cannot touch the target of the spell, though it can cast spells or make ranged ormelee attackswith weapons. However, affected creatures have disadvantage onattackrolls against the target, and the target has advantage on all saving throws made against spells or traits of an affected creature.

If the target moves so that an affected creature is forced to touch the target, the spell ends.

Necropolis, © 2021, Necromancer Games; Author Mark Greenberg, Bill Webb

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Sandstorm.name: Sandstorm
Sandstorm.components: V, S, M (handful of sand or dust)
Sandstorm.description:
Class(es): Druid, Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You conjure a swirling sandstorm centered on yourself, filling the area with blinding sand and debris. Each other creature within the radius must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage and isblindeduntil the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn’tblinded. A small sandstorm rages on in the area for as long as you are concentrated on the spell or until the spell ends, making the areadifficult terrainfor creatures other than you that are flying.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd. Additionally, the radius of the sandstorm increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 3rd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Doom of Night.name: Doom of Night
Doom of Night.description:
You create a 30-foot-radius sphere of pulsing, luminous purple mist centered on a point you choose within range. This area is heavily obscured. When a creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 5d12 necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Creatures are affected even if they hold their breath or don’t need to breathe.

After leaving the mist, the creature takes 5 points of necrotic damage per round until it succeeds on aConstitutionsaving throw or dies.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d12 for each slot level above 6th. The follow-on damage increases by 1 point for each slot level above 6th.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Throne of Sacred Mistletoe.name: Throne of Sacred Mistletoe
Throne of Sacred Mistletoe.description:
You create a gleaming seat of crystal twined about with verdant mistletoe and berries of silver and gold, arching over you and gleaming with bright light equivalent to daylight in a 30-foot radius, sparkling through innumerable transparent, ghostly silver and gold sprigs of leaves floating through the air. These crystalline leaves float harmlessly, but they explode in deadly shards in the presence of violence. Creatures that attempt to use an action toattackyou or your allies take 5d6 piercing damage, 5d6 slashing damage, and 5d6 radiant damage and must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or the action they attempted to use to attack is spoiled without effect and the creature forfeits all actions remaining that round other than movement. The glittering sprigs refract the vision of creatures hostile to you, causing them to have disadvantage on allranged attacksmade when they or their targets are within range. You may designate yourself or another creature within range as the rightful regent to sit upon that royal seat, and as long as that creature remains seated upon the throne, it gains a +6 bonus toCharisma(to a maximum of 24). The verdant mistletoe of the throne lashes out to protect the designated creature from attacks, granting them advantage onDexteritysaving throws as long as they remain seated, while both ranged andmelee attacksagainst that creature have disadvantage.

The Dragon’s Hoard #14 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Gates of Heaven.name: Gates of Heaven
Gates of Heaven.description:
Choose a point within range. A 20-foot-high and 20-foot-wide marble arch appears, centered on it. The arch is a one-waygatefrom heaven and sheds bright light in a 90-foot cone emerging from the designated point. The aberrations, fiends, and the undead within the light must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 radiant damage and isfrightenedfor 1 minute. On a successful save, the damage is halved and the creature is notfrightened. Also, a celestial of your choice of challenge rating 2 or lower comes forth through thegate. The celestial disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. The celestial is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Rollinitiativefor the celestial, which has its own turns. It obeys no verbal commands you issue to it, but acts in the way that is most beneficial to you. The GM has the celestial’s statistics.

On each of your turns until the spell ends, you can use your action to make thegateshed bright light, dealing the radiant damage again, and summoning another celestial of challenge rating 2 or lower.

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Mass Contagious Healing.name: Mass Contagious Healing
Mass Contagious Healing.description:
A wave of magical disease washes out from a point of your choice within range. Choose up to three creatures in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. Each target is infected by a magical disease and regainshit pointsequal to 3d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

The next time an infected target takes damage, the disease ends on the target and infects a new friendly creature within 10 feet of the first. The new target regainshit pointsequal to 2d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. The next time the new target takes damage, the disease ends on it and moves to another friendly creature within 10 feet of it.

The disease continues moving from target to target in this way, reducing the amount ofhealingby 1d8 each time the disease moves to a new target. The final target regainshit pointsequal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier and that instance of the disease ends. This spell ends early if all instances of the disease end. A creature can be healed multiple times by this spell but can have only one instance of the disease on it at a time. If a creature already has an instance of this disease and would gain another, the previous instance of the disease immediately moves to another valid target as if the creature had taken damage. This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th-level or higher, thehealingincreases by 1d8 for each slot level above 7th.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Ill-Fated Word.name: Ill-Fated Word
Ill-Fated Word.description:
You call out a distracting epithet to a creature, worsening its chance to succeed at whatever it’s doing. Roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from anattackroll, ability check, or saving throw that the target has just made; the target uses the lowered result to determine the outcome of its roll.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Viper Spit.name: Viper Spit
Viper Spit.description:
You spew forth a spray of virulent venom in a 10-foot cone, causing all creatures in the area to take 4d6 poison damage and becomeblindedfor 1 minute. Creatures in this area can attempt aConstitutionsaving throw for half damage and to negate theblindedeffect. A blinded creature can attempt a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.

Boricubos: The Lost Isles (5E) © 2021, Legendary Games; Author: Miguel Colon.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Minor Disguise.name: Minor Disguise
Minor Disguise.description:
You use magic to make minor, cosmetic changes in your appearance as if using a disguise kit. The spell does not change the actual structure of either your features or body.

It can add color to hair, paint wrinkles upon your face, give you a scar, darken your teeth, etc. Using this spell does not speed up the disguising process but it can be used in conjunctions with spells that do. This spell gives you advantage when using a disguise kit made during the casting of the spell.

Breath of Life: The Lathspell (5e), © 2023, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Elf Locks.name: Elf Locks
Elf Locks.description: You cause ahumanoidcreature’s hair to grow at an incredible rate, and animate it to bind them. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or its hair instantly grows to 10 feet and attempts to ensnare it. A target that fails itsConstitutionsaving throw must make aDexteritysaving throw versus your spell save DC at the beginning of each of its turns for the spell’s duration or berestrainedby the hair. Oncerestrained, the target may break free of the hair with a successfulStrength(Athletics) orDexterity(Acrobatics) check against the hair’sStrength(Athletics) check (treat the hair as having aStrengthscore equal to your primary spellcasting ability score). Once the spell ends, the hair created by the spell remains in place, though it is perfectly mundane in nature.

Summon Mutants.name: Summon Mutants
Summon Mutants.description:
Classes:sorcerer,warlock,wizard

This spell functions as conjure animal except that the creatures you summon all have the mutant template (see page xx).

The Dragon’s Hoard #42© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke

Copy Smite.name: Copy Smite
Copy Smite.description:
The first time you hit with a melee weaponattackduring this spell’s duration, your weapon is wreathed in magical energy, dealing an extra 3d6 force damage. Additionally, when you attack a creature of the same size or one size larger than yourself, you can choose one attack of the creature’s to copy. For the duration of the spell you can choose to use this copied attack as your action. Once you have used the copiedattack, the spell immediately ends but any effects of the attack retain their normal duration. The attack cannot be a spell but may be an attack with magical effects. The magic of this spell augments your body in such a way to make most attacks possible (such as magical claws or teeth) but the full extent of attacks you can copy is up to your GM.

If the attack you copy requires a saving throw, and you use it against the creature you copied the move from, that creature makes the saving throw with advantage.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Decapitate.name: Decapitate
Decapitate.components: V, S, M (sliver from a guillotine blade or headsman’s axe)
Decapitate.description:
When an ally within range scores a critical hit with a slashing weapon against a Huge or smaller creature with at least one head, you can cast this spell to make theirattackmore lethal.

The blow ignoresresistance(but not immunity) to slashing damage and deals triple damage rather than double. The blow also deals an additional 4d6 slashing damage and 4d6 necrotic damage, or half as much on a successful Fortitude save. If the target fails its saving throw and damage fromattack(including additional damage from the spell) reduces it below 10hit points, its head is cut off and it dies immediately. Creatures with legendaryactions, immunity to slashing damage, or with multiple heads (or that simply are not slain by the loss of a head) are not killed by decapitate.

Alternatively, when a creature within range is reduced to0 hit points, you can cast this spell as areaction. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is instantly decapitated and dies, as if it had failed three death saving throws.

The Dragon’s Hoard #24 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Decapitate.material_component: sliver from a guillotine blade or headsman’s axe

Dream Serpent.name: Dream Serpent
Dream Serpent.components: V, S, M (scale or feather from an extraplanar serpent or serpentine outsider)
Dream Serpent.description:
You draw a serpentine phantasm from the subconscious of one target. This shadowy serpent of shifting colors twines around the target, who must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomeGrappled, taking 1d6 Bludgeoning at the beginning of each of its turns until it escapes. Since the Dream Serpent is entirely illusory, it can’t escape physically; instead, each time it attempts to escape using itsStrengthorDexterity, it instead makes aWisdomsaving throw to disbelieve the illusion and break free. A creature that is immune to beingCharmedhas Advantage on theirWisdomsaving throw against the Dream Serpent.

The Dragon’s Hoard #61© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Robert J. Grady, Ismael Alvarez, Amber Scott, Jeff Ibach, Katherine Schuttler.

Dream Serpent.material_component: scale or feather from an extraplanar serpent or serpentine outsider

Nature’s Balance.name: Nature’s Balance
Nature’s Balance.components: V, S, M (leaf from the most ancient tree in the world)
Nature’s Balance.description:
You invoke the equilibrium of nature, creating a field of balance around you. For the duration, you and any number of creatures you designate at the time of casting have advantage on ability checks,attackrolls, and saving throws while within 60 feet of you. Any other creature within the same radius has disadvantage on ability checks,attackrolls, and saving throws.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Nature’s Balance.material_component: leaf from the most ancient tree in the world

Moon’s Song.name: Moon’s Song
Moon’s Song.components: V, S, M (bottle of water collected at morning or night, depending on the spell, which the spell consumes.)
Moon’s Song.description:
You whistle a charming tune that appears to change the time of day to its exact opposite. If it is day it changes to night, if it is night, you change it to day. Each creature within the range of the spell must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw against your spell save DC or believe the change has occurred. The illusion is so real to them, their body reacts to the changes. Any damage that would be taken from these changes is psychic damage. The affected creatures can attempt aWisdomsaving throw at the start of their turns todispelthe illusions effects on them. For example, creatures that cannot see in dim light would be blind in a moonless night illusion. Creatures that take damage from sunlight would take damage from the day illusion. Even lycanthropy based on the moon could be activated in this way. The day is high noon, bright sun and the night is midnight, with the moon phases at your discretion.

Howling Agony.name: Howling Agony
Howling Agony.components: V, S, M (needle and a dried eyeball)
Howling Agony.description:
You send writhing pain coursing through the body of a creature within range, and that creature must make aCharismasaving throw. Whenever a target that fails this saving throw makes anattackroll, damage roll, orDexteritysaving throw before the spell ends, the target must roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from its result. If the target is attacked while the spell persists, the attacking creature adds 1d4 to its attack and damage. If the target takes areactionto scream as loudly as possible before the d4 is rolled, it can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. The target has advantage on the saving throw if it’s triggered by damage. On a success the spell ends.

Shapechange.name: Shapechange
Shapechange.components: V, S, M(a jade circlet worth at least 1,500 gp, which you must place on your head before you cast the spell)
Shapechange.description:
You assume the form of a different creature for the duration. The new form can be of any creature with a challenge rating equal to your level or lower. The creature can’t be a construct or an undead, and you must have seen the sort of creature at least once.

You transform into an average example of that creature, one without any class levels or the Spellcasting trait.

Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the chosen creature, though you retain your alignment and Intelligence, Wisdom, andCharismascores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus listed in its statistics is higher than yours, use the creature’s bonus in place of yours. You can’t use anylegendary actionsor lair actions of the new form.

You assume the hit points and Hit Dice of the new form. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. If you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren’t knocked unconscious.

You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them, provided that your new form is physically capable of doing so. You can’t use any special senses you have (for example, darkvision) unless your new form also has that sense. You can only speak if the creature can normally speak.

When you transform, you choose whether your equipment falls to the ground, merges into the new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal. The GM determines whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature’s shape and size. Your equipment doesn’t change shape or size to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can’t wear must either fall to the ground or merge into your new form. Equipment that merges has no effect in that state.

During this spell’s duration, you can use your action to assume a different form following the same restrictions and rules for the original form, with one exception: if your new form has more hit points than your current one, your hit points remain at their current value.
Shapechange.material_component: a jade circlet worth at least 1,500 gp, which you must place on your head before you cast the spell

Champion’s Sacrifice.name: Champion’s Sacrifice
Champion’s Sacrifice.description:
When casting this spell you empower your weapon with the power to destroy the enemies of your faith with your own life force. Theattackdeals an extra 3d6 radiant damage and you take half the extra damage dealt back to you as necrotic damage.

The necrotic damage cannot be reduced byresistanceor immunity.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you increase radiant damage dealt, and subsequently damage dealt to yourself, by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Solar Apocalypse.name: Solar Apocalypse
Solar Apocalypse.components: V, S, M (firefly and amber worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes)

You close your eyes and cast the spell as you imagine the sun devouring heretics. Choose up to five creatures within range.

Each target must make aWisdomsaving throw. A target has a vision of the sun falling out of the sky, and crashing on it with great force, taking 5d12 fire damage and 5d12 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Even if a target understands that this is an illusion, it is still affected by the spell.

Scarify.name: Scarify
Scarify.description:
You lock a stowed or sheathed weapon in place on a creature’s body. To draw the weapon, the creature must first use an action to succeed at a Strength check against the spell DC. Doing so can provoke a reaction whether the attempt succeeds or fails

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th or higher, if a weapon is drawn, it attempts to sheath or stow itself. The creature holding the weapon must succeed on a Strength check against the spell DC. If they fail the weapon is sheathed and the spell operates as the base version. If there is no sheath or place to stow the weapon, the weapon is dropped and the Strength check is required to retrieve it from the ground.

Butterfly Effect.name: Butterfly Effect
Butterfly Effect.description:
You cause a cloud of illusory butterflies to swarm around a target you can see within range. The target must succeed on aCharismasaving throw or becharmedfor the duration. Whilecharmed, the target can’t takereactionsand must roll a d10 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior for that turn.

At the end of each of its turns, and each time it takes damage, the target can make anotherCharismasaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

Vomit Swarm.name: Vomit Swarm
Vomit Swarm.description:
You vomit forth a swarm of insects that attacks all other creatures within its area. The swarm begins in one of the squares adjacent to you, but if no living creatures are within its area, it moves in one direction of your choosing at its normal speed.

You can move the swarm or change the swarm’s direction by spending a bonus action to concentrate on the swarm, otherwise it continues moving in its current direction.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can vomit up one additional swarm of insects for each slot level above 2nd. You can control the movement of all swarms as part of the same bonus action.

Greater Flaming Sphere.name: Greater Flaming Sphere
Greater Flaming Sphere.components: V, S, M (bit of tallow, a pinch of brimstone, and a dusting of powdered iron)
Greater Flaming Sphere.description:
A 10-foot-diameter sphere of fire appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of the sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. The creature takes 5d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If there’s room within the sphere, the creature that fails its save is trapped within it. The sphere can contain a maximum of one Large creature, four Medium creatures, eight Small creatures, or 16 Tiny creatures. The sphere is opaque. A creature that passes through the sphere (for example, a trapped creature attempting to exit it) takes 5d8 fire damage. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the sphere for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The interior of the sphere deals no damage. As a bonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make the saving throw against the sphere’s damage, and the sphere stops moving this turn. When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. The sphere ignites flammable objects not being worn or carried, and it sheds bright light in a 40-foot radius and dim light for an additional 40 feet.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 5th.

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

When you cast this spell, frost seems to hang in the air around you. For the duration, you gainresistanceto fire damage, and all creatures within 10 feet of you take 4d6 cold damage and gain the first level ofexhaustion. This spell cannot cause a creature to go above the first level of exhaustion.

The creature may make aConstitutionsaving throw to halve the damage and negate theexhaustioneffect.

At Higher Levels. When casting this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher, the cold damage dealt by your aura increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3rd.

Curse of Echoing Agony.description:
You amplify the pain of a creature you can see, causing its agony to echo back upon it. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed for the duration. Each time a creature cursed in this way takes damage, it must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take additional psychic damage equal to half the damage taken (rounded down).

Dimensional Shackles.name: Dimensional Shackles
Dimensional Shackles.components: V, S, M (small iron sigil worth at least 250 gp)
Dimensional Shackles.description:
Target: One creature within range

Classes: Cleric, Summoner, Wizard

You seal a creature within the current plane of existence, severing its ability to leave it through magical means. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, the creature cannotteleportor use any other form of extraplanar travel (such as theplane shiftspell) for the duration. Additionally, while affected by this spell, the creature has disadvantage on saving throws against being banished or forcibly be teleported against its will, as its connection to dimensional energies has been disrupted.

Once affected and until the spell ends, the creature is aware that something is interfering with its ability toteleport, but it does not automatically know the source unless it has reason to suspect it.

Mudslide.name: Mudslide
Mudslide.description:
You create and cause a cascade of mud to flow from a point on the ground you can see within range. The mud flows in a direction of your choice in a 30-foot line that is 10 feet wide. Each object in the line that isn’t being worn or carried is buried under 5 feet of mud. Each creature in the line must make aStrengthsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to half the length of the line in a direction following the line, knockedprone, and buried under the mud. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed, knockedprone, or buried. A buried creature isrestrainedand unable to breathe or stand up. A buried creature, or a creature within reach of a buried creature, can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, the buried creature is no longer buried.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the line’s length increases by 5 feet and the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 4th.

You attempt to end one condition affecting you by instantly clearing your mind. While you arecharmedorfrightened, you can use yourreactionto reroll the saving throw.

Sinful Suspicion.name: Sinful Suspicion
Sinful Suspicion.components: V, S, M (piece of charcoal and a strip of black silk)
Sinful Suspicion.description:
You stir mistrust and paranoia in the minds of your target creatures with an evil alignment, compelling them to suspect even their closest allies of plotting betrayal and harm. You can target one creature per caster level with this spell, as long as no two targets are more than 30 feet apart. The target is allowed aWisdomsaving throw; a successful save negates this effect.

For the duration of the spell, affected creatures view all other creatures as potential threats. They do not consider any creature to be their ally, and they react with hostility even to those they previously trusted. They take opportunity attacks against creatures they threaten whenever the opportunity arises, even against creatures they would normally consider allies. Additionally, they must attempt saving throws against any harmless or beneficial spells cast on them by other creatures.

At the start of each of the affected creature’s turns, if a creature it once considered an ally has attacked it during the duration of the spell, the affected creature is compelled to attack that former ally on its turn. If no former ally has attacked it, the affected creature has a 50% chance each round of being compelled to attack the nearest former ally, prioritizing evil-aligned allies over non-evil allies. The affected creature can use any available means to attack, including melee or ranged weapons, spells, special abilities, or other methods.

Affected creatures can include other creatures in area effects or abilities that target multiple creatures.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level, the range of the spell increases by 20 feet.

Glacial Blade.description:
Classes:sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You brandish the weapon used in the spell’s casting and make amelee attackwith it against one creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects suffers the attack’s normal effects and it becomes encased in a thin sheath of ice until the start of your next turn. If the target uses its action to make a weapon attack, it immediately takes 1d8 cold damage, and the spell ends.

At 5th level, the melee attack deals an extra 1d8 cold damage to the target on a hit, and the damage the target takes for making a weapon attack increases to 2d8. Bothdamage rollsincrease by 1d8 at 11th level (2d8 and 3d8) and again at 17th level (3d8 and 4d8).

Shield of Fortification.name: Shield of Fortification
Shield of Fortification.description:
You enhance the protective power of the target’s armor or shield, helping it to shield their vital organs. If the target takes a critical hit, roll 1d20. If the result is 16 or higher, treat that hit as a normal hit instead of a critical hit. Each time the spell negates a critical hit, the target number required to treat the next critical hit as a normal hit increases by 2.

If the target is not wearing armor or using a shield, this spell has no effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level, when the target would take a critical hit, they must roll a 10 or higher to treat the hit as a normal hit instead.

Shield of Ephemera.name: Shield of Ephemera
Shield of Ephemera.description:
Dream-like, indistinct patterns and shapes surround you.

Until the start of your next turn, you becomeinvisible, and you are immune to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. At the start of your next turn, any creature that saw you in the past minute but that can’t see you now forgets it saw you for the next 24 hours, Chapter 5 Spell Descriptions 223 its mind filling gaps in details or dismissing any memory of you as a dream. This effect ends early if the creature sees you within that time frame.

Leeching Sprouts.name: Leeching Sprouts
Leeching Sprouts.description:
You scatter seeds at the feet of a creature within range, which burst into entangling sprouts which sap a creature’s strength. The creature must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or berestrainedby the sprouts until the spell ends. At the start of each of the creature’s turns, it takes 2d10 acid damage, and you regainhit pointsequal to half the amount of acid damage dealt. A creature can use its action to repeat this saving throw on its turn.

Spare the Living.name: Spare the Living
Spare the Living.description:
Classes:pale master,warlock,wizard

You feed off the lingering fragments of life-force from the dying. Select a humanoid that has0 hit pointsand is not stable that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Death saving throw. On a failure, the creature inches closer to death and you gain 1d4temporary hit points.

Alternatively, you can target a humanoid corpse that has died within the last minute to gain this benefit. You cannot use the same corpse more than once.

You gain one additional 1d4temporary hit pointsat 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

Classes:sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You create aninvisibleforce barrier that protects you fromattack. You gain a +1 bonus to your AC against theattackthat triggered yourreaction. At 11th level, this bonus increases to +2.

At 5th level, you can cast deflect with a range of Touch and at 17th level with a range of 30 feet.

Globe of Reflection.components: V, S, M (small mirror that shatters when the spell ends)
Globe of Reflection.description:
An immobile, faintly shimmering cloud springs into existence in a 10-foot radius around you and remains for the duration. Any creature within the cloud has advantage on any saving throw against spells of 6th level or lower. Additionally, if any creature within the radius makes a successful saving throw against a spell or a spellattackthat misses it, the creature can choose another target (including the spellcasters) they can see within 30 feet. As areaction, the protected creature causes spell to target the chosen target instead of them. If the spell forced a saving throw, the target makes its own save. If the spell was an attack, the attack roll is rerolled against the target.

Instant Snare.name: Instant Snare
Instant Snare.components: V, S, M(a loop of twine)
Instant Snare.description:
You create a snare on a point you can see within range. You can leave the snare as a magical trap, or you can use yourreactionto trigger the trap when a Large or smaller creature you can see moves within 10 feet of the snare. If you leave the snare as a trap, a creature must succeed on anIntelligence(Investigation) orWisdom(Perception) check against your spell save DC to find the trap. When a Large or smaller creature moves within 5 feet of the snare, the trap triggers. The creature must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or be magically pulled into the air. The creature isrestrainedand hangs upside down 5 feet above the snare’s location for 1 minute. Arestrainedcreature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, escaping the snare on a success. Alternatively, a creature, including therestrainedtarget, can use its action to make anIntelligence(Arcana) check against your spell save DC. On a success, therestrainedcreature is freed, and the snare resets itself 1 minute later. If the creature succeeds on the check by 5 or more, the snare is destroyed instead.

This spell alerts you with a ping in your mind when the trap is triggered if you are within 1 mile of the snare. This ping awakens you if you are sleeping.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can create one additional snare for each slot level above 3rd. When you receive the mental ping that a trap was triggered, you know which snare was triggered if you have more than one.

Frost Nova.name: Frost Nova
Frost Nova.description:
You unleash the arctic cold to freeze your foes. Each creature other than yourself within 20 feet of you must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 6d6 cold damage and has disadvantage onDexteritysaving throws until the end of your next turn.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage of this spell increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Ping.name: Ping
Ping.description:
Describe an object that is familiar to you. If the object is within range, you receive a counter ping, alerting you to its presence.

If more than one object fitting your description is present, multiple pings will be received, alerting you to roughly how many are around.

This spell can’t locate an object if any thickness of lead, even a thin sheet, blocks a direct path between you and the object.

When casting the spell, the caster may restrict the range if they wish to any amount less than the maximum.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the range is doubled for each higher level used.

Tails of the City © 2020, Silver Games, Llc; Authors: David Silver

Doom of False Friendship.name: Doom of False Friendship
Doom of False Friendship.description:
You try to convince a creature you can see within range that you are its ally. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, it will try to avoid treating you as an enemy for the duration. If combat occurs while the target is affected, the creature does notattackyou unless no other targets are available to it, and it does not choose you as the target of a harmful spell. If the target casts a spell or otherwise produces an effect that specifically targets enemies, you are not affected. If the target doesattackyou, it tries to render youunconsciousrather than kill you. Creatures that are immune to beingcharmedare not affected by this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can choose an additional target for each slot level above 5th.

Sonic Whip.name: Sonic Whip
Sonic Whip.components: V, S, M (miniature silk or leather whip)
Sonic Whip.description:
You create a lash of solid sound equivalent to a normal whip, which you can wield with proficiency. The sonic whip is treated as a magical weapon and deals either 1d4 bludgeoning or 1d4 slashing damage (your choice) plus an additional 1d4 thunder damage on each hit. In addition, you can crack the sonic whip overhead as a bonus action, causing all ordinary beasts with a Challenge of 2 or less to back away from you and not come within 30 feet unless they succeed on aWisdomsaving throw. If you strike such a creature, it must make an additionalWisdomsaving throw or becomefrightenedfor 1 round. Insects, arachnids, and similar nearly mindless creatures are immune to this effect, and creatures specifically trained for combat (or otherwise extremely aggressive, at the GM’s option) have advantage on their saving throw.

The Dragon’s Hoard #32© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, James-Levi Cooke.

Crimson Path.name: Crimson Path
Crimson Path.description:
You cut your palm dealing 1 damage and touch a living creature, violently and bloodily entering their body, and exiting in a similar fashion from a nearby creature.

Youteleport10 feet when touching Small or smaller creatures and the distance teleported doubles for eachsizecategory larger than small. Medium would be 20 feet, Large 40, and so on. The touched creature and the endpoint creature must makeConstitutionsaving throws or be dealt 12d6 necrotic damage. A successful saving throw halves this damage but does not prevent the teleportation. This spell cannot use bloodless creatures as a target or end point. If there is no valid endpoint creature available, this spell fails. You cannot enter and exit the same creature.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 5th.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

High Ground.name: High Ground
High Ground.description:
With a word, you gesture across an area and cause the terrain to rise up into a 10-foot-tall hillock at a point you choose within range. You must be outdoors to cast this spell. The hillock is up to 30 feet long and up to 15 feet wide, and it must be in a line. If the hillock cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the hillock or to the top of the hillock (your choice). Theranged attackdistance for a creature on top of the hillock is doubled, provided the target is at a lower elevation than the creature on the hillock. At the GM’s discretion, creatures on top of the hillock gain any additional bonuses or penalties that higher elevation might provide, such as advantage on attacks against those on lower elevations, being easier to spot, longer sight distance, or similar.

The steep sides of the hillock are difficult to climb.

A creature at the bottom of the hillock that attempts to move up to the top must succeed on aStrength(Athletics) orDexterity(Acrobatics) check against your spell save DC to climb to the top of the hillock.

This spell can’t manipulate stone construction, and rocks and structures shift to accommodate the hillock.

If the hillock’s formation would make a structure unstable, the hillock fails to form in the structure’s spaces. Similarly, this spell doesn’t directly affectplant growth. The hillock carries any plants along with it.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell at 4th level or higher, you can increase the width of the hillock by 5 feet or the length by 10 feet for each slot above 3rd.

Cloak of Flame.name: Cloak of Flame
Cloak of Flame.components: V, S, M (drop of oil and a spark)
Cloak of Flame.description:
This spell envelops you in a torrent of magical flames that conceal you, protect you from fire and cold, and can damage your enemies. The flames do not harm you or your equipment.

All attacks made against you have disadvantage from concealment. Any creature attacking you with natural weapons suffers 2d6 fire damage with each successfulattack. Anyone grappling with you automatically takes 3d6 fire damage every round.

Furthermore, you gain immunity to fire damage and haveresistanceto cold damage while the spell is in effect. You may also use your action to make melee spell attacks that inflict 2d6 fire damage upon other creatures within your reach. The cloak of flame is dispelled if it is submerged or doused with enough water to extinguish a large campfire.

You either create or destroy sand.

Classes: Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

Additionally, when you are hit by amelee attackfor the first time in a turn, the attacker takes 1d4 force damage as the shield lashes out in retaliation.

If it hits, the target takes 2d8 psychic damage and must make a successfulIntelligencesaving throw or beincapacitateduntil the start of your next turn.

Timeshift Spell.name: Timeshift Spell
Timeshift Spell.description:
You send a creature that you can see within range up to one minute into the future.

You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell that has an area of effect. If the creature is casting a spell of 2nd level or lower, you shunt it forward in time and the spell has no immediate effect. If it is casting a spell of 3rd level or higher, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell’s level. On a success, the creature’s spell is shunted forward in time and has no immediate effect. You determine when the spell manifests again in the time stream, up to the duration of your concentration (10 rounds maximum). If you lose your concentration, the spell manifests onyour turn. When the spell reappears it has the same area effect in the same spot as when it was originally cast.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the interrupted spell is shunted forward in time if its level is less than or equal to the level of the spell slot you used.

Nightwing Dusk.name: Nightwing Dusk
Nightwing Dusk.components: V, S, M (pitch and a bat wing)
Nightwing Dusk.description:
You conjure three bat swarms, which must be summoned so that each swarm is adjacent to at least one other swarm. You may summon them so that they share the area of other creatures.

Each swarm is stationary after being summoned and will not pursue fleeing creatures. The illumination level in a space occupied by abat swarmis filled by magicaldarkness, as thedarknessspell. Thisdarknessdissipates if thebat swarmis killed.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the number ofbatswarms increases by 1 for each slot level above 4th.

Lingering Sigh.name: Lingering Sigh
Lingering Sigh.components: V, S, M (pinch of chalk dust and a feather)
Lingering Sigh.description:
For the duration, you can sense and communicate with the lingering spiritual imprints that people leave upon places when they die. You are magically aware of how many humanoids have died in the location you currently occupy (within 30 feet of you), and you have a general understanding of how they died and how long ago it happened. Additionally, you can ask the GM three questions while the spell lasts. Each question must pertain directly to one of the deceased humanoids the spell makes you aware of.

The GM answers each question truthfully, but each answer is limited to information that would be available to someone who witnessed the subject’s death firsthand.

For instance, you can’t ask for a person’s name or identity, but you could ask what they looked like just before death, possibly recognizing the description. You also can’t ask how the person felt about someone else, but you could ask for a description of anyone present when the subject died. Then, as another question, you could ask what the deceased’s apparent emotional state was in those final moments (fear, anger, contentment, etc.).

If an answer would entirely contain information outside of the spell’s scope, you receive no answer, but it doesn’t count as one of your three questions.

The spell lasts for the duration even after all three questions have been asked and answered, but no further answers are given after the third.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can ask one additional question for each slot level above 3rd.

Dark Path.name: Dark Path
Dark Path.description:
You conjure a shadowy road between two points within range to create a bridge or path. This effect can bridge a chasm or create a smooth path throughdifficult terrain.

The dark path is 10 feet wide and up to 50 feet long. It can support up to 500 pounds of weight at one time. A creature that adds more weight than the path can support sinks through the path as if it didn’t exist.

Enchanted Strike.description:
You speak ancient words of power as you touch your ranged weapon. The next time you make a ranged weaponattackduring the spells duration, choose a damage type from the below list. Your attack does 2d8 damage of a chosen type in addition to the normal damage from the attack. The chosen damage type also causes an additional effect:

At higher levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the additional damage for each effect increases by 1d8 for each slot above third.

Tundra Hold.name: Tundra Hold
Tundra Hold.components: V, S, M (handful of snow or ice)
Tundra Hold.description:
Magical ice quickly spreads from a point you touch, extending in a line 60 feet long and 20 feet wide. Each creature caught in the ice’s path must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 cold damage and isrestrainedby ice. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’trestrained. The line then becomesdifficult terrainfor 10 minutes.

A creaturerestrainedby the ice must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the start of each of its turns, taking 1d8 cold damage on a failed save. A creaturerestrainedby the ice can use its action to make aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longerrestrained. If a creature remainsrestrainedby the ice for three of its turns, it becomespetrifiedat the start of its fourth turn, turning into an ice sculpture.

Arcane Eye.name: Arcane Eye
Arcane Eye.components: V, S, M(a bit of bat fur)
Arcane Eye.description:
You create an invisible, magical eye within range that hovers in the air for the duration.

You mentally receive visual information from the eye, which has normal vision anddarkvisionout to 30 feet. The eye can look in every direction.

Curse of Fractured Fate.name: Curse of Fractured Fate
Curse of Fractured Fate.components: V, S, M (cracked die worth at least 50 gp)
Curse of Fractured Fate.description:
Target: One creature you can see within range

Classes:Bard, Cleric,Sorcerer, Warlock,Wizard

You weave the threads of destiny, inducing a momentary lapse in fortune upon a creature you can see within range. Until the spell ends, the target is cursed, and it must roll any saving throw it makes with disadvantage.

Masking Nebula.description:
You create a 20-foot radius sphere of multicolored gas centered on a point you choose within range. For the duration of this spell, creatures friendly to you starting their turn in that cloud becomeinvisibleuntil the spell ends. Whenever aninvisiblecreature in the cloud is missed by anattack, they mayteleportup to 15 feet in any direction of their choice.

Steal Voice.name: Steal Voice
Steal Voice.duration: is concentration, up to 10 minutes. If
Steal Voice.description:
You steal away the target’s power of speech with a curse unless it succeeds on aWisdomsaving throw. While its voice is stolen, the target cannot make themselves heard unless they spend a bonus action to force their voice out, and even then they only can be heard by creatures within 20 feet.

The target must succeed on a DC 10Constitutionsaving throw in order to successfullycast a spellwith a verbal component or use acommandword to trigger a magic item, though they have advantage on this saving throw if they spend a bonus action to force their voice out. Even if spellcasting succeeds, targets gain advantage on their saving throw against any spell that involves speech as part of the spell’s effect, such ascommand,enthrall,suggestion, or power word spells. Remove curse ends this spell immediately.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. If you use a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is increased to 8 hours and the spell no longer requires concentration and cannot be ended bydispel magic. If you use a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the duration is increased to 24 hours. If you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, it is permanent until removed.

Paper Fan.name: Paper Fan
Paper Fan.description:
A folding fan of black paper stretched across stiffened spines decorated with feathered patterns appears in your hand. This is a simple finesse weapon and you may wield it, dealing 1d4 points of slashing or piercing damage on it hit. In addition, if you are aware of your opponent you may use a paper fan defensively in either of the following ways. When you are attacked with finesse or one-handed melee weapon you can expend 1 minute of the spell’s remaining duration as areactionto make to disarm your attacker using the paper fan. The target must make successfulDexteritysaving throw or you successfully disarm them. If this maneuver succeeds and you have a free hand, you can take the target’s weapon as if you had made the disarm check while unarmed, otherwise, the weapon drops to the floor within 10 feet of the attacking creature in a square of your choice. When you are attacked with a thrown weapon, you can expend 1 minute of the spell’s remaining duration as areactionto deflect that weapon, taking no damage from theattack.

Disengage into Darkness.name: Disengage into Darkness
Disengage into Darkness.description:
Immediately after you’ve completed your movement after taking theDisengageaction, if you are in a space that is lightly or heavily obscured, you areinvisibleuntil the end of your next turn; anything you are carrying or wearing is alsoinvisibleas long as it remains with you. You become visible if youattackorcast a spell.

Enervating Bolts.name: Enervating Bolts
Enervating Bolts.description:
You create three bolts of necromantic power and hurl them at targets within range. You can hurl them at one target or several. Make a ranged spellattackfor each bolt. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 necrotic damage. The target’s hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken.

The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you create one additional bolt for each slot level above 3rd.

Blood Spear.name: Blood Spear
Blood Spear.components: V, S, M (r recently spilled blood)
Blood Spear.description:
As part of the casting of this cantrip, you inflict 2 points of damage to yourself. The blood from your self-inflicted injury forms into a sharpened spear of crimson that rapidly soars toward a creature within range, drying as it flies through the air. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d12 piercing damage. The spell creates more than one blood spear when you reach higher levels (you take 2 additional points of damage for every extra spear formed): two spears at 5th level, three spears at 11th level, and four spears at 17th level. You can direct the spears at the same target or at different ones. Make a separateattackroll for each spear.

Vile spells are cruel and exploitative, bent to inflict unnatural pain or gain power from the suffering of victims.

They manipulate blood, blaspheme existence, pervert the physical form, conjure evil entities, or worse. Classes able to cast spells add all vile spells to their class spell list, but only creatures with a Sin ability score or evil alignment are able to cast spells from this school of magic without using a scroll or other magic item.

Vile spells leave an evil aura behind them, detectable withdetect evil and good. If the caster has no Sin ability score, use double the spell level to determine the strength of the aura left behind. Evil auras dissipate 10 minutes for every spell level + a number of minutes equal to double the caster’s Sin score. For example, a vile spell of 3rd-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 15 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour; a 3rd-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 30 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 15 doubled. A vile spell of 5th-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 20 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour and 30 minutes; a 5th-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 50 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 20 doubled.

Book of Exalted Darkness. © 2018 Mike Myler, published under license by Legendary Games.

Magic Ballista.name: Magic Ballista
Magic Ballista.description:
You create a floating, spectral ballista within range that lasts for the duration or until you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can make a ranged spellattackagainst a creature within 480 feet of the weapon. On a hit, the target takes 3d10 force damage. As an action onyour turn, you can move the weapon up to 20 feet and repeat theattackagainst a creature within 480 feet of it.

Up to two friendly spellcasters within range can contribute magical bolts to the ballista by sacrificing a spell slot of 3rd level or higher as a bonus action. A 3rd level spell increases the damage by 1d10, with an additional 1d10 for each two spell slots above 3rd level sacrificed in this fashion.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for every two slot levels above 3rd.

Savage Maw.name: Savage Maw
Savage Maw.description:
Your teeth become razor-sharp fangs, transforming your mouth by extending your jaw in a frightening display. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 piercing or slashing damage (you choose each time), and you are proficient with your unarmed strikes. When you hit a creature with your unarmed strike while the spell persists, it must succeed on aConstitutionsave at the end of each of its turns or take 1d6 damage of the same type your unarmed strike dealt. A creature only takes this damage once each turn, and anyhealingends the spell on the target.

Power Word: Pain.name: Power Word: Pain
Power Word: Pain.description:
You speak a word of power that can wrack the target with pain. If the target has less than 100hit pointsor fewer, it takes 2d6 psychic damage at the beginning of each of its turns. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

The affected target must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, thispoisonedeffect ends.

Merge with Familiar.name: Merge with Familiar
Merge with Familiar.description:
Classes:sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You can place yourself into a pocket dimension within the body of your familiar. You can use its senses, control its movements and attacks, and even speak through its mouth, though you cannot cast spells or use any other magical abilities through the familiar. Your body is treated asincapacitatedwithin the pocket dimension and can take noactionsother than communicating with and through your familiar. Attacks against your familiar do not affect you, though if your familiar is reduced to0 hit pointsit disappears and you immediately reappear in an adjacent square of your choice.

As an action, you can cause your body to reappear in a space adjacent to your familiar, or while you are adjacent to your familiar you can place your body back into the pocket dimension. If you are affected by any kind of ongoing harmful effect, that effect continues each round while you are in the pocket dimension. Any beneficial spells affecting you have no effect while you are in the pocket dimension.

The Dragon’s Hoard #38© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors: Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Jeff Lee, and Dan Dillon.

Soulbound Servant.name: Soulbound Servant
Soulbound Servant.description:
You temporarily bind a spirit to an object, causing it to animate the object and complete tasks for you.

Only one animated object or corpse may be controlled by the caster at a time. When the servant has completed three tasks, the object falls apart and is no longer functional-the spirit is released. In order to create a new animated object while one is already functional, you must physically destroy the existing object. If directed toattack, it uses the statistics for azombie,skeleton, oranimated object, as appropriate. Fighting for up to 5 rounds counts as a task. Theanimated objectspeaks with the voice of a deceased loved one; anyone hearing it hears a different voice, even though the message is the same. While the object fulfills the command, the object suffers minor cosmetic disintegration, losing bits and pieces but remaining functional. It also emits some sensory element that renders its nature apparent to the observant: an animated cat might leave pawprints which smolder for a second or two as it walks, a lantern might emit a scent of brimstone while it operates.

The spirit is required to accurately, correctly, and promptly complete the tasks ordered by you and to respond truthfully to your questions.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is extended for 1 day and one task per level of the spell slot used.

Warlock Grimoire 2. Authors: Wolfgang Baur, Celeste Conowitch, David “Zeb” Cook, Dan Dillon, Robert Fairbanks, Scott Gable, Richard Green, Victoria Jaczko, TK Johnson, Christopher Lockey, Sarah Madsen, Greg Marks, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Lysa Penrose, Richard Pett, Marc Radle, Hannah Rose, Jon Sawatsky, Robert Schwalb, Brian Suskind, Ashley Warren, Mike Welham. © 2020 Open Design LLC.

Earthquake.name: Earthquake
Earthquake.components: V, S, M(a pinch of dirt, a piece of rock, and a lump of clay)
Earthquake.description:
You create a seismic disturbance at a point on the ground that you can see within range. For the duration, an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 100-foot-radius circle centered on that point and shakes creatures and structures in contact with the ground in that area.

The ground in the area becomes difficult terrain. Each creature on the ground that is concentrating must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature’s concentration is broken.

When you cast this spell and at the end of each turn you spend concentrating on it, each creature on the ground in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone.

This spell can have additional effects depending on the terrain in the area, as determined by the GM.

Fissures: Fissures open throughout the spell’s area at the start of your next turn after you cast the spell. A total of 1d6 such fissures open in locations chosen by the GM. Each is 1d10 × 10 feet deep, 10 feet wide, and extends from one edge of the spell’s area to the opposite side. A creature standing on a spot where a fissure opens must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fall in. A creature that successfully saves moves with the fissure’s edge as it opens. A fissure that opens beneath a structure causes it to automatically collapse (see below).

Structures: The tremor deals 50 bludgeoning damage to any structure in contact with the ground in the area when you cast the spell and at the start of each of your turns until the spell ends. If a structure drops to 0 hit points, it collapses and potentially damages nearby creatures. A creature within half the distance of a structure’s height must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 5d6 bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is buried in the rubble, requiring a DC 20Strength(Athletics) check as an action to escape.

The GM can adjust the DC higher or lower, depending on the nature of the rubble. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn’t fall prone or become buried.

Wall of Bones.name: Wall of Bones
Wall of Bones.duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Classes: wizard
Wall of Bones.description:
This spell causes a wall of bones to erupt from the earth.

The wall appears within range on a solid surface and lasts for the duration. You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight. When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d8 piercing damage, or half as much damage on a successful save. A creature can move through the wall, albeit slowly and painfully. For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement. Furthermore, the first time a creature enters the wall on a turn or ends its turn there, the creature must make aDexteritysaving throw. It takes 3d8 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If you maintain your concentration on this spell for its whole duration, the wall becomes permanent and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disappears when the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, both types of damage increase by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

Holy Verdict: Retribution.name: Holy Verdict: Retribution
Holy Verdict: Retribution.description:
Choose a target that you can see within range. You utter a single word. The clouds give way to a heavenly golden spear, which falls down from heaven upon the target to destroy it, demonstrating the power of retribution. The target must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 10d8 piercing damage and 10d8 radiant damage. If the target is evil, it has disadvantage on the saving throw.

If this damage reduces the target to0 hit points, all good creatures within 120 feet of the spear gain 10temporary hit pointsfor 8 hours.

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

Fire Storm.name: Fire Storm
Fire Storm.description:
A storm made up of sheets of roaring flame appears in a location you choose within range. The area of the storm consists of up to ten 10-foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish. Each cube must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube.

Each creature in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. It takes 7d10 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The fire damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren’t being worn or carried. If you choose, plant life in the area is unaffected by this spell.

Timeless Engine.name: Timeless Engine
Timeless Engine.description:
You halt the normal processes of degradation and wear in a nonmagical clockwork device, making normal maintenance unnecessary and slowing fuel consumption to 1/10th that of normal. For magical devices and constructs, the spell greatly reduces wear.

A magical clockwork device, machine, or creature that normally needs daily maintenance only needs care once per year. If it previously needed monthly maintenance, it now requires attention only once per decade.

Zobeck: Clockwork City © 2022 Open Design Llc; Author: Wolfgang Baur, Mike Franke, James J. Haeck, Ben Mcfarland, Richard Pett, Christina Stiles, Matthew Stinson.

Lightning Chain.name: Lightning Chain
Lightning Chain.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You release a bolt of lightning that arcs towards a target you can see within range. The bolt then leaps from that target to another target of your choice within 30 feet of the first target. After striking the second target, the bolt leaps again to another target within 30 feet of the second target (even back to the original target if you choose). A target must make aDexteritysaving throw for each bolt they are targeted with, taking 2d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the number of times the bolt leaps increases by one for each slot level above 2nd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Fortify Object.name: Fortify Object
Fortify Object.description:
For the duration, an object you touch hasresistanceto bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing (your choice). If the object is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, the creature can make aDexteritysaving throw to avoid your touch.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Ice Spear.name: Ice Spear
Ice Spear.description:
You send a spear of ice hurtling at a creature within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 piercing and 1d4 cold damage. On impact, the spear can freeze up to a one-foot sphere of non-magical liquid. Any creature within the liquid is shunted to the nearest unoccupied space.

At Higher Levels. This spell’s piercing and cold damage each increase by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4 piercing plus 2d4 cold), 11th level (3d4 piercing plus 3d4 cold), and 17th level (4d4 piercing plus 4d4 cold).

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Doom of Serpent Coils.name: Doom of Serpent Coils
Doom of Serpent Coils.description:
You drink a dose of venom or other poison and spread the effect to other living things around you. If the poison normally allows a saving throw, your save automatically fails. You suffer the effect of the poison normally before spreading the poison to all other living creatures within 10 feet of you. Instead of making the usual saving throw against the poison, each creature around you makes aConstitutionsaving throw against the spell. On a successful save, a target suffers no damage or other effect from the poison and is immune to further castings of doom of serpent coils for 24 hours. On a failed save, a target doesn’t suffer the poison’s usual effect; instead, it takes 4d6 poison damage and ispoisoned. Whilepoisonedin this way, a creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a subsequent failed save, it takes 4d6 poison damage and is stillpoisoned. On a subsequent successful save, it is no longerpoisonedand is immune to further castings of doom of serpent coils for 24 hours.

Multiple castings of this spell have no additional effect on creatures that are alreadypoisonedby it. The effect can be ended byprotection from poisonor comparable magic.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Flame Blade.name: Flame Blade
Flame Blade.description:
You evoke a fiery blade in your free hand. The blade is similar in size and shape to a scimitar, and it lasts for the duration. If you let go of the blade, it disappears, but you can evoke the blade again as abonus action.

You can use your action to make a melee spell attack with the fiery blade. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 fire damage.

The flaming blade sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 2nd.

Half-Life.name: Half-Life
Half-Life.components: V, S, M (diamond worth at least 250 gp, which the spell consumes)
Half-Life.description:
You restore temporary life to a body that has been dead for less than 48 hours. If the creature’s soul is both willing and at liberty to rejoin the body, the creature returns to life with 1 hit point. This spell also neutralizes any poisons and cures nonmagical diseases that affected the creature at the time it died. This spell doesn’t, however, remove magical diseases, curses, or similar effects; if these aren’t first removed prior to casting the spell, they take effect when the creature returns to life. The spell can’t return an undead creature to life. This spell closes all mortal wounds, but it doesn’t restore missing body parts. If the creature is lacking body parts or organs integral for its survival—its head, for instance—the spell automatically fails. Coming back from the dead is an ordeal. The target takes a ?4 penalty to allattackrolls, saving throws, and ability checks.

The spell lasts for 24 hours, after which the target dies again. The target still counts as a dead corpse (but not undead) for the purpose of spells that revive dead creatures, and spells likeraise deadcan be cast on the target even while this spell is active. Once a creature has been revived with half-life, this spell cannot be used on it again until it is permanently raised from the dead.

Shadow Siphon.name: Shadow Siphon
Shadow Siphon.description:
You open a rift to the shadow plane and attempt to divert some of the energy of a damaging spell off of your current plane and transform the spell into a quasi-real illusion. The target of, or part of the area of the spell must be within range. Creatures that would be damaged take only half as much damage.

Any spell of 5th level or lower is partially shunted to the shadow plane. For any spell of 6th level or higher, you must make an ability check using your spellcasting ability modifier. The DC equals 10 + the spell’s level. On a successful check, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you automatically shunt part of the spell to the shadow plane if the spell’s level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you used.

Temple’s Denial.description:
You create the illusion of a temple around you in an area that is 60 feet long, 40 feet wide, and 12 feet high. When you are targeted by a spell, an illusory reflection of the spell bounces off the temple gates, and is reflected back to its caster. You are affected normally by the spell, and the caster of the spell is also affected by its own spell.

Bleed for your Master.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,druid,ranger,wizard

When you would be hit by anattackthat requires an attack roll or are within a harmful area effect that allows aDexteritysaving throw, with a touch you can compel your familiar or companion animal, or any creature you have conjured, dominated, or bound into your service (as withplanar binding), to throw itself in front of the blow and shield you from harm. Creatures not bound to your service in one of these ways are immune to this spell, and the spell has no effect if the target creature isfrightened.

If an attack roll triggered this spell’s casting, the target takes the damage from the attack instead of you, even if the attack roll would have missed your companion creature’s Armor Class.

If the effect allows aDexteritysaving throw, you instead gain a +2 bonus on your saving throw (if the creature is smaller than you. If the creature is larger than you, you have advantage on the saving throw and you take no damage from the effect if you succeed on your saving throw, or half as much damage as normal if you fail. Your companion creature automatically fails itsDexteritysaving throw against the effect.

After this spell is cast, your companion creature is immediatelyfrightenedfor 1 minute. A creature that is magically controlled by you also can make aCharismasaving throw (with disadvantage, unless it is immune to beingfrightened); if it succeeds, the effect that was controlling it ends.

Read Cypher.description:
You can magically manipulate the symbols on a page, making it much easier and faster to decipher hidden messages.

When you cast this spell on a coded message, you can use theIntelligence(Arcana) skill to decode it against the normal DC. If you are proficient in bothArcanaand cryptographer’s tools, you can add double your bonus. Furthermore, you can ignore the time needed to decode complex messages listed in the Decoding Difficulty and Time table, decoding any message at the end of the spell’s casting time.

Time Regression.description:
You can regress apparent time by six seconds into the past.

In effect, you “replay” the previous round of activity.

This spell regresses time to the point along the time stream just prior to your previous turn, undoing the effects of everyone else’sactionsin the meantime. Once you have used time regression, only you retain knowledge of what happened during the round that is being replayed; however, you can communicate that knowledge verbally to your companions, if desired. During the round that you live through a second time, you can act on knowledge you previously gained by already living through the immediate future. In all likelihood, you’ll probably not choose to manifest time regression during your second pass through the time stream, instead taking completely newactions.

Your radiant magic blankets you and your allies, preventing corruption and rot. Shadows cling to your form and reach out to those who harm you. When a creature within 15 feet of you hits you with an attack, it must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomefrighteneduntil the end of its next turn, as shadows whisper threats and omens of doom.

Travel via Crowd.description:
While in a crowd or within a crowded area (generally defined as a group of creatures or densely packed objects, as determined by the GM), you canteleportup to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see adjacent to any member of that crowd or within that crowded area. If the space you can see is occupied (you may believe a space is unoccupied when it is not), you appear in the nearest unoccupied space to your intended destination within range. Opalescent Glare.name: Opalescent Glare
Opalescent Glare.description:
You invest your eyes with the light of heaven, rippling out in deadly waves that strike terror and death into the wicked. Evil creatures within range take 2d10 necrotic damage and 2d10 radiant damage, or half as much if they succeed on aWisdomsaving throw. An evil creature with 5 or fewer Hit Dice reduced to0 hit pointsby your opalescent glare instantly dies, with no death saving throws allowed.

In addition to the damage dealt, evil creatures failing their saving throw arefrightenedfor 1 minute. Creatures with more than 5 Hit Dice can attempt a newWisdomsaving throw each round at the end of their turn to end this effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the radius of the effect increases by 10 feet.

Tem’s Proscribed Prose.name: Tem’s Proscribed Prose
Tem’s Proscribed Prose.components: V, S, M (powdered ruby worth at least 100g, which the spell consumes)
Tem’s Proscribed Prose.duration: Until dispelled or triggered Classes: Bard, Warlock, Wizard
Tem’s Proscribed Prose.description:
Your magic creates a small, nearly invisible symbol in the text of one written work such as a book, scroll, or map. When the text containing the symbol is read, not just viewed, the sigil takes on the form of an animal of your choice and strikes the reader.

A creature that uses its action to inspect the book for traps or magic can detect the sigil with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. A creature viewing the target object while under the effects ofdetect magiccan discern only that the entire object is magical.

Upon inscribing the sigil, you can choose any number of conditions under which the book may be read. You can allow creatures to read the text by name, type, race, alignment, or other physical or mental characteristics. You can allow the text to be read while in specific places, such as the throne room of a specific kingdom, or in general locations, such as a temple to a deity of knowledge. You can also allow the text to be read only at a certain time, such as the first day of the new millennium, or at midnight on the day of the winter solstice. Additionally, you can set a spoken password that allows the text to be read.

If a creature attempts to read the text of the target work without first satisfying the set conditions, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become cursed for 24 hours. While cursed in this way, a shimmering force field surrounds the creature, preserving it in a state of suspended animation. The creature is unconscious, immobile, unaware of its surroundings, and unaffected by the passage of time. The creature is not invincible, but taking damage from an outside source allows it to repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

The curse can be ended with the use of thegreater restoration,remove curse, orwishspells. You can also end the curse early by using an action to dismiss it.

At Higher Levels.If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration of the curse increases to 10 days. If you use a spell slot of 9th level, the curse lasts until removed by one of the methods listed above.

Captain Shineheart's Gold © 2021, The Eldritch Press; Authors Fletcher Haug and Guy Corey

Catastrophic Tempest.name: Catastrophic Tempest
Catastrophic Tempest.description:
You unleash a devastating storm of apocalyptic proportions. A 40-foot radius sphere of tempestuous energy forms at a point you choose within range. Each creature in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw, taking 6d8 lightning and 6d8 thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The storm createsdifficult terrainand deafens creatures within it for the duration.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the lightning damage or the thunder damage (your choice) increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 6th.
