Earthbind.name: Earthbind
Earthbind.description:
You cause the ground to erupt with roots and vines, forming a magical cage in a 10-foot radius centered on a point within range. Each creature of your choice in that area must make aDexteritySaving Throw or be trapped within for the duration. Trapped creatures cannot move beyond the confines of the affected area, they may notattackcreatures outside of the trapped area, and they cannot cast spells affecting creatures or an area beyond the trapped area. Magic that would normally allow escape such asTeleport,Passwall, andEtherealnessdo not function althoughPlane Shiftdoes. Similarly, creatures within the cage cannot be affected by spells or attacks from outside the cage. This caster can end this spell at will as a BonusAction.

Concussion Bomb.name: Concussion Bomb
Concussion Bomb.components: V, S, M (any spherical object the caster can throw)
Concussion Bomb.description:
Sometimes you just need a little boom.

When this spell is cast, you enchant one spherical object to explode after being thrown. As a bonus action, you can throw the object to a point within 60 feet, causing a shockwave in a 10-foot-radius from that point. Creatures within range must make aConstitutionsaving throw. A creature takes 2d6 force damage and is forcedproneon a failed save. Creatures who succeed on the save take half damage and remain standing.

The enchanted object is destroyed in the blast. If the object is not thrown within one minute of the spell cast, the magic dissipates, and the object remains intact. The object may be thrown by another creature, but if the object moves over 60 feet from the caster before exploding, the magic dissipates.

At the GM’s discretion, objects which are particularly bad for throwing (such as a large inflatable ball) may give advantage on the saving throw to creatures in the spell’s radius.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can enchant one additional object for each slot level above 2nd. All objects must be thrown within one minute of the spell being cast. After one minute, the magic dissipates from any objects which have not been thrown.

Until the end of your next turn, you haveresistanceagainst cold and fire damage dealt by spells and environmental effects.

War Song.description:

Whenever a target that fails this saving throw makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save.

This spell allows the caster to skim a small portion of mystical energy from the Source which can act as a shield to incoming damage. By drawing on the Source for protection, even the mightiest of blows can be reduced to harmlessness. You create a field of protective magical energy around yourself. If you are struck by anattack, spell, or effect while this spell is in effect, you may use yourreactionto reduce the damage by 6d6. The spell’s effect ends once it is used.

Class(es): artificer, sorcerer, wizard

Upon completing the spell, any creature who touches the object must succeed on a DC 13Constitutionsaving throw or suffer 3d8 poison damage and ispoisonedfor 1 minute. You summon a ferocious sandstorm centered on yourself. The storm obscures vision and isdifficult terrainfor all creatures but you. Each round onyour turn, creatures within the storm, other than you, take 3d6 bludgeoning damage from the swirling sands. Additionally, ranged weapon attacks that pass through the storm are made with disadvantage.

You impose a magicalsilenceon a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed until the end of its next turn, becoming unable to speak, make any vocal sounds, or cast spells that have verbalcomponents.

Luring Melody.name: Luring Melody
Luring Melody.description:
You use a hypnotic melody to compel creatures to follow you. Choose a specific kind of creature to be affected by the spell, which must be a more narrow choice than type (for instance, you could choose goblins but not humanoids, or rats but not animals).

You can be as specific or general as you like (such as all goblins or only white rats). All chosen creatures within range of the spell must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becharmeduntil the spell ends.

As a bonus action on your subsequent turns for the duration, you can continue the melody. You can stop at any time and end the spell.

Whilecharmedby the spell, a creature isincapacitated. If acharmedcreature is more than 5 feet away from you, on its turn it must move toward you by the most direct route. Acharmedcreature avoids any obvious dangers, such as hostile creatures or dangerous terrain. If acharmedcreature takes damage, it can attempt another saving throw. Acharmedtarget can also repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. If the saving throw is successful, the effect ends on that creature.

Herculean Force.name: Herculean Force
Herculean Force.description:
Your body surges with superhuman might. For the duration of this spell, you count as Large-sized when determining how much weight you can carry.

You can also lift, push, and drag Medium-sized objects, regardless of weight, and throw them up to 5 feet.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, increase bothsizecategories mentioned by one, and the throwing distance by 5 feet, for each two slot levels above 5th.

Grease.name: Grease
Grease.components: V, S, M(a bit of pork rind or butter)
Grease.description:
Slick grease covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within range and turns it into difficult terrain for the duration.

When the grease appears, each creature standing in its area must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fall prone. A creature that enters the area or ends its turn there must also succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fall prone.

Investigative Mind.name: Investigative Mind
Investigative Mind.description:
Your mind is able to correlate information effectively. When attempting anIntelligencecheck, you can choose to gain advantage on the roll, or to ignore disadvantage. This has no effect if you already have advantage on the roll. You can use this benefit up to three times, after which the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can use this benefit one additional time per slot level above 2nd. In addition, the maximum duration increases to 8 hours at 4th level and to 24 hours at 6th level.

Gray Asphodel.name: Gray Asphodel
Gray Asphodel.description:
An asphodel blooms on a creature you touch, drawing strength from spirits fleeing to the next life. For the duration of the spell, the target has advantage on death saving throws. Whenever a creature with a Challenge Rating of 1 or higher within 15 feet of the target dies, the target heals 2d10hit points.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the healing increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 6th.

Symbol of Life.name: Symbol of Life
Symbol of Life.description:
This spell functions assymbol, except the symbol that is drawn causes all undead targets to make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 10d10 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful save. An undead creature failing its saving throw is alsofrightenedfor 1 minute. Afrightenedcreature can attempt aWisdomsaving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.

Attempts to create undead within 60 feet of asymbol of lifeautomatically fail.

The Dragon’s Hoard #15 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Storm of Arrows.name: Storm of Arrows
Storm of Arrows.description:
ComponentsV M (a ranged weapon)

When casting this spell, you make aranged attackwith your equipped ranged weapon against any enemy within range of the weapon. Roll one attack roll and compare it to all targets within range, and this attack cannot be a critical hit.

Breath of Life - The Scout (5e)© 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions; Authors: Norman Mitchell Jr. and Connor Bates

Templar’s Mercy.name: Templar’s Mercy
Templar’s Mercy.description:
Your quick prayer prevents catastrophe. The target regains 1 hit point. The triggering effect is a death saving throw, the target regains the hit point immediately, even if the saving throw is the target’s third failed death saving throw.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Arcane Arbitration.name: Arcane Arbitration
Arcane Arbitration.description:
You create an arcane pool of countermagic that you may use to prevent spellcasting. While you concentrate on this spell, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you begins tocast a spell, you can use yourreactionto attempt to interrupt the spellcasting. Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell’s level. On a success, the triggering spell fails and has no effect. Regardless of the outcome, this spell ends.

Ice Wave.name: Ice Wave
Ice Wave.description:
You touch the ground within 5 feet of you, sending a wave of ice shooting forward. The ice forms a line outward from your position that is 5 feet wide and up to 40 feet long and up to 20 feet tall. Each creature within the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 cold damage and 2d8 bludgeoning damage, and its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage, its speed is unaffected, and it must move to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the ice wall’s area.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the cold damage or the bludgeoning damage (your choice) increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Fever’s Gift.name: Fever’s Gift
Fever’s Gift.description:
You infect yourself with a magical fever for the duration.

While infected, you arepoisoned, and you can use a bonus action on each of your turns to experience a portentous hallucination. If you do so, one friendly creature within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you has advantage on the next ability check,attackroll, or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

Spirit of the Bear.name: Spirit of the Bear
Spirit of the Bear.components: V, S, M (tuft of bear fur)
Spirit of the Bear.description:
You are engulfed in a shimmering blue-white aura that resembles a ferocious bear. You gain the following benefits.

Dream Canopy.name: Dream Canopy
Dream Canopy.description:
You summon a verdant and shifting canopy that depicts the dreams of nearby plants. The canopy extends out from you to a distance of 5 feet for the duration, surrounding you in the images and minor sounds of these dreams.

When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it. At the start of each of your turns, choose one of the following effects. The effect remains until the start of your next turn when you can choose another effect or to maintain that same effect.

Blade of Grass.name: Blade of Grass
Blade of Grass.description:
You transform a blade of grass into a scimitar that glows with emerald radiance. A +2 scimitar appears in your hand for the spell’s duration. Attacks made with this weapon are melee spell attacks, and all damage dealt by this weapon is radiant damage. When this weapon leaves your grasp, it reverts to a blade of grass. As long as this spell is active, you may create another sword by picking another blade of grass.

Endless Gullet.name: Endless Gullet
Endless Gullet.description:
You alter your jaw so it can unhinge wider, enough to swallow a smaller creature, and turn your stomach into an extradimensional space that can expand to hold those you swallow. Until this spell ends, as an action you may make an unarmedattackagainst a creature whosesizeis up to one step smaller than you. If you succeed, you swallow the creature. Your enlarged stomach can hold up to one creature asizecategory smaller than you, two creatures twosizecategories smaller than you, or four creatures threesizecategories smaller than you.

Endless gullet: Caught in the snake’s coils and about to be a meal in its extradimensional gut. Any creature that begins its turn inside your stomach suffers 4d6 acid damage. The target creature or creatures are blind andrestrainedwhile in your stomach. If the swallowed creature inflicts at least 20 points of damage in a single turn to you from inside your stomach, it is regurgitated and exits your mouth, where it becomespronein an unoccupied space in front of you. You may choose to regurgitate a creature as a bonus action. When the spell ends, all creatures held within your stomach are regurgitated.

Bilocation.name: Bilocation
Bilocation.description:
You split time and space to allow you to exist in two places at once. The copy of yourself appears in an adjacent square. Onyour turn, both copies may move. All otheractionsare shared between the two, meaning only one action, bonus action orreactionmay be made between the two, but theactionsmay originate from either version of you.

If both of you are within an area of effect, you are only affected once, and only treated as one creature for targeting purposes. However conditions apply to both versions of you and you share hit points. If you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed, both versions of you remain until the spell expires. The link and the two versions of you may be separated by an unlimited amount of distance, even across planar boundaries.

You choose which version of you is real when the spell expires or is dismissed.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Gravity Well.name: Gravity Well
Gravity Well.components: V, S, M (an apple made of gold worth 50 gp)
Gravity Well.description:
Class(es):druid,sorcerer,wizard

You momentarily create intense gravity at a point you can see within range. Each creature within 30 feet of the point must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be pulled 10 feet closer to the point. Objects that are not being worn, held, or anchored and weigh less than 50 pounds are automatically pulled toward the point. Once a creature or object is pulled within 5 feet of the point —or if it is already within 5 feet of the point when the spell is cast —it is pulled no closer, and it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage and 2d12 force damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the effect’s radius increased by 5 feet for each slot level above 4th, and creatures that fail the saving throw are pulled an additional 5 feet closer to the point for each slot level above 4th.

Cloud Barge.name: Cloud Barge
Cloud Barge.description:
You create an elaborate vessel sculpted of ivory and alabaster, floating upon a cloud, which lifts you and the targets of the spell into the air and whisks you away at incredible speed. The cloud barge moves at a speed of 10 miles per minute and moves the passengers smoothly and without disturbance through any kind of weather; the passengers are unaffected by natural or magical precipitation or wind.

Any creatures other than the ones you designate cannot ride the cloud barge, falling through it as if it were made of insubstantial mist. While riding in the cloud barge, you and the other passengers are ingaseous formas per the spell, but you can cast spells that affect yourselves and each other and can otherwise interact with each other normally. The cloud barge and its passengers have concealment from creatures outside of it, or total concealment if in an area of mist or cloud. When the spell ends, whether from the expiration of its duration, dismissing the spell, or if it is dispelled, the cloud barge and its passengers float gently to the ground asfeather fallfor 1 round.

The Dragon’s Hoard #7 © 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

Burdened By Life.name: Burdened By Life
Burdened By Life.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You focus negative energy on a number of targets in a 15-foot radius area. Each living affected creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw or be affected by theSlowspell. Undead affected by the spell gain advantage on saving throws for the duration of the spell.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Storm of Wings.name: Storm of Wings
Storm of Wings.components: V, S, M(a drop of honey)
Storm of Wings.description:
You create a storm of spectral birds, bats, or flying insects in a 15-foot-radius sphere on a point you can see within range. The storm spreads around corners, and its area is lightly obscured. Each creature in the storm when it appears and each a creature that starts its turn in the storm is affected by the storm.

As a bonus action onyour turn, you can move the storm up to 30 feet. As an action onyour turn, you can change the storm from one type to another, such as from a storm of bats to a storm of insects.

Bats. The creature takes 4d6 necrotic damage, and its speed is halved while within the storm as the bats cling to it and drain its blood.

Birds. The creature takes 4d6 slashing damage, and has disadvantage onattackrolls while within the storm as the birdsflyin the way of the creature’s attacks.

Insects. The creature takes 4d6 poison damage, and it must make aConstitutionsaving throw each time it casts a spell while within the storm. On a failed save, the creature fails to cast the spell, losing the action but not the spell slot.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Snake Swarm.name: Snake Swarm
Snake Swarm.components: V, S, M(a severed snake head)
Snake Swarm.description:
You summon a mass of vipers or constrictors that fills a 10-foot square area. (You may summon the swarm so that it shares the area of other creatures.) The swarm has 30hit pointsand AC 14. You can direct the swarm with a bonus action to move up to 20 feet; the swarm otherwise remains where you it was summoned. The snakes are either venomous vipers or entangling constrictors (you choice when you cast the spell). When the swarm is first cast, and as an action once on each of your turns thereafter, the swarm attacks each creature in its area. Use your spellcasting ability to make amelee attackagainst each target in the swarm, the effect of which depends upon the type of swarm you summon.

Tooth of The Wyrm.name: Tooth of The Wyrm
Tooth of The Wyrm.description:
Your touch opens a magical wound in a creature you try to touch. Make a melee spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 necrotic damage. Until the spell ends, the target takes necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns. The necrotic damage increases by 1d4 each subsequent round, dealing 2d4 necrotic damage on the target’s first turn after being hit, 3d4 on the target’s second turn after being hit, and so on.

At the end of each of its turns, the target can make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends. Alesser restorationspell cast on the target also ends the spell.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Aimless Arrow.name: Aimless Arrow
Aimless Arrow.description:
ComponentsV, M (a broken arrow)

You curse the target’s ability to target at range. For the duration of the spell anyranged attack, spell, or otherwise, has disadvantage on theattackroll.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Bladebite Curse.name: Bladebite Curse
Bladebite Curse.description:
Classes: antipaladin,bard,cleric,ranger,warlock

The power of your spoken curse compels a target that fails itsWisdomsaving throw to strike itself with whichever weapon it is currently wielding, dealing full damage to itself, including any bonuses that would apply to theattack. If the target has the sneakattackclass feature, it adds this damage to the amount it deals to itself. If the target is currently wielding more than one weapon or has multiple “natural” weapons like bite and claw attacks, it uses whichever weapon deals the most damage.

The Dragon’s Hoard #46© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Scott Young, Mike Welham, Miguel Colon, and Matt Kimmel

Finder’s Mark.name: Finder’s Mark
Finder’s Mark.description:
Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard

You touch a creature and mark it. Until the spell ends, that creature has advantage on anyIntelligence(Investigation),Wisdom(Perception), andWisdom(Survival) checks to find a living blood relative (parents, siblings, spouse, and children) the target names when you cast the spell, who appears with the same mark on its forehead so long as the target and blood relative are on the same plane of existence. If the target has no living blood relatives or they are on another plane of existence, the spell fails. The spell ends when the target touches the named blood relative.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Elation.name: Elation
Elation.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 10 minutes

You fill the subject with joy and energy, granting them a +2 and add the result to anattackroll, saving throw, or skill check that rely onStrengthorDexterity. Additionally, the speed increases by 5 feet.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2 levels higher, you increase the bonus by +1 and the speed increase goes up by 5 feet.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

Heal.name: Heal
Heal.description:
Choose a creature that you can see within range. A surge of positive energy washes through the creature, causing it to regain 70 hit points. This spell also ends blindness, deafness, and any diseases affecting the target. This spell has no effect on constructs or undead.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the amount of healing increases by 10 for each slot level above 6th.

Crown of Clarity.name: Crown of Clarity
Crown of Clarity.description:
Class(es):cleric,druid,ranger,warlock

You create a magical halo around the target that bends and focuses light like a lens and then disappears, sharpening their senses and heightening their intuition. The target gains a +1 bonus on saving throws against illusions and onWisdom(Insight) andWisdom(Perception) check. Their passivePerceptionalso increases by 1 and they do not have Disadvantage onWisdom(Perception) checks to see things that are lightly obscured.

As areactionor bonus action, the wearer of the crown of clarity can boost the effect in one of two ways. They can extend the crown of clarity’s power to enhance the senses of all allies within 20 feet with the benefits above. Alternatively, they can focus its power on themselves, granting Advantage in addition a +1 bonus the listed die rolls. They also gain blindsight anddarkvisionand can seeinvisiblecreatures and objects. These effects lasts until the end of the wearer’s next turn, after which the spell ends.

The Dragon’s Hoard #53© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Darrin Drader, Robert J. Grady, Eytan Bernstein, Katherine Schuttler.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Going in Circles.name: Going in Circles
Going in Circles.components: V, S, M(a piece of the target terrain)
Going in Circles.description:
You make natural terrain in a 1-mile cube difficult to traverse. A creature in the affected area has disadvantage onWisdom(Survival) checks to follow tracks or travel safely through the area as paths through the terrain seem to twist and turn nonsensically. The terrain itself isn’t changed, only the perception of those inside it. A creature who succeeds on twoWisdom(Survival) checks while within the terrain discerns the illusion for what it is and sees the illusory twists and turns superimposed on the terrain. A creature that reenters the area after exiting it before the spell ends is affected by the spell even if it previously succeeded in traversing the terrain.

A creature that castsfind the pathautomatically succeeds in discovering a way out of the terrain. When you cast this spell, you can designate a password. A creature that speaks the password as it enters the area automatically sees the illusion and is unaffected by the spell.

If you cast this spell on the same spot every day for one year, the illusion lasts until it is dispelled.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page
Going in Circles.material_component: a piece of the target terrain

Unholy Witness.name: Unholy Witness
Unholy Witness.description:
Tool Proficiencies: Artisan’s tools

Equipment: A set of artisan’s tools (one of your choice), a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp

Your Sin increases by 1. Roll 1d20 whenever you spend a vilis point. On a result of 19 or 20 you do not have to expend the vilis point to benefit from it.

Book of Exalted Darkness. © 2018 Mike Myler, published under license by Legendary Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Undertow.name: Undertow
Undertow.description:
You target a creature in the water with a powerful riptide dragging them below the surface and dealing 3d6 bludgeoning damage, or half as much on a successfulStrengthsaving throw. A creature failing its saving throw also is dragged 30 feet down in the water. Each round you can attempt to drag them under again, forcing them to repeat the save as long as you maintain concentration.

Creatures dragged down by the undertow can move on their turn but, whether swimming or moving along the seafloor if they succeed on aStrength(Athletics) check against the spell’s save DC. Checks made to swim upwards have disadvantage. A creature withfreedom of movementcan be dragged downwards and take damage from the undertow, but they automatically succeed onStrength(Athletics) checks to swim against the undertow.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher, you can target another creature per spell level above 4th.

The Dragon’s Hoard #21 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Winds of Vengeance.name: Winds of Vengeance
Winds of Vengeance.description:
Classes:cleric,druid,sorcerer,wizard

You surround yourself with a buffetingshroudof supernatural tornado-force winds, allowing you toflywith a speed of 60 feet. The winds of vengeance grant you immunity to other wind effects, as well as harmful gases or vapors, and also provide you with a shell of breathable air. Ranged weapon attacks are deflected by the winds of vengeance and automatically miss you, even huge weapons like hurled boulders and siege weapons.

Melee attacks by Tiny creatures are also automatically deflected and have no effect on you, while Small creatures have disadvantage onmelee attacksagainst you.

In addition, when a creature hits you with amelee attack, as areactionyou can direct a blast of wind against them dealing 5d8 bludgeoning damage, or half as much with a successfulStrengthsaving throw. Creatures failing their save are also pushed 10 feet away from you if they are larger than you, 20 feet away if they are the samesizeas you, and 30 feet away if they are smaller than you. Tiny creatures and swarms take double damage from this blast of wind.

The Dragon’s Hoard #25 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Power Word: Navi.name: Power Word: Navi
Power Word: Navi.description:
You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving it weakened. If the target has 75hit pointsor fewer, it deals only half damage with weapon attacks that useStrengthand has disadvantage onStrengthchecks. Otherwise, the spell has no effect. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, theStrengthpenalties end.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you affect one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Create Armored Vehicle.name: Create Armored Vehicle
Create Armored Vehicle.description:
Exactly what you need to ride into the heart of danger.

When you cast this spell, touch a box, crate, storage container, or similar object ofsizeHuge or larger. The object morphs into an armored vehicle that can carry up to eight people on benches in a 20-foot-long, 15-foot-wide cargo space, with a cab that can carry two more. Thesizeof the cargo space is fixed, regardless of thesizeof the original container. This spell creates nothing in the cargo space apart from benches for the characters to sit on. Any other physical details desired by the caster, such as slits for seeing outside, must be made part of the original container.

The vehicle needs no outside fuel source. It has a maximum movement speed of 400 feet (45 mph), AC 18, 150HP, andresistanceto bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from normal weapons. It has no weapons of its own, but if its movement takes it into a target, it can ram that target for 4d6 damage when traveling at or below 200 feet per round (approximately 23 mph) and 8d6 damage if traveling at a higher speed. If the target is a creature, it can make aDexteritysave against the spell DC of the vehicle’s creator. If the creature fails the save, it takes full damage and is knockedprone; on a success, it evades the truck and takes no damage. If the target is a stationary object, it takes double damage from the ram (no save), and the vehicle takes the same amount of damage.

The spell ends after twenty-four hours or when the vehicle loses all itshit points. If the spell ends due to damage, the container collapses into small, useless fragments.

Tails of the City © 2020, Silver Games, Llc; Authors: David Silver

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Dividing Trench.name: Dividing Trench
Dividing Trench.description:
You excavate a trench in soil, sand, clay, or bare earth, 5 feet wide and deep and up to 20 feet long. You can shape the trench, but each square must be adjacent (including diagonally) to another square, and you can’t create the trench in a space occupied by a creature. The trench provides HalfCoverfor attacks passing into or out of it (or Three-QuartersCoverif a creature is Small or smaller (or is Medium andProne) inside the trench. Creatures can jump over the trench. They also can climb into or out of it by spending 5 extra feet of movement (and succeeding on a DC 10Strength(Athletics) check if they are Medium or smaller). When the spell’s duration expires, the ground in the trench returns to its normal position, carrying any creatures in the trench up with it.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can increase the length of the trench by 20 feet for each spell slot level above 1. In addition, if you increase the slot level by 2, you make the duration permanent.

The Dragon’s Hoard #61© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Robert J. Grady, Ismael Alvarez, Amber Scott, Jeff Ibach, Katherine Schuttler.

Disappearing Striker.name: Disappearing Striker
Disappearing Striker.description:
Choose a creature that you successfully damaged with a sneakattackusing a ranged weapon this round. That target must make aWisdomsaving throw. If it fails the saving throw, the target believes you have disappeared; with respect to that target, you areinvisible. Until the spell ends, if you do not attack the target or cast a spell that affects or damages the target, you remaininvisiblewith respect to the target; if you attack the target or cast a spell that affects or damages the target, the target regains the ability to see you normally.

At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. If the target succeeds on this save, it can see you normally.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can, as areactiononce each round, duplicate the effect of this spell so long as you choose a different target each time.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Danger Zone.name: Danger Zone
Danger Zone.components: V, S, M (drop of refined fuel)
Danger Zone.description:
A 30-foot cube containing dangerous potential energy originates from a point of your choosing within range. Creatures that enter the cube have advantage onattackrolls and disadvantage on saving throws against other creatures within the cube. Spell damage is doubled inside the cube, if cast from a creature within the cube. Creatures in the cube can land a critical hit on 18-20 if attacking creatures inside the cube. If a creature leaves the cube, the dangerous energy lasts until the start of their next turn, giving them the same advantages and disadvantages against other creatures inside the cube or with the same trailing energy.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the cubesizeincreases by 15 feet for every spell slot used above 5th.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Id Insinuation.name: Id Insinuation
Id Insinuation.description:
You partition and isolate the target’s consciousness, causing it to act as aconfusionspell if it fails aWisdomsaving throw.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can influence itsactionswhile confused for 1 round for each slot level above 2nd.

During this time, roll twice to see what action the target takes on its turn; you can choose which of these twoactionsit takes.

The Dragon’s Hoard #49© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Nick Hite, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Dan Dillon, Matt Kimmel, David N. Ross

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Clearing The Field.name: Clearing The Field
Clearing The Field.description:
With a harsh word and a vicious chopping motion, you cause every tree, shrub, and stump within 40 feet of you to sink into the ground, leaving the vacated area clear of plant life that might otherwise hamper movement or obscure sight. Overgrown areas that counted asdifficult terrainbecome clear ground and no longer hamper movement. The original plant life instantly rises from the ground again when the spell ends or is dispelled. Plant creatures are not affected by clearing the field.

Ritual Focus. If you expend your ritual focus, each Plant creature in the area must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or decrease insizeas if it failed the saving throw against the reduce effect of theenlarge/reducespell.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Shadefire.name: Shadefire
Shadefire.description:
A sphere of thick, wreathing shadows appears at a point you choose within range. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 6d6 necrotic damage and isrestrainedby shadowy tendrils until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half damage and is notrestrained.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

The Gates of the Shadowmage © 2020, The Eldritch Press; Authors Fletcher Haug and Guy Corey

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Inscribe Vilespeech.name: Inscribe Vilespeech
Inscribe Vilespeech.components: V, S, M (page of humanoid-skin vellum)
Inscribe Vilespeech.description:
Once triggered, every creature in a 20-foot radius must make aWisdomsaving throw or have their gaze drawn to the blasphemous words. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 psychic damage and is either insane (25%) or enraged (25%) until it takes a short rest. Aremove cursespell cast on the creature ends this effect. On a successful save a creature takes half damage but is otherwise unaffected. While insane, a creature can’t takeactions, read, speak anything but gibberish, or understand what other creatures say. The GM controls the creature’s movement, which is erratic. While enraged, a creature mustattackthe nearest other creature that it can see to the best of its ability, can’t understand what other creatures say, and speaks only in gibberish. If no other creature is in sight, the creature attacks itself.

You must know Vilespeech in order to cast this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th-level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot above 3rd.

Vile spells are cruel and exploitative, bent to inflict unnatural pain or gain power from the suffering of victims.

They manipulate blood, blaspheme existence, pervert the physical form, conjure evil entities, or worse. Classes able to cast spells add all vile spells to their class spell list, but only creatures with a Sin ability score or evil alignment are able to cast spells from this school of magic without using a scroll or other magic item.

Vile spells leave an evil aura behind them, detectable withdetect evil and good. If the caster has no Sin ability score, use double the spell level to determine the strength of the aura left behind. Evil auras dissipate 10 minutes for every spell level + a number of minutes equal to double the caster’s Sin score. For example, a vile spell of 3rd-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 15 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour; a 3rd-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 30 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 15 doubled. A vile spell of 5th-level cast by a creature with a Sin score of 20 has an evil aura that lingers for 1 hour and 30 minutes; a 5th-level spell’s evil aura lasts a minimum of 50 minutes, plus the caster’s Sin of 20 doubled.

As part of the casting of this cantrip, you inflict 2 points of damage to yourself. The blood from your self-inflicted injury forms into a sharpened spear of crimson that rapidly soars toward a creature within range, drying as it flies through the air. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d12 piercing damage. The spell creates more than one blood spear when you reach higher levels (you take 2 additional points of damage for every extra spear formed): two spears at 5th level, three spears at 11th level, and four spears at 17th level. You can direct the spears at the same target or at different ones. Make a separateattackroll for each spear.

Book of Exalted Darkness. © 2018 Mike Myler, published under license by Legendary Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Tamer’s Whip.name: Tamer’s Whip
Tamer’s Whip.description:
A 15-foot-long whip of magical force springs from your hand. You can wield it as a normal whip, except it does force damage. Animals you strike with the whip becomefrightenedof you for 1d4 rounds unless they pass aWisdomsaving throw. As an action, you may crack the whip overhead, causing all animals within 30 feet to become frightened of you for 1 round unless they pass aWisdomsaving throw. If unable to escape, a frightened animal may fight.

The Dragon’s Hoard #8 © 2021, Legendary Games; Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Glyph of Warding.name: Glyph of Warding
Glyph of Warding.components: V, S, M(incense and powdered diamond worth at least 200 gp, which the spell consumes)
Glyph of Warding.description:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a glyph that harms other creatures, either upon a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, a scroll, or a treasure chest) to conceal the glyph. If you choose a surface, the glyph can cover an area of the surface no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If you choose an object, that object must remain in its place; if the object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly invisible and requires a successfulIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be found.

You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, the most typical triggers include touching or standing on the glyph, removing another object covering the glyph, approaching within a certain distance of the glyph, or manipulating the object on which the glyph is inscribed. For glyphs inscribed within an object, the most common triggers include opening that object, approaching within a certain distance of the object, or seeing or reading the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.

You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind (for example, the ward could be set to affect aberrations or drow), or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don’t trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

When you inscribe the glyph, chooseexplosive runesor aspell glyph.

Explosive Runes: When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the glyph. The sphere spreads around corners. Each creature in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 5d8 acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage on a failed saving throw (your choice when you create the glyph), or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spell Glyph: You can store a prepared spell of 3rd level or lower in the glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyph. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way. When the glyph is triggered, the stored spell is cast. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on that creature. If the spell summons hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the intruder and attack it. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts until the end of its full duration.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage of anexplosive runesglyph increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd. If you create aspell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the slot you use for theglyph of warding.

Malicious Spite.name: Malicious Spite
Malicious Spite.components: V, S, M (powdered turquoise worth 150 gp)
Malicious Spite.description:
You inflame feelings of malice and hatred in one creature toward another creature you choose (Will negates). The creature plots and schemes against the object of its hatred, usually acting indirectly or subtly and within its means and resources, but working hard to bring ruin to them. Each day, if the target begins a Long Rest without having perform a spiteful act against its hated enemy, they take 4d6 psychic damage when they awaken and have Disadvantage onWisdom-based D20 Tests until they perform a spiteful act and then complete another Long Rest. Spiteful acts include damaging or destroying its enemy’s gear, home, vehicle, or pets; starting rumors or framing them for a crime; blackmailing them; kidnapping friends, family, or pets; or paying others to accost, poison, or evenattackthem. When Malicious Spite ends, the target remembers itsactionsbut not why it did them.

Malicious Spite cannot be dispelled, but Remove Curse orGreater Restorationends it.

Sleepwalk.name: Sleepwalk
Sleepwalk.components: V, S, M(a sprig of belladonna)
Sleepwalk.description:
With a successful melee spellattack, you send the target into magical slumber. If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw, it falls asleep. Undead and creatures immune to beingcharmedaren’t affected by this spell. While the creature isunconscious, it does not fallproneunless you wish it. It can move at half speed but cannot take any otheractions, even freeactions. It follows if led or guided, or as a bonus action you can compel it to move in a direction of your choice. It has disadvantage onDexterityandStrengthsaving throws and ability checks. The spell ends if the creature takes damage. A creature using an action to try to shake or slap the sleeping creature awake grants it a new saving throw but does not automatically awaken it.

Poison Food or Water.name: Poison Food or Water
Poison Food or Water.description: All nonmagical food and drink within a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range ispoisoned; all who consume the substance must succeed at aConstitutionsave or becomepoisoneduntil they complete a short or long rest.

Cloak of Silence.name: Cloak of Silence
Cloak of Silence.description:
When casting this spell, you create aninvisiblemobile zone ofsilencethat surrounds you. The spell functions by bending all types of noise and sound around you but allows you to hear yourself speak. Because the spell stops all sound, it provides immunity to thunder damage, and renders youdeafenedwith regard to other creatures. Casting a spell that includes a verbal component is possible while under the effects of this spell, but any spell or effect that requires your target to be able to hear you automatically fails.

Curse of Shattered Fate.name: Curse of Shattered Fate
Curse of Shattered Fate.description:
Target: One creature you can see within range

You shatter the target’s sense of fate, causing uncertainty in their actions. The target is cursed for the duration. Each time a creature cursed in this way makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, it must roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from the result. A cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Determinism.name: Determinism
Determinism.components: V, S, M (diamond from a parallel universe)
Determinism.description:
You curse a creature you are aware of within range, altering its fate to determine its futureactions. When the target attempts to take its action on each of its turns, it must offer you an alternative action that it is able to take that cannot be the same type of action as the first (Attack,Cast a Spell,Dodge, etc.). You select which action the creature must take between the two options presented. The creature need not tell you what it will do with theseactionsor how they work, only that it wishes to take them.

At the end of each of its turns, the creature may attempt aWisdomsaving throw to end the effect. If the creature succeeds on twoWisdomsaving throws in this manner, the spell ends.

Curse of Echoing Void.name: Curse of Echoing Void
Curse of Echoing Void.components: V, S, M (piece of void crystal)
Curse of Echoing Void.description:
Target: A point you choose within range

Classes:Sorcerer, Warlock,Wizard

Magicaldarknessspreads from a point you choose within range to fill a 30-foot-radius sphere for the duration. The darkness spreads around corners. A creature withdarkvisioncan’t see through this darkness, and non-magical light can’t illuminate it. If the point you choose is on an object you are holding or one that isn’t being worn or carried, the darkness emanates from the object and moves with it. Completely covering the source of the darkness with an opaque object, such as a bowl or a helm, blocks the darkness. A creature that starts its turn within the darkness must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 2d8 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. If any of this spell’s area overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of 4th level or lower, the spell that created the light is dispelled.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th. Additionally, the level of the spells creating an area of light dispelled if they overlap with the spell’s area increases by 1 for each slot level above 4th.

Condemned To Rot.name: Condemned To Rot
Condemned To Rot.description:
You touch the target and infect them with a cursed disease of wasting. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw or be unable to be healed by magical means, cannothealby using hit dice, orhealby regeneration.Medicineskill checks do nothelp.

Additionally, if they have any damage, they additionally must make aConstitutionsaving throw each time they rest overnight or take 1d8 necrotic damage. Aremove cursespell ends this effect.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, the spell lasts until it is dispelled.

Magic Robe.name: Magic Robe
Magic Robe.description:
Your robes become fortified against anattack. You gain a +1 bonus to AC against the triggeringattackunless you are a student on academy grounds, in which case the bonus is +2.

At Higher Levels: Your AC bonus increases to +2/+3 on academy grounds at 5th level, +3/+4 at 11th level, and +4/+5 at 17th level.

Blink.name: Blink
Blink.description:
Roll a d20 at the end of each of your turns for the duration of the spell. On a roll of 11 or higher, you vanish from your current plane of existence and appear in theEthereal Plane(the spell fails and the casting is wasted if you were already on that plane). At the start of your next turn, and when the spell ends if you are on the Ethereal Plane, you return to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of the space you vanished from. If no unoccupied space is available within that range, you appear in the nearest unoccupied space (chosen at random if more than one space is equally near). You can dismiss this spell as an action.

While on the Ethereal Plane, you can see and hear the plane you originated from, which is cast in shades of gray, and you can’t see anything there more than 60 feet away. You can only affect and be affected by other creatures on the Ethereal Plane.

Creatures that aren’t there can’t perceive you or interact with you, unless they have the ability to do so.

Call Mounts.name: Call Mounts
Call Mounts.duration: 1 hour Classes: druid, paladin, ranger, wizard
Call Mounts.description:
Classes:druid,paladin,ranger,wizard

You summon up to 6 ordinary light horses or ponies (or similar quadrupedal mounts appropriate to the terrain, at the GM’s discretion) into unoccupied spaces you can see within range. Each beast arrives with a bit and bridle and riding saddle and has ordinary statistics for a creature of its type. The mounts are docile and do not fight even if attacked, but they willingly carry riders or carry packs.

They disappear immediately along with their saddles and harness if reduced to0 hit points, the spell ends, or they move more than 100 feet from you. They also disappear if you cast another call mounts spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level, you can increase the duration to 8 hours.

Labyrinthine Conundrum.name: Labyrinthine Conundrum
Labyrinthine Conundrum.components: V, S, M (drawing of a maze worth 10 gp)
Labyrinthine Conundrum.description:
You trick the targets into contemplating an abstract intellectual problem or riddle that completely preoccupies them. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw when you cast this spell or be affected by it. An affected creature isincapacitatedand has a speed of 0.

At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make aWisdomsaving throw. If it succeeds, this effect ends for that target.

This spell is also contagious. Anyone who converses with someone under this spell must also make aWisdomsaving throw or be drawn into contemplating the conundrum.

The spell ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage.

Silk Self.name: Silk Self
Silk Self.description:
You compress yourself into a flexible and perfectly flat image of yourself with height and width but no depth, shunting your third dimension into an extradimensional space that moves with you. Your flowing flat form grants you halfcoverand attacks against you have a 20% miss chance, and you take no damage from bludgeoning damage in this form. In addition, as areactionyou can turn sideways in response to anattack, granting you three-quarterscover; even if theattackhits, you take only half damage. You take double damage when there are two hostile creatures adjacent to you and one hits you with a piercing or slashing weapon.

As a bonus action, you can turn yourself sideways and shunt your second dimension into the space, leaving only a virtuallyinvisiblesingle silken thread.See invisibilitydoes not reveal your location, buttrue seeingallows creatures to see your thread and effects likefaerie fireand glitterdust reveal your presence as a sinuous line. Your own senses function normally and you can move normally in this form and can pass through any gap small enough to admit a silken thread, and can slip through impediments as if usingfreedom of movement. You are immune to virtually all forms ofattackin this shunted form, though your senses can be affected by illusions, and effects that rely on sight, and you can beblinded, ordeafenednormally. You must still breathe in this form, and inhaled poisons and similar effects can affect you. You can hold your breath and avert your eyes as normal.

You can cast spells or use items or abilities that affect only you in this form, but you cannot cast spells that affect an area, affect other creatures, or create an object or effect outside your body. You can return to your two-dimensional flat state as a bonus action.

Wake of Light.name: Wake of Light
Wake of Light.description:
You must be mounted to cast this spell, leaving a trail of glowing heavenly mist behind you and your mount as you move, 10 feet wide and up to 120 feet long. The wake of light floats one foot above the ground, shedding bright light within 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond that. The wake of light can cross boggy or marshy terrain but cannot extend across water more than a few feet deep, nor go underwater or into the air, even if your mount is capable of such movement. You must concentrate while creating the wake of light, but once it is created it remains for 1 minute after you cease concentration. If you leave your mount or your mount is killed, you cannot extend the wake of light any farther, but any existing mist persists until the spell ends. Good creatures can traverse the wake of light like solid ground, ignoringdifficult terrainbased on the ground’s actual surface (though not due trees and thick vegetation above ground level), while evil creatures treat the wake of light asdifficult terrain. Neutral creatures are not affected by it, while unaligned mounts are affected by the wake of light based on their rider’s alignment.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can extend the wake of light an additional 120 feet for each level above 2nd.

Compulsory Conversion.name: Compulsory Conversion
Compulsory Conversion.description:
You force the target to change its alignment to a new alignment you designate, which must be within one step of your own alignment and your deity’s alignment. If the target fails its saving throw, its alignment changes and it believes that it has always had that alignment and that its alignment represents its true ethical and moral outlook. The target makes no efforts to return to its former alignment, and in fact views that possibility as horrifying and does whatever possible to avoid it. Compulsory conversion can be reversed bywishor by another compulsory conversion spell.

Clerics & Cultists© 2021, Legendary Games; Author Darrin Drader, Nicholas Hite, Sean K Reynolds, Jason Nelson, Jenny Jarzabski, Miguel Colon, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Daley, Nathan Reinecke.

Savage Break.name: Savage Break
Savage Break.components: V, S, M (tiny vial of cow’s milk)
Savage Break.description:
You magically yank a bone out of one creature and hurl it at another. Choose one creature you can see within range that has bones. It must make aConstitutionsaving throw. If it fails the saving throw, the creature takes 4d6 piercing as one of its smaller bones breaks and erupts out of its body. You can immediately make a ranged spellattackto hurl the broken bone at another creature you can see within 30 feet of the first that failed its saving throw. If theattackhits the second creature, it deals 2d6 piercing damage. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and no bones are ripped from its body.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot and the target fails its saving throw, you pull two bones out of the spell’s initial target, dealing 8d6 piercing damage, and can make two spell attacks at one or more other creatures within 30 feet of the target, each dealing 3d6 piercing damage on a hit. If you cast this spell using an 8th-level spell slot and the target fails its saving throw, you pull three bones out of the spell’s initial target, dealing 12d6 piercing damage, and can make three spell attacks at one or more other creatures within 30 feet of the target, each dealing 4d6 piercing damage on a hit.

Caustic Ray.name: Caustic Ray
Caustic Ray.description:
Class(es): Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You fire a thin, green ray of caustic energy at a creature within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 acid damage. On a critical hit, you can choose to make the caustic energy erupts in a violent explosion around the target. Each creature within 5 feet of the target must make aDexteritysaving throw or take 1d6 acid damage on a failed save.

At Higher Levels. The spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8). The spell’s caustic energy eruption damage on a critical hit increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Power Word Rend.name: Power Word Rend
Power Word Rend.description:
You speak a word of power that causes the internal organs of a creature you can see within range to rupture. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. It takes 4d6 + 20 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the target is below half its hit point maximum, it has disadvantage on this saving throw. This spell has no effect on creatures without vital internal organs, such as Constructs, Oozes, and Undead.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 4th. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Court The Flame.name: Court The Flame
Court The Flame.description:
You court the power of a nearby fire to shield you. Choose one source of nonmagical fire that is thesizeof a torch or larger within 5 feet of you. You gain a +2 bonus to your AC for the duration. Until this spell ends, if you would take fire damage from any source, you can use yourreactionto reduce that damage to 0. If you do, the spell ends.

If you spend at least 1 minute more than 5 feet away from the source of fire you chose when you cast this spell, the spell immediately ends.

Touch of Despair.name: Touch of Despair
Touch of Despair.description:
You touch a creature and fill it with a sense of impending failure.

Once before the spell ends, the target touched must make aWisdomsaving throw. If they fail the saving throw, you can roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from one ability check of your choice made by the target. You can roll the die before or after they make the ability check. The spell then ends.

GoodHope - Crushing Despair (5E), © 2022, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Ancestral Wrath.name: Ancestral Wrath
Ancestral Wrath.description:
You call forth the spirit of one of your ancestors, rebuking an opponent for their misdeeds and invoking this ancestral spirit to administer divine punishment. The spirit streaks towards the target, automatically hitting and dealing 5d6 radiant damage to living targets and 5d8 radiant damage to undead targets. An undead target must succeed at aWisdomsaving throw or on it must spend its next turn trying to move as far away from you as it can. An undead creature affected in this way cannot willing move into a space within 30 feet of you. It also cannot takereactions. For its action, it can only use theDashaction or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there’s nowhere to move, the undead can use theDodgeaction.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 3rd-level spell slot or higher, the damage dealt increases by 1d6 against living targets and 1d8 against undead targets for each slot level above 2nd.

Lower Magic Resistance.name: Lower Magic Resistance
Lower Magic Resistance.description:
You point at a creature you can see, reducing itsresistanceto magic. The creature must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, it has disadvantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects for the duration. A creature with the MagicResistancetrait has advantage on the saving throw against this spell, but if it fails, the disadvantage cancels out its advantage on saving throws.

Jump.name: Jump
Jump.components: V, S, M(a grasshopper’s hind leg)
Jump.description:
You touch a creature. The creature’s jump distance is tripled until the spell ends.

The following is content created by a publisher other than Wizards of the Coast.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 2nd level spell slot, the target’sStrengthscore increases to 20 for the purposes of determining itsjumpdistance. If you use a 3rd level slot, itsStrengthbecomes 24. If you use a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the target’sStrengthbecomes 28.

Wall of Paper.name: Wall of Paper
Wall of Paper.description:
Classes: artifactor, bard, sorcerer, wizard

You conjure a sheet of paper up to 10 feet high and 10 feet across. The wall of paper must be flat but can be vertical, horizontal, or any orientation in between. The wall of paper needs no support and can even hover in mid-air. If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (your choice).

At 5th level, you can conjure a second 10-foot-by-10-foot panel. You can conjure a third panel at 11th level and a fourth panel at 17th. All panels must be contiguous and have the same orientation.

Each 10-foot section of paper has AC 10 and 1 hit point.

It is immune to poison and psychic damage. Reducing a panel to0 hit pointsdestroys it. Any effect that requires an ability check or saving throw to avoid being moved, such as agust of windspell, destroys the entire wall.

Once the spell ends, the paper fades away to nothing.

Forbiddance.name: Forbiddance
Forbiddance.components: V, S, M(a sprinkling of holy water, rare incense, and powdered ruby worth at least 1,000 gp)
Forbiddance.description:
You create a ward against magical travel that protects up to 40,000 square feet of floor space to a height of 30 feet above the floor. For the duration, creatures can’t teleport into the area or use portals, such as those created by thegatespell, to enter the area. The spell proofs the area against planar travel, and therefore prevents creatures from accessing the area by way of the Astral Plane, Ethereal Plane, Plane of Faerie, Plane of Shadow, or theplane shiftspell.

In addition, the spell damages types of creatures that you choose when you cast it. Choose one or more of the following: celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. When a chosen creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature takes 5d10 radiant or necrotic damage (your choice when you cast this spell).

When you cast this spell, you can designate a password. A creature that speaks the password as it enters the area takes no damage from the spell.

The spell’s area can’t overlap with the area of anotherforbiddancespell. If you castforbiddanceevery day for 30 days in the same location, the spell lasts until it is dispelled, and the material components are consumed on the last casting.

Offering To The Wild.name: Offering To The Wild
Offering To The Wild.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a sacrificial animal or other suitable sacrifice)

Duration1 day You complete the sacrifice and anoint up to 8 creatures to be protected with some part of the sacrifice, typically blood or ash, leaving the rest to the spirits of nature.

For the duration the protected creatures gain advantage bonus oninitiativechecks,Naturechecks,Perceptionchecks,Stealthchecks, andSurvivalchecks while within 10 miles of the spot spell was cast in.

Additionally, any beast native to the affected wilds begins with a neutral disposition and will not run from norattacka protected creature, unless attacked first or impelled by some outside means. This spell does not function in urban terrain.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

Earthen Escape.name: Earthen Escape
Earthen Escape.description:
You throw your hand above your head, clenching it into a fist as you do, and the friendly creature, which can include yourself, that was attacked is magically pulled into and through the ground by an earthen hand. The hand pops up in an unoccupied space on the ground within 30 feet of where the target was previously located and deposits the target in that space before disappearing. The triggeringattackagainst the target fails.

The area within 10 feet of the origin and destination spaces becomesdifficult terrainuntil the start of your next turn.

You and the target must be on the same ground, rock, soil, sand, or similarly earthen surface, or the spell fails.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Conjure Swarm.name: Conjure Swarm
Conjure Swarm.description:
You summon swarms of insects, rodents, or other tiny creatures that appear in a space within range that you can see. Choose one of the following options for what appears:

A summoned swarm disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The summoned swarms are friendly to you and your companions. Rollinitiativefor the summoned creatures as a group, which have their own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures but otherwise take noactions.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using certain higher level spell slots, you choose one of the summoning options above and more creatures appear: twice as many with a 6th-level slot and three times as many with an 8th-level slot.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Festering Boils.name: Festering Boils
Festering Boils.description:
This spell causes inflamed, pus-filled boils to form over a target’s entire body. The character must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 12d8 necrotic damage on a failure, or half as much damage with a success. Additionally, a creature that fails the saving throw succumbs to the following conditions:

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Undo Decay.name: Undo Decay
Undo Decay.description:
Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard

A construct, object, or structure you touch regains a number ofhit pointsequal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Misstep.name: Misstep
Misstep.description:
You gesture to a creature within range that you can see. If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw, it uses itsreactionto move 5 feet in a direction you dictate. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. The spell automatically fails if you direct the target into a dangerous area such as a pit trap, a bonfire, or off the edge of a cliff, or if the target has already used itsreaction.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Reciprocating Portal.name: Reciprocating Portal
Reciprocating Portal.description:
With a gesture and a muttered word, you cause an inky black, circular portal to open on the ground beneath one or more creatures. You can create one 15-foot-diameter portal, two 10-foot-diameter portals, or six 5-foot-diameter portals. A creature that’s standing where you create a portal must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature falls through the portal, disappears into ademiplanewhere it isstunnedas it falls endlessly, and the portal closes.

At the start of your next turn, the creatures that failed their saving throws fall through matching portals directly above their previous locations. A falling creature landspronein the space it once occupied or the nearest unoccupied space and takes falling damage as if it fell 60 feet, regardless of the distance between the exit portal and the ground.

Flying and levitating creatures can’t be affected by this spell.

Hide from Undead.name: Hide from Undead
Hide from Undead.description:
A creature you touch becomesinvisibleand undetectable by sound or scent to undead creatures until the spell ends.

Undead creatures that possess keen senses such as hearing or smell or unusual abilities to sense the presence of living creatures do not gain advantage onPerceptionchecks to notice the target of this spell. Anything the target is wearing or carrying is likewise hidden from undead as long as it is on the target’s person. The spell ends for a target that attacks or casts a spell, even if their target is not undead.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

Swap Forms.name: Swap Forms
Swap Forms.description:
Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard

Choose two creatures you can see. The creatures swap forms. The spell lasts for the duration, or until the target drops to0 hit pointsor dies. If you concentrate on this spell for the full duration, the transformation lasts until it is dispelled. This spell has no effect on a target with0 hit points. Unwilling creatures can make aWisdomsaving throw, and if one of them succeeds, neither is affected by this spell. The swapped form is limited to a challenge rating that is equal to or less your level—if either creature’s form is higher than your level, the spell fails. The target’s game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the statistics of the new form. It retains its alignment and personality. The target assumes thehit pointsof its new form, and when it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the number ofhit pointsit had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form.

As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce the creature’s normal form to0 hit points, it isn’t knockedunconscious. The creature is limited in theactionsit can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can’t speak, cast spells, or take any other action that requires hands or speech, unless its new form is capable of suchactions. The target’s gear melds into the new form. The creature can’t activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment.

Curse of the Leech.name: Curse of the Leech
Curse of the Leech.description:
Target: One creature within range

You curse a creature, leeching its life force. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed, the creature takes 1d4 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, and you regainhit pointsequal to the damage dealt. The curse ends early if you and the target are more than 60 feet away at any time during the spell’s duration.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the necrotic damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 1st.

Quick Trap.name: Quick Trap
Quick Trap.components: V, S, M (small handful of sand and a drop of water)
Quick Trap.description:
You create a magical trap on the ground in a 5-foot square you can touch. The trap is nearlyinvisibleand requires a successfulIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC to detect. When a creature other than you enters the trap’s space, the ground immediately liquefies, and the creature must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fall into a magical pit that forms beneath it. A creature that fails the save fallsproneand becomesrestrainedas it sinks into the pit, which partially fills with earth or mud. To escape, the creature must use its action to succeed on a DC 20Strength(Athletics) check. On a successful saving throw, the creature fallspronein an adjacent unoccupied space of its choice.

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the trap occupies another 5-foot square for each additional level. Each additional square must be adjacent to the square you are touching.

Ray of Radiance.description:
You fire a bright white or golden ray of light from your hand. Make a ranged spellattack. On a hit, the target takes 10d6 radiant damage. If the target is undead or a fiend, the damage increases to 10d8.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you deal an additional 1d6 (or 1d8) radiant damage for each spell slot above 4th.

Litany of Rest.description:
You can touch up to six creatures, who can immediately spend Hit Dice to regainhit pointsas if they completed a short rest. If a creature rolls a 1 on any of these Hit Dice, they may reroll the die, but must take the second result.

Aura of Death.name: Aura of Death
Aura of Death.description:
You radiate a 30-foot aura of negative energy. The aura is centered on you and moves with you. With a bonus action, you can cause one creature in the area to suffer 3d6 necrotic damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for every three slot levels above 3rd.

Time Hop.name: Time Hop
Time Hop.description:
The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or disappear in a shimmer of silver energy. The subject reappears in exactly the same orientation and condition as before at the end of the duration. From the subject’s point of view, no time has passed at all. The target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, you can target up to nine additional creatures.

Wall of Force.name: Wall of Force
Wall of Force.components: V, S, M(a pinch of powder made by crushing a clear gemstone)
Wall of Force.description:
An invisible wall of force springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose, as a horizontal or vertical barrier or at an angle. It can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a sphere with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1/4 inch thick. It lasts for the duration. If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (your choice which side).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can’t be dispelled bydispel magic. Adisintegratespell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel through the wall.

Clear the Board.name: Clear the Board
Clear the Board.components: V, S, M(obsidian or ivory chess piece)
Clear the Board.description:
You send your allies and your enemies to opposite sides of the battlefield. Pick a cardinal direction.

With a shout and a gesture, you and up to five willing friendly creatures within range are teleported up to 90 feet in that direction to spaces you can see. At the same time, up to six hostile creatures within range must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the hostile creature is teleported up to 90 feet in the opposite direction of where youteleportyourself and the friendly creatures to spaces you can see. You can’tteleporta target into dangerous terrain, such as lava or off the edge of a cliff, and each target must be teleported to an unoccupied space that is on the ground or on a floor.

Vitrific Visibility.name: Vitrific Visibility
Vitrific Visibility.description:
Classes:bard,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

With an incantation and a gesture of your hands, a wave of liquid crystal flows out from you.Invisiblecreatures caught in the 15-foot cone are covered in a layer of crystal that instantly reveals their presence.

Invisiblecreatures are also trapped by the crystal coating for 1 round and are consideredrestrained. Creatures who make a successfulDexteritysaving throw are notrestrainedbut are still coated in crystal. This spell has no effect on visible creatures.

Ultimate Treasury (5E)© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors: Jason Nelson, Loren Sieg, Pedro Coelho, Matt Goodall, Linda Zayas-Palmer, Thurston Hillman, Jeff Ibach, and Alex Augunas
