Celestial Healing.components: V, S, M (1 drop of blood from an good extraplanar creature)
Celestial Healing.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (1 drop of blood from an good extraplanar creature)

Duration5 + spellcasting modifier rounds

NoteThis spell is a rework of the core spell of the same name.

You anoint the target with the blood of a good extraplanar creature, using the inherent magic properties to heal them 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns. If the target is dying while under the effect of this spell, they automatically succeed their death saving throw for the round instead of being healed to 1hpimmediately. This does not heal necrotic damage.

This spell has no effect on constructs.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or higher, the healing granted each round increases to 2. The healing further increases to 3 if you instead use a spell slot of 5th or higher.

Sea Spray.description:
Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard

You conjure a burst of salty seawater. Each creature in a 10-foot cone must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage and has disadvantage on the nextattackroll it makes before the end of its next turn. This spell’s damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

Circular Breathing.name: Circular Breathing
Circular Breathing.description:
You begin carefully regulating your breath so that you can continue playing longer, or keep breathing longer in adverse conditions.

You can maintain concentration on this cantrip in addition to another spell. If you lose concentration on another spell while concentrating on this cantrip, you also stop concentrating on this cantrip.

While maintaining concentration on this spell you can breathe underwater, and you can cast spells using verbal components and bardic performances that would normally require breathable air. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against gasses and adverse atmospheres. The number of minutes you can maintain concentration on this spell increases by 1 when you reach 5th level (6 minutes), 11th level (7 minutes), and 17th level (8 minutes).

Disguise Weapon.name: Disguise Weapon
Disguise Weapon.description:
Classes: antipaladin,bard,ranger,warlock,wizard

You make one manufactured weapon look like a different weapon of the same generalsize, so a weapon with thelight, heavy, reach, or two-handed property can only be made to look like another weapon with the same property. You can even change the appearance of an improvised weapon, like making a short stick appear to be a shortsword or similar blade. You can obscure minor features on the weapon, such as runes, engravings, or decorations, orhidebloodstains or other identifying marks, and can make the weapon appear to be made of a different material. Disguise weapon does not affect the weapon’s actual properties.

A creature examining the weapon can attempt anIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC to recognize the illusion and discern its true form.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can disguise the weapon as something different than its own category.

In addition, if you cast it using a 2nd-level spell slot (or 3rd level, if you are changing the weapon’s apparentsize), you can increase the duration to 8 hours. If you cast it using a 3rd-level spell slot (or 4th level for a change in weaponsize), you increase it to 24 hours.

Shadow Resilience.name: Shadow Resilience
Shadow Resilience.description:
Shadow matter moves and shifts around you. For the duration, this moving and shifting matter grants you a +5 bonus to yourDexterity(Stealth) check when you take theHideaction; in addition, you gain a number oftemporary hit pointsequal to one-half the result of yourDexterity(Stealth) check. When the spell ends, any remainingtemporary hit pointsare lost.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Waterfall.name: Waterfall
Waterfall.description:
A cascading wall of water falls to the ground at a point you choose within range. The falling water appears at the top of the affected area, conjured from the elemental plane of water. It disappears at the bottom of the area, returning to the elemental plane of water. You can make the wall up to 50 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot thick. You can shape the wall in any way you choose so long as it makes one continuous path along the ground. The wall lasts for the duration.

When the waterfall appears, each creature within its area must make aStrengthsaving throw. A creature takes 3d8 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The falling water keeps fog, smoke, and other gasses at bay. Small or smaller flying creatures or objects can’t pass through the waterfall. Loose, lightweight materials brought into the waterfall are dragged downward. Arrows, bolts, and other ordinary projectiles launched at targets behind the waterfall are deflected downward and automatically miss. (Boulders hurled by giants or siege engines, and similar projectiles, are unaffected.) Creatures ingaseous formcan’t pass through it.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Alpha Instinct.name: Alpha Instinct
Alpha Instinct.components: V, S, M (bit of musk from a socially dominant animal)
Alpha Instinct.description:
Animals perceive you as their social superior.

You have advantage onCharisma(Animal Handling) checks, and if you have a friendly animal available you can use a bonus action to interact with it while making anIntelligence(Nature),Wisdom(Survival), or—if the animal is at least yoursize—Strength(Athletics) check.

This counts as the animal’sreactionas well as its bonus action on its next turn. Animals made friendly with this spell do not aid you in combat and flee if in danger.

At any point during the spell’s duration, you can issue a nonverbal command to all animals within 60 feet, inducing them to forage for food for you. These animals disappear into the surrounding wilderness for 1 hour, after which they return to the location where you issued the command with an offering of 5 pounds of edible food. This ends the spell.

The Dragon’s Hoard #26© 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

Aura of Resolve.description:
Target: Allied creatures in a 60-foot radius

You radiate an aura of strength and resolve. You and friendly creatures within 60 feet become immune to beingcharmedorfrightened.

Transport via Plants.name: Transport via Plants
Transport via Plants.description: This spell creates a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within range and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence. You must have seen or touched the destination plant at least once before. For the duration, any creature can step into the target plant and exit from the destination plant by using 5 feet of movement.

Frostscythe.name: Frostscythe
Frostscythe.description:
Target: Each creature in a 15-foot cone

You swing an icy scythe in a wide arc in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 4d8 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails the saving throws also has its speed halved until the end of its next turn.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Hypnotic Pattern.name: Hypnotic Pattern
Hypnotic Pattern.components: S, M(a glowing stick of incense or a crystal vial filled with phosphorescent material)
Hypnotic Pattern.description:
You create a twisting pattern of colors that weaves through the air inside a 30-foot cube within range. The pattern appears for a moment and vanishes. Each creature in the area who sees the pattern must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomescharmedfor the duration. Whilecharmedby this spell, the creature is incapacitated and has a speed of 0.

The spell ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage or if someone else uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.
Hypnotic Pattern.material_component: a glowing stick of incense or a crystal vial filled with phosphorescent material

Feast of Ashes.name: Feast of Ashes
Feast of Ashes.description:
You curse the target with a hunger no food can assuage. If the target fails aConstitutionsaving throw, they begin to starve. They gain no nutrition from food they eat, and even attempting to eat provokes cramps and nausea, forcing the target to make aConstitutionsaving throw to avoid beingpoisonedfor 1 round. Other than providing nutrition, objects they eat have their normal effects, such aspoisoneditems, potions, etc. The target can go without food for a number of days equal to 3 + theirConstitutionmodifier (minimum 1). At the end of each day beyond that limit, the target automatically gains one level ofexhaustion.

Feast of ashes can be removed withdispel evil and good,greater restoration,remove curse, orwishor by consuming a heroes’ feast, but anyexhaustiongained as a result of the spell remains until it is removed by rest or magic. While the curse remains, taking a long rest does not reduce the target’sexhaustionlevel since they are treated as having not ingested any food during their rest.

The Dragon’s Hoard #25 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Light of Salvation.name: Light of Salvation
Light of Salvation.description:
You offer a prayer of salvation for an ally in need and a holy light envelops them. Choose one ally within range. Each hostile creature within 10 feet of the chosen ally must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 1d4 radiant damage. The chosen ally then gainstemporary hit pointsequal to the total radiant damage dealt.

At higher levels. When you cast this spell using a 3rd- or 4th level spell slot, the damage increases to 2d4. When you cast it using a 5th- or 6th-level spell slot, the damage increases to 5d4. When you cast it using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases to 8d4.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Sunburst.name: Sunburst
Sunburst.components: V, S, M(fire and a piece of sunstone)
Sunburst.description:
Brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in that light must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 12d6 radiant damage and isblindedfor 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’tblindedby this spell. Undead and oozes have disadvantage on this saving throw.

A creatureblindedby this spell makes anotherConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, it is no longerblinded.

This spell dispels any darkness in its area that was created by a spell.
Sunburst.material_component: fire and a piece of sunstone

Slipsand.name: Slipsand
Slipsand.description:
You transform an area of natural sand into tiny nodules of vitrified glass that are exceptionally smooth and slippery, filling up to 6 10-foot cubes within range, each of which must be adjacent (including diagonally) to another. Slipsand is similar in effect to ordinary quicksand, but far more deadly, as it gives way under any amount of weight and creatures cannot swim or tread water in it; they immediately sink to the bottom and must hold their breath or begin to suffocate. A creature in Slipsand isBlindedand has Disadvantage on otherWisdom(Perception) checks. If able to find the edge of the area, they can attempt to climb out of the smooth-sided pit with aStrength(Athletics) check against your spell save DC. Slipsand resembles ordinary sand. A creature actively exploring it can notice the difference with a successfulWisdom(Perception) check, but anIntelligence(Nature) check is needed to understand exactly what it is. The DC for either check is equal to your spell save DC. A creature running or charging can’t search for Slipsand. Allies can use theHelpaction to assist a creature in climbing out of Slipsand or can throw a rope or similar tool for them to grab. They can then pull the creature out of the Slipsand with a DC 10Strengthcheck. You can create areas of Slipsand adjacent to each other horizontally or diagonally, but you can’t stack them vertically. A Huge or larger creature can move through the Slipsand without difficulty, though they must spend 10 feet of movement to climb out of the Slipsand. You can cast this spell on exposed earth, clay, or soil that is not sand, but this reduces the size of each cube to 5 feet and grants Advantage onWisdom(Perception) checks to notice it.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect two additional cubes for each spell slot level above 4. In addition, if you increase the slot level by 2, you make the duration permanent.

The Dragon’s Hoard #61© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, Robert J. Grady, Ismael Alvarez, Amber Scott, Jeff Ibach, Katherine Schuttler.

Destiny Bond.name: Destiny Bond
Destiny Bond.components: V, S, M (lock of hair, scales, fur, or another small bit of the target)
Destiny Bond.description:
Choose a willing creature that you can see within range. For the duration, any damage you or the target receives is split between both of you (rounded down). If the target is killed while under the effects of this spell, you immediately drop to0 hit pointsand areunconscious. If either you or the target receivehealing, thehealingis split between you two (rounded down). If the target is attacked by a damage type you are resistant to, the damage is still split equally between the two of you, negating anyresistanceeffects you may have. It is the same if you are attacked by a damage type they are resistant to. Additionally, if they are attacked by a damage type that you are vulnerable to, the damage is still split equally, and vice versa. This spell loses its effect if the target moves 1,000 feet or more away from you or moves to another plane after this spell is cast.

Silver Arc.name: Silver Arc
Silver Arc.description:
You create an arcing beam of moonlight between two targets within range and within 60 feet of each other.

This moonlight deals 10d6 points of radiant damage to both targets and any creatures in the line connecting them. Additionally, all affected creatures are affected by the effects of moonlight if they have abilities or 30 conditions triggered by moonlight. Any creature that has their resistances passed by silver instead takes 10d8 damage. A successfulConstitutionsaving throw halves the damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 or 1d8 for each slot level above 5th.

Faith Burst.name: Faith Burst
Faith Burst.description:
You conjure a symbol of your deity momentarily with a burst of light. All other creatures within 5 feet of you must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or take 1d6 radiant damage. Your allies have advantage on this saving throw. An ally that worships the same deity as you does not take this damage.

At Higher Levels. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Frog in Your Throat.name: Frog in Your Throat
Frog in Your Throat.description:
Choose a creature you can see within range. Until the start of your next turn, that creature has disadvantage on spellattackrolls if the spell cast has a verbal component.

Galder’s Gazetteer Author(s) Matt Click, Gabe Hicks, Jess Ross

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Affliction of the Betrayer’s Mark.name: Affliction of the Betrayer’s Mark
Affliction of the Betrayer’s Mark.components: V, S, M (a drop of ink mixed with your own blood)
Affliction of the Betrayer’s Mark.description:
You mark a creature with a symbol of betrayal that only you can see. For the duration, you always know the direction and distance to the marked target as long as it is on the same plane of existence as you. If a marked creature attempts to lie to you, it must succeed on aCharismasaving throw or be compelled to speak the truth.

Group Telepathy.name: Group Telepathy
Group Telepathy.description:
You and up to three creatures of your choice within range gain the ability to communicate telepathically over limited distance for a short time. The targeted creatures can communicate regardless of language with any creature within 50 feet. Affected creatures also take a -2 penalty to saving throws against enchantment, charm, or other mind-affecting effects, and have tactical disadvantage against the attacks and abilities of extraterrene creatures.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Unfortunate Origami.name: Unfortunate Origami
Unfortunate Origami.description:
Any item you touch is transformed into a delicate facsimile of itself crafted of folded paper. A paper item has its weight reduced to 25% normal, its hardness reduced to 0, and itshit pointsreduced to 10% of the normal amount (or 2hit pointsper inch for solid barriers). If the item is held by another creature, that creature may attempt aConstitutionsaving throw to negate the effect. An origami weapon deals only 1 point of damage (plus any magical bonuses it possesses) on a successful hit, and the weapon itself takes 1d6 points of damage each time it strikes an opponent. Origami armor and shields provide no bonus to AC, though if they are magical their bonuses still apply. Origami items retain their magical properties but are very fragile and susceptible to damage from being worn or wielded, forcing their wearer or wielder to succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each day to avoid the item’s destruction. Items transformed into paper by unfortunate origami can be restored to normal withremove curseorwish.

The Dragon’s Hoard #14 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

Hieroglyphic Barrier.name: Hieroglyphic Barrier
Hieroglyphic Barrier.description:
You create a screen of glowing hieroglyphs and translucent pictograms in an Egyptian style up to 100 ft. long, and 10 ft. tall. The hieroglyphic barrier does not block line of sight but does provide light obscuring in both directions to creatures on the opposite side of the barrier.

The glowing glyphs and images shed bright light within 10 feet and normal light 10 feet beyond this.

In addition to the visual effects described above, any creature passing through a hieroglyphic barrier is affected as if the barrier were aglyph of warding. The caster must designate the type of glyph at the time of casting and it cannot be changed thereafter. This spell functions likeanimate dead, except you can animate two creatures and set a specific condition for when the animation occurs, which can be at any point within 10 days. The condition can be simple, such as being touched, a command word, or hearing a specific sound, or you can set the creature’s animation to happen at a specific time.

Choose up to 5 creatures within range that you can see.

Those creatures must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save each target suffers the same pain and damage it inflicts upon others for the duration. This does not include damage they cause using spells that have an area of effect.

If a creature is reduced to0 hit pointsby damage they receive from this spell, they fallunconscious, but are stable.

Each time any creature dies within 30 feet of an affected target, the target must succeed on an additionalWisdomsaving throw or bestunneduntil the end of their next turn.

If more than one creature dies in the same turn, this effect is cumulative.

For the duration, creatures affected by this spell have advantage onWisdom(Animal HandlingandInsight) andCharisma(Persuasion) checks.

Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Sorcerer

You summon a shield made of magical coral to surround a creature of your choice within range.

The target gains a +2 bonus to AC andresistanceto bludgeoning damage for the duration.

The target can see in all directions without having to physically look at them, and the range of its sight (includingdarkvisionand truesight) is doubled. As an action, you can cause yourshadowto pulsate with power tearing open a rift to the plane of shadows at your location. You unleash a horde of shadowy monsters that attempt to drag every creature besides you through the opening. Each creature, other than you, within 30 feet must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or be dragged to the closest unoccupied space where they areprone. If the creature fails by 5 or more, it is dragged through the rift to the plane of shadows. This rift closes at the end ofyour turnleaving behind oneshadowin the closest unoccupied space for each creature dragged through the rift. The shadows are friendly to you and dissipate into mist when they drop to0 hit points, or dawn arrives. The shadows share yourinitiativecount but take their turn immediately after yours. They obey any verbal commands you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to the shadows, they take theDodgeaction and will use their move to avoid danger.

Blood Bullets.description:
When you cast this spell, you spill blood from your palm by drawing an enchanted pattern onto it with a weapon that deals piercing or slashing damage.

Your blood rises from your hand and forms up to five bullets you fling at creatures you can see. Make a ranged spellattackagainst each target. On a hit, a target takes 2d8 piercing damage. The bullets all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several. Hit or miss, the blood bullet then explodes. Every target and each creature within 5 feet of the point where a blood bullet exploded must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 2d6 necrotic damage. You take 1d4 points of damage for each blood bullet formed. This damage cannot be avoided and ignores both resistances and immunities. Creatures that do not have any blood are unable to cast this spell.

Dream Debate.duration: instantaneous Dreaming Descriptor Spells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest.
Dream Debate.description:
Dreaming DescriptorSpells with the “dreaming” descriptor. Spells with the dreaming descriptor can only be cast while taking an 8-hour or longer long rest. You must have the spell slots needed to do so when you go to sleep, but the same slots are also expended when you wake—you cannot regain them for use the next day. You cannot cast more than 8 spell-levels worth of dreaming spells in a single night. These spells generally have casting times of hours, but those are hours during which you are asleep. Regardless of how long you sleep, you cannot cast more than 8 hours worth of dreaming spells in one 24-hour period. Dreaming spells with a duration of “1 day or until expended” also end if you sleep for 1 hour or more before they are expended.

You cast this spell while sleeping. You target either yourself or a sleeping, willing creature within range to have a dream of an academic setting where numerous studious dream figments debate a single problem, philosophical issue, or memory.

At the end of this dream, anytime in the next 24 hours, the target may make a singleIntelligence– orWisdom-based skill check with advantage. A target can only benefit from one dream debate at one time.

A 5-foot-diameter sphere of holy light appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. The creature takes 2d4 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a bonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make the saving throw against the sphere’s damage, and the sphere stops moving this turn. When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. The sphere ignites flammable objects not being worn or carried, and it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet.

You know exactly what your comrade needs to hear to bolster their spirits and keep them in the fight.

Choose a target within range and if that target can hear and understand you they receive 1d4temporary hit pointsuntil the end of your next turn and receive advantage on their nextattackroll.

Entrenchment.name: Entrenchment
Entrenchment.description:
This spell excavates a trench 20 feet long that is 5 feet wide and 5 feet deep. Creatures in the area where the trench appears are knockedpronein the pit unless they make a successful saving throw. If they make a successful saving throw, they land on their feet in the pit, or on either side of it (creature’s choice).

The dirt excavated by the spell is hurled up to form a 5-foot-high earthen berm along one side of the trench. This berm is of loosely packed soil, with 90hit pointsper 5-foot section. Creatures in the area where the berm appears are partially buried and gain therestrainedcondition unless they succeed on a Reflex save. A successful save allows them to move into an adjacent square and avoid beingrestrained.

A creature partially buried can free themselves with a successful DC 10StrengthorDexteritycheck or can dig themselves out by dealing 15 points of damage to the berm.

Convalesce.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a pinch of sand)

Creatures affected by this spell can completely relax their bodies and minds, as though they had slept significantly longer. If the target completes a full night’s rest, it is treated as though it had two periods of long rest (regaining all losthit pointsand spent Hit Dice). Any interruption during the rest (such as being awoken) ends the effect of the spell on the awakened target.

Targets sleeping with an attuned somnifer instead treat the full night’s rest as if it was a long rest and a use of the recuperating downtime activity. The target must have been attuned to their somnifer before convalesce was cast.

If a target with an attuned somnifer loses their somnifer before they wake up, they do not benefit from convalesce and are treated as only having a short rest. The target suffers one level ofexhaustionuntil they are reunited with their somnifer, or the duration of convalesce would expire.

Scramble.components: V, S, M (an egg, which smash when casting the spell)
Scramble.description:
You momentarily warp space, swapping creatures’ positions randomly. Each creature (excluding you) within range must succeed on aCharismasaving throw or become scrambled. The scrambled creature with the lowest result on its saving throw chooses a scrambled creature (excluding itself) and magically swaps places with it. Then the creature with the next lowest saving throw chooses the same or another scrambled creature (excluding itself) and swaps places with it. Continue until every scrambled creature has swapped places with another, then you can swap places with one of the scrambled creatures, and the spell ends.

If only one creature fails the saving throw, the creature doesn’t swap places with another creature, but you can swap places with it.

Enemies take 8d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Allies in the sphere take minimum (8) damage instead, or half as much on a successful save.

You create a potent seal on a surface or an object touched that repels fiends and undead. The seal covers an area in a 20-foot-radius centered on the point touched. Any fiend or undead creature that attempts to enter the area must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, the creature cannot enter the area for the duration of the spell.

Weighty Restraints.description:
You infuse a pair of manacles that a creature is wearing with the mass and empty magnitude of the Void. The creature wearing the manacles gains four levels ofexhaustionwhilerestrainedby them. A creaturerestrainedby the manacles cannot gain more levels ofexhaustion, and it cannot lose levels ofexhaustionby finishing a long rest. The manacles can be removed by making aDexterity(thieves’ tools) check against your spell save DC. If the tools are not magical, the check is made with disadvantage. A creature can only be affected by one pair of manacles enchanted by this spell at a time.

Feasting Forest.name: Feasting Forest
Feasting Forest.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You instill a violent, bloodlust into the nature spirits and bring them to violence against your enemies. A 120-foot radius area within range is affected as follows, depending on the terrain within:

Any area within the affected area that is covered by such terrain becomes magicaldifficult terrainfor your enemies and any creature passing through takes on 1d4 necrotic damage which continues at the beginning of each of their rounds thereafter until they receivehealing. If a creature is currently taking ongoing necrotic damage from this terrain and moves through the area on another turn the necrotic damage increases by 1.

Trees or other Large Plants: At the beginning ofyour turn, any enemy within 10 feet of a tree in the affected area takes 4d6 slashing or bludgeoning damage. A successfulDexteritysaving throw halves this damage.

Any creature that fails their saving throw is also subject to an immediate grapple attempt by the trees using your spellcasting modifier for theAthleticscheck.

Roots, Vines and Kelp: Any area with such plant material in the area acts as though under aBlack Tentaclesspell using this spell’s DCs.

Rocks, Ice or Crystals: As a bonus action onyour turn, you can cause a loose chunk of such material to launch and strike an enemy within the area of the spell or 10 feet outside of its area. You make a ranged spellattackand on a hit, you deal 3d6 bludgeoning damage.

If the spell deals damage, afterward, the affected area permanently looks more verdant and healthy.

When casting the spell you can designate a number of creatures that are not affected by the spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

Chain Counterspell.name: Chain Counterspell
Chain Counterspell.description:
You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell, and if successful, you can chain additional counterspell attempts for the rest of the round. If the target creature is casting a spell of 3rd level or lower, its spell fails and has no effect. If it is casting a spell of 4th level or higher, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 + the spell’s level). On a success, the creature’s spell fails and has no effect.

As a bonusreactionuntil the beginning of your next turn, you can attempt to counterspell any creature you can see casting a spell within 60 feet of you. Regardless of the level of spell the creature is casting, you must make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 + the spell’s level). On a success, the creature’s spell fails and has no effect.

As long as you continue to make successful ability checks, you may continue to use bonusreactionsto counterspell. If you fail one of these ability checks, this spell ends.

Sphere of Ultimate Evil.description:

A 5-foot-diameter sphere of pure evil appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. The sphere obliterates all matter it passes through and all matter that passes through it. Artifacts are the exception. Unless an artifact is susceptible to damage from a sphere of ultimate evil, it passes through the sphere unscathed. Anything else that touches the sphere but isn’t wholly engulfed and obliterated by it takes 22 (4d10) necrotic damage. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. A good creature takes 28 (8d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature or neutral or evil alignment takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If this damage reduces the target to0 hit points, it is disintegrated. A disintegrated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. The creature can be restored to life only by means of atrue resurrectionor awishspell. As a bonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. The Restrained condition ends if the ice is destroyed or the creature escapes. Each creature in the area is subjected to an irresistible freeze. When frozen in this way, a creature immediately takes 8d8 cold damage but is otherwise unaffected by any other events or effects around it until freed. Its speed becomes zero, it can’t move, takeactions, bonusactions, orreactions, and becomes encased in unbreakable ice, impervious to all damage.

Faceless Disguise.name: Faceless Disguise
Faceless Disguise.description:
You make yourself and all your gear appear as a featureless, genderless humanoid statue of pale stone, smooth in appearance yet coarse to the touch, seeming to crumble slightly into drifts of dust when strongly struck. You have advantage onDexterity(Stealth) skill checks in areas of natural stone or rubble and advantage onDexterity(Sleight of Hand) tohidesmall objects on your person. A creature interacting with you including attacking or being attacked by you, must succeed at aWisdomsaving throw to reveal it to be an illusion. Creatures seeing through the outer illusion instead perceive you as an emaciated, naked, genderless, hairless, eye-less, nose-less, many-toothed, slick, clay-colored humanoid of indeterminate age. The only distinguishing marks which appear upon the illusion at all are a series of shifting, jagged geometric diagrams in lieu of a face. Those perceiving this second illusion are filled with horror and revulsion, and have disadvantage on allCharismasaving throws for 1 hour. Creatures withIntelligenceof 2 or less are immune. Those making their second save see through both layers of the illusion and suffer no ill effects from interacting with you.

Traitor.name: Traitor
Traitor.description:
You begin play with one magic item of uncommon rarity chosen from the following list (roll 1d10): 1—bag of tricks(rust), 2—boots of elvenkind, 3—boots of striding and springing, 4—cloak of elvenkind, 5—decanter of endless water, 6—eversmoking bottle, 7—eyes of minute seeing, 8—eyes of the eagle, 9—gloves of missile snaring, 10—gloves of climbing and swimming.

You cannot sell or trade this item until you have reached at least 5th level (though you may lose it or have it stolen from you if circumstances prevail).

In addition, your Sin score increases by 4 and you are hunted by those that seek vengeance for whatever you did to acquire your wealth. The full breadth of what your nemeses will do to have their revenge is at the GM’s discretion (though at the very least bounty hunters, Justitia, and private investigators attempt to capture you once each month).

Army of the Dead.name: Army of the Dead
Army of the Dead.components: V, S, M (diamond dust worth 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
Army of the Dead.description:
Target: Unoccupied spaces that you can see within range

Classes: Cleric, Warlock, Wizard

You summon an army of undead creatures, choosing one the following options for what appears:

The summoned creatures appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within range and disappear when they drop to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends, disintegrating into dust and leaving no physical trace of their existence. They follow your commands (no action required by you), and they act duringyour turnin combat. If you don’t issue any commands to them, they will protect you fromharmandattackany creature that attacks you.

At the Game Master’s discretion, the Army of the Dead spell can be used to summon an army of undead creatures whose combined Challenge Rating (CR) is equal to or less than 15. The caster can choose any combination of undead creatures as long as their total CR does not exceed this limit.

This allows for greater flexibility and creativity in the deployment of the Army of the Dead spell, facilitating moments of epic and cinematic gameplay that enhance the overall gaming experience as per the rule of cool. For instance, if the narrative and dramatic tension of a session would be heightened by summoning a horde of lesser undead creatures instead of a few stronger ones, the Game Master might allow this variation of the spell. The original wording of the spell is crafted for ease of use and efficiency during gameplay, aiming to prevent excessive delays during turns and excessively slowing down the game while mantaining an engaging pace of play.

Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard

A humanoid you touch must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or age 30 years for the duration of the spell. While aged, the target suffers physical ability score penalties to itsStrength,Dexterity, andConstitution. A humanoid that becomes middle-aged suffers a -1 penalty, a humanoid that becomes old suffers a -2 penalty, a humanoid that becomes venerable suffers a -3 penalty.

You warp the threads of fate when a creature within range makes a die roll, forcing them to immediately reroll that die and take the second result instead. You strike the target with a spiraling violet ray that spins like a corkscrew towards them. If you hit with a ranged spellattack, the target experiences vertigo and has difficulty coordinating its movement and otheractions. If the target succeeds on aWisdomsaving throw, its speed is reduced by 10 feet and it takes a -1 penalty onDexteritychecks, saving throws, or attack rolls that useDexterityfor 1 round, after which the effects of the ray of dizziness end. If the target takes no actions on its turn, it can attempt a newWisdomsaving throw at the end of its turn to end this vertigo. The effects of a successful saving throw are as noted above, while failure results in the full effects of dizziness remaining in place an additional round. This spell summons forth a single serpentine servant of the World Eater to serve you. You may choose any one of the following creatures:

Amphisbaena: This two-headed snake is a monstrosity (see sidebar).

Hebina: This variant of the succubus has long red?scaled serpents for arms granting it a reach of 10 and replacing its claw attacks with bites. Damage does not change, but each bite injects a soporific poison that dulls the target’s mind.

Crows are legendary allies of wolves; wolves follow crows to look for fresh meat and crows follow wolves for a potential meal. This spell recalls the pact between the two species.

You summon three friendly swarms of ravens that appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within range. The swarms disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. You call upon the deep sea to summon a powerful beast from its depths. You choose which beast is summoned, which must be of challenge rating of 5 or lower and have a swimming speed. The summoned creature appears in an unoccupied space you can see within range. It acts as an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the creature shares yourinitiativecount but takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes noactions. The summoned creature disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

Aura of Filth.name: Aura of Filth
Aura of Filth.description:
Putrefying energy radiates in a 30-foot radius around you.

Each creature in the aura, including you, has disadvantage on saving throws against poison and disease and on death saving throws. In addition, each creature in the aura can’t be cured of a disease or poison, except by means of ahealorwishspell.

Dying or decaying material within the aura, such as corpses, picked flowers, or food, rapidly putrefy, decaying an additional day for each round it is in the aura. This effect increases the amount of time a corpse has been dead, counting against the time limit of spells such asraise dead.

Dark Command.name: Dark Command
Dark Command.description:
You issue a command filled with dark power to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed in this way, a creature must follow your command on its turn. The spell has no effect if the target is undead, if it doesn’t understand your language, or if your command is directly harmful to it. A cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Ectoplasmic Expulsion.name: Ectoplasmic Expulsion
Ectoplasmic Expulsion.description:
You call upon tendrils of ephemeral ectoplasm to pass through one creature you can see within range and carry away all harmful psychic afflictions. You end each spell or effect thatcharmedorfrightenedthe target. In addition, if the target is possessed, the possession ends. Each expelled effect manifests momentarily as a colored aura or other sensory cue that imparts to you its school of magic (if any) and then vanishes in the general direction of its caster or source. For the duration, the target has advantage on saving throws against all the expelled spells and effects (whether from the same source or a different one).

Snapdragon Fireworks.name: Snapdragon Fireworks
Snapdragon Fireworks.description:
You create fireworks in the shapes of tiny dragons, flowers, or almost anything you like. Each round as a bonus action, you may launch a firework on a zigzag path to strike a 5-foot-square, erupting with a bright flash and a loud bang and dealing 1d4 fire damage and 1d4 thunder damage, or half as much on a successfulDexteritysaving throw.

Creatures failing their saving throw against a firework are dazzled by their brightness, taking a -1 penalty onattackrolls, AC, andWisdom(Perception) checks for 1 round.

Each round you continue concentrating, you may launch another firework, and you can change their coloration or appearance each time.

This spell is very popular at pastoralhalflingcelebrations and feasts, especially around midsummer. Normally when this spell is used as part of a festival, the chosen target is high in the sky to increase visibility and protect observers.

Danger Sense.name: Danger Sense
Danger Sense.description:
You have advantage on aDexteritysaving throw against an effect that you can see, such as a trap or spell. To gain this benefit, you can’t beblinded,deafened, orincapacitated.

Ball of Nothing.name: Ball of Nothing
Ball of Nothing.description:
A two-foot-diametersphere of annihilationappears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. You can use an action to control the sphere. You can move it in one direction of your choice, up to a number of feet equal to 5 x your spellcasting modifier. If you fallunconsciousbefore the spell ends, the sphere acts as an uncontrolledsphere of annihilationuntil the spell ends, at which point it disappears.

The sphere obliterates all matter it passes through and all matter that passes through it. Artifacts are the exception. Unless an artifact is susceptible to damage from asphere of annihilation, it passes through the sphere unscathed. Anything else that touches the sphere but isn’t wholly engulfed and obliterated by it takes 4d10 force damage.

A creature whose space the sphere enters must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or be touched by it, taking 4d10 force damage. If the sphere comes into contact with a planar portal such as that created by thegatespell or an extradimensional space such as that within aportable hole, the GM determines randomly what happens, using the following table.

Jaguar Spirit.name: Jaguar Spirit
Jaguar Spirit.components: V, S, M(a jaguar tooth or claw)
Jaguar Spirit.description:
You conjure into existence a floating, spectral jaguar that appears within range and lasts for the whole duration. When you cast the spell, you can make a melee spellattackagainst a creature within five feet of the jaguar. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 force damage and isgrappled(escape DC equals your spell save DC). A creature that starts its turn alreadygrappledby the jaguar takes 3d6 force damage. As a bonus action onyour turn, you can move the jaguar up to 20 feet and repeat theattackagainst a creature within five feet of it. If the jaguar moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature right before biting it, the target must succeed on aStrengthcheck against your spell save DC or be knockedprone.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 3rd.

Last Strike.name: Last Strike
Last Strike.description:
You grant yourself a last burst of energy when deeply wounded. Before you fallunconscious, you gain one action. Any roll you make, such as for an ability check orattackroll, has advantage. You automatically fail your first death saving throw.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Counter Curse.name: Counter Curse
Counter Curse.description:
This curse allows you to disrupt the spellcasting ability of anyone you touch. When you cast this spell, one creature of your choice within range must make aCharismasaving throw. If they fail, the next four times the target attempts tocast a spell, they must succeed on a spell check against your spell save DC or the spell fails and the spell slot is lost.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell with a 5th-level slot or higher, the number of spells increases by 1 per additional level.

ComponentsV, S, M (a magnifying glass)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

A beam of brilliantlightflashes out from your hand in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long line. Each creature in the line must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 radiant damage and isblindeduntil your next turn and take 1 level ofexhaustion(to a maximum of 3 levels). On a successful save, it takes half as much damage, isn’tblindedby this spell, and does not increase theirexhaustionlevel.

Undead and oozes have disadvantage on this saving throw but are immune to theexhaustion. They instead arestunnedfor 1 round.

You can create a new line of radiance as your action on any turn until the spell ends.

For the duration, a mote of brilliant radiance shines in your hand. It sheds brightlightin a 30-foot radius and dimlightfor an additional 30 feet. Thislightis sunlight.

Weaken Object.name: Weaken Object
Weaken Object.description:
For the duration, an object you touch hasvulnerabilityto bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing (your choice). If the object is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, the creature can make aDexteritysaving throw to avoid your touch.

Greater Flight.name: Greater Flight
Greater Flight.description:
Your fly movement increases to 120 feet.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the fly movement increases by 10 feet for each spell slot above 2nd.

Wish.name: Wish
Wish.description:
Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal creature can cast. By simply speaking aloud, you can alter the very foundations of reality in accord with your desires.

The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of 8th level or lower. You don’t need to meet any requirements in that spell, including costly components. The spell simply takes effect.

Alternatively, you can create one of the following effects of your choice:

You might be able to achieve something beyond the scope of the above examples. State your wish to the GM as precisely as possible. The GM has great latitude in ruling what occurs in such an instance; the greater the wish, the greater the likelihood that something goes wrong. This spell might simply fail, the effect you desire might only be partly achieved, or you might suffer some unforeseen consequence as a result of how you worded the wish. For example, wishing that a villain were dead might propel you forward in time to a period when that villain is no longer alive, effectively removing you from the game. Similarly, wishing for a legendary magic item or artifact might instantly transport you to the presence of the item’s current owner.

The stress of casting this spell to produce any effect other than duplicating another spell weakens you. After enduring that stress, each time you cast a spell until you finish along rest, you take 1d10 necrotic damage per level of that spell. This damage can’t be reduced or prevented in any way. In addition, yourStrengthdrops to 3, if it isn’t 3 or lower already, for 2d4 days. For each of those days that you spend resting and doing nothing more than light activity, your remaining recovery time decreases by 2 days. Finally, there is a 33 percent chance that you are unable to castwishever again if you suffer this stress.

Flaming Sphere.name: Flaming Sphere
Flaming Sphere.components: V, S, M(a bit of tallow, a pinch of brimstone, and a dusting of powdered iron)
Flaming Sphere.description:
A 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. The creature takes 2d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

As abonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make the saving throw against the sphere’s damage, and the sphere stops moving this turn.

When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. The sphere ignites flammable objects not being worn or carried, and it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.
Flaming Sphere.material_component: a bit of tallow, a pinch of brimstone, and a dusting of powdered iron

Exhausting Dash.name: Exhausting Dash
Exhausting Dash.description:
You force a creature to run itself toexhaustion. The target creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw take theDashaction and move away from you by the safest available route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. The creature can use theDashaction a number of times equal to 3 + itsConstitutionmodifier.

Each additionalDashaction it takes requires the creature to succeed on a DC 10Constitutioncheck at the end of its turn or gain one level ofexhaustion. The creature can make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, the spell ends for that creature.

Alter Object.name: Alter Object
Alter Object.description:
An object no larger than 1 cubic foot you touch transforms into another object in the same kingdom. Only inanimate, non-magical, non-living objects made of animal or vegetable matter are affected. For example, a piece of parchment can be transformed into a handkerchief.

Hush.duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour For the duration, all sounds (no matter how loud) within
Hush.description:
For the duration, all sounds (no matter how loud) within a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range are muted and sound as if they are whispers. Attempts to hear any sound more than five feet from its point of origin (or from the perimeter of the sphere for sounds originating outside the sphere) require a successfulWisdom(Perception) check with a DC equal to 8 + the distance from the origin point in feet. Any creature or object entirely inside the sphere is immune to thunder damage.

Locate Creature.name: Locate Creature
Locate Creature.components: V, S, M(a bit of fur from a bloodhound)
Locate Creature.description:
Describe or name a creature that is familiar to you. You sense the direction to the creature’s location, as long as that creature is within 1,000 feet of you. If the creature is moving, you know the direction of its movement.

The spell can locate a specific creature known to you, or the nearest creature of a specific kind (such as a human or a unicorn), so long as you have seen such a creature up close-within 30 feet-at least once. If the creature you described or named is in a different form, such as being under the effects of apolymorphspell, this spell doesn’t locate the creature.

This spell can’t locate a creature if running water at least 10 feet wide blocks a direct path between you and the creature.

Heat Haze.name: Heat Haze
Heat Haze.description:
When you cast this spell, a 10-foot radius of superheated air appears around you and remains centered on you while it lasts.

Any liquids, including potions, within the area boil. Liquids in enclosed containers rupture their container. Flammable objects in the area that are not worn or carried ignite. Creatures in the area must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 1d8 fire damage.

Slither.name: Slither
Slither.components: V, M (ashes fromwooden statue of you made into ink and used to draw your portrait, worth at least 50 gp)
Slither.description:
You momentarily become a shadow (a humanoid-shaped absence of light, not the Undead creature of that name). You can slide under a door, through a keyhole, or through any other tiny opening. All of your equipment is transformed with you, and you can move up to your full speed during the spell’s duration. While in this form, you have advantage onDexterity(Stealth) checks made in darkness or dim light and you are immune to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. You can dismiss this spell by using an action to do so.

If you return to your normal form while in a space too small for you (such as a mouse hole, sewer pipe, or the like), you take 4d6 force damage and are pushed to the nearest space within 50 feet big enough to hold you. If the distance is greater than 50 feet, you take an extra 1d6 force damage for every additional 10 feet traveled.

While in shadow form, you can’t talk or manipulate objects, and any objects you are carrying or holding can’t be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. In addition, you can’t attack or cast spells while in shadow form.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target an additional willing creature that you touch for each slot level above 2nd.

The target of the spell becomes more bestial in appearance and grows a large, powerful, wolf-like jaw. They gain a 1d6 biteattack. If the bite attack hits, the target of the bite must make aDexteritysaving throw against your spell save DC or be knockedprone.

A creature you touch gains an additional action on each of its turns. That action can be used only to take theAttack(one weaponattackonly) action.

Solar Shroud.name: Solar Shroud
Solar Shroud.components: V, S, M (piece of sunlight-infused crystal)
Solar Shroud.description:
You enshroud the target in a brilliant halo of radiance, creating an aura ofdaylightcentered on them. Undead and evil creatures within this aura have disadvantage onattackrolls and saving throws against your spells and abilities.

Additionally, you gaindamage resistanceagainst attacks made by these creatures. Thisdamage resistanceapplies even against spells and abilities that deal hit point damage, as long as they are delivered by amelee attack.

Furthermore, when the target of the spell is struck by amelee attackfrom an undead or evil creature, it can use itsreactionto release a burst of holy radiance. This burst causes 1d6 fire damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level, the duration lasts an additional round.

Devil Blight.name: Devil Blight
Devil Blight.description:
You unleash waves of force that wrack the bodies of fiends.

The target takes 2d6 force damage on a failedConstitutionsaving throw, or half as much on a successful one. A fiend with thedevilsubtype that fails its save is alsostunnedfor 1 round and does not gain advantage on its saving throw if it has the MagicResistancetrait. This saving throw repeats each round you concentrate. If a devil fails its saving throw on three consecutive rounds, the spell ends and it is banished back to its home plane.

You assume a different form. When you cast the spell, choose one of the following options, the effects of which last for the duration of the spell. While the spell lasts, you can end one option as an action to gain the benefits of a different one.

The following is content created by a publisher other than Wizards of the Coast.

Create Butter Cat.name: Create Butter Cat
Create Butter Cat.components: V, S, M (ball of yarn, one or more spindles, and a cat’s whisker)
Create Butter Cat.description:
While speaking an intricate incantation, you wind the yarn around one or more spindles and insert a cat’s whisker, creating a special construct called a butter cat. The butter cat lives for a day, during which time it can be sent to steal and retrieve milk, up to 5 gallons. If at any time the butter cat takes damage, you suffer an equal amount of damage of the same type as the butter cat. If the butter cat is killed before the spell ends, you suffer 1d10 psychic damage. You can have only one butter cat at a time. If you cast this spell while your butter cat lives, the spell fails.

With a growl, you call forth dozens of bears to overrun all creatures in a 20-foot cube within range.

Each creature in the area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage and is forcedprone. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t forcedprone. The bears disappear after making their charge.

Arcane Hand.name: Arcane Hand
Arcane Hand.components: V, S, M(an eggshell and a snakeskin glove)
Arcane Hand.description:
You create a Large hand of shimmering, translucent force in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The hand lasts for the spell’s duration, and it moves at your command, mimicking the movements of your own hand.

The hand is an object that has AC 20 and hit points equal to your hit point maximum. If it drops to 0 hit points, the spell ends. It has aStrengthof 26 (+8) and aDexterityof 10 (+0). The hand doesn’t fill its space.

When you cast the spell and as abonus actionon your subsequent turns, you can move the hand up to 60 feet and then cause one of the following effects with it.

Clenched Fist: The hand strikes one creature or object within 5 feet of it. Make a melee spell attack for the hand using your game statistics. On a hit, the target takes 4d8 force damage.Forceful Hand: The hand attempts to push a creature within 5 feet of it in a direction you choose. Make a check with the hand’sStrengthcontested by theStrength(Athletics) check of the target. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check. If you succeed, the hand pushes the target up to 5 feet plus a number of feet equal to five times your spellcasting ability modifier. The hand moves with the target to remain within 5 feet of it.Grasping Hand: The hand attempts to grapple a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. You use the hand’sStrengthscore to resolve the grapple. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check. While the hand is grappling the target, you can use abonus actionto have the hand crush it. When you do so, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to 2d6 + your spellcasting ability modifier.Interposing Hand: The hand interposes itself between you and a creature you choose until you give the hand a different command. The hand moves to stay between you and the target, providing you with half cover against the target. The target can’t move through the hand’s space if itsStrengthscore is less than or equal to the hand’sStrengthscore. If itsStrengthscore is higher than the hand’sStrengthscore, the target can move toward you through the hand’s space, but that space is difficult terrain for the target.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage from the clenched fist option increases by 2d8 and the damage from the grasping hand increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 5th.

It has AC 16 andhit pointsequal to half your hit point maximum, disappearing if reduced to0 hit points. It uses your saving throws. It is immune to psychic or poison damage but takes damage from all other effects normally.

The versatile hand hasStrengthandDexterityscores of 18 (+4). At the time of casting (and each round thereafter as a bonus action) you can move the versatile hand up to 60 feet and have it perform one of the these effects:

When you cast this spell, you touch up to 4 creatures or objects. While this spell is active, those creatures leave no path, are forgotten the instant a creature turns from them, and are hidden from even the most doggeddivinationspells.

Rewind and Redo.description:
When you cast this spell, you bend time to your will to reverse the flow of existence. You reverse time exactly one turn for the world.

Hit points, conditions, locations, spell slots, and everything else in the world is exactly the same as it was exactly one turn ago from whichever turn you just interrupted. Unless specifically sensing for this spell, not even the gods know this occurred. You are the only one who has a memory of what happened before you cast the spell.

Classes:bard,cleric,druid,paladin,ranger

You purge weariness from all living creatures within range. Sleeping creatures are awakened, even if magically asleep, and theirexhaustion(if any) is reduced by 1 level. In addition, each creature’s hit point maximum and currenthit pointsare increased by 10 for 1 minute.

Tree Stride.name: Tree Stride
Tree Stride.description:
You gain the ability to enter a tree and move from inside it to inside another tree of the same kind within 500 feet. Both trees must be living and at least the same size as you. You must use 5 feet of movement to enter a tree. You instantly know the location of all other trees of the same kind within 500 feet and, as part of the move used to enter the tree, can either pass into one of those trees or step out of the tree you’re in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination tree, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the tree you entered.

You can use this transportation ability once per round for the duration. You must end each turn outside a tree.

Glyph of Controlling.components: V, S, M (incense and powdered diamond worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
Glyph of Controlling.description:
When you cast this spell, you craft a series of glyphs. By themselves, they have no effect. However, if you cast aglyph of wardingspell while having cast a glyph of controlling that has yet to be dispelled or triggered, you can tie it to this spell.

When doing so, the trigger for theglyph of wardingyou previously cast is tied to this glyph of controlling. While standing upon the glyph of controlling, you can use an action to trigger the previously tied glyphs of warding.

You can tie up to your Spellcasting ability modifier glyphs of warding to this spell when casting it. There is no limit, however, to the number of glyphs of controlling you can create.

Broken Charge.name: Broken Charge
Broken Charge.description:
When an enemy that you can see moves to within 5 feet of you, you utter a perplexing word that alters the foe’s course. The enemy must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or take 2d4 psychic damage and use the remainder of its speed to move in a direction of your choosing without provoking opportunity attacks.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 2d4 for each slot level above 1st.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Twine Double.name: Twine Double
Twine Double.description:
You shape an illusory duplicate of yourself. The duplicate is a creature, partially real and formed from cloth and twine, and it can takeactionsand otherwise be affected as a normal creature. The double looks exactly like you except its eyes are balls of twine (DC 10Intelligence(Investigation) check to recognize double’s strange eyes). It wears clothing and gear that appear exactly like what you are wearing at the time of casting. Its copies of your magic items are nonfunctional but radiate magic and have the same auras as your items. Its aura is identical to yours. It is ananimated object, a creature of the construct type, that has half your hit point maximum, cannotattack, has no special abilities, and has a +0 bonus on all saves and checks.

The twine double is friendly to you and creatures you designate. It obeys your spoken commands, moving and acting in accordance with your wishes and acting onyour turnin combat. You know what the double is experiencing, and when controlling it telepathically you can see and hear everything it sees and hears, though events at your location may drown out the sensory inputs from the double. If you cast this spell again, any currently active duplicates you created with this spell are instantly destroyed.

When your heroes are on the hunt for fabulous treasure, they need all their abilities in tip-top shape, with an array of awesome character options tailored for every kind of campaign. In this section, you’ll find a wide array ofdruidcircles,fightermartial archetypes,bardcolleges,warlockpatrons and invocations, and more, along with fantastic feats for any class.

Drowsy Fireflies.name: Drowsy Fireflies
Drowsy Fireflies.description:
You summon a small cloud of glimmering fireflies that fills a 5-foot radius, obscuring vision into or through the cloud (providingcoverif line of sight must pass through 5 feet or more of the swarm), and causing all creatures within the swarm to become dazzled (no save). In addition, the drowsy fireflies secrete a soporific pheromone that causes all creatures within the cloud to fall into a light slumber for 2d6 rounds if they fail aConstitutionsaving throw. The slumber induced by the drowsy fireflies is not as deep as that caused by sleep, and loud noises such as combat allow sleeping creatures to attempt a DC 10Wisdom(Perception) ability check each round at the end of their turns to awaken. ThisWisdom(Perception) ability check is made with disadvantage. Sleeping creatures can be automatically awakened by an ally as an action.

Reshape Skeleton.name: Reshape Skeleton
Reshape Skeleton.components: V, S, M (pinch of powdered giant bone)
Reshape Skeleton.description:
You cause one creature you can see to suffer a bonecracking rearrangement of itsskeleton. Choose one creature you can see within range that has a bony or cartilaginous skeletal structure. That creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw or its bone structure becomes mutable for the duration.

Until the spell ends, you can use a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns to adjust the target’s bone structure, limiting its ability to act. The target must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 3d10 bludgeoning damage and suffer one of the following effects of your choice until the end of its next turn: halved speed or disadvantage onattackrolls.

At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for every two slot levels above 4th.

Shapechanger’s Gift.name: Shapechanger’s Gift
Shapechanger’s Gift.components: V, S, M (piece of the creature whose form you plan to grant)
Shapechanger’s Gift.description:
You transform a willing creature into a beast with a challenge rating of 1/2 or lower with no fly speed. The creature gains the abilities of that beast as if it had the Wild Shape class feature of an 4th-leveldruid. Alternatively, you can cast this spell on two willing creatures, transforming each of them into a beast with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower with no fly or swim speed, with each gaining abilities as if they had the Wild Shape class feature of a 2nd-leveldruid. Both creatures must be transformed into the same type of beast.

The target(s) decide whether their equipment falls to the ground in their space, merges with their form, or is worn by it. Creatures affected by shapechanger’s gift can resume their natural form as an action and can resume their beast form as an action.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, for each slot level above 5th you can select one of the following enhancements:

Chinampa.name: Chinampa
Chinampa.description:
You create a one-foot-thick parcel of solid, dry land that springs into existence atop up to 1,600 square feet of water (an area 40 feet square, or 64 five-foot squares, or 16 10-foot squares). Each square must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another square. The parcel of land you create consists of bare earth devoid of any vegetation or life. The chinampa cannotcoverany existing landmass at or above the water’s surface, though you can incorporate any existing landmasses into the parcel you create. If a creature is partially submerged beneath the water when the land appears, it must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw to emerge atop the dry land if it so chooses. On a failedDexteritysaving throw, the creature is pushed into the water beneath the dry land. The creature can voluntarily sink beneath the water’s surface without attempting aDexteritysaving throw.

The land has the stability to support the weight of any creatures atop it, though structures made from stone or other heavy materials cause the ground directly beneath it to sink underneath the water’s surface until it settles on the bottom. The land is an object that can be damaged and thus destroyed. Each square has AC 12 and 20hit pointsper inch of thickness. Reducing a square to0 hit pointsdestroys it and causes the soil to break apart and sink to the bottom. If you maintain your concentration on this spell for the whole duration, the land becomes permanent and cannot be dispelled.

The land retains its stability subject to the previously mentioned limitations. It is still subject to natural forces such as erosion or flooding that may erode or inundate it. Otherwise, the land disappears when the spell ends.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Unstoppable Moon.name: Unstoppable Moon
Unstoppable Moon.components: V, S, M (stone carving of a moon and a pat of butter)
Unstoppable Moon.description:
You create a 15-foot-diameter sphere of moonrock that slams down in an unoccupied space you can see within range and lasts for the duration. Each creature within 10 feet of that space when you first create the sphere must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 bludgeoning damage and 5d10 radiant damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knockedprone.

As a bonus action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d10 bludgeoning damage and 2d10 radiant damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, the creature takes half the damage and isn’t knockedprone. The sphere stops moving only if you ram it into a Huge or larger creature, but a creature can be affected by the sphere only once on each of your turns, regardless of how many times you roll the sphere into it.

When you move the sphere, you can direct it to roll over barriers up to 10 feet tall andjumpit across pits up to 20 feet wide.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Hooded Eyes.name: Hooded Eyes
Hooded Eyes.description:
As you cast a little dust into the air, your enemies start to feel calm and sleepy.

Every visible target you designate within a 60-foot-radius of you must make aWisdomsaving throw. Creatures who fail their saves have their passivePerceptionreduced by half (rounded up) for the duration of the spell. They receive noWisdombonus to activePerceptionchecks, and they lose theirDexteritybonus to AC (if applicable) andinitiativeduring the first round of any combat that begins while the spell is in effect.

Any hostile action against an affected creature ends the effect. An ally can also use an action to shake an affected creature out of their stupor and end the effect.

Tails of the City © 2020, Silver Games, Llc; Authors: David Silver

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Guardian Hearth.name: Guardian Hearth
Guardian Hearth.description:
You exude an aura of protectiveness which manifests as the gentle glow of a well-kept fire. For the duration of the spell, you emit bright light in a 20 foot radius.

When a creature friendly to you takes damage within this light, you or one other creature friendly to you within the light may use areactionto move up to their speed towards the damaged creature. A creature who ends this movement within 5 feet of the damaged creature gainstemporary hit pointsequal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Blood Shadow.name: Blood Shadow
Blood Shadow.description:
You call to the blood of a gravely injured creature, gathering it into an undead creature which attacks your target. When you cast this spell you must target a creature with fewer than 50% its normal maximumhit points. If the target fails aConstitutionsaving throw, blood from their body rips free dealing 3d8 necrotic damage and coalesces into an undead with the same statistics as ashadow. This blood shadow attacks the targeted creature until one of them is slain or the duration ends.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Private Sanctum.name: Private Sanctum
Private Sanctum.components: V, S, M(a thin sheet of lead, a piece of opaque glass, a wad of cotton or cloth, and powdered chrysolite)
Private Sanctum.description:
You make an area within range magically secure. The area is a cube that can be as small as 5 feet to as large as 100 feet on each side. The spell lasts for the duration or until you use an action to dismiss it.

When you cast the spell, you decide what sort of security the spell provides, choosing any or all of the following properties:

Casting this spell on the same spot every day for a year makes this effect permanent.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can increase the size of the cube by 100 feet for each slot level beyond 4th. Thus you could protect a cube that can be up to 200 feet on one side by using a spell slot of 5th level.
Private Sanctum.material_component: a thin sheet of lead, a piece of opaque glass, a wad of cotton or cloth, and powdered chrysolite

Dragonclaw.name: Dragonclaw
Dragonclaw.components: V, S, M (dragon nail or scale)
Dragonclaw.description:
Your hands turn into massive dragon claws capable of rending and tearing through mail and leather. When you take theattackaction, you may make two Claw attacks. A clawattackis a melee weaponattackusing either yourDexterityorStrengthmodifier.

You are considered proficient in thisattack. On a hit, you deal 2d8 slashing damage plus yourCharismamodifier in extra damage of a type of your choosing (fire, cold, poison, acid, or lightning).

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell with a 4th-level spell slot or higher, you may add an additional damage type and additional damage equal to yourCharismamodifier for each level above 3rd.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Seeking Hellfire.name: Seeking Hellfire
Seeking Hellfire.description:
Choose a creature that you have seen at least once; the creature must have been visible and within 30 feet at the time, but you do not have to see the creature when you cast the spell. If there is an unobstructed path to the creature and it is within range, you throw an ember that travels to the target in the most direct path, which can pass through gaps up to 1 inch wide but not through the spaces of creatures. The ember moves at a speed of 120 ft and cannot be attacked. Upon reaching the target, the ember creates an explosion centered upon the target. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw. It takes 4d6 fire damage and 4d6 necrotic damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. Other creatures within 20 feet of the center of the target’s space must also make aDexteritysaving throw. Each creature takes 4d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the fire damage to all targets increases by 1d6 per slot level above 5th. If you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can choose either for the spell to not consume the material component or to increase the range to 5 miles per slot level above 6th. If you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the spell requires no material component, but if you do provide the component, creatures other than the target caught in the blast also take 4d6 necrotic damage.

Sandy Petersen’s Planet Apocalypse, © 2021, Petersen Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Boneblade Chance.name: Boneblade Chance
Boneblade Chance.components: V S F (bone at least six-inches in length)
Boneblade Chance.description:
ComponentsV S F (a bone at least six-inches in length)

The caster changes a bone into a blade of the caster’s choosing. The boneblade may take the form of a finesse sword weapon that deals 1d6 damage or a standard sword that deals 1d10 damage. This blade deals an extra +1d6 points of damage to living targets and an additional +1d6 points of damage to good-aligned targets.

This spell confers no proficiency with the blade, but the caster doesn’t need to be the one wielding the blade for it to be effective.

At Higher Levels. When casting this spell with a 4th level spell slot the weapon is a +1 magic weapon. With a 6th level spell slot, it becomes a +2 weapon and with a 8th level spell slot, it becomes a +3 magic weapon.

Breath of Life: The Lathspell (5e), © 2023, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.
