Raise Dead.name: Raise Dead
Raise Dead.components: V, S, M(a diamond worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
Raise Dead.description:
You return a dead creature you touch to life, provided that it has been dead no longer than 10 days. If the creature’s soul is both willing and at liberty to rejoin the body, the creature returns to life with 1 hit point.

This spell also neutralizes any poisons and cures nonmagical diseases that affected the creature at the time it died. This spell doesn’t, however, remove magical diseases, curses, or similar effects; if these aren’t first removed prior to casting the spell, they take effect when the creature returns to life. The spell can’t return an undead creature to life.

This spell closes all mortal wounds, but it doesn’t restore missing body parts. If the creature is lacking body parts or organs integral for its survival-its head, for instance-the spell automatically fails.

Coming back from the dead is an ordeal. The target takes a −4 penalty to all attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks. Every time the target finishes along rest, the penalty is reduced by 1 until it disappears.

Raise deadis another spell with roots in the earliest days of RPGs. The variants here are twisted, limited, or expanded in several ways. They all return a creature to life but in unexpected ways: as ghosts, for a short period, without memories or skills, or under a particular compulsion.

Two aspects ofraise deadare easy to change: the raised creature’s appearance and the traumatic effect of returning to life. TheRaise Dead Random Effects tableoffers a dozen options for reskinningraise deadin random ways.

When the spell is cast, roll a d12 or choose the option that best suits the situation or the caster. This change need not be a one-time thing; it can be emblematic of that caster, as recognizably personal as a signature, a catchphrase, or a coat of arms.

You return a dead creature you touch to a ghostly and incorporeal form, provided it has been dead no longer than 10 days. The creature can see and hear, and it can speak in a hollow, sepulchral tone if it chooses to. Whether it’s willing to speak to you depends on its whim and its prior relationship with you, if any.

The affected creature is not undead; it is alive but incorporeal, with 1 hit point. It can’t interact with the physical world,attackor cause damage, or cast spells. It is immune to nonmagical damage. It can move through creatures and objects as if they weredifficult terrain, but it takes 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

It regainshit pointsnormally through resting or spending hit dice but never recovershit pointsvia magic spells, items, or potions.

This spell also neutralizes any poison and cures nonmagical diseases that affected the creature at the time it died. This spell doesn’t remove magical diseases, curses, or similar effects; if these aren’t removed prior to casting the spell, they take effect when the creature returns to life.

The spell also closes mortal wounds, but it doesn’t restore missing body parts. If the creature is lacking body parts or organs integral for its survival-its head, for instance-the spell automatically fails.

Coming back from the dead is an ordeal. The target has a -4 penalty to saving throws and ability checks. Every time the target finishes along rest, the penalty is reduced by 1 until it disappears.

A creature affected byraise ghostis restored to normal, physical life byraise deador comparable magic.Raise ghosthas no effect if cast on an undead creature.

This spell is identical toraise deadin every way except duration; the creature is restored to life for only 24 hours.

The spell can be recast on the same creature, but on the second and subsequent castings, the caster must roll a d20. If the roll equals or is less than the number of prior castings on the same creature, the spell fails and cannot affect that creature again. Each new casting resets the clock to 24 hours; it doesn’t stack another 24 hours onto a previous casting.

This spell is identical toraise ghostin every way, except the ghostly figure can manipulate, hold, or carry objects weighing up to 5 pounds. Note that while 5 pounds of force is enough to pick up many melee weapons, it’s not sufficient to wield one in combat, or to draw a bow.

This spell is identical toraise dead, except it simultaneously raises two creatures with opposite alignments. For example, if you raise a Lawful Goodpaladin, then somewhere nearby, a Chaotic Evil warrior of similar power also returns to life. The second corpse must be within 100 miles. The two raised creatures have a vague sense of the direction and distance to their nemesis. They aren’t compelled to battle one another or even to seek each other out. Their lives are, however, inextricably bound together in such a way that if either of them dies, the other also drops dead instantly.

Evil NPCs brought back with raise nemesis typically see it as an opportunity to create every sort of trouble imaginable.

If the spell is cast on a creature of true Neutral alignment, only that creature is restored to life.

This spell is identical toraise dead, but it works only on a creature that died of old age. The spell grants the raised elder one additional year of life. The raised creature has entirely white hair, its eyes are weak, and it loses 2 points each fromStrengthandConstitution; no magic less potent than awishcan restore these lost points. In all other respects, the creature can live out its life normally until the added year elapses.

Raise elder has no effect if it’s cast on the same creature a second time.

This spell is identical toraise dead, except it empowers you to impose ageason the creature you raise. The targeted soul can opt to decline thegeas, in which case it isn’t restored to life. If the creature accepts yourgeas, it must complete the task within 30 days. If it accepts but fails to meet the conditions of thegeas, it dies on the dawn of the 31st day and its spirit again departs the mortal world. If it accomplishes the task, it’s free to live out the remainder of its restored life as it chooses.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th or 8th level, the creature has a year to fulfill itsgeas, allowing for much more complex demands. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 9th level, thegeaslasts until it’s fulfilled, no matter how long that takes, or until it’s ended byremove curse,greater restoration, orwish.

Your touch inflicts disease. Make a melee spellattackagainst a humanoid or giant within your reach. On a hit, the target ispoisoned. At the end of each of thepoisonedtarget’s turns, the target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. If the target succeeds on three of these saves, it is no longerpoisoned, and the spell ends. Death Dirge.description:
This spell creates a terrifying song of death that emanates from a point you choose within range. It is loud, ominous noise that obstructs hearing. Creatures within the spell’s 20-foot-radius area are effectivelydeafeneduntil the spell ends or they leave the area.

When a creature enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 8d8 psychic damage and has disadvantage on ability checks andattackrolls until it leaves the area or the spell ends. If the save is successful, the creature takes half as much damage and does not gain disadvantage from this spell.

Creatures are affected even if they cover their ears or are deaf. This spell dispelssilenceand is not attenuated in any way bysilencebeing cast in its area.

You can move the source of the music up to 10 feet in any direction at the start ofyour turn(no action from you).

Riddle.name: Riddle
Riddle.description:
When you cast this spell, you must tell a riddle.

The riddle must be unique, you must know the answer, and no living person other than yourself can have ever solved it. You then tell a target creature within range that shares a language with you. That creature must answer the riddle. If they fail to answer correctly, you gain their truename. If the creature guesses it correctly, they gain knowledge of your truename. If the creature does not wish to relinquish its truename, they can bargain for something else, such as their firstborn, a mountain of treasure, or the truename or someone else. If they fail to deliver on this promise within a fortnight (14 days), they are cursed as per thebestow cursespell, and it cannot be broken short of fulfilling the terms of the bargain, guessing the riddle correctly before the fortnight is over, or awishspell.

Classes: Cleric, Warlock,Wizard

You invoke a malevolent curse of desolation to affect creatures within a 50-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you can see within range. Each creature in that area must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 20d8 necrotic damage and is cursed for 24 hours. While cursed in this way, a creature cannot regainhit points, and its hit points maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken.

As a Bonus Action, you can move the Sleep Smoke up to 30 feet and it moves with a sighing susurrus. If it enters a creature’s space, it stops moving and the creature must save as if it had entered the cloud.

You transform a handful of materials into a Huge armored vehicle. The vehicle can take whatever form you want, but it has AC 18 and 100hit points. If it is reduced to0 hit points, it is destroyed. If it is a ground vehicle, it has a speed of 90 feet. If it is an airborne vehicle, it has a flying speed of 45 feet. If it is a waterborne vehicle, it has a speed of 2 miles per hour.

The vehicle can hold up to four Medium creatures within it. A creature inside it has three-quarterscoverfrom attacks outside the vehicle, which contains arrow slits, portholes, and other small openings.

A creature piloting the armored vehicle can take the Careen action. To do so, the vehicle must move at least 10 feet in a straight line and enter or pass through the space of at least one Large or smaller creature. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks. Each creature in the armored vehicle’s path must make aDexteritysaving throw against your spell save DC.

On a failed save, the creature takes 5d8 bludgeoning damage and is forcedprone. On a successful save, the creature can choose to be pushed 5 feet away from the space through which the vehicle passed. A creature that chooses not to be pushed suffers the consequences of a failed saving throw. Until the spell ends, when you take damage, you can use yourreactionto prevent the damage to yourself, moving it into the shadow. When the shadow has absorbed 30 damage, it ruptures. At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, your shadow can absorb 10 more damage for each slot level above 3rd. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the necrotic damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 3rd.

You convert the magical energy in a scroll to a blade of force. The blade is similar insizeand shape to a scimitar, and it lasts for the duration. If you let go of the blade, it disappears, but you can evoke the blade again as a bonus action. You can use your action to make a melee spellattackwith the scroll blade. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 force damage. This scroll is consumed in the casting.

Nostalgia.name: Nostalgia
Nostalgia.description:
You fill the target’s head with visions of good events and happy memories that leave them stuck in a bittersweet reverie. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or bestunnedfor the duration of the spell. Each round at the end of its turn, a creature affected by this spell may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect.

Claws of the Bear.name: Claws of the Bear
Claws of the Bear.description:
ComponentsS M (an animal’s claw)

You gain the ability to manifest and dismiss claws as a bonus action. These claws deal 1d6 slashing damage and function as melee weapon attacks. If you have both hands free as part of anAttackaction you can make two claw attacks.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell with a 2nd level or higher spell slot, the damage dealt by the claws are considered magic for the purposes of resistances or immunities.

Celebration.name: Celebration
Celebration.description:
You create a 30-foot-radius area around a point that you choose within range. An intelligent creature that enters the area or starts its turn there must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature starts to engage in celebratory revelry: drinking, singing, laughing, and dancing. Affected creatures are reluctant to leave the area until the spell ends, preferring to continue the festivities. They forsake appointments, cease caring about their woes, and generally behave in a cordial (if not hedonistic) manner. This preoccupation with merrymaking occurs regardless of an affected creature’s agenda or alignment. Assassins procrastinate, servants join in the celebration rather than working, and guards abandon their posts.

The effect ends on a creature when it is attacked, takes damage, or is forced to leave the area. A creature that makes a successful saving throw can enter or leave the area without danger of being enchanted. A creature that fails the saving throw and is forcibly removed from the area must repeat the saving throw if it returns to the area.

Ritual Focus. If you expend your ritual focus, an unaffected intelligent creature must make a new saving throw every time it starts its turn in the area, even if it has previously succeeded on a save against the spell.

Power Word Fist.name: Power Word Fist
Power Word Fist.description:
You pull forward all the martial powers of the greatest brawlers through time, creating 12 ethereal fists. Each fist attacks a creature you can see within range, targeting a single creature or spreading to multiple targets. Make a ranged spellattackfor each fist. On a hit, it deals 1d12 + your spellcasting modifier force damage. If a fist rolls a 20, it deals 3d12 + your spellcasting modifier force damage. If a fist rolls a 1, it simply vanishes without dealing damage.

Phantasmal Success.name: Phantasmal Success
Phantasmal Success.description:
You create a phantasm that taps into the thoughts and intentions of the target. When the target attempts an action that requires a die roll to determine success, they must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, the action fails but they see a phantasmal image of their success. The target then acts as though they succeeded until the beginning of their next turn, after which they realize they were fooled.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot, on a failure the target has disadvantage on all d20 rolls for 1d4 rounds. For every spell slot above 5th, the duration of the disadvantage increases by 1 round.

Rolling Thunder.name: Rolling Thunder
Rolling Thunder.description:
A tremendous bell note explodes from your outstretched hand and rolls forward in a line 30-foot long and 5-foot wide. Each creature in the line must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or be deafened for 1 minute. A creature made of inorganic material, such as stone, crystal, or metal, has disadvantage on saving throws against this spell.

While a creature is deafened in this way, it is wreathed in thundering energy. It takes 2d8 thunder damage at the start of its turn, and its speed is halved. A deafened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turn, ending the effect on itself on a success.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increase by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

Handkerchief Tent.name: Handkerchief Tent
Handkerchief Tent.description:
This spell causes up to three handkerchiefs into tents. Up to two of the tents contains up to five beds or, if there are non-humanoid creatures among the caster’s party, appropriate bedding for them so long as they are Medium or smaller-sized. The furnishings include enough camp chairs equal to the number of creatures in the tent and a single table large enough to seat them. If there are at least two handkerchiefs, one of them is a dining tent. It contains a table and chairs large enough to seat all members of the caster’s party and dishes in the dining tent, with plenty of those things necessary to use in cooking. The tent contains a kettle that produces a fine stew, smoking hot, with many kinds of vegetables and dumplings and a rich, delicious gravy. There are several other dishes on the table, all carefully covered, revealing bread and butter, cakes, cheese, pickles and fruits—including some of the luscious strawberries of Oz. The food consists of 45 pounds of food, enough to sustain up to 10 humanoids for 24 hours. The food and furniture disappears after 8 hours and the handkerchiefs shrink back down to their originalsize, ejecting any residents and equipment if need be.

Azalea Skin.name: Azalea Skin
Azalea Skin.description:
Dozens of azaleas blossom on your skin. Until this spell ends, if a creature hits you with anattackwhile within 5 feet of you, it takes 1d6 poison damage. If a creature within 5 feet of you scores a critical hit against you, the azaleas release a burst of poisonous pollen. Each creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or take 2d6 poison damage and bepoisoneduntil the end of its next turn. The spell then ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 1st.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Creation.name: Creation
Creation.components: V, S, M(a tiny piece of matter of the same type of the item you plan to create)
Creation.description:
You pull wisps of shadow material from the Plane of Shadow to create a nonliving object of vegetable matter within range: soft goods, rope, wood, or something similar. You can also use this spell to create mineral objects such as stone, crystal, or metal. The object created must be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and the object must be of a form and material that you have seen before.

The duration depends on the object’s material. If the object is composed of multiple materials, use the shortest duration.

Using any material created by this spell as another spell’s material component causes that spell to fail.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the cube increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 5th.

Waves of Blood.name: Waves of Blood
Waves of Blood.components: V, S, M (drop of the caster’s blood)
Waves of Blood.description:
You cause torrents of roiling blood to push your opponents away from you. Creatures in the area must attempt either aStrengthsaving throw orDexteritysaving throw (their choice). If the save is failed, they are pushed 10 feet away from you, or 20 feet away from you if they are Small or smaller. Living creatures in the area also must make aConstitutionsaving throw or becomepoisonedfor 1d6 rounds as they are stricken with nausea by the sanguine flood. They can attempt a new saving throw each round at the beginning of their turn to end thepoisonedcondition.

The area covered in blood remains dangerously slick for 1 round. The area is treated asdifficult terrain, and creatures moving through it must succeed on a DC 10Dexterity(Acrobatics) check or fallprone. A creaturepronein the area must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw each round at the beginning of its turn or becomepoisonedfor 1 round.

The Dragon’s Hoard #24 © 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Alex Riggs, Mike Myler, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young.

Kneeling Cur.name: Kneeling Cur
Kneeling Cur.components: V, S, M (four grains of rice)
Kneeling Cur.description:
You exploit the cowardice of the soul, forcing a living creature to cower and grovel before you. Pick one creature you can see within range. It must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature fallsprone. As long as the creature can see you, it cannot stand. A creature that averts its eyes gains theblindedandfrightenedconditions but can stand up and move until it is able to see you again, at which point it fallsproneand is no longerblindedorfrightened. At the end of each of its turns and each time it takes damage, the creature can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. The creature has advantage on the saving throw if it’s triggered by damage. On a success, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd-level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Ephemeral Dominion.components: V, S, M (legendary artifact of rulership once belonged to the greatest ruler of the multiverse)
Ephemeral Dominion.description:
Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You assert your dominance over the ephemeral planes, reshaping reality to your will and establishing your rule over a vast area. All creatures within a 100-mile radius from the point in which spell is cast are affected by a powerfulgeasas long as the spell lasts, compelling them to follow your commands for the next 100 years without any chance to resist (no action required by you). Any creature entering the spell’s area is instantly affected by the spell, while any creature leaving it is immediately breaks free from any effect. Deities or beings of similar power are unaffected by this spell.

Drizzle.description:
You conjure up a very light rain, enough to dampen the ground in a 20-foot square but not enough to drink or to put out a fire of anysizelarger than a candle or match. If sustained for 1 minute, the ground is wet to the touch, and if sustained for 10 minutes, the affected area is slightly muddy or slippery, though not enough to impede movement. In freezing weather, this may generate a coating of thin ice.

Starry Brilliance.description:
You momentarily glow with the blinding brilliance of a star. All other creatures within 10 feet of you that fail aConstitutionsaving throw take 3d6 radiant damage and areblindeduntil the end of your next turn. Creatures that succeed on the saving throw take half damage and are notblinded.

Tomb Curse.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a piece of funerary treasure worth 5,000+ GP)

DurationVaries (by version of the spell)

You create a lingering curse upon a tomb, barrow, graveyard, or similar enclosed burial site, placing the funerary treasure within the tomb at the completion of casting. If there are no physical remains within 10 feet of the focus object at the time of casting, the spell fails. The effect of the tomb curse passes through solid barriers and even extradimensional spaces within the tomb and extends into the Ethereal Plane.

Any creature entering the area of the tomb curse must make a saving throw against eitherBestow CurseorContagion, as specified by the caster. A creature that successfully saves is immune to the Tomb Curse for 24 hours but must save again if it enters the area again after that time.

Removing the object from the area after the spell is cast does not alter the tomb curse. However, any creature touching or carrying the object for more than 1 round is exposed to the tomb curse. The effects of the Tomb Curse cannot be dispelled but can be removed with Remove Curse. Ending the Tomb Curse spell itself, however, requires a successful Remove Curse cast directly on the focus object.

If the object is missing or unavailable, the Tomb Curse can be ended only by powerful magic such asWish.

Night Terrors.name: Night Terrors
Night Terrors.description:
Classes:bard,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

The target of this spell gains no benefit from normal or magicalsleep, writhing in a series of nightmares that torture its psyche and diminish its ability to perform strenuous tasks. A target that fails aWisdomsaving throw doesn’thealability or hit point damage naturally and can’t prepare spells or regain spell slots. After one night of poorsleep, the target gains anexhaustionlevel. A creature affected by this spell doesn’t recover fromexhaustioninflicted by this spell after resting, nor do spells such aslesser restorationorgreater restorationprovide any respite.

The images from previous nightmares continue to haunt the target’s mind while awake. If the target has rested at least once while affected by night terrors it then becomes subjected to thefrightenedcondition with the focus of itsfearbeing all sentient creatures it meets except close friends or relatives (like the party).

The affected creature can attempt a new saving throw once per day to end night terrors, but multiple attempts to rest in a given day do not afford the target multiple saves. A creature that successfully saves against night terrors ends the spell and rests normally that night but gains the benefits of only that night’s rest, not any benefits missed on previous nights.

If your campaign uses the Sanity ability score, use this saving throw instead ofWisdom.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration of the spell increases by 1 day.

Emergence.name: Emergence
Emergence.description:
You touch the forehead of astunnedorunconsciouscreature, removing both conditions. If an ongoing spell causes this condition that affects the target, make anIntelligencecheck vs. DC 10 + the spell’s level. On a successful check, the stun orunconsciouseffect ends.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

Harrying Hounds.name: Harrying Hounds
Harrying Hounds.components: V, S, M(tuft of fur from a hunting dog)
Harrying Hounds.description:
When you cast this spell, choose a direction (north, south, northeast, or the like). Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw when you cast this spell or be affected by it. When an affected creature travels, it travels at a fast pace in the opposite direction of the direction you chose as it believes a pack of dogs or wolves follows it from the chosen direction. When an affected creature isn’t traveling, it isfrightenedof your chosen direction.

The affected creature occasionally hears howls or sees glowing eyes in the darkness at the edge of its vision in that direction. An affected creature will not stop at a destination, instead pacing half-circles around the destination until the effect ends, terrified the pack will overcome it if it stops moving. An affected creature can make aWisdomsaving throw at the end of each 4-hour period, ending the effect on itself on a success.

An affected creature moves along the safest available route unless it has nowhere to move, such as if it arrives at the edge of a cliff. When an affected creature can’t safely move in the opposite direction of your chosen direction, it cowers in place, defending itself from hostile creatures but otherwise taking noactions. In such circumstances, the affected creature can repeat the saving throw every minute, ending the effect on itself on a success. The spell’s effect is suspended when an affected creature is engaged in combat, allowing it to move as necessary to face hostile creatures.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the duration increases by 4 hours for each slot level above 5th. If an affected creature travels for more than 8 hours, it risksexhaustionas if on a forced march.

Evaporate Fluid.name: Evaporate Fluid
Evaporate Fluid.components: V, S, M(a pinch of salt)
Evaporate Fluid.description:
You vaporize three 10-foot cubes of uncontained liquid within range. The liquid evaporates into the atmosphere, expanding rapidly. This affects water, acid, oil, blood, liquid metals, poisons, potions, and liquid rock – any liquid can be vaporized. When changed out of liquid form, the substance is rendered inert and poses no threat or danger of any kind; toxic and thermal properties are normalized and neutralized. If a portion of a larger body of liquid is vaporized, liquid rushes in to fill the remaining space.

At higher levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot higher than fourth, you can evaporate an additional 10-foot cube of liquid for each level above fourth.

Terror Storm.name: Terror Storm
Terror Storm.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 minute

You create an evil-looking, 360-foot-radius, black storm cloud in the air. Each creature under the cloud must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or befrightenedof the cloud for 1d4 x 10 minutes.

Each round you continue to concentrate, the spell generates additional effects as noted below. Each effect occurs onyour turn.

Arctic Haze.name: Arctic Haze
Arctic Haze.description:
You create a 20-foot-high, 30-foot-radius Cylinder of thick white fog. Vision through the Arctic Haze is Lightly Obscured within 5 feet and Heavily Obscured beyond 5 feet. The fog is also bitterly chilly, causing creatures entering or beginning their turn within it to take 1d4 Cold damage. In addition, tiny shards of ice infuse the Arctic Haze, causing any creature moving through it to take 1 Slashing damage for every 5 feet they move.

Like aFog Cloud, the Arctic Haze can be dispersed in 1 round by a strong wind (likeGust of Wind). This blasts the icy shards within it against creatures within the cloud, dealing 1d4 Cold damage and 1d4 Slashing damage as the cloud is blown away.

Divine Conduit.name: Divine Conduit
Divine Conduit.description:
You touch a nonmagical weapon or a weapon with a +1 bonus. If the weapon is actively being wielded by a creature, that creature must be willing to allow you to cast this spell upon their weapon. Until the spell ends, that weapon becomes amagic weaponwith a +2 bonus toattackrolls anddamage rolls. Additionally, it deals 2d6 damage of one of the following types that you choose: Cold, Fire, Lightning, Radiant, or Thunder. Any other magical traits the target weapon possesses are suppressed until the end of the spell’s duration. Divine Conduit ends if the caster dismisses it as a BonusAction, or ifDispel Magicis cast using a spell slot of 4th level or higher spell upon the weapon.

Divine Conduit has no effect upon artifacts, and it cannot be used to suppress the existing magical abilities of a weapon that is currently wielded by a hostile creature.

Expeditious Retreat.name: Expeditious Retreat
Expeditious Retreat.description:
This spell allows you to move at an incredible pace. When you cast this spell, and then as abonus actionon each of your turns until the spell ends, you can take the Dash action.

The following is content created by a publisher other than Wizards of the Coast.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, until the spell ends your speed increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 1st.

Energy Vulnerability.name: Energy Vulnerability
Energy Vulnerability.description:
You weaken your enemies against other forms of harm.

You can choose a single creature within range or two adjacent creatures within range. They must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or gain damagevulnerabilityto one type of energy you choose. If the target normally hasresistanceto that type of energy, they instead lose thatresistancefor the duration of the spell. A creature immune to that type of energy is unaffected. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw nonetheless takes a -1 penalty on saving throws against effects using your chosen energy type as long as you concentrate.

Vine Trestle.name: Vine Trestle
Vine Trestle.components: V, S, M (1-inch piece of green vine that is consumed in the casting)
Vine Trestle.description:
You cause a vine to sprout from the ground and crawl across a surface or rise into the air in a direction chosen by you. The vine must sprout from a solid surface (such as the ground or a wall), and it is strong enough to support 600 pounds of weight along its entire length, which can be a number of feet up to 5 × your spellcasting level. The vine collapses immediately if that 600-pound limit is exceeded. A vine that collapses from weight or damage instantly disintegrates.

The vine has many small shoots, so it can be climbed with a successful DC 5Strength(Athletics) check. It has AC 8,hit pointsequal to 5 × your spellcasting level, and a damage threshold of 5.

Ritual Focus. If you expend your ritual focus, the vine is permanent until destroyed or dispelled.

Ghostly Glow.name: Ghostly Glow
Ghostly Glow.description:
This spell functions likedancing lights, except as noted. The radiance of the ghostly glow is always eerie and unwholesome, and if the caster concentrates the glow into a single Medium or smaller point of light (rather than multiple smaller lights) it causes creatures nearby to feel unsettled and nervous. Creatures coming within or beginning their turn within 30 feet of the ghostly glow become afraid, taking disadvantage on saving throws that would make themfrightenedand onWisdom(Perception) ability checks. Creatures succeeding on their save are immune to this effect; those that fail their save are affected as long as they remain within 30 feet of the ghostly glow, or if they return to the area after leaving it. You are immune to the effect of your own ghostly glow. You can end the spell early as a bonus action, causing it to burst in a horrifying phantasmagoria of tormented ectoplasmic faces, causing creatures within 30 feet of the ghostly glow to becomefrightenedof you for 1 round. A successfulWisdomsaving throw negates this condition.

Night’s Ember.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a piece of coal)

DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You hold up the coal which alights in a soft orangelight.

Thislightdoes not burn your hand, however any creature in a 60-foot radius that hails from theshadowplane or currently in an area of dimlightordarknessis covered is a nimbus of orange flame, glowing like a like the spellFaerie Fire. Additionally at the beginning of their turn, an affected creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw or take 1 fire damage. A successful saving throw negates damage but not theFaerie Fireeffect.

Power Word Stun.name: Power Word Stun
Power Word Stun.description:
You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving it dumbfounded. If the target has 150 hit points or fewer, it isstunned. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

Thestunnedtarget must make aConstitutionsaving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this stunning effect ends.

Speak with Dead.name: Speak with Dead
Speak with Dead.description:
You grant the semblance of life and intelligence to a corpse of your choice within range, allowing it to answer the questions you pose. The corpse must still have a mouth and can’t be undead. The spell fails if the corpse was the target of this spell within the last 10 days.

Until the spell ends, you can ask the corpse up to five questions. The corpse knows only what it knew in life, including the languages it knew. Answers are usually brief, cryptic, or repetitive, and the corpse is under no compulsion to offer a truthful answer if you are hostile to it or it recognizes you as an enemy. This spell doesn’t return the creature’s soul to its body, only its animating spirit. Thus, the corpse can’t learn new information, doesn’t comprehend anything that has happened since it died, and can’t speculate about future events.

Bane of Excellence.name: Bane of Excellence
Bane of Excellence.description:
A creature of your choice within range must make aCharismasaving throw. On a failed save, the next ability check,attackroll, or saving throw the target makes, within the duration, that results in a roll of 20 on a d20, fails to have any effect. The number of times this cantrip can turn a natural 20 into a failure increases by one when you reach 5th level (two natural 20s), 11th level (three natural 20s), and 17th level (four natural 20s).

Book of Ebon Tides © 2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Wolfgang Baur, Celeste Conowitch.

Biting Wind.components: V, S, M (vial of air and water collected from a storm)
Biting Wind.description:
You fill a 20-foot-radius sphere with cold winds and light snow centered on a point within range. The sphere spreads around corners, and its area is lightly obscured. Conditions within the area have several effects.

Baleful Transposition.name: Baleful Transposition
Baleful Transposition.description:
Classes:bard, eldritch knight,sorcerer,wizard

You cause two Large or smaller creatures (one of which can be you) within range to switch places, teleporting into each other’s space. If one creature is larger than the other, there must be enough unoccupied space for the larger creature to appear or the spell fails. You can choose any part of the larger creature’s space for the smaller creature to appear. There must be a solid surface sufficient to bear each creature’s weight between them, including the ground or even a rope. An unwilling creature can resist being teleported with aWisdomsaving throw; if either creature saves, the spell fails. Only the target creatures are teleported; creatures riding or carried by a target of the spell do not accompany them (except for familiars).

The Dragon’s Hoard#52 © 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Darrin Drader, Mike Welham, Robert J. Grady, Adam Gonzalez, and Matt Kimmel.

Eruption of the Lost Age.name: Eruption of the Lost Age
Eruption of the Lost Age.description:
You cause the ground at a point you choose within range to erupt in a geyser of ancient, magical energy. Each creature in a 20-foot radius, 40-foot high cylinder must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 8d6 force damage and 4d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The area becomesdifficult terrainfor 1 minute, littered with shards of ancient magic.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the force damage or the radiant damage (your choice) increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 6th.

Imperfect Portrait.components: V, S, M (piece of blank parchment, which the spell consumes)
Imperfect Portrait.description:
You instantly create a visual representation of everything you see. Everything you can see at the moment you cast this spell is instantly painted onto a piece of parchment, creating an almost life-like facsimile for later examination. The approximate contents are up to the Gm’s discretion. Unnoticed aspects of the painting are not recreated in an exact way if you did not have a full line of sight, your view was blocked by an object, or you failed to notice that element of the environment.

Galder’s Gazetteer Author(s) Matt Click, Gabe Hicks, Jess Ross

Conflicting Fog.name: Conflicting Fog
Conflicting Fog.description:
You create a hazy cloud of malevolent spirits in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within range.

The sphere spreads around corners, and its area is lightly obscured. Creatures within the cloud see other creatures within it as jeering, twisted forms. All creatures in the cloud are considered enemies to one another. Whenever a creature in the cloud chooses another creature as a target, it must choose the target at random from among the creatures it can see within the cloud. A creature within the cloud must make anattackof opportunity whenever one is provoked by another creature’s movement, if it is able.

The cloud dissipates at the end of this spell or if a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.

Conjure Dream-Dwellers.name: Conjure Dream-Dwellers
Conjure Dream-Dwellers.components: V, S, M (sand and a silver key worth 500 gp)
Conjure Dream-Dwellers.description:
You summon one or more creatures from the Dreamlands, which appear in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. Choose one of the options below (see Chapter 9 for statistics):

The creature disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The Dreamlands creature is friendly to you and your companions for the duration unless it succeeds on a Charisma saving throw, in which case it acts as it wills.

Roll initiative for the creature, which has its own turns. If you control it, it obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (requiring no action from you), as long as they don’t violate its interests. If you don’t issue any commands to it, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.

If your concentration is broken, the summoned creature doesn’t disappear. Instead, you lose control of the creature, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it might attack. An uncontrolled summoned creature can’t be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using certain higher-level spell slots, you can choose one of the summoning options above and more creatures appear: twice as many with a 7th-level slot, or three times as many with a 9th-level slot. You can instead choose to summon a single more potent creature, so long as the spell slot is at least the indicated slot level: a Large Leng spider with a 5th-level slot, a gug with a 7th-level slot, a Huge Leng spider with an 8th-level slot, or a bhole hatchling with a 9th-level slot. If you summon a bhole hatchling, it automatically succeeds on its Charisma saving throw and may act as it wishes.

This spell functions asdominate person(commanded toattacka creature), but the target of the spell is also shrouded in a faceless disguise spell.

Doom of Deceleration.name: Doom of Deceleration
Doom of Deceleration.description:
You stab yourself in the leg while you cast this spell, dealing 1d4 damage to yourself. Each creature within range, including you, must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a successful save, the creature’s speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. On a failed save, the creature becomesrestrainedfor 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. On a success, the target is no longerrestrained.

Bind Soul.name: Bind Soul
Bind Soul.components: V, S, M (diamond dust worth at least 200 gp, which the spell consumes)
Bind Soul.description:
You touch a nonmagical item, thereby calling on the soul of a deceased creature with whom you are familiar, not so that they walk the earth once more, but so that you can fill the item with a part of the creature’s consciousness. If the soul is willing, it can choose a part of its consciousness to bind to the item. You can communicate with the soul telepathically provided that you are on the same plane of existence as the item and that you are attuned to it. The soul has blindsight out to a range of 60 feet. You cannot be surprised if the soul senses the dangers and informs you.

If you bind the soul to a weapon, you gain a +1 bonus toattackanddamage rollsmade with it.

If you bind the soul to an armor orshield, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing the armor or carrying the shield.

If you bind the soul to another type of item, you gain a +1 bonus to saving throws while you wear or carry it.

The soul shares a part of its consciousness with the item; however, it stays in the same plane of existence it was in before this spell was cast.

The soul can dismiss its bond with the item at will. However, 167 when it does, the soul cannot be affected by this spell again for 1 year.

Dark Fireball.components: V, S, M (ball of void goo)
Dark Fireball.description:
Classes: Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

A dark streak flashes from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range, and then blossoms with a low roar into an explosion of cold fire. Each creature in a 20 foot radius sphere, centered on that point, must make aDexteritysaving throw. A target takes 3d6 cold damage and 3d6 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The dark fire spreads around corners.

Spoil Food And Water.name: Spoil Food And Water
Spoil Food And Water.description:
You spoil 45 pounds of food, grain, or seeds and 30 gallons of water, ale, or other potable drinks on the ground or in containers within range, normally enough to sustain up to fifteen humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The food becomes moldy, rotten, vermin-infested, or liquefied. The water is filthy and foul-smelling, and any creature consuming either the food or the beverage is ill for the next 24 hours, moving at half speed and with disadvantage on all ability checks and saving throws.

At Higher Levels. If cast at 4th level, you spoil up to 150 pounds of food and 100 gallons of beverage. If cast at 5th level, you spoil up to 500 pounds of food and 300 gallons of beverage.

Moonstruck.name: Moonstruck
Moonstruck.components: V, S, M(a pinch of powdered moonstone)
Moonstruck.description:
You invoke the mystical power of the moon to drive the target into a mad, bestial frenzy.

If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw, it isincapacitatedfor 1 round, dropping held items as its nails and teeth elongate and sharpen and it takes on a crazed, bestial appearance. The target gains proficiency with its clawattack(dealing 1d4 slashing damage) and biteattack(dealing 1d6 piercing damage) and gains a +1 bonus onattackanddamage rollswith those weapons and can take the following action:

Multiattack. The moonstruck creature makes one biteattackand one clawattack. Each round on its turn after the first, the target rolls 1d4 and behaves as noted below:

After any round in which the target acts normally, it can attempt a newWisdomsaving throw at the end of its turn to end the spell. When the moonstruck spell ends, the creature’s body and proficiencies return to normal. However, it must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or gain 1 level ofexhaustion.

Direction and Distance.name: Direction and Distance
Direction and Distance.description:
The target gains the benefit of aFind the Pathspell, with you as the target destination.

Breath of Life: The Marshal (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Michael Messinger

Depth Charge.name: Depth Charge
Depth Charge.components: V, S, M (small metal canister or sphere)
Depth Charge.description:
You can hurl a canister of hyper-compressed water that explodes in water. Each creature within a 15-foot cube take 3d8 bludgeoning damage, or half as much on a successfulConstitutionsave. Creatures failing their save also are pushed 15 feet away from the center of the depth charge area. A depth charge deals double damage to the hulls of boats, ships, submersibles, and other water vehicles. A depth charge deals no damage to creatures or objects that are not in the water.

Rather than hurling a depth charge for immediate detonation, you may drop the depth charge into the water and allow it to sink at a rate of 30 feet per round, delaying its explosion by up to 3 rounds. A creature in the water can pick up the depth charge and move it, though there is a 25% chance each round it is handled that it detonates immediately.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd, and you can delay the detonation of a dropped charge by an extra round.

Dream Walk.name: Dream Walk
Dream Walk.components: S, V, M (500 gp in crushed sapphires)
Dream Walk.description:
You drift off into a sleeping state, projecting your mind into the dreams of another sleeper to terrorize their dreams. The target must make aWisdomsaving throw, taking 5d10 psychic damage on a failure, or half that on a success. If they succeed on their save, your body teleports to an open space adjunct to them; this causes them to wake up.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Frost Strike.name: Frost Strike
Frost Strike.description:
Target: Each creature in a 5-foot radius

You strike the ground with necrotic energy, releasing a burst of frost that chills all creatures within 5 feet of you. Each creature in that area other than you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 cold damage and has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and its speed is not reduced.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Circle of Serpents.name: Circle of Serpents
Circle of Serpents.description:
Snakes emerge from the ground, writhing around a creature you can see within range in a 5-foot radius circle. The snakes do not attack or otherwise harm the creature unless the creature steps outside the circle during the duration of the spell, at which point the snakes attack using yourreaction. The creature must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 5d6 poison damage, after which the spell ends. On a successful save, the target takes half damage.

Tongue Pick.name: Tongue Pick
Tongue Pick.description:
The tongue of a creature you touch changes into a long and slender—but still fleshy—skeletonkey. For the duration, the target can use its transformed tongue to pick locks and disarm traps as if its tongue was a set of thieves’ tools. The target is proficient in using its tongue in this way.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the target doubles its proficiency bonus when using its tongue to pick locks and disarm traps. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the target has advantage on its checks to pick locks and disarm traps with its tongue.

Unicorn Arrow.name: Unicorn Arrow
Unicorn Arrow.components: V, S, M (an ivory replicof a unicorn worth 25 gp)
Unicorn Arrow.description:
You conjure a shimmering spectral unicorn’s head and neck with a bright-gleaming horn and streaming mane into midair, streaking toward a creature you choose within range. If your ranged spell attack hits, the target takes 4d8 piercing damage and must make aStrengthsaving throw or be pushed backwards 5 feet, or by 10 feet if they fail their save by 5 or more.

If the target has anattackor ability that deals poison damage, it takes an additional 1d8 piercing damage and the potency of its poison is diminished for 1 round, reducing the save DC of its poison by 1 and reducing poison damage dealt by 5 (minimum 0).

The material component of this spell is not destroyed when the spell is cast and can be reused.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can create an additional unicorn arrow for each slot level above 3rd. A creature struck by more than one unicorn arrow needs to make only a singleStrengthsaving throw to avoid being pushed back, but it has disadvantage on the saving throw. If the target is a poison-using creature, the effects described above last for 1 round for each unicorn arrow that struck it.

Dust Devil.name: Dust Devil
Dust Devil.description:
You create a small whirlwind of dry, choking dust anywhere within range. When a living creature within 10 feet of the DustDeviltakes damage, as aReactionyou can leach the moisture from that creature. If that creature fails aConstitutionsaving throw, it gains 1 level ofExhaustionand its MaximumHit Pointsare reduced by an amount equal to the damage it takes. ThoseHit Pointscannot be restored until the creature removes itsExhaustion. A creature cannot You can move the DustDevilto a new location within range as a BonusAction.

Cloak of Grotesque Multitudes.name: Cloak of Grotesque Multitudes
Cloak of Grotesque Multitudes.description:
You bite back your revulsion and cover your body with a swarm of parasites that disgusts your opponents and confuses their strikes. Each time a creature targets you with amelee attackduring the spell’s duration, it must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failure, the target creature’s attack misses you and they instead take 1d6 piercing damage and become infested. On a success, the creature’s attack continues as normal.

This spell ends when your saving throw is failed three times or when you dismiss it as an action. While this spell is active, you have disadvantage on allCharisma-based skill checks butIntimidation.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the number of saving throw failures that can be experienced before the spell ends increases by 1 for each slot level above 2nd.

Tranquility.name: Tranquility
Tranquility.duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Arcane sigils begin to glow in
Tranquility.description:
Arcane sigils begin to glow in a calming pattern in the air within 60 feet of you. For the duration of the spell, if a creature within 120 feet of you makes a weaponattackor casts a spell which deals damage or requires a target to make a saving throw, that creature is teleported to a safe point that you choose 120 feet away from you and takes 1 level ofexhaustion.

Outmaneuver.name: Outmaneuver
Outmaneuver.description:
When a creature provokes an opportunityattackfrom an ally you can see within range, you can force the creature to make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, the creature’s movement is reduced to 0, and you can move up to your speed toward the creature without provoking opportunity attacks. This spell doesn’t interrupt your ally’s opportunityattack, which happens before the effects of this spell.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Soul Stones.name: Soul Stones
Soul Stones.description:
If a soul stone is destroyed by physical force, the magic is dispelled on the stone, or it enters anantimagic field, it crumbles to dust and the soul contained within is released, free to go to whatever revival or afterlife awaits. For the purposes ofdispel, it is treated as the original soul trap spell effect that captured the soul.

A spell stone, regardless of the material component used, changes to reflect the soul encased within. So if the spell were used on an evil necromancer, the stone may change into a black onyx pulsing with an inner red light while apaladinmay change the stone into a translucent quartz that glows with a steady bright light. Let your imagination run wild.

Contact Other Plane: World of the Old Scrolls I (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions; Author: Connor Bates

Antilife Shell.name: Antilife Shell
Antilife Shell.description:
A shimmering barrier extends out from you in a 10-foot radius and moves with you, remaining centered on you and hedging out creatures other than undead and constructs. The barrier lasts for the duration.

The barrier prevents an affected creature from passing or reaching through. An affected creature can cast spells or make attacks with ranged or reach weapons through the barrier.

If you move so that an affected creature is forced to pass through the barrier, the spell ends.

Flight of the Chonchón.name: Flight of the Chonchón
Flight of the Chonchón.description:
When you cast this spell, your head detaches from your body and turns into a chonchón for the duration. You retain your proficiency bonus,Intelligence,WisdomandCharismascores and can cast any spell you know that has only a verbal component. Your equipment transforms with you. You otherwise take on the traits of the chonchón. Your body remains behind, and you are aware of its condition at all times.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you increase the spells duration by 1 hour.

Latin American Monsters (5E)© 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Miguel Colon, Ismael Alvarez, Robert J. Grady, Jason Nelson.

Feast from the Dead.name: Feast from the Dead
Feast from the Dead.description:
You target the corpse of a Small or Medium creature within range that died within the last 24 hours. At the completion of the spell, 10 tiny, plump, white grubs crawl out of the corpse, which decomposes rapidly, reducing the corpse to dust. A creature may use an action to eat one of the grubs, and the creature doing so recovers 1d8hit points. After one hour, the grubs explode into little pools of goo and lose all magical properties.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Antiflame Aura.name: Antiflame Aura
Antiflame Aura.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You surround yourself with an aura of eerie blue mist that gives youresistanceto fire damage. In addition, minor fires (those that deal 10 points of damage or less) are snuffed out when they touch your antiflame aura, dealing no damage to you. You can touch and extinguish such a fire as a bonus action.

As an action, you can touch an existing magical fire, such as aflaming sphereorwall of fire, and attempt todispelit as if you had castdispel magic. If your attempt todispelfails, you take damage from the fire (reduced by the antiflame aura) and your antiflame aura remains in place. If your dispelling succeeds, the fire spell ends and so too does your antiflame aura. This has no effect on instantaneous or permanent magical flames.

As areaction, you can attempt todispelan instantaneous fire spell that would affect you (including area spells as well as targeted spells). This is also treated as adispel magicspell; however, you have disadvantage on your check todispel magic. If thedispelcheck succeeds, the fire spell is entirely negated, not affecting you or any other creature or object, and the antiflame aura ends. If thedispelcheck fails or if you attempt to counter a spell that does not deal fire damage, your antiflame aura persists.

While your antiflame aura requires concentration, you never need to makeConstitutionsaving throws to maintain concentration due to taking fire damage.

The Dragon’s Hoard #31© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, James-Levi Cooke.

Earthen Wall.name: Earthen Wall
Earthen Wall.components: V, S, M (small block of clay)
Earthen Wall.description:
Class(es): Druid, Sorcerer, Synthetist, Wizard

You cause the earth to rise up and form a wall on a solid surface within range. The wall is up to 10 feet long, 4 feet high, and 1 foot thick. It can providecoverdepending on thesizeof the attacking and attacked creatures. The earthen wall has AC 12 and 15hit points. If the wall is reduced to0 hit points, it crumbles away.

Prayer of Resolve.name: Prayer of Resolve
Prayer of Resolve.description:
You remind your allies of the perseverance that will be required of them. Choose up to six creatures you can see within range. Each target gainstemporary hit pointsequal to 1d10 + your spellcasting ability modifier for the duration. This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, thetemporary hit pointsincrease by 1d10 for each slot level above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Crown of Might.name: Crown of Might
Crown of Might.description:
Class(es): antipaladin,cleric, eldritch knight,paladin

You create a bronze crown embossed with a bull’s head and horns upon the brow of a willing ally. They gain a +1 bonus onmelee attackanddamage rollsand also gain a +1 bonus on allStrength-based D20 tests and saving throws.

As areactionor bonus action, the wearer of the crown of might can massively increase their physical prowess until the end of their next turn. During this time, they have Advantage onmelee attackrolls andStrength-based D20 tests and saving throws. They also add 1d6 extra damage (of the same type their weapon normally deals) on any hit with amelee attackand can lift 10 times their normal maximum weight. After this round, the spell ends and the crown of might disappears.

The Dragon’s Hoard #53© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Darrin Drader, Robert J. Grady, Eytan Bernstein, Katherine Schuttler.

Shroud of Stars.name: Shroud of Stars
Shroud of Stars.components: V, S, F (black silken and velvet mask studded with crushed black and star sapphires – 1000 gp)
Shroud of Stars.description:
Classes:sorcerer,warlock(Old Ones patron),wizard

You cloak yourself in a cosmic curtain, your silhouette filled with inky blackness and swirling celestial bodies. While your outline is unchanged, the details of your appearance cannot be seen while so glamered. Attacks against you have disadvantage. You gaindarkvisionout to 30 feet (or double yourdarkvisionif you already have it) and if outdoors at night youregenerate2hit pointsper round so long as you have 1 hit point.

The shroud of stars renders you immune to effects that generate light or darkness or impose thecharmedcondition as well as grantingresistanceto radiant and necrotic damage.

In addition, if a spell of these types includes you in its area of effect, as areactionyou can make a spellattackroll against a DC equal to 10 plus the caster level of the effect. With a successful check, the entire effect is harmlessly absorbed by the shroud of stars. However, this reduces the remaining duration of the shroud of stars by a number of rounds equal to the level of the absorbed spell. You can attempt to absorb existing effects of these types as an action, but the DC is increased to 15 plus the creator’s caster level. The shroud of stars also protects you from the harmful effects of all prismatic spells, and a successful spellattackroll against a DC of 15 plus the caster level of the prismatic spell’s creator enables you to pass through the prismatic effect as if you had cast the spell. This reduces the remaining duration of the shroud of stars by 10 rounds.

The Dragon’s Hoard #46© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Scott Young, Mike Welham, Miguel Colon, and Matt Kimmel

Ethereal Step.name: Ethereal Step
Ethereal Step.description:
You step into the Ethereal Plane, gaining the ability to phase through the material world. Until the end of your next turn you can move through creatures and objects as if they weredifficult terrain, and you gainresistanceto all damage except force and psychic. If you endyour turninside a creature or object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 2d10 force damage.

The Dragon’s Hoard #51© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Matt Kimmel, Michael Mifsud, and Darrin Drader.

Radiant Rosette.name: Radiant Rosette
Radiant Rosette.description:
A rosette of magic resembling a dandelion of energy appears in your hand. The magical flower remains there for the duration. When you cast this spell, you blow gently on the rosette, sending a stream of glowing seeds at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 radiant damage. Until the spell ends, you can blow on the rosette and make the attack again on each of your turns as an action.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Lizard Scales.name: Lizard Scales
Lizard Scales.description:
Your skin grows a layer of thick, jagged scales that causes melee and ranged weapon attacks against you to have disadvantage. In addition, the spiny protrusions on each scale deal 1d4 piercing damage to any creature grappling you.

Boricubos: The Lost Isles (5E) © 2021, Legendary Games; Author: Miguel Colon.

Weight Spike.name: Weight Spike
Weight Spike.description:
You envelope your hand in a purple light and increase the pull of gravity on a creature you touch. Make a melee spellattackagainst the target. You have advantage on theattackroll if the target is wearing heavy armor or is Large or larger. On a hit, the target takes 2d4 bludgeoning damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn as its own weight pulls on it.

The spell’s damage increases by 2d4 when you reach 5th level (4d4), 11th level (6d4), and 17th level (8d4).

Amber Salve.name: Amber Salve
Amber Salve.description:
You imbue a flask of honey with arcane energies, transforming it into a thick orange paste. This balm can be applied to a creature’s injuries over 1 minute, giving the creature the benefits of a long rest. A creature cannot benefit from an application of amber salve again until they complete a long rest.

The balm loses most of its magical potency after 24 hours. If applied after this time, the balm instead restores a number ofhit pointsequal to 5d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

Pulse of Hate.name: Pulse of Hate
Pulse of Hate.components: V, S, M (carved heart with a pin thrust through it)
Pulse of Hate.description:
Classes:antipaladin,cleric,warlock

Your entire form pulses with an angry red light, inflaming hatred in those around you. Enemies within 20 feet of you take 2d6 mental damage, or half as much on a successfulWisdomsaving throw. In addition, creatures that fail their save must use their action on their next turn to make amelee attackagainst a random creature other than you within its reach. If there is no creature within reach, the creature can act normally.

Each round thereafter that you concentrate on your spell, the pulse of hate flashes again at the beginning ofyour turn. As a bonus action, you can delay the pulse of hate until later inyour turn, which can be during your movement or at the end ofyour turn.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 5th. If you increase its level to 7th or higher, a creature failing its save attacks a random creature other than you within 10 feet, moving toward that creature toattack.

Battlecry Ballad.name: Battlecry Ballad
Battlecry Ballad.description:
You fill your allies with glorious honor and a thirst for battle using triumphant song. Expend and roll a Bardic Inspiration die to determine the number of rounds you can maintain concentration on this spell. For the duration, each creature you choose within 30 feet of you (including you) gains a bonus toattackanddamage rollsequal to half the number of rounds you have maintained concentration on this spell (rounded up, minimum 1). You cannot cast another spell through your spellcasting focus while concentrating on this spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can maintain concentration on this spell for an additional round for each slot level above 3rd.

Divine Impediment.name: Divine Impediment
Divine Impediment.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You create a block between the target and their divine power. The creature must make a saving throw using their spellcasting ability score. On a failure, the creature must roll a concentration check to cast anyclericordruidspell or any divinely granted innate spells. The target must also roll concentration checks to use divinely-granted special abilities like apaladin’s channel divinity, adruid’s wildshape, or special abilities of celestials or fiends. If the target fails their concentration check, the action fails. Each round at the beginning of their turn, the target may roll another saving throw to end the effect early.

In addition to the block imposed over the usage of divine abilities, the target gains advantage on saving throws against divine spells or abilities.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can target an additional creature for each slot level above 4th.

The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Wall of Light.name: Wall of Light
Wall of Light.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (a chip of mica)

DurationConcentration, up to 10 minutes

An immobile, blinding curtain of white light that blocks line of sight springs into existence. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, and 20 feet high, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter and 20 feet high. The wall blocks line of sight. The wall sheds bright light to a range of 60 feet in all directions and dim light for an additional 60 feet. A creature that is adjacent to the wall must close their eyes or make aConstitutionsaving throw; on a failed save, the creature isblindeduntil the end of their next turns. A creature that passes through the wall is automaticallyblinded, even if its eyes are closed. An undead that fails a saving throw has their maximumhit pointsreduced by 5; this reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0. An undead that passes through the wall must make a saving throw to avoid this effect even if its eyes are closed.

Smuggler’s Boon.components: V, S, M (strip of leather or cloth)
Smuggler’s Boon.description:
You touch one bag which is currently holding no more than 30 pounds or one cubic foot of material.

The contents of the bag vanish for the duration of the spell, and you are free to fill it again as a normal bag.

When the spell ends, all the original contents reappear. If the new contents and original contents are more than the bag can hold, the new contents spill out from the opening.

Mindful Insight.name: Mindful Insight
Mindful Insight.description:
You reveal the strengths and weaknesses of a creature against mind-altering effects. Target a creature within range. The target must succeed on aCharismasaving throw, or you find out if the creature is immune to beingcharmedorfrightened.

Spirit Drain.description:
Target: One creature within range

Classes: Cleric, Druid, Warlock, Wizard

You drain a sliver of life force from a creature you can see within range. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw or take 1d4 necrotic damage. You gain a number oftemporary hit pointsequal to half the damage dealt (rounded down).

This spell’s damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

You summon tiny air elementals that propel the targeted creature along, allowing it to move faster or jump further. You choose one of the two following effects when you cast the spell:

Divinatory Expungement.name: Divinatory Expungement
Divinatory Expungement.description:
You designate a specific area and a time in the immediate past (no more than ten minutes ago), protecting it from divinations that would reveal what happened there and then. The area of the spell consists of up to ten 10-foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish. Each cube must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube. Only divination spells of 6th level or higher can determine events taking place in the warded area during the time you designated.

For example, if a wizard were to break into a tower, then cast this spell after leaving, it would hinder the effectiveness of divinations seeking to reveal the break-in, the party responsible, or exactly what occurred. Someone usingdivination(a 4th-level spell) would be unable to gain information about thewizard‘s activities in that time and place. Since this spell affects only the past, however, the wizard’sactionsmight have been observed (such as withclairvoyanceorscrying) while they were ongoing.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the level of divination needed to overcome this protection increases by 1 for each slot level above 5th. Thus, using a 6th-level spell slot protects against divinations up to 6th level, a 7th-level spell slot protects against divinations up to 7th level, and so on.

Impaling Spike.name: Impaling Spike
Impaling Spike.description:
You fire a very high-speed spike at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target.

On a hit, the target takes 1d8 piercing damage.

On a critical hit, if the damaged target is a creature, it must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failure, the spike remains lodged in the target and the target has disadvantage onDexterityandStrengthchecks until the spike is removed (requiring a successfulDexterityorStrengthcheck with the same DC as the saving throw of this spell) or until it disappears at the end of the target’s next turn.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

Gout of Flame.name: Gout of Flame
Gout of Flame.description:
Durationconcentration, up to 1 minute

You spray a long gout of flame from your fingertips to burn your foe. While the spell is a 30-foot long and 5-foot wide line, only the closest target to you is affected in each round you concentrate on the spell. The affected target must make aDexteritysaving throw or be dealt 1d6 fire damage. You may elect to exclude the square adjacent to you from the area of effect if you so choose to avoid affecting allies. Any creature that fails theirDexteritysaving throw against this spell two rounds in a row takes 1d4 additional fire damage. The extra fire damage lasts for 1 round after they are no longer being targeted by this spell or until they succeed on theDexteritysaving throw for this spell two rounds in a row. Each round while concentrating on the spell, you may redirect the line of effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage dealt each round increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Canine Companion.name: Canine Companion
Canine Companion.description:
You summon a fey spirit that takes the form of a mastiff or other size Medium dog. The dog obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to the dog, it defends itself from hostile creatures, but otherwise takes noactions. The dog is either a hunting dog or a guard dog and performs the prescribed task to the best ability of a well-trained canine. It is also considered fey, and it disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The dog is friendly to you and your companions.

Rollinitiativeseparately for the dog, which has its own turns.

Liberating Command.name: Liberating Command
Liberating Command.description:
Classes:bard,paladin,ranger,sorcerer

When an ally isgrappledorrestrainedand you target them with this spell, they can make an Escape check as areaction, with advantage on the check. This has no effect on allies who areparalyzed,petrified, orunconscious, or against effects which do not allow an Escape check. You cannot use this spell on yourself.

Legendary Classes: Templars & Tyrants© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Clinton J. Boomer, Amber Scott

Expedite Work.name: Expedite Work
Expedite Work.description:
A 50-foot-radius around you becomes conducive to getting work done. Within this space, you can execute any mundane task or crafting effort, halving the required time spent on these tasks for the duration of the spell. You must provide your own tools.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 2nd-level spell slot or higher, the spell increases the radius of the workspace by 10 feet for every two levels above 1st.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Lionheart.name: Lionheart
Lionheart.description:
You touch your ally and imbue them with comfort and confidence. They are immune to thefrightenedcondition as long as the spell lasts. If they already werefrightenedwhen you cast lionheart, they can attempt a new saving throw each round at the beginning of their turn to end the effect, after which they gain immunity.

Sin Sight.name: Sin Sight
Sin Sight.description:
Your eyes glow with a silvery-white light as you attune your senses to the presence of evil auras. For the duration of the spell, you can see evil auras within 120 feet of you. This effect operates similarly to the detect evil spell, but does not require concentration.

You can sense the location of all evil auras within your sight.

You can also discern a creature’s Hit Dice, type, and alignment.

As an action, you can focus your attention on a specific creature within 120 feet of you to determine whether it has any spellcasting or spell-like abilities, and whether these are arcane or divine (abilities that mimic spells register as arcane).

Additionally, you can ascertain the level of the most potent spell or spell-like ability the creature currently has available for use.

If you identify an evil creature capable of casting divine spells and you subsequently use your Divine Smite feature against that creature, you gain a +2 bonus toattackrolls and saves made against it.

Empty Rain.name: Empty Rain
Empty Rain.description:
A frigid, draining rain falls in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point you specify within range. Each creature that starts its turn in the area or enters the area for the first time on its turn must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 3d8 cold and 3d8 necrotic damage on a failed save and half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also prohibited from casting spells while it is 223 within the area and until the beginning of its next turn after leaving the area.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this with a slot of 6th-level or higher, you deal an extra 2d8 cold or necrotic damage (your choice) for each slot level above 5th.

*NoteAll spells with the void keyword have a verbal component and must be uttered in Void Speech, which cannot be precluded by use of any other feat, feature, or spell.

Warlock Grimoire 4. ©2023 Open Design LLC. Authors: Lou Anders, Wolfgang Baur, HH Carlan, Robert Fairbanks, Basheer Ghouse, Richard Green, Tim Hitchcock, Jeremy Hochhalter, Victoria Jaczko, Rajan Khanna, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Jonathan Miley, Kelly Pawlik, Sebastian Rombach, Adam W. Roy, Paul Scofield, Amber Stewart, Brian Suskind, Mike Welham.

Toothless Beast.name: Toothless Beast
Toothless Beast.description:
You hinder the natural attacks of a creature you can see within range. The creature must make aWisdomsaving throw. On a failed save, any time the creature attacks with a bite, claw, slam, or other weapon that isn’t manufactured, it must roll the weapon’s damage dice twice and use the lower total. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherWisdomsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target. This spell has no effect on constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind
