Wall of Thorns.components: V, S, M(a handful of thorns)
Wall of Thorns.description:
You create a wall of tough, pliable, tangled brush bristling with needle-sharp thorns. The wall appears within range on a solid surface and lasts for the duration. You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick or a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 7d8 piercing damage, or half as much damage on a successful save.

A creature can move through the wall, albeit slowly and painfully. For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement. Furthermore, the first time a creature enters the wall on a turn or ends its turn there, the creature must make aDexteritysaving throw. It takes 7d8 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Vigor.name: Vigor

You instill the target with a mote of radiant energy. For a living creature this causes them to heal 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns. If the target is dying while under the effect of this spell, they automatically succeed their death saving throw for the round instead of being healed to 1hpimmediately.

If the target is undead, they instead take one radiant damage per round at the beginning of their turn.

This spell has no effect on constructs.

On a failed save, the target can’t regainhit pointsfrom the Regeneration trait or similar spell or trait for the duration. The target can receive magicalhealingor regainhit pointsfrom other traits, spells, oractions, as normal. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make anotherConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

The target’s hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and you gaintemporary hit pointsequal to that amount. You cover a 20-foot square of ground with hard, crumbly snow that crunches loudly when trodden upon. Creatures in the area have Disadvantage onDexterity(Stealth) checks and their footprints clearly show their location, so if attacking anInvisiblecreature in the Crunchy Snow you take only a -1 penalty onattackrolls rather than having Disadvantage. Crunchy Snow covers tracks underneath it at the moment it is cast, butWisdom(Survival) checks to track creatures moving across it have a +10 bonus.

Crunchy Snow is not particularly slippery, though it is somewhat unstable and if cast on a slope creatures moving across it have a -1 penalty onDexterityD20 Tests. A creature fallingpronein Crunchy Snow takes 1 Cold damage and 1 Slashing damage.

The Crunchy Snow evaporates into nothing when the spell ends.

On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and 2d8 radiant damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knockedprone.

Comfort Food.description:

Additionally, the food is instilled with such flavor and bolstering magics that it grants the consumer of the food immunity tofearandtemporary hit pointsequal to your Spellcasting ability modifier at the start of each of its turns. Hunter’s Senses.description:
This spell grants you supernatural senses.

However, you must decide what kind of benefit to gain, choosing between sight, hearing, or smell. You can only benefit from one of these supernatural abilities at any given time. While the spell is in effect, you have advantage on anyWisdom(Perception) and passivePerceptionchecks that apply to the specific bolstered sense. In certain circumstances, you are able to use your senses to perform supernatural feats, such as sighting enemy movement a mile away, tracking by scent, or hearing a distinct sound within a crowded city.

You decide what action the vehicle will take and where it will move during its next turn. The vehicle can only take theDodge,Dash, orDisengageaction. Chaotic Contrition.name: Chaotic Contrition
Chaotic Contrition.description:
You fill one creature you can see within range with profound remorse and guilt. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or beincapacitateduntil the end of its next turn. When the condition ends on the target, the nearest hostile creature within 30 feet of the first target must make the saving throw, becomingincapacitateduntil the end of its next turn on a failed save. If more than one creature qualifies, you break the tie and choose which of those creatures becomes the spell’s next target.

On a failed save, a creature is overwhelmed by an unbearable sense of despair, becomingparalyzedandblindedby tears for the duration. The spell also generates an oppressive aura of sorrow that suppresses all sound in the area, enforcing complete silence and preventing the casting of spells with verbal components.

Energy Respite.description:
Touch a willing creature and infuse it with revitalizing energy. For the duration the creature can ignore the effects of all levels ofexhaustionthey have. Gaining 6 levels ofexhaustionwill still kill them.

Orb of Acid.name: Orb of Acid
Orb of Acid.description:
You create a surging ball of acid the size of your fist that you can hurl at a creature within range as a ranged spellattack. If you hit, the target takes 8d6 acid damage, or half as much on a successfulConstitutionsaving throw. In addition, a creature failing its save ispoisonedfor 1 round by the noxious fumes.

Creatures within 5 feet of the target take 4d6 acid damage, or half as much on a successfulDexteritysaving throw.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 4th.

Dispel Magic.description:
Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any spell of 3rd level or lower on the target ends. For each spell of 4th level or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell’s level. On a successful check, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you automatically end the effects of a spell on the target if the spell’s level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you used.

Heavenly Grace.name: Heavenly Grace
Heavenly Grace.description:
You wreath yourself in heavenly power, your body glows with bright light out to 30 feet and dim light for an additional 30 feet. This means you have disadvantage onStealthchecks. However, for the duration, you deal an additional +2 damage with weapons and spells and you gain a +10 feet to your base speed.

Bend Space.name: Bend Space
Bend Space.description:
This spell allows you to bend space around yourself to divert anattack. If theattackaffects an area, you suffer only half damage. If it is targeted at you, it has a 50% miss chance (or a 50% chance to simply fail, if it does not require anattackroll), and you gain a +2 deflection bonus to your AC against it. You may instead choose to bend yourself around space. Until the end ofyour turn, your reach is increased by 5 feet. With either use of the spell, you must succeed on a DC 15Constitutionsaving throw to enable your body to readjust to normal space; if failed, you take (2d10) damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, your AC bonus increases by +1, and your reach is increased by 5 feet for each level it is increased.

Flood Waters.description:
This spell summons a forceful wave of sea water that emanates from you in a 30-foot cone. It knocks creatures down and pushes them away from you.

Creatures size Large and smaller caught in the area of this wave must make aStrengthsaving throw or suffer 2d8 bludgeoning damage, be knockedprone, and be washed back 10 feet. Those who make the saving throw suffer half damage, are pushed 5 feet, and are not renderedprone. Large creatures with more than two legs, such as horses, have advantage on the saving throw. Huge and larger creatures cannot be knockedpronewith this spell. Creatures takingcoverbehind fixed objects, such as a stone pillar, are not affected. All open flames in the area are extinguished.

Boiling Rain.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
Boiling Rain.description:
Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

A storm of burning falls to the ground in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point within range.

Each creature in the cylinder must make aDexteritysaving throw. A creature takes 13 (3d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Until the spell ends, you can use a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns to cause this damage again.

Icicle Eruption.name: Icicle Eruption
Icicle Eruption.description:
You cause razor-sharp shards of blue-white ice to explode out of the ground beneath the feet of up to 10 creatures within range. Each creature you target takes 8d6 cold damage and 8d6 piercing damage, or half as much with a successfulDexteritysaving throw. In addition, creatures that fail their saving throw have their movement halved for 1 minute due to pain and injury to their legs and feet. An icicle eruption does not affect swimming or flying creatures unless they are within 10 feet of the ground (including a cliff, wall, or similar solid natural surface).

Power Word Reveal.name: Power Word Reveal
Power Word Reveal.description:
You utter a word of power and every creature within range perceives things as they actually are. Each creature within 120 feet of you has truesight in the spell’s area until the start of your next turn.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration increases by 1 round for each slot level above 4th.

Hero of Fable.name: Hero of Fable
Hero of Fable.description:
You make a creature capable of great deeds, like a storybook champion, and at the same time empower that creature’s foes to become worthy of a hero’s attention. A creature of your choice within range gains advantage on all ability checks,attackrolls, and saving throws for the duration. At the same time, creatures thatattackyour target, or that make a saving throw against a spell or effect originating from your target, have advantage on their roll. If your target is unwilling, it must succeed on aCharismasaving throw to avoid the effects.

At Higher Levels. You can target one additional creature for every slot level above 6th if you cast this spell using a 7th level or higher spell slot.

Floral Bouquet.name: Floral Bouquet
Floral Bouquet.description:
A flower bulb streaks from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range and then bursts open and releases floral aromas and pungent scents. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must succeed on aConstitutionsaving throw or bestunnedby the sensory overload. A creature that has advantage onWisdom(Perception) checks that rely on smell, such as the Keen Smell trait, has disadvantage on itsConstitutionsaving throw. At the end of each of its turns, astunnedcreature can make anotherConstitutionsaving throw.

Creatures with the Keen Smell trait still suffer disadvantage on thisConstitutionsaving throw. On a success, the creature is no longerstunned.

Pollen Cloud.name: Pollen Cloud
Pollen Cloud.description:
A yellow-green streak flashes from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range and then explodes with a loud pop into a thick cloud of irritating pollen. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make aConstitutionsaving throw. A target takes 4d6 poison damage and becomespoisonedandblindedon a failed save. These conditions persist for 1d6 rounds.

Creatures that succeed at the saving throw take half as much poison damage, are notblinded, and arepoisonedfor just 1 round.

A creature that failed its saving throw can attempt anotherConstitutionsaving throw at the end of its turn. On a successful save, theblindedandpoisonedconditions end for it.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 and thepoisonedandblindedconditions persist for 1d4 more rounds for every two spell slots above 3rd.

Eye of the Dragon.name: Eye of the Dragon
Eye of the Dragon.description:
After casting this spell and concentrating for one minute, you can tell the exact value of any number of coins in a five-foot cube, in their respective denominations. This knowledge is retained for one hour after the spell ends and then is forgotten.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you add another five-foot cube to thesizeof the pile of coins you can count.

Timely Inspiration.name: Timely Inspiration
Timely Inspiration.description:
A word of your encouragement can snatch victory fromseemingdefeat. When an ally you can see within range fails on anattackroll or ability check, as areactionyou can grant them a +1 bonus on the die roll. If this is enough to turn the roll from failure to success, the roll succeeds and you also can choose to grant that ally a Bardic Inspiration die.

They cannot use the die immediately but can use it in a future round. If the bonus is not enough to meet the DC, the roll fails and you cannot grant that ally inspiration as part of the spell.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you increase the bonus by 1 for every two slot levels above 1st.

The Dragon’s Hoard #42© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke

Holy Ice.name: Holy Ice
Holy Ice.components: V, S, M (vial of holy water)
Holy Ice.description:
You create a mass of frozen holy water that can be used to create one of the following effects:

Holy Glacier. You attempt to encase a single creature within a block of frozen holy water. If the target succeeds on aDexteritysaving throw, takes 1d4 cold damage 1d4 radiant damage and is entangled by chunks of ice until the end of its next turn. During this time, its movement is halved and it takes a -1 penalty onattackrolls and AC.

If the creature fails its saving throw, it is wholly entombed in the ice. It takes 1d6 cold damage and 1d6 radiant damage and isrestrained. It can still breathe through cracks in the ice, but it otherwise has totalcover. The holy glacier can be destroyed if it takes 30 points of damage, and fire deals double damage to it. Damage dealt to the holy glacier does not harm the trapped creature, even if the amount of damage exceeds what is required to shatter the ice.

The trapped creature also can use its action on its turn to break free with aStrengthsaving throw, and the DC of this saving throw goes down by 2 each round after the first. Each round a creature ends its turn trapped in the holy glacier, it takes an additional 1d6 cold and 1d6 radiant damage. Incorporeal creatures cannot be trapped in a holy glacier, but gaseous or liquid creatures can be.

Holy Icicles. You create three javelin-sized icicles that fly towards one or more targets (all targets must be within 10 feet of each other). Make a ranged spellattackfor each icicle, which is destroyed after being used regardless of whether they hit. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 piercing damage, 1d6 cold damage, and 1d6 radiant damage.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can hurl one additional icicle or attempt to trap one additional creature in a holy glacier for each slot level above 5th.

The Dragon’s Hoard #26© 2022, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, James-Levi Cooke.

Tree Heal.description:
You touch a plant and it regains 1d4hit points.

Alternatively, you can cure it of one disease or remove pests from it. Once you cast this spell on a plant or plant creature, you can’t cast it on that target again for 24 hours. This spell can be used only on plants and plant creatures.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

Distant Accuracy.name: Distant Accuracy
Distant Accuracy.description:
You enchant one ranged weapon with the ability to strike creatures far beyond its normal range, doubling its range. This effect applies to all ammunition shot from a ranged weapon. Any creature wielding these weapons gains this benefit.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 2nd level spell slot or higher, you can enchant one more weapon for every slot level above 1st.

Curse of Lingering Despair.name: Curse of Lingering Despair
Curse of Lingering Despair.description:
Target: Up to three creatures you can see within range

You weave a spell that sows seeds of despair in the hearts of your enemies. Up to three creatures of your choice must make aWisdomsaving throw or be cursed with despair for the next 24 hours.

During this time, the cursed target can’t gain the benefits of resting, and can’t be affected by spells or effects that would restore itshit pointsor end any harmful conditions affecting it. If a creature cursed in this way drops to 0hit points, it instantly dies, and its soul is shattered, unable to be resurrected by any means short of atrue resurrectionorwishspell.

Earth to Mud.name: Earth to Mud
Earth to Mud.description:
You cause a 10-square-foot patch of natural soil to become thick, viscous mud. The mud is too thin to wade through yet too thick to easily escape. Any creature caught in the area when the spell is cast or that ends its turn in the mud risks being pulled under. They must make aStrengthsaving throw or become mired in the mud,restrained. Any creature that begins its turn mired in the mud must make aStrengthsaving throw or be pulled under, drowning in the fetid muck. The mud isdifficult terrain.

Fungi Shield.components: V, S, M (handful of dried mushrooms)
Fungi Shield.description:
A barrier of tiny fungi grows instantaneously and protects you. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +3 bonus to AC, including against the triggeringattack.

Reaper’s Balm.components: V, S, M (pinch of grave dirt mixed with resin)
Reaper’s Balm.description:
Your touch wards a creature against death. For the duration, the target has advantage on death saving throws.

If a dying creature affected by this spell succeeds on three death saving throws and becomes stable, the spell ends.

You send a pulse of energy through a creature that either boosts or reverses theirhealingability. Against an unwilling creature, make a melee spellattack. You disrupt the control a spellcaster has over a creature.

Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability, with a bonus equal to the level at which this spell was cast. The DC equals 8 + the triggering spell’s level.

On a success, thecharmedor summoned creature is also under the effect of the spellconfusion. This lasts for the duration of the triggering spell.

Detect Emotion.description:
For the duration, you sense the emotional state of creatures within 30 feet of you that you can see. If you sense emotion in this way, the emotion appears as a faint aura around the creature, and you can determine the type of emotion based on the following:

Questions verbally directed at the target creature naturally shape the course of its thoughts and can change the color of its aura.

Galder’s Gazetteer Author(s) Matt Click, Gabe Hicks, Jess Ross

Burden of Sins.description:
You touch a creature and cause it to see all the deeds of evil it has ever committed in an instant. The creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be overwhelmed by the evil it has done, having a brief vision in which it sees itself in a dark place being tormented by its past self, taking 10d10 psychic damage as a result.

Corrosive Touch.description:

On a hit, the target takes 1d8 acid damage, and nonmagical armor worn by the target is partly dissolved and takes a permanent and cumulative ?1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10.

The spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

Torpor Touch.description:
Classes: Cleric, Warlock, Wizard

You touch a creature that has at least 1 hit point, and that creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or become cursed for the duration of the spell. While cursed, if the creature dies, it is animated as azombieunder your control at the start of your next turn.

On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to mentally command the zombie if it is within 60 feet of you.

You decide what action the zombie will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor.

If you issue no commands, the zombie only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the zombie continues to follow it until its task is complete. The zombie is under your control for 10 minutes, after which point the foul magic that animated it fades, and the zombie dies. The GM has the zombie’s statistics.

Venomous Thoughts.components: V, S, M (the tongue of an asp)
Venomous Thoughts.description:
You protect your mind with psychic poison. Until the spell ends, each time a creature attempts to read or detect your thoughts, speak with you using telepathy, influence your dreams, or perceive you through magicalscryingsensors, it must make anIntelligencesaving throw, taking 4d10 poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on successful one.

Etheric Envelope.name: Etheric Envelope
Etheric Envelope.components: S, M (skein of threads braided together)
Etheric Envelope.description:
You place yourself into folded cocoon of misty non-space on the Ethereal Plane, where you meditate in safety. You can choose to complete either a short rest or long rest inside the etheric envelope, and if you choose the latter you can prepare spells and attune magic items while inside it.

The etheric envelope isinvisibleexcept to creatures already on the Ethereal Plane, and even to them it appears as a featureless mass of misty threads, requiring a DC 20Wisdom(Perception) check to notice in the misty space of the Ethereal Plane. A determined creature canattack(AC 20, 30hit points); the ethereal envelope is immune to bludgeoning, necrotic, poison, psychic, and radiant damage and hasresistanceto all other forms of damage except force and piercing or slashing damage from magical or adamantine weapons. If the etheric envelope is destroyed, the spell ends.

When the spell ends, the etheric envelope dissolves around you, shunting you back to the exact location where you cast the spell. If that space is occupied, you are shunted into the nearest available open space, and you are treated as if under aslowspell for 1 round as your body readjusts to its new location on the Material Plane.

The Dragon’s Hoard #48© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Matt Kimmel, Michael Mifsud, Wren Roy, Matt Goodall, Ismael Alvarez

Gleipner’s Binding.name: Gleipner’s Binding
Gleipner’s Binding.description:
Choose a Huge or larger creature within range that you can see. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or be bound by your magical influence for the duration. On a successful save, the spell has no effect. While under the effects of this spell, the target isrestrainedand its movement speed is reduced to 0. The creature’s senses remain sharp, but it is compelled to follow your mental commands to the best of its ability. You can use your bonus action on each of your turns to mentally issue a single command to the creature, which it must obey on its subsequent turn. If you issue a command that would cause harm to the creature or if the creature takes any damage while bound by the spell, it can make anotherWisdomsaving throw to break free.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can target a Gargantuan creature.

Weaponification.name: Weaponification
Weaponification.components: V, S, M (broken pieces offormer magic weapon)
Weaponification.description:
You touch a willing creature and transform it into a sentient weapon of your choice. The weapon can look however you want, as long as the GM approves. The target’s gear melds into the new form. The creature can’t activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment. You or the target creature can dismiss the spell as a bonus action. If the creature transforms back to its original form while being carried or wielded by a creature, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space.

While transformed into a weapon, the creature can’t move, speak, cast spells, benefit from spells and magical effects (other than this spell), and is limited to the followingactionsand benefits:

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

Ineffectual Attacks.name: Ineffectual Attacks
Ineffectual Attacks.description:
You cause chaos magic to disrupt up to six creatures of your choice in a 40-foot cube within range. Each target must succeed on aCharismasaving throw or be affected by this spell for the duration.

If an affected creature’s damage roll from their weapon or spellattackis among the die’s highest two numbers, the damage die must be rerolled. For example, if an affected creature is using a shortsword and the damage roll is 5 or 6, the player must re-roll the damage and use the new number even if it is 5 or 6.

Doom of The Endless Void.name: Doom of The Endless Void
Doom of The Endless Void.description:
You open a rift into the Void itself, tearing apart reality around you. All creatures within 20 feet of you must make aConstitutionsaving throw. You must also make this save.

On a failed save, the target takes 6d6 + 20 force damage. If this damage reduces the target to0 hit points, it is disintegrated. A disintegrated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. The creature can be restored to life only by means of atrue resurrectionorwishspell. This spell automatically disintegrates a Large or smaller nonmagical object or acreationof magical force. If the target is a Huge or larger object orcreationof force, this spell disintegrates a 10-foot-cube portion of it each round. A magic item is unaffected by this spell.

If you maintain concentration on the spell, the same saving throw is required again on your next turn-you must make your saving throw before any target creatures do. If the spell kills you, the effect ends immediately.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Mind Ward.name: Mind Ward
Mind Ward.description:
You tap your forehead with your wand. Until the end of your next turn, you haveresistanceagainst psychic damage.

Magic Whetstone.name: Magic Whetstone
Magic Whetstone.description:
This spell sharpens all slashing and piercing weapons within a 10-foot radius, as if they were sharpened with a whetstone. It straightens edges in weapons, smoothing out any dents and nicks, which makes the weapon look brand new (although the hilt may tell a different story). This spell does not bestow anyattackor damage bonuses to the weapons.

Ratcatcher’s Revenge.name: Ratcatcher’s Revenge
Ratcatcher’s Revenge.components: V, S, M (pint of animal blood and a rat’s tail)
Ratcatcher’s Revenge.description:
You infest a humanoid creature with crawling rats burrowing out of its flesh. If the target fails itsConstitutionsaving throw, three rats claw out of the target’s body, dealing 6d6 slashing damage and causing the target to have disadvantage onattackrolls, saving throws, and ability checks from the agony. Once they burrow forth, the three rats immediately transform into wererats and attack the target of the spell and any other creatures nearby, armed with their teeth and shortswords made of bone. They do not attack the caster and creatures the caster designates as their allies; the wererats can understand the caster’s speech. If the target is slain, these wererats scurry away to attack others. The wererats created by this spell perish and crumble into bits of bloody, matted fur 1 hour after being created, but any lycanthropy they infect creatures with persists even after they die.

Herald of Ruin.description:
You release a wave of necrotic energy, symbolizing the impending doom. Each creature in a 30-foot radius must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 necrotic damage and its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, with no reduction to its hit point maximum.

Mass Rime.components: V, S, M (1 piece of cold stone)
Mass Rime.description:
ComponentsV, S, M (1 piece of cold stone)

Duration5 + spellcasting modifier rounds

NoteThis spell is a rework of the core spell of the same name.

You cover all creatures in a 30-foot-radius sphere with frost. If the targets fails aConstitutionsaving throw, they are dealt 1 cold damage at the beginning of each of their turns. If this spell is cast upon a creature affected by an embers spell of equal level, both spells end. If the embers spell is of higher level, this spell fails, if this spell is higher level, the embers spell ends.

At Higher LevelsWhen you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th or higher, the damage dealt each round increases to 2. The damage further increases to 3 if you instead use a 9thlevel spell slot.

Conjure Cats.name: Conjure Cats
Conjure Cats.description:
You summon celestial spirits that take feline form and appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within range.

Choose one of the following options for what appears:

Each beast is also considered a celestial, and it disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The summoned felines are friendly to you and your companions. Rollinitiativefor the summoned creatures as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures, but otherwise take noactions.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using certain higher-level spell slots, more creatures appear with your chosen summoning option: twice as many with a 4th-level slot, three times as many with a 6th-level slot, and four times as many with an 8th-level slot.

Prismatic Mist.name: Prismatic Mist
Prismatic Mist.description:
You conjure a thin mist that glows with shifting multihued light. The prismatic mist sheds light like a candle but lightly obscures a 30-foot-radius sphere. Each time a creature enters or begins its turn within the prismatic mist, roll on the table below to see which color of the mist touches them. A successful save of the listed type reduces damage by half or negates the listed effect that round.

The Dragon’s Hoard #44© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Darrin Drader, Mark Hart, Dustin Knight, Robert J. Grady, James-Levi Cooke.

Venomous Cloud.name: Venomous Cloud
Venomous Cloud.description:
You create a 10-foot-radius Sphere of toxic gas centered on a point within range. Creatures beginning their turn in the area take 2d8 Poison damage, or half as much with a successfulConstitutionsaving throw. Creatures failing their save are alsoPoisoneduntil the spell ends.

The Dragon’s Hoard #59© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Matt Kimmel, Dan Dillon, James-Levi Cooke.

Greater Dyscrasia.name: Greater Dyscrasia
Greater Dyscrasia.description:
You unleash a virulent disease on a humanoid or giant that you can see within range. The target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, it takes 14d6 necrotic damage, or half as much damage on a successful save. The damage can’t reduce the target’shit pointsbelow 1. If the target fails the saving throw, its hit point maximum is reduced for 1 hour by an amount equal to the necrotic damage it took. Any effect that removes a disease allows a creature’s hit point maximum to return to normal before that time passes.

Blood Mantra.name: Blood Mantra
Blood Mantra.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 minute

You let out a chant or series of sounds that resound that heightens the blood of you and your allies. For as long as you concentrate on the spell, you and your allies within 60 feet of you can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to anattackroll or saving throw. The target must be able to hear you and if you are silenced, the effect ends.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Quicksand Mire.name: Quicksand Mire
Quicksand Mire.description:
You transform the terrain into a deep mire of quicksand at a point you choose within range, affecting a 60-foot-radius circle. The area becomesdifficult terrain, and each creature that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on its turn must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or berestrainedand start sinking into the quicksand.

On a failed save, in addition to beingrestrained, a creature begins to sink, being pulled 5 feet into the quicksand and taking 8d6 bludgeoning damage due to the constricting pressure of the sand. For each subsequent turn a creature starts in the quicksand and fails theStrengthsaving throw, it sinks an additional 5 feet and the damage increases by 4d6 (to a maximum of 20d6).

Foretell Distraction.name: Foretell Distraction
Foretell Distraction.description:
Thanks to your foreknowledge, you know exactly when your foe will take his or her eyes off you. Casting this spell has the same effect as making a successfulDexterity(Stealth) check, providedcoveror concealment is available within 10 feet of you. It doesn’t matter whether enemies can see you when you cast the spell; they glance away at just the right moment. You can move up to 10 feet as part of casting the spell, provided you’re able to move (notrestrainedorgrappledor reduced to a speed of less than 10 feet for any other reason). This move doesn’t count as part of your normal movement. After the spell is cast, you must be in a position where you can remain hidden: a lightly obscured space, for example, or a space where you have totalcover. Otherwise, enemies see you again immediately and you’re not hidden.

The Scarlet Citadel. © 2021 Open Design LLC. Authors: Steve Winter, Wolfgang Baur, Scott Gable, and Victoria Jaczo.

Clone.name: Clone
Clone.components: V, S, M(a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp and at least 1 cubic inch of flesh of the creature that is to be cloned, which the spell consumes, and a vessel worth at least 2,000 gp that has a sealable lid and is large enough to hold a Medium creature, such as a huge urn, coffin, mud-filled cyst in the ground, or crystal container filled with salt water)
Clone.description:
This spell grows an inert duplicate of a living creature as a safeguard against death. This clone forms inside a sealed vessel and grows to full size and maturity after 120 days; you can also choose to have the clone be a younger version of the same creature. It remains inert and endures indefinitely, as long as its vessel remains undisturbed.

At any time after the clone matures, if the original creature dies, its soul transfers to the clone, provided that the soul is free and willing to return.

The clone is physically identical to the original and has the same personality, memories, and abilities, but none of the original’s equipment. The original creature’s physical remains, if they still exist, become inert and can’t thereafter be restored to life, since the creature’s soul is elsewhere.
Clone.material_component: a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp and at least 1 cubic inch of flesh of the creature that is to be cloned, which the spell consumes, and a vessel worth at least 2,000 gp that has a sealable lid and is large enough to hold a Medium creature, such as a huge urn, coffin, mud-filled cyst in the ground, or crystal container filled with salt water

Silent Image.name: Silent Image
Silent Image.components: V, S, M(a bit of fleece)
Silent Image.description:
You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot cube. The image appears at a spot within range and lasts for the duration. The image is purely visual; it isn’t accompanied by sound, smell, or other sensory effects.

You can use your action to cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it. A creature that uses its action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successfulIntelligence(Investigation) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.

Prismatic Spray.name: Prismatic Spray
Prismatic Spray.description: Eight multicolored rays of light flash from your hand. Each ray is a different color and has a different power and purpose. Each creature in a 60-foot cone must make aDexteritysaving throw. For each target, roll a d8 to determine which color ray affects it.

Binding Earth.name: Binding Earth
Binding Earth.description:
You cause the earth around a creature to harden and bind it. A target within range must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage and berestrainedfor the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and is notrestrained.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Counting Quill.name: Counting Quill
Counting Quill.description:
You manifest a Tiny spectral quill, hovering in an unoccupied space of your choice within 60 feet of you. The quill is intangible and doesn’t occupy its space. As a bonus action, you can cause the quill to hover up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you or it can see. It can pass through creatures but not objects. The counting quill can add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers. By expending a bonus action, the caster can cause the counting quill to perform a series of mathematical exercises and write the answer on any writing surface. The counting quill never runs out of ink. The counting quill stops manifesting if it is ever more than 300 feet away from you or if someone castsdispel magicon it, if you die, or if you dismiss the counting quill as a bonus action.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Phantasmal Combat.name: Phantasmal Combat
Phantasmal Combat.description:
DurationConcentration, Up to 1 minute

You create phantasmal sensations of a pitched battle in a 20-foot-radius area. Any who enter the area must make aWisdomsaving throw or be affected by the phantasm. You and any creatures that succeeded on theirWisdomsaving throws see shadowy shapes, all other creatures do not see anything.

Creatures that failed theirWisdomsaving throws move cautiously and try to avoid the dangers of the battle. They cannot makereactionsand all attacks against them have advantage. If the creature leaves the area, they are no longer affected and do not perceive the battle. If they re-enter the area, they are allowed anotherWisdomsaving throw to disbelieve the phantasm with advantage.

When casting the spell, you can designate a number of allies that are immune to the spell and can see its shadowy presence equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

Breath of Life: The Beguiler (5e), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates and Norman Mitchell Jr.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Commune with Spirits.name: Commune with Spirits
Commune with Spirits.components: V, S, M (incense and an offering worth 10 gp)
Commune with Spirits.description:
You reach out your consciousness into the spirit world and contact one spirit within range. You can ask the spirit a number of questions equal to your spellcasting modifier. These questions must be yes or no questions. If such an answer would be misleading or against the spirit’s own interests it may answer with a short phrase of a few words instead, which counts as two answers for the purpose of the spell. The spirit’s knowledge is limited to its own perceptions and interests, and it usually answers questions literally and may not volunteer information, though some spirits are more apt to be helpful and some spirits are more likely to attempt to deceive (while giving literally true answers).

You cannot contact the same spirit more than once per week.

The Dragon’s Hoard #7 © 2021, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Miguel Colon, Robert J. Grady, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Kimmel, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

Ghost Ship.name: Ghost Ship
Ghost Ship.description:
Classes: Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard

You create an illusory ghost ship that sails across a 30-foot cube within range. Each creature within the area that can see the ship must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or becomefrightenedfor the next minute. Afrightenedcreature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Pirates and Plunder A Compendium For 5e © 2024 Published by Mythos Chronicles; Author Filippo Bardoscia

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Faceless Wanderer.name: Faceless Wanderer
Faceless Wanderer.description:
While under the effects of this spell, nobody you encounter will remember your physical features once you have left their presence. Upon recollection, you will appear in their memories as someone with your vague shape and a blurred face. This spell can be seen through with truesight, detected withdetect magic, and dispelled bydetect magic.

5E: Age of Antiquity Adventure and Intrigue in the Ancient World © 2019 Aruzian Publishing, Stephen Delucchi, Marcus Lundin

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Pnak Otic Word.name: Pnak Otic Word
Pnak Otic Word.description:
Your utterance of impossible syllables confounds the minds of all enemies within 20 feet of you. Each such enemy with fewer than 100hit pointsis affected byconfusion, as the spell. At the end of its turn, an affected creature can attempt aWissave to end the effect, but has tactical disadvantage on the saving throw if another affected creature is within 10 feet.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Rift.name: Rift
Rift.description:
You conjure a small rift to another plane on a point you can see within range. When you cast this spell, choose one of the following natures.

The rift exhibits the chosen nature for the duration.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Wall of Visions.name: Wall of Visions
Wall of Visions.description:
Classes: bard, sorcerer, warlock, wizard

You conjure a wall of silvery mist in which float hundreds of spectral eyes. You can make the wall up to 40 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick or create a ringed wall up to 15 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick.

The wall is opaque, but while the spell lasts you can choose to see as though you were standing at any point on either side of the wall. Among other things, this allows you to target creatures on the other side of the wall with attacks and spells. Other than seeing from a different location, this vision uses your normal senses.

The mist of the wall is insubstantial, and creatures can pass through it unhindered, but any creature other than you that does so experiences terrifying visions. The first time a creature enters the wall on a turn or when it starts its turn inside the wall, it must make aWisdomsaving throw. The creature takes 4d8 psychic damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Hawk’s Vision.name: Hawk’s Vision
Hawk’s Vision.description:
You gain extraordinary visual acuity. For the duration, you gain Advantage onWisdom(Perception) checks that rely on sight, and the ability to seeinvisiblecreatures. Additionally, short range on ranged weapons is doubled.

The Dragon’s Hoard #58© 2025, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Tom Knauss, Robert J. Grady, Darrin Drader, Michael Mifsud, James-Levi Cooke.

Enervating Ray.name: Enervating Ray
Enervating Ray.description:
You create three rays of necromantic energy and hurl them at targets within range. You can hurl them at one target or several.

Make a ranged spellattackfor each ray. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 necrotic damage. If this damage reduces an organic target to0 hit points, it dies instantly and rots away to a steaming pile of offal. Inorganic targets such as constructs (except wood or flesh constructs) do not rot but are not immune to this spell’s damage.

This spell automatically causes up to a 10-foot cube of nonmagical plants, excluding plant creatures, to rot on a hit.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you create one additional ray for each slot level above 2nd.

Troubadours & Tenders of the Grove, Pugilists & Pact Makers A Scarred Lands Character Options Supplement By Vorpal Tales Authors: Patrick Warren, Shawn McNamara, Tyler Middleton, Zachery Naldrett

Necrotic Burst.name: Necrotic Burst
Necrotic Burst.description:
Classes: Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard

You release a burst of necrotic energy from your body. Each creature in a 10-foot radius around you (other than yourself) must make aConstitutionsaving throw, taking 1d6 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Conduit.name: Conduit
Conduit.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Warlock, Wizard The
Conduit.description:
Classes: Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Warlock, Wizard

The target must make aWisdomsaving throw, or for the duration of the spell, you can use your action to cast spells as if you were in the target’s space, with the target acting as a conduit for your spellcasting. Each spell you cast through the target requires a spell slot of the spell’s level or higher. If the target is subjected to a charm or compulsion effect while under the influence of this spell, it can make a secondWisdomsaving throw. If both saving throws fail, the spell ends and you are affected by the spell instead.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Guiding Star.name: Guiding Star
Guiding Star.components: V, S, M (sprinkle of flash powder)
Guiding Star.duration: of the spell, as an action
Guiding Star.description:
Classes:druid,ranger,sorcerer,warlock

You form a bond with your current location when you cast this spell. For the remaining duration of the spell, as an action you can determine your approximate distance from that area as well as the direction you must travel in order to reach it.

You cannot determine the location of the area if you are on a different plane. The area counts as “very familiar” for the purposes ofteleportor similar spells. You can only attune yourself to one location at a time. If you cast the spell at another spot you lose the ability to locate your original area.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a 3rd-level slot, the duration is increased to 7 days.

Legendary Classes: Templars & Tyrants© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Clinton J. Boomer, Amber Scott

Primeval Interdiction.name: Primeval Interdiction
Primeval Interdiction.description:
Area: one creature or 20-foot radius

Some cultists venerate primordial beings whose existence predates the rise of more modern religions, even those of civilizations now thought ancient. To those who worship in his name he therefore is able to grant the power to interrupt the flow of divine energies of beings less ancient than he. This spell can be used in three ways.

Area Interdiction: You can cut off an area from the power of other divinities, creating an emanation that interferes with the ability of creatures to castcleric,druid,paladin, orrangerspells, or to use magical class abilities of those classes. A creature wishing to use such an ability must succeed at aWisdomsaving throw, taking a -1 penalty on their saving throw for every 5 points of the caster’s Madness score (as above). If theWisdomsaving throw fails, the spell or ability is wasted without effect. It has no effect on magic items. If this spell is cast on in an area with ahallowspell cast upon an altar of an eldritch being, such as a Great Old One or Elder God, the area of effect is increased to a 20-foot radius.

Divine Dispelling: You can use primeval interdiction just as you woulddispel magic, but it affects onlycleric,druid,ranger, andpaladinspells and it automatically dispels spells of 6th level or lower. You can add 1 to your checks todispelhigher-level spells for every 5 points of your Madness score.

Cleric,druid,paladin, orrangerspells with the mythos descriptor are unaffected by primeval interdiction.

The Dragon’s Hoard #3 © 2021, Legendary Games; Lead Designer: Jason Nelson. Authors Matt Kimmel, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Scott D. Young, Mark Hart, and Jeff Ibach.

Recall Death.name: Recall Death
Recall Death.description:
A creature you choose in range must make aCharismasaving throw. It takes 7d8 + 30 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Redeemer of Souls.name: Redeemer of Souls
Redeemer of Souls.components: V, S, M (fragment of your life energy)
Redeemer of Souls.description:
You touch an evil-aligned creature, stare into its eyes, and look deep into its very soul. You sacrifice a part of your vitality to send the evil-aligned creature to another plane of existence and have a vision in which it can see all the potential of a life lived by the virtues of the good. This spell strains the confines of your soul so much that you take 10d10 necrotic damage, which can’t be reduced or prevented by any means.

The creature must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw, or be banished to a harmlessdemiplanethat looks like it’s straight out of heaven. The creature sees itself helping the poor, saving the innocent, praying in a temple, and fighting the good fight around every corner; and witnesses the serenity, peace, and happiness it might have experienced if it had chosen this different path. The target can be deeply affected by, and may even choose to be redeemed as a result of these visions.

The vision lasts a year in thedemiplaneand an hour in the material plane. After an hour, if the creature has decided to walk the path of atonement, it reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. If the target does notwishto be atoned, it returns somewhere in its native plane of existence and it cannot use the benefits of planar travel for 10d100 years by any means.

Corpus Angelus © 2022 Dream Realm Storytellers LTD.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Spire of Stone.name: Spire of Stone
Spire of Stone.description:
You cause a spire of rock to burst out of the ground, floor, or another surface beneath your feet. The spire is as wide as your space, and lifting you, it can rise up to 20 feet in height. When the spire appears, a creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on aDexteritysaving throw or fallprone.

As a bonus action onyour turn, you can cause the spire to rise or descend up to 20 feet to a maximum height of 40 feet. If you move off of the spire, it immediately collapses back into the ground. When the spire disappears, it leaves the surface from which it sprang unharmed. You can create a new spire as a bonus action for the duration of the spell.

Instant Armor.name: Instant Armor
Instant Armor.description:
Classes:antipaladin,cleric,paladin,ranger,sorcerer

You immediately conjure a suit of armor around yourself.

It can resemble any type of armor you wish, but it always provides AC 14 + yourDexteritymodifier (maximum 2).

If you wish, the armor can be emblazoned with your holy symbol. While the instant armor exists, it replaces any other armor or protective garments you are wearing. When the instant armor disappears, your existing armor returns.

Instead of calling a suit of armor, you can instead conjure a shield, which replaces any shield you are using.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC for each slot level above 2nd, up to a maximum of +3.

Legendary Classes: Templars & Tyrants© 2023, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Darrin Drader, Miguel Colon, Clinton J. Boomer, Amber Scott

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Awareness.name: Awareness
Awareness.description:
You touch a creature and grant it a heightened awareness of its surroundings. For the spell’s duration, the target creature can makeWisdom(Perception) checks as a bonus action.

Warlock Grimoire 4. ©2023 Open Design LLC. Authors: Lou Anders, Wolfgang Baur, HH Carlan, Robert Fairbanks, Basheer Ghouse, Richard Green, Tim Hitchcock, Jeremy Hochhalter, Victoria Jaczko, Rajan Khanna, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Jonathan Miley, Kelly Pawlik, Sebastian Rombach, Adam W. Roy, Paul Scofield, Amber Stewart, Brian Suskind, Mike Welham.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Hesitate.name: Hesitate
Hesitate.description:
Classes:bard,cleric,sorcerer,warlock,wizard

You cause a creature to perceive its enemies as mighty and impossible to defeat, filling it with doubt and foreboding as it begins its turn. If the target fails aWisdomsaving throw, it can move normally but cannot take any other action, bonus action, orreactionon that turn. A creature with legendary actions can still take them.

Each round thereafter, the target can use a bonus action to attempt a new saving throw to end the spell. If failed, the effects continue for an additional round. If youattackthe target, the spell ends immediately.

The Dragon’s Hoard #47© 2024, Legendary Games; Authors Jason Nelson, Michael Mifsud, Darrin Drader, Scott Young, Mike Welham, Miguel Colon, and Matt Kimmel

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Summon Mascot.name: Summon Mascot
Summon Mascot.description:
You call forth a Triptych’s mascot. It manifests in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. This corporeal form uses the Triptych Mascot stat block (see Chapter 6: Monsters). The creature resembles the mascot of your Triptych, which determines certain traits in its stat block. The creature disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. The creature is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the creature shares yourinitiativecount, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any, it takes theDodgeaction and uses its move to avoid danger.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2 nd level or higher, use the higher level whenever the spell’s level appears in the stat block. At 3rd level, you can choose the creature’ssizeto be Small or Medium and at 6th level, you can choose the creature’ssizeto be Small, Medium, or Large.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Sickening Reality.name: Sickening Reality
Sickening Reality.description:
DurationConcentration, up to 1 minute

You place a curse on the target that forces them to seek some kind of mind-altering state. The target must make aWisdomthrow or anytime the target is not subject to an enchantment or illusion spell of 2nd level or higher or if they are not under the influence of a drug, they arepoisoned. If the target creature ispoisonedand subject to an effect that also imposes thepoisonedcondition, they are alsostunned.

At Higher Levels. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. If you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration is 8 hours. If you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration is 24 hours. If you use a 9th level spell slot, the spell lasts until it is dispelled. Using a spell slot of 5th level or higher grants a duration that doesn’t require concentration.

Ear Piercing Scream (5E), © 2024, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Connor Bates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Conjure Construct.name: Conjure Construct
Conjure Construct.description:
You summon a construct of challenge rating 5 or lower to harry your foes. It appears in an unoccupied space you can see within range. It disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends.

The construct is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Rollinitiativefor the construct, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any commands to the construct, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes noactions.

If your concentration is broken, the construct doesn’t disappear. Instead, you lose control of the construct, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it mightattack. An uncontrolled construct can’t be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it.

The construct deals double damage to objects and structures.

The GM has the construct’s statistics.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the challenge rating increases by 1 for each slot level above 5th.

Tome of Heroes ©2022 Open Design LLC; Authors: Celeste Conowitch, Jeff Lee, Sarah Madsen, Ben McFarland, Kelly Pawlik, Brian Suskind

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Rite of Rain.name: Rite of Rain
Rite of Rain.description:
You conduct a special rite through dance or prayer. At the end of the rite, you touch a point on the ground beneath you. For the duration, the area within 30 feet of that point is blessed by refreshing rains. The area isdifficult terrainfor creatures hostile to you. In addition, when a creature in the area rolls a 1 on a damage die for a spell that deals cold damage or lightning damage, the creature can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

If you cast this spell every day for 10 days in the same location, plants in the area grow twice as quickly and yield twice as much for 1 year.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Aqua Stomp.name: Aqua Stomp
Aqua Stomp.description:
Invoking the primal power of water, you conjure a colossal surge of water directly above a target area within range, causing it to crash down in a devastating impact. The deluge affects a 40-foot-radius, 100-foot-high cylinder centered on a point you choose within range.

Each creature in the area must make aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d10 bludgeoning damage, is knockedprone, and is submerged 20 feet under water. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and is not knockedproneor submerged.

The sheer force of the water modifies the terrain and creates a temporary pool that is 20 feet deep and remains until it naturally drains or evaporates.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Cataclysmic Rebuke.name: Cataclysmic Rebuke
Cataclysmic Rebuke.description:
Class(es): sorcerer, warlock,wizard

In response to taking damage, you release a burst of cataclysmic energy. The creature that damaged you must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, it takes 10d6 force damage and is knockedprone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’t knockedprone.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 5th.

Cure Wounds.name: Cure Wounds
Cure Wounds.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of hit points equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.

Soul Power.name: Soul Power
Soul Power.description:
Choose a willing creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, the target gains 3d6temporary hit points, has advantage onConstitutionsaving throws,resistanceto necrotic damage, and adds 1d4 to allattackrolls, skill checks, and saving throws.

Bloodlet.name: Bloodlet
Bloodlet.description:
Choose one creature you can see within range. That creature makes aConstitutionsaving throw. On a failure, the target takes 2d6 slashing damage, and 1d6 additional slashing damage each time it takes slashing or piercing damage before the spell ends. On a success, the target takes half damage and the spell ends. The target may make aConstitutionsaving throw each time it takes damage from this spell and again at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. This spell has no effect on undead, elementals, constructs, or creatures without blood.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the initial and later damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 1st.

Tome of Spell Mastery, © 2024, Necromancer Games; Author: Frog God Games.

Song of The Forest.name: Song of The Forest
Song of The Forest.components: V, S, M (dried leaf, crumpled and released)
Song of The Forest.description:
You attune your senses to the natural world so that you detect every sound that occurs within 60 feet: wind blowing through branches, falling leaves, grazing deer, trickling streams, and more. You can clearly picture the source of each sound in your mind. The spell gives you tremorsense out to a range of 10 feet. In addition, you have advantage onWisdom(Perception) checks that rely on hearing. Creatures that make no noise or that are magically silent cannot be detected by this spell’s effect.

Song of the forest functions only in natural environments; it fails if cast underground, in a city, or in a building that isolates the caster from nature (GM’s discretion).

Ritual Focus. If you expend your ritual focus, the spell also gives you blindsight out to a range of 30 feet.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Conjure Nature’s Sleigh.name: Conjure Nature’s Sleigh
Conjure Nature’s Sleigh.description:
You chant a hymn of the Old Faith, turning your material component into a Medium-sized sleigh or open carriage and summoning a team of beasts to pull it. At the GM’s discretion, other teams of beasts can be used than those listed inTable: Conjure Nature’s Sleigh. Any beast summoned by this spell has anIntelligenceof 6, can understand one language of your choice that you speak, and gainstemporary hit points. While at least half of your summoned beasts pull the sleigh, you ignoredifficult terrainaccording to the type of beasts you summoned.

Your sleigh serves you as a mount, both in combat and out, and you share an instinctive bond with your summoned beasts that allows you to act as a seamless unit. While in the sleigh, you can make any spell you cast that targets only you also target your summoned beasts. The sleigh itself provides halfcover(+2 to AC andDexteritysaving throws). The summoned beasts are only able to take theDashandDodgeactions.

The beasts act as a singular unit. When half of your summoned beasts are reduced to0 hit points, the sleigh’s movement drops to half speed, and you must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw to maintain your intrinsic bond. On a failure, the beasts scatter and the sleigh reverts back into its material component. As an action, you can release the summoned beasts from their bond, causing them to disappear.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can make the sleigh large enough to fit one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Heavy Metal.name: Heavy Metal
Heavy Metal.components: V, S, M (small marble of lead)
Heavy Metal.description:
Choose a manufactured metal object, such as a metal weapon, a suit of heavy or medium metal armor, or a metal statue, that you can see within range. The object’ssizecan’t be larger than a 5-foot cube. The object’s density instantly increases, making the object ten times heavier.

A weapon affected by this spell gains the Heavy property and loses the Finesse property, if it has that property. A creature wielding a weapon affected by this spell has disadvantage onattackrolls with the weapon, and the weapon deals an extra 1d6 force damage on a hit.

If an affected weapon is two-handed, a creature that starts its turn holding that weapon must succeed on aStrengthsaving throw or drop the weapon.

While a creature wears armor that is affected by this spell, the creature gains a +2 bonus to its AC, and its speed is reduced depending on the type of armor: reduced by 5 feet if the armor is light, halved if the armor is medium, and reduced to 5 feet if the armor is heavy.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Amaurosis.name: Amaurosis
Amaurosis.description:
You point at a creature in range. The creature must make aConstitutionsaving throw or bepoisoned. At the end of each of thepoisonedtarget’s turns, the target must make aConstitutionsaving throw. If the target succeeds on three of these saves, it is no longerpoisoned, and the spell ends. If the target fails three of these saves, the target is no longerpoisonedbut its eyes swell shut and it isblinded.

Since this spell induces a disease in its target, any effect that removes a disease or otherwise ameliorates a disease’s effects apply to it.

Runic Dart.name: Runic Dart
Runic Dart.description:
Target: A creature within range

Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard

You toss a dart of runic energy at a creature you can see. Make a ranged spellattackagainst the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 force damage. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 at 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Resounding Voice.name: Resounding Voice
Resounding Voice.description:
The touched target’s voice becomes magically enhanced. It becomes three times as loud as normal and they have Advantage onCharisma(Intimidation) checks. In addition, the first time the target speaks within aSilencespell, thatSilencespell is dispelled.

Breath of Life: The Marshal (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Author: Michael Messinger

Shapechanger-Bane Weapon.name: Shapechanger-Bane Weapon
Shapechanger-Bane Weapon.description:
You touch a nonmagical weapon. Until the spell ends, that weapon becomes a magic weapon with a +1 bonus toattackanddamage rollsagainst shapechangers. You can use a bonus action and reduce the duration by 10 minutes to have advantage onattackrolls with the weapon against shapechangers until the start of your next turn.

For the purpose of this spell, “shapechanger” refers to any creature with the Change Shape bonus action or the Shapechanger trait or any creature that isn’t in its true form, such as from thepolymorphspell.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.

Conjure Giant.name: Conjure Giant
Conjure Giant.description:
You summon a giant of challenge rating 6 or lower, which appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The giant disappears when it drops to0 hit pointsor when the spell ends. The giant is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Rollinitiativefor the giant, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you) as long as your commands don’t violate its alignment.

If you don’t issue any commands to the giant, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise take noactions. If your concentration is broken, the giant doesn’t disappear, but instead, you lose control of it: the giant becomes hostile toward you and your companions and mightattack. An uncontrolled giant can’t be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after summoned.

The GM has the giant’s statistics.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the challenge rating increases by 1 for each slot level above 6th.

Rain of Sacred Petals.name: Rain of Sacred Petals
Rain of Sacred Petals.description:
You create a flurry of celestial roses that rain down upon a 30-foot-radius area. Fiends and undead entering or beginning their turn in the area must succeed at aConstitutionsaving throw each round or take 11d6 radiant damage. In addition, the falling petals cloud their vision of you and your allies within the area, resulting in a 20% miss chance onranged attacksthey make while either they or their target is within the rain of sacred petals.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a 7th level spell slot or higher, the damage increases by 2d6 for each slot level above 6th.

Clerics & Cultists© 2021, Legendary Games; Author Darrin Drader, Nicholas Hite, Sean K Reynolds, Jason Nelson, Jenny Jarzabski, Miguel Colon, Michael “solomani” Mifsud, Matt Daley, Nathan Reinecke.

S-Smite.name: S-Smite
S-Smite.description:
The first time you hit with a melee weaponattackduring this spell’s duration, your weapon is wreathed in magical energy, dealing an extra 5d6 force damage. Additionally, theattackflashes with a burst of force energy. Every hostile creature within 30 feet of the target must make a successfulConstitutionsaving throw or take 2d6 force damage and be pushed back 10 feet. They take half as much damage and are not pushed back on a successful save.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Tectonic Communion.name: Tectonic Communion
Tectonic Communion.description:
You briefly become one with nature and gain knowledge of the surrounding territory. In the outdoors, the spell gives you knowledge of the land within 100 miles of you. The spell doesn’t function where nature has been replaced by construction, such as in dungeons and towns.

You instantly gain knowledge of up to three facts of your choice about any of the following subjects as they relate to the area:

For example, you could determine the location of powerful undead in the area, the location of major sources of safe drinking water, and the location of any nearby towns.

Breath of Life: The Chosen (5e), © 2025, Orphaned Bookworm Productions, LLC, Authors: Connor Bates, Norman Mitchell Jr., and Paulo César Viola da Silva Maia

Cobra’s Spit.name: Cobra’s Spit
Cobra’s Spit.description:
For the duration of this spell, you gain the ability to spit venom up to 30 feet as an action. When you spit venom, choose one target within range and make a ranged spellattack. On a successful hit, the target takes 4d8 damage and ispoisoneduntil the end of its next turn.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Pierce the Veil.name: Pierce the Veil
Pierce the Veil.description:
You perceive reality as it is, not as illusions. You have advantage on saving throws to perceive illusions and onWisdom(Perception) checks that rely on sight for the duration.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Eye Of The Valkyrja.name: Eye Of The Valkyrja
Eye Of The Valkyrja.description:
This spell entices a valkyrja to notice an enemy combatant and take measures to add the target to the hosts of the valiant dead. As an action, choose one humanoid creature currently engaged in combat that you can see. The target must succeed on aWisdomsaving throw or come to the attention of a valkyrja. Until the end of your next turn, all melee weaponattackrolls made against the target have advantage and the target has disadvantage on all ability checks and saving throws.

However, a valkyrja’s attention is a doubleedged sword. While the spell is in effect, any creature that scores a critical hit on the spell’s target or deals maximum damage on a hit to the spell’s target catches the valkyrja’s eye and consequently suffers the effects of the spell.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Planar Lock.name: Planar Lock
Planar Lock.components: V, S, M (shard of planar crystal worth at least 1,000 gp)
Planar Lock.description:
You create a ward against magical travel that protects up to 40,000 square feet of floor space to a height of 30 feet above the floor. For the duration, creatures can’tteleportinto the area or use portals, such as those created by thegatespell, to enter the area. The spell proofs the area against planar travel, and therefore prevents creatures from accessing the area by other planes of existence.

In addition, the spell damages creatures from other planes of existence. When a creature from another plane enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it takes 10d6 force damage as reality resists its passage.

When you cast this spell, you can designate a password. A creature that speaks the password as it enters the area can bypass the spell’s travel limitation and takes no damage from the spell.

The spell’s area can’t overlap with the area of another planar lock spell. If you cast this spell every day for 30 days in the same location, the spell lasts until it is dispelled, and the material components are consumed on the last casting.

Bow of the Spirit.name: Bow of the Spirit
Bow of the Spirit.description:
You summon to your hand a bow stylized in a manner befitting your inner spirit. This bow counts as a magical longbow and you are proficient with it.

You have a +2 bonus toattackanddamage rollswith it. Choose necrotic, psychic, or radiant when you cast the spell. You can draw the bowstring without an arrow as part of an attack with the bow to create an arrow of shimmering light that deals the chosen damage instead of piercing. When you release this weapon or the spell ends, the bow vanishes.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the bonus increases to +3.

Sandy Petersen’s Planet Apocalypse, © 2021, Petersen Games.

This is not the complete license attribution -see the full license for this page

Vortex of Steam.name: Vortex of Steam
Vortex of Steam.description:
A swirling vortex of hot steam in a 5-foot-radius, 15-foot-high cylinder erupts in the space of a Large or smaller creature you can see within range. The target must make aDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 3d6 fire damage and isrestrainedfor the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half the damage and isn’trestrained. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it must make anotherDexteritysaving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d6 fire damage and remainsrestrained. On a successful save, it doesn’t take any damage and escapes the vortex into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the vortex.

Until the spell ends, if the vortex isn’t restraining a creature, you can use a bonus action to move it up to 20 feet. If you ram the vortex into a creature, that creature must make theDexteritysaving throw with the DC equal to the vortex’s damage, becomingrestrainedon a failed save as normal, and the vortex stops moving. When you move the vortex, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall, hover it at ground level over pits up to 10 feet deep, and skim it across the surface of calm water.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 (both initial and later) for each slot level above 3rd.

Deep Magic Volume 2 ©2023 Open Design Llc; Authors: Celeste Conowitch and Jon Sawatsky.
